On 8 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen in large numbers attacked civilians and shot sporadically in Chibob (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna), coded as Zangon Katab, and killed three persons. Several houses were burnt by the assailants.

On 8 February 2022, Niger militiamen on about 100 motorcycles attacked civilians in Gulbin Boka (Mariga, Niger), killed three residents and abducted several others. Many houses were burnt down, animals food items were stolen.

On 8 February 2022, suspected Deebam militiamen attacked and killed 7 community leaders at their houses in Obufie-Mmahu community (Ohaji, Imo). The victims would be suspected members of the Deewell militia.

On 8 February 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists in large numbers attacked civilians and shot sporadically in Sabon Kaura (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) and killed three persons, other sources report four fatalities. Several houses were burnt by the assailants and many persons were missing.

On 8 February 2022, Nigerian military forces repelled an attack by Waja communal militiamen in Nyuwar (Balanga, Gombe). One soldier was killed, several houses were affected, residents of the town and neighboring town fled due for safety.

On 8 February 2022, sea pirates attacked fishers from the Ilaje ethnic group while they were fishing in Town-Brass (Brass, Bayelsa). Five fisher were killed, scores were wounded and unspecified number of others are missing. The assailants also stole the victims' engines, Ilaje residents have fled the community.

On 8 February 2022, an armed group contracted by a traditional ruler and some chiefs from the Beachland Estate attacked journalists living at the Arepo estate (Obafemi, Ogun) and destroyed the entrance arc of the estate over the journalists' refusal to pay homage to the palace.

On 8 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians, killed an unspecified number of persons and burned down farms in Hayin Dan Miciji, Gusau LGA (Zamfara). An unspecified number of persons were abducted, animals were rustled and houses were looted by the assailants who shot sporadically. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 8 February 2022, Katsina militiamen clashed with Gidan Kanawa militia men in Gidan Kanawa, Funtua LGA (Katsina) as they tried to repel an attack on civilians, killing three persons. The attack was a reprisal for a previous attack that was repelled by local vigilantes in the area.
On 8 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen in large numbers attacked civilians in Zaman Dabo (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) and killed one person. The victim was burnt to death, several houses were set ablaze.
On 8 February 2022, armed individuals abducted a man from Oko town (Aguata, Anambra), there are no reports about ransom demands. The abductors also attacked civilians in Ekwulobia [coded separately].

On 8 February 2022, unidentified armed individuals killed a traffic controller and one other person when they invaded Ekwulobia town (Aguata, Anambra). Other sources claim three persons were killed, the assailants robbed a filling station in the town.

Around 9 February 2022, armed individuals killed a man after he and his wife were abducted on the way to their farm between Ifon and Molege (Ose, Ondo). The wife was released to inform their families about the abduction and to raise ransom money. The deceased body was found during a search by security operatives.

Around 9 February 2022, Niger militiamen numbering over 200 attacked civilians in Bangi village (Mariga, Niger), an unspecified number of children were killed. Several houses and shops were looted, vandalized and burned while at least 250 cattle were stolen in Argida, Babugadi, Warari, Birnin Boga and Mogola [coded separately]. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

Around 9 February 2022, Niger militiamen numbering over 200 attacked civilians in Babugadi, Birnin Boga and Mogola village, Rijau LGA (Niger) [coded to Warari], Warari and Argida [coded separately]. Several houses and shops were looted, vandalized and burned while at least 250 cattle were stolen. Casualties are unknown.

Around 9 February 2022, Niger militiamen numbering over 200 attacked civilians in Warari village (Rijau, Niger), Babugadi, Argida, Birnin Boga and Mogola [coded separately]. Several houses and shops were looted, vandalized and burned while at least 250 cattle were stolen. Casualties are unknown.

Around 9 February 2022, Niger militiamen numbering over 200 attacked civilians in Argida village (Rijau, Niger), Babugadi, Warari, Argida, Birnin Boga and Mogola [coded separately]. Several houses and shops were looted, vandalized and burned while at least 250 cattle were stolen. Casualties are unknown.
On 9 February 2022, armed individuals shot and killed a woman in Yelewata (Guma, Benue), coded to Gbajimba. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 9 February 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with IPOB militants enforcing a sit in order in Ihiala town (Ihiala, Anambra). Four militants were killed; guns, ammunition, a motorcycle and substances suspected to be cannabis were recovered.

On 9 February 2022, security operatives (presumed police) and local vigilantes clashed with Niger militiamen who attacked civilians in Kasuwan Garba (Mariga, Niger). Four civilians were killed, several others, including women were abducted.

On 9 February 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Niger militiamen in Labi coded to Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The air force also conducted airstrikes in the area. Scores of militiamen were killed and one soldier, accidently bombed by a fighter jet, later died. The group was fleeing from airstrikes in Niger. Total fatalities coded as 21.
On 9 February 2022, policemen engaged armed individuals in an armed clash in Obo Aiyegunle (Ekiti, Kwara) and rescued two abductees. The abductors fled with gunshot wounds.

On 9 February 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked the Secretary of Delta State Council for Islamic Affairs when he was traveling to the mosque for evening prayers in Uloho Avenue in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta). He was killed in the attack.

On 9 February 2022, security operatives from the police and military, supported by local vigilantes, clashed with Katsina militiamen in an attempt to repel an attack in Magama section of Jibia town (Jibia, Katsina). The wife of a businessman in the town was abducted; two policemen, including one DPO, and a civilian were killed, while two soldiers were severely wounded; other sources claim one soldier and unspecified number of civilians were killed, one other soldier was wounded. Fatalities coded as 3.

Around 9 February 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted the wife of Senior Advocate of Nigeria in Aba (Aba South, Abia). Her whereabouts are not known. The abductors fired shots before taking her from the entrance of her home.

On 9 February 2022, a suspected member of an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a commercial motorcyclist and a student of Federal Polytechnic Ede at the Agbalemobode area of the town (Ede North, Osun). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 9 February 2022, armed individuals abducted a former Ekiti state lawmaker and an unspecified number of commuters in the Ijesa-Iju axis of Ikole LGA (Ekiti). The victims were released following efforts from the police, hunters and Amotekun corps [no report of a clash].

On 10 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen engaged in an armed clash with a local defence militia when they attacked Rogoji in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). Five civilians were killed; the attack would be a punishment to residents for cooperating with security operatives.
On 10 February 2022, Niger militiamen abducted an unspecified number of civilians during a house to house search in Bobi (Mariga, Niger). The District Head was also abducted.

On 10 February 2022, 6 armed individuals attacked policemen at a checkpoint at the Marylan axis of Independence Layout (Enugu North, Enugu). Between 2 to 4 policemen were killed and one civilian was abducted by the assailants along the Ugwaji road before the attack.

On 10 February 2022, Nigerian troops and the Civilian JTF engaged Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in an armed clash at Dunga Lawanti (Gubio, Borno). Scores of militants and one soldier were killed; four rifles and two motorcycles were recovered from the militants. Fatalities coded as 21.

On 10 February 2022, two factions of the NURTW clashed in Agbado (Alimosho, Lagos) over collection of tickets at motor parks. Some properties were vandalized and movement in the area was restricted, casualties unknown.

On 10 February 2022, a web developer was beaten by about 20 individuals after being tied up and taken to an incomplete building in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) after being requested a meeting concerning a website he developed at a hotel in Okhoro Street. The man was then taken to a river, stripped naked and beaten again; a ransom was demanded to his family while he was with the group. The group also took valuables that was with the victim.

On 10 February 2022, members of OSPMS engaged in an armed clash with Federal Boys in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). One OSPMS member was killed, security operatives were deployed to the area to restore normalcy. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 10 February 2022, armed individuals attacked and shot at Nigeria customs operatives at a checkpoint in Ozalla (Nkanu West, Enugu). One operative was killed and three others sustained gunshot wounds.

On 11 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked civilians in Ma Kura village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna), coded to Zonkwa. The locals organized themselves against the assailants and the casualties were reduced, but it is not clear if they were armed or clashed with the attackers. About two persons were killed, several others were wounded, houses and food items were set ablaze.

On 11 February 2022, security operatives (presumed police) clashed with Kaduna militiamen nearby Hanyin Liman, in the Zangon Shanu area (Sabon Gari, Kaduna), as the group was abducting people in close-by villages. A mother and baby, abducted from Tudun Mun Tsira village, were rescued, two residents sustained varying degrees of injuries.

On 11 February 2022, policemen foiled an attack by Katsina militiamen and engaged them in an armed clash in Nasarawa Bugaje (Jibia, Katsina). The assailants fled and left rustled animals. 200 cows and 150 sheep were recovered by the policemen. There were no fatalities.

On 11 February 2022, armed individuals suspected to be assassins killed the Director Operations at Kaduna Geographic Information Service at his residence in Barakallahu (Igabi, Kaduna). The reason for the attack is unknown, a nearby community was invaded by the assailants however no attack or looting was carried out.

On 11 February 2022, Nigerian troops, made up of the Air Force and ground troops, conducted a raid on ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants camps in Gujba LGA (Yobe). Scores of militants were killed, others fled with persons suspected to be their family members. Fatalities (scores) coded as 20.

Around 11 February 2022, Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP militants and rescued commuters under threat along the Bula Yobe-Darel Jamel road. Location coded to state capital Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno).
On 11 February 2022, policemen clashed with armed individuals attacking to a police station at Uli (Ihiala, Anambra). The assailants fled, and abandoned their vehicle, there were no casualties.

Around 11 February 2022, Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash at the Banki junction (Bama, Borno) as the militants set up illegal vehicle checkpoints and attacked commuters. The militants fled and abandoned an unspecified number of commuters who were rescued by the soldiers. Some commercial vehicles were hit in the clash; there were no casualties.

On 11 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted a presumed off-duty Customs operative from his residence in Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara); his brother was abducted hours later. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded; the operative was released on 16 February after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 11 February 2022, loyalists of the leader of OSPMS clashed with loyalists of Yoruba activist Sunday Igboho in Soka (Ibadan South West, Oyo). The clash is related to supremacy tussle between the two groups; one member of Sunday Igboho's group was attacked; it is unknown whether he was killed or wounded, his body was not found.

On 12 February 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed one person in Omuobizu clan, Ibaa community (Emohua, Rivers). The attack is suspected be a result of factionalization of the disbanded OSPAC; other sources claim two persons were killed.

On 12 February 2022, Niger militiamen attacked civilians in communities in Magama LGA (Niger), coded to Nasko and assumedly in villages around Nasko, from where the group came through. Some residents were killed, many residents, mostly women and children, were abducted, cattle were rustled. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 12 February 2022, armed individuals, suspected to be security operatives [coded as military], wounded a woman when they invaded Umuonyeoka community (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo), coded as Oru. The security operatives were searching for a member of IPOB to arrest him. They set houses belonging to his siblings ablaze, other properties were destroyed.

On 12 February 2022, suspected cult militiamen killed a man and wounded several others at Akalovo (Owerri North, Imo). The reason is assumed to be a cult war. The victim's body was found the following morning.

On 12 February 2022, Nigerian police and military forces, together with local vigilantes, engaged Niger militiamen in a clash in Nasko (Magama, Niger), after the militiamen attacked civilians at villages around Nasko (coded separately). Scores of militiamen were killed; 20 abductees were rescued, large herds of cattle, weapons and ammunition were recovered. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 12 February 2022, an unidentified armed group dressed in security clothing attacked Ihitte Afoukwu and Okpokunme, coded to Oru (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo). The attackers shot sporadically. Fatalities unknown but some were injured.

On 12 February 2022, a senior military officer shot and wounded his subordinate [assumed to be off-duty] in Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta). The victim was attacked after he requested for a leave to enable him visit his family.

On 12 February 2022, PDP militiamen attacked an agent of the APC and left him critically wounded at a polling unit in Kuje LGA (FCT) during the local council elections. The victim was attacked when he noticed the PDP agents counting disqualified voter sheets to their advantage.
On 12 February 2022, Niger militiamen attacked and killed ten civilians in Kpakegywei and Alaiyi communities in Kudodo district (Shiroro, Niger).
On 12 February 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked policemen on a stop and search duty at a checkpoint in Obeagu, also called Ugboka (Nkanu East, Enugu). Four policemen were killed.

On 12 February 2022, suspected security forces (assumed military forces) attacked Ihitteafoukwu, Umu Okirika, Mpam, Ogbor Umeze and Oparanadim (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo). Some fatalities were reported, coded as 3. The reason for the attack is not known.

On 12 February 2022, armed individuals invaded the house of the Yoruba activist, Sunday Igboho, and killed one occupant in Soka (Ibadan South West, Oyo). Several other people were wounded. Some properties belonging to Sunday Igboho were destroyed.
On 13 February 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed three residents of Apiababum village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna), coded to Zangon Katab.
On 13 February 2022, two unidentified cult militias clashed in Orile Agege (Agege, Lagos). Casualties unknown.

On 13 February 2022, members of KADVS clashed with Kaduna militiamen who invaded Hayin Gada (Giwa, Kaduna), abducted a man and his two children. The militiamen were trailed into the bush, three of them were killed and the abductees were rescued.
On 13 February 2022, Sokoto militiamen attacked and killed two civilians in Adamawa village, Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto).
On 13 February 2022, Sokoto militiamen raped several women and beat residents of Rambadawa village, Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto).
On 13 February 2022, armed individuals shot and killed a chieftain of the PDP in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 13 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted six women from Tsafe LGA (Zamfara) and fled before the arrival of the Joint Task Force operating in the area. There are no reports about demands for ransom.

Around 13 February 2022 (as reported), a security operative, presumed police, beat up a truck driver to a coma at the Joita checkpoint on the Wukari-Zaki Biam highway (Wukari, Taraba). The victim was attacked over his refusal to pay an extra 1000 naira to the security operatives at the checkpoint.

Around 13 February 2022 (between 12 - 15 February), the Nigerien contingent of MNJTF carried out a combined air-ground operation involving air and artillery strikes and ground assaults against Boko Haram (JAS or ISWAP Lake Chad faction) in the areas of Abadam (Abadan, Borno) and Jabulam (Mobbar, Borno) in Nigeria, and Bague Kiessa [Bague Kiessa Koura], Dagaya, Boulayi, and Boula Gana (Bosso, Diffa) in Niger. About twenty militants were killed and weapons and ammo seized. Fatalities are split across six events.

Around 13 February 2022 (between 12 - 15 February), the Nigerien contingent of MNJTF carried out a combined air-ground operation involving air and artillery strikes and ground assaults against Boko Haram (JAS or ISWAP Lake Chad faction) in the areas of Jabulam (Mobbar, Borno) and Abadam (Abadan, Borno) in Nigeria, and Bague Kiessa [Bague Kiessa Koura], Dagaya, Boulayi, and Boula Gana (Bosso, Diffa) in Niger. About twenty militants were killed and weapons and ammo seized. Fatalities are split across six events.

On 13 February 2022, armed individuals invaded a police divisional headquarters and engaged in an armed clash with policemen in Aguata (Aguata, Anambra). Four of the assailants were killed; weapons, ammunition and three phones were recovered.
On 13 February 2022, armed individuals invaded a police station and were repelled by policemen in Ekwulobia (Aguata, Anambra). The assailants fled. There were no casualties.

On 14 February 2022, policemen repelled an attack on a police station by unidentified armed individuals at Ezillo (Ishielu, Ebonyi). The assailants shot and killed three policemen at a checkpoint and attempted to infiltrate the police station before they were repelled, a police van was burnt in the clash.

On 14 February 2022, armed individuals attacked civilians, killed one person and abducted ten others near Adogo (Ajaokuta, Kogi). A ransom of 10 million naira has been demanded, other sources report the demanded amount as 20 million.

On 14 February 2022, the security detail of the Minister of Interior comprising of DSS, NSCDC and NIS operatives repelled armed individuals during an attack on the minister's convoy in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The armed group is suspected to be connected to a political militia.
On 14 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked residents of Tudun Mare community in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). One person was killed, six others were abducted.
On 14 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted six residents of Afogo (Kajuru, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 14 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen engaged in an armed clash with local vigilante members at the Damba Housing Estate in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) as the militiamen attacked civilians. Two local vigilantes were wounded; the wife and two children of the director of Finance at the State Ministry of Finance were abducted; there are no reports about demands for ransom.
On 14 February 2022, Boko Haram militants attacked civilians in Buni (Gujba, Yobe). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 14 February 2022, suspected armed Fulani herders attacked a farmer at his farm in Owalaye (Owo, Ondo). He was chased and then shot. There were no fatalities. He received treatment for his injuries.
On 14 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed the son of a councilor and abducted the councilor and village head in Rimau (Kajuru, Kaduna).
On 15 February 2022, armed individuals ambushed and killed two commuters along the Tsokondi expressway, Wukari LGA (Taraba). The reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 15 February 2022 (as reported), Sokoto militiamen attacked civilians across communities in Tureta LGA (Sokoto), Dange-Shuni and Bodinga LGAs [coded separately]. Three persons were killed and 17 others were abducted; three fatalities split across three events coded as 1.

Around 15 February 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group shot a members of a local self defense militia in Ologbo community (Ikpoba Okha, Edo). One person was shot, according to the Iyatsere of Warri kingdom.

On 15 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked civilians in Anguwar Azara, coded to nearby Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). One person was wounded with a machete and was left unconscious. 10 others, including the two women married to a community leader and four daughters of the community leader, were abducted. One of the women was later released due to her ill health. A ransom of 500 million, which was reduced to 15 million, then 5 million, for the relatives of the traditional ruler has been demanded.

Around 15 February 2022 (as reported), Sokoto militiamen attacked civilians across communities in Dange-Shuni LGA (Sokoto), Bodinga and Tureta LGAs [coded separately]. Three persons were killed and 17 others were abducted; three fatalities split across three events coded as 1.

On 15 February 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked traders at Abia Abbatoir market in Omumauzor community (Ukwa West, Abia), coded to Oke-Ikpe. Eight persons and over 70 cows, assumedly from Fulani pastoralists, were killed. HURIWA claimed that the attack was carried out by members of the deep state and foreign mercenaries.

Around 15 February 2022 (as reported), Sokoto militiamen attacked civilians across communities in Bodinga LGA (Sokoto), Dange-Shuni and Tureta LGAs [coded separately]. Three persons were killed and 17 others were abducted; three fatalities split across three events coded as 1.

On 15 February 2022, Nigerian Navy personnel responded to sporadic shooting by IPOB militants at a checkpoint and engaged the militants in an armed clash at the Uga junction (Ogbaru, Anambra), coded as Atani. One militant was killed, four others were arrested; one vehicle, two machetes, two pistols, hammers and phones were recovered.

On 15 February 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two miners at a mining site in Yelwa-Zangam (Jos North, Plateau), coded to Jos. Other persons escaped the attack. The military task force claimed one person was killed and one was wounded.

On 16 February 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked civilians, wounded four persons and abducted 22 others in Idon town (Kajuru, Kaduna). The assailants shot sporadically during the attack, broke windows and doors.

On 16 February 2022, armed individuals killed a man and abducted the son of the traditional ruler of Gwombe community when they blocked the road between Gwargwada and Gwobe, Kuje LGA (FCT). The abductors demanded for 4 million naira and 2 bags of rice to release the abductee together with 15 others who were abducted separately.

On 16 February 2022, policemen clashed with Katsina militiamen at a point near Zurukuntun (Kankara, Katsina) after the group attacked civilians at Fuloti and Gandu Karfi, Malumfashi LGA. One militiaman was killed, four female abductees and their babies were rescued, 82 cows, 72 sheep and one rifle were recovered.

On 16 February 2022, armed individuals attacked commuters at the Bida Bidi junction (Jos North, Plateau), coded to Jos. Between 2 to 4 persons were killed, many others were wounded. The reason for the attack is unknown, the assailants beat up the victims and stab them with machetes.

On 16 February 2022, Tiv and Jukun militia clashed in Wurukum (Makurdi, Benue) following disagreements over a fishing pond and fishing turns. At least two people were injured and several houses were burned. The house of the area's kindred head was also burnt.
On 16 February 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted eight locals from Agasha (Guma, Benue) at their farms. The victims were rescued by soldiers around 20 February.

On 16 February 2022, policemen clashed with Katsina militiamen who were blocking the road and extorting commuters along the Kankara-Zango road (Kankara, Katsina), coded to Zango. One militiaman was killed and a motorcycle was recovered.

On 16 February 2022, Katsina militiamen attacked civilians at Fuloti and Gandu Karfi, Malumfashi LGA. Four women and their babies were abducted; 82 cows, 72 sheep assumedly from Fulani pastoralists were rustled.

On 17 February 2022, an armed group shot at the vehicle of a candidate for the Benue state House of Assembly for 2023 (name and political party unknown) along the Ukwo-Orokam road in Owukpa, coded to Otukpa (Ogbadibo, Benue). The assailants were later arrested by local vigilantes, casualties unknown.
On 17 February 2022, a large number of armed individuals attacked civilians in Tse Udeghe, Mbapa ward (Gwer West, Benue). Four persons were killed, several others were wounded.

On 17 February 2022, armed individuals hit a man on the head, who fainted, and abducted his wife, while the two, together with their baby and maid, were driving along the Rounder area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) to their home. The victim was released on 19 February after 3 million naira was paid as ransom.
On 17 February 2022, a group kidnapped a woman at her house in the Oke Ode area, Ayetoro road, in or around Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).

On 17 February 2022, unidentified armed group abducted eight persons, including the son of a traditional ruler, at Illela village (Karim Lamidu, Taraba), coded as Karim Lamido. A ransom of 120 million naira was demanded.

On 17 February 2022, armed individuals attacked workers of Okomu palm oil company in or around Okomu (Ovia South West, Edo). The attack was assumed to be a reprisal for the arrest of two persons over their involvement in a previous attack.

On 17 February 2022, an operative of SARS shot and killed the leader of a private security outfit after an argument in Oke Ado (Ibadan South West, Oyo). The victim was also a member of OPC, he died on 19 February from the gunshot wounds.
On 17 February 2022, armed individuals attacked commuters around the Ahume village, along Naka-Makurdi (Gwer West, Benue). One person was killed.
On 18 February 2022, unidentified gunmen attacked civilians around Koko LGA (Kebbi), coded to Lani-Kango. Casualties unknown.

On 18 February 2022, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants attacked two bank staffs in Akwa-Etiti (Idemili South, Anambra). The assailants assumed the victims were security operatives and shot at them, in their car. They were injured.

On 18 February 2022, Niger militiamen attacked civilians and killed seven persons in Gpekure (Shiroro, Niger), coded to Tungan Makuba. Five women and two men were also abducted, houses and food stuff were burnt by the assailants.

On 18 February 2022, policemen and local vigilante engaged Zamfara militiamen around the Gurgurwa axis of Bungudu LGA (Zamfara) as they were attacking and abducting civilians. 24 abductees were rescued while the assailants fled.

On 18 February 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked and killed at least 18 civilians in Kadadaba (Anka, Zamfara). An unspecified number of persons were wounded; money, foodstuff and domestic animals were looted in the attack that lasted till the next morning.
On 18 February 2022, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with the Nigerian army in Ajigin (Damboa, Borno). Several soldiers were killed and wounded, one vehicle was burned. Several fatalities coded as 3.
On 18 February 2022, ISWAP claimed a mortar shell attack in Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). There were no casualties.

On 18 February 2022, Rufu and Lissam communal militias clashed in Ussa LGA (Taraba), coded to Lissam. An unspecified number of properties were destroyed, a curfew was imposed on the area by the local government chairman.
Around 19 February 2022 (as reported), unidentified armed individuals abducted a high chief at Igasi Akoko (Akoko North West, Ondo). The abductee escaped when the abductors fell asleep.
On 19 February 2022, unidentified cult militiamen killed a man during the primary election of the APC at Atakumosa East LGA (Osun), coded to Iperindo.

On 19 February 2022, unidentified gunmen killed two Fulani civilians on their way to Bakin-Turu (Shanga, Kebbi). The assailants were on their way to attack the village when they saw the victims and killed.
On 19 February 2022, a unidentified gunmen mounted a blockade and killed three commuters along the Yauri-Koko road (Koko, Kebbi). Several other commuters were wounded by the assailants.

On 19 February 2022, unidentified gunmen abducted an unspecified number of residents in Bakin-Turu (Shanga, Kebbi). The abductees include men and women, domestic animals were rustled by the assailants. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 February 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed three civilians along the Lordye- Gbajimba road, (Guma LGA, Benue). The victims were ambushed while returning from a funeral.
On 19 February 2022, Nigerian soldiers clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists in Gbekyor village (Guma, Benue), coded to Gbajimba, and rescued 8 abductees. Casualties unknown.

On 19 February 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked and shot two operatives of the NDLEA at a checkpoint in Ezamgbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). One operative was killed; the other was wounded; the assailants set a patrol truck ablaze, and stole one rifle.

On 19 February 2022, Sokoto militiamen attacked civilians, wounded one person and abducted nine others in Yartsakuwa (Rabah, Sokoto). Over 20 persons were initially abducted, others were returned, except nine; among the abductees were a serving councilor and the wives and daughter of a former councilor. The assailants stole food, drugs and several motorcycles from shops and houses, a ransom of 60 million naira was demanded.
On 19 February 2022, Niger militiamen attacked civilians and killed one person in Tungan Makuba (Shiroro, Niger).

On 20 February 2022, unidentified armed individuals killed two private security guards of a fuel station in Ilishan-Remo (Ikenne, Ogun). The assailants did not steal anything from the station, the bodies of the victims were found the following morning.

On 20 February 2022, suspected IPOB/ESN militants attacked a police divisional headquarters clashing with policemen in Umundugba (Isu, Imo). The assailants threw petrol bombs and IEDs that ignited the station, killed two policemen, wounded one and destroyed some vehicles. 17 men and a woman were arrested in connection with the attack.
On 20 February 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed a businessman around the Ukpor-Lilu-Orsumoghu-Azia-Mbosi road, coded to Lilu (Ihiala, Anambra).
On 20 February 2022, unidentified militiamen attacked and killed three civilians in Sabon Gari village, in Bashar district (Wase, Plateau).

Around 5 March 2022 (as reported), members of OSPAC shot and killed an off duty soldier in Obele Gorri (Emohua, Rivers) following an argument that ensued when the soldier tried to free some of his relatives from OSPAC members. Two other persons related to the soldier sustained gunshot wounds.

Around 6 March 2022 (as reported), soldiers attacked Obelle (Emohua, Rivers) after their off-duty colleague was killed by an armed group that had built a checkpoint against illegal oil bunkering (coded as a separate event). The military arrested some, burnt down a local vigilante camp and destroyed another checkpoint built by the police of the community. There were no fatalities.

Around 6 March 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked a suspected off-duty military officer who had returned home in Obelle (Emohua, Rivers). He was shot dead in front of his residency. The attackers had created checkpoints against illegal oil bunkering.

On 6 March 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a large number Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants who attacked a forward operating base in Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). 17 militants were killed, three others were arrested; motorcycles and other weapons were recovered.
On 6 March 2022, Sokoto militiamen attacked and killed two farmers working on their farmlands in Sardauna (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). A third farmer fled to a nearby village unhurt.
On 7 March 2022, armed individuals ambushed Yansakai militia members in Zuru emirate, Sakaba LGA (Kebbi). Between 57 to 63 Yansakai members were killed.

On 7 March 2022, Niger militiamen clashed with CJTF and local defense fighters in Anguwan-Toma, near Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). At least 5 people were killed and others were injured. The group left with an unspecified number of cattle.

Around 7 March 2022 (as reported), Ochon and Alesi Communal militias clashed around Ochon (Obubra, Cross River) and Alesi (Ikom LGA), over a land dispute. About 15 persons were killed, four were wounded on both sides and over 2000 persons were displaced.

On 7 March 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed civilians including many women and children in Tor-Damisa (Donga, Taraba). Several other persons were wounded; several houses and valuables were also destroyed. The attack was a reprisal over an attack that left a Fulani man wounded by suspected Tiv militia in the area [coded separately]. The police claim 7 persons, including just one woman killed and many others were wounded while others suggest at least 20 persons. Fatalities coded as 7.

On 7 March 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed the traditional ruler of Olowe Gbagura at his residence in Gbagura (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The victims body was set ablaze by the assailants; the reason for the attack is unknown; the victim however had a land dispute with some individuals.
On 7 March 2022, Nigerian troops repelled an attack by ISWAP militants in Damboa LGA (Borno). The militants fled and casualties unknown.

On 7 March 2022, Ebube Agu security officers attacked civilians in the Amankwo community (Orsu, Imo). A couple were killed, with witness stating that many other were also dead; the group torched the timber section of the community's market. The residents fled. Fatalities split between 2 events.

On 8 March 2022, police and military forces of Nigeria repelled an attack by Katsina militiamen in Barawa village (Batagarawa, Katsina). The militiamen fled with gunshot wounds, five of their motorcycles were recovered and burnt.

On 8 March 2022, armed individuals killed at least eight military officers in Zuru emirate, Sakaba LGA (Kebbi) following their deployment in response to the killing of Yansakai members (coded separately) in the area.

Around 8 March 2022 (as reported), operatives of the DSS shot a presumed off duty soldier in the stomach in Lekki (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos). The victim tried to produce his identity card when he was shot; he died in the hospital.
On 8 March 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists killed about five persons in Ahentse community, Ndzorov ward (Guma, Benue). Many others were seriously wounded in the attack.

On 8 March 2022, around 600 armed individuals on over 200 motorcycles attacked the convoy of the Kebbi state deputy governor and clashed with soldiers, policemen and local self-defense militants in Kainya village (Danko, Kebbi). 19 people were killed (13 soldiers, 5 policemen and 1 local vigilante); 8 others soldiers were wounded, two others were missing, one gun truck belonging to the army was burnt. Fatalities coded as 19.
On 8 March 2022, NDLEA police officers clashed with an unidentified gang or cult along the Airport road in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). 1 person was killed and 6 others were injured.

On 8 March 2022, armed individuals hit a man, causing him to pass out in Aiyetoro (Egbado North, Ogun), while abducting two of his grandchildren. A ransom of 15 million naira was demanded for the release of the abductees.
On 8 March 2022, a group kidnapped two siblings in Aiyetoro (Egbado North, Ogun). They were released around 15 March after the payment of ransom.

On 8 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed two of security guards of a Catholic priest in Kudendan (Chikun, Kaduna). The priest was abducted, together with a woman and two of her children. Other reports mention one guard and one other resident were killed. There are no reports about ransom demands; the priest was killed while he was still in captivity [coded separately].

Around 8 March 2022 (as reported), Kaduna militiamen shot and killed a man, presumably around Rigacikun (Igabi, Kaduna), whom they abducted in the village on February 24 [coded separately]. A ransom of 1 million naira was paid to the abductors before the victim was killed.
On 8 March 2022, ISWAP and Boko Haram (presumed JAS faction) militants engaged in an armed clash at Yauma Wango village in Mobbar LGA (Borno), coded to Damasak. Nine militants were killed.
On 8 March 2022, Boko Haram elements attacked and killed a Cameroonian soldier in Wulgo [Kirta Wulgo] (Monguno, Borno).

On 8 March 2022, Ebube Agu security officers attacked civilians for the second day in the Amankwo community (Orsu, Imo). A couple were killed, with witness stating that many other were also dead; the group torched the timber section of the community's market. The residents fled. Fatalities split between 2 events.
On 9 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed three persons and abducted two others at the Galadima area of Goni Gora (Chikun, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands for the abductees.

On 9 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists shot and injured three people in Uwheru (Ughelli North, Delta). The group kidnapped a student and three contractors working at a secondary school and demanded money and food items for their release.

On 9 March 2022, armed individuals killed a police operative of So Safe Corps while on surveillance duty in Areke area of Shagamu LGA (Ogun), coded to Shagamu. The operational vehicles of the operatives was shot at by the assailants who fled the scene.

On 9 March 2022, suspected cult militias members beat and beheaded one person in Sagbama (Sagbama, Bayelsa) after dragging him out of his house. The event happened within the context of clashes over supremacy among the Icelanders, Greenlanders and Bobos cult groups in the state. It is unknown whether the victim was part of a group; the man's head was taken.

Around 9 March 2022 (between 9 - 10 March), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two people in Yelwata, Guma LGA (Benue), coded to Gbajimba, and Iye [coded separately]. The assailants were presumed to have come from neighboring Nassarawa state. Reports state the victims were farmers.

Around 9 March 2022 (between 9 - 10 March), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed between 4 to 6 fishers in Iye (Guma, Benue) and Yelwata [coded separately]. The assailants were presumed to have come from neighboring Nassarawa state.
Around 9 March 2022 (between 9 - 10 March), an armed group shot and killed a poultry farmer at his farm in Ago Aduloju (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 9 March 2022, armed individuals shot and killed a woman at her residence in Bashorun (Akinyele, Oyo). The victim was the daughter of the immediate past Iyalode of Ibadan land; the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 9 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked students and staff of a secondary school in Ohoror, Ughelli North LGA (Delta), coded to Ughelli. Many people were injured.
On 9 March 2022, armed individuals killed a newspaper vendor while he was trying to board a vehicle at Kabusa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 9 March 2022, presumed ISWAP/Boko Haram fired mortar shells against civilians in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). Casualties unknown.

Around 10 March 2022 (between 10 - 11 March), armed individuals attacked civilians in Shimfida (Jibia, Katsina). Seven children died and others were injured in a stampede caused by the attack, which took place after soldiers evacuated the city.

On 10 March 2022, Nigerian ground troops with air support carried out a clearance operation against armed individuals around Sakaba LGA (Kebbi), in the boundary between Kebbi and Zamfara state. Scores of militiamen were killed and three informants were arrested. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 10 March 2022, an armed group opened fire against students during a sports competition in a high school in Ikare-Akoko (Akoko North East, Ondo). 1 students was killed and two others were injured.

On 10 March 2022, ISWAP/Boko Haram militants abducted one IRC aid worker and two (likely unarmed) guards when they infiltrated the compound of a humanitarian organization in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals kidnapped no fewer than 14 worshippers in a mosque in a community near Tudun Amada (Giwa, Kaduna). Several houses were also invaded, with the group abducting 10 women. Four abductees were released later the day.

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals abducted no fewer then 11 people, the majority elderly women, as they were heading to a refugee camp near Shimfida (Jibia, Katsina), following an attack on their village (coded separately).

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals started shooting in an attempt to disarm a local defensce militia providing security to a funeral in Ndingbu village, Nnewi North LGA (Anambra), coded to Nnewi. Casualties unknown.

On 11 March 2022, Niger militiamen in large numbers attacked an evangelical church, killed three persons and abducted eight others in Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). The assailants, who left the area before the arrival of policemen, demanded for a ransom of 250 million naira for the abductees release.
Around 11 March 2022, armed individuals abducted a person in Mararaban Daudu, Muya LGA (Niger), coded to Sarkin Pawa.

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals killed at least one trader and kidnapped another in a rural market in Chibani, Muya LGA (Niger), coded to Sarkin Pawa. The group took food items and destroyed goods.

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals killed an (presumed off-duty) Operations Officer of the 3 Battalion of the Nigerian Army behind the Urhobo College, at the Enerhen road in Warri (Warri South, Delta). Some suspects were arrested.

On 11 March 2022, armed individuals kidnapped a staff member of a local defense group in Utuh (Nnewi South, Anambra), also setting the group's office on fire after opening fire at a funeral in Ndingbu village (coded separately).
On 11 March 2022, two children were kidnapped by two unidentified individuals at the Akorede market in Ilesa (Ilesha West, Osun).
On 11 March 2022, a student was beaten, shot and injured by a police officer during a stop-and-search operation between Eruwa and Ibadan (Akinyele, Oyo). The police officer was arrested.

Around 11 March 2022 (as reported), soldiers shot sporadically at a market and killed two civilians while trying to shoot suspected Kaduna militiamen in Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). The suspected militiamen fled.
On 11 March 2022, an unidentified armed group beat up a pastor and robbed him of his car at Mile 1 in Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The attack occurred beside a police checkpoint.

On 11 March 2022, police operatives clashed with an armed group in Kanyar-Nogora road, Kukar-Sheka village, Kankara LGA (Katsina), coded to Kankara, during an operation in response to an attack to Yammama, Malumfashi LGA (coded separately). Three armed individuals were killed and 7 cows were recovered.
On 12 March 2022, armed individuals kidnapped a pastor from the Christ Apostolic Church in Oke Ako (Ikole, Ekiti). The group demanded ransom for his release, but the pastor managed to escape.

On 12 March 2022, members of a Christian church were beaten, injured and detained by navy officials in Ikot Obong Village, Ikpa Ibekwe clan, Ikot Abasi LGA (Akwa Ibom), coded to Ikot Abasi, as church members were beginning construction on the church's land. According to the church members, the Navy officers are opposed to the land developing opposite of their base.

Around 12 March 2022, the military claimed to have clashed with armed individuals during an operation in Obayantor (Ikpoba Okha, Edo). At least nine people (two soldiers and seven civilians) were killed. More than one hundred people escaped to neighboring areas. There are reports of a land/authority dispute within the community with actors involved in the event, but the police affirmed it was an operation deployed from information about criminal operation in the area.

Around 12 March 2022 (as reported), armed individuals kidnapped at least 15 people from the Kekun Waje district, Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The group demanded the disarmament of the local vigilante group for the release of the abductees, the victims were released after 4 million naira was paid for a total of 75 abductees, the abductors kept a 6 year old girl behind and claimed a member of the militia adopted her. The girl was released by the wife of the militia member on 6 June after he was killed in a clash.
On 12 March 2022, a journalist was abducted by unidentified individuals in the Chika area of Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory).
Around 12 March 2022 (as reported), a local hunter shot and killed a Fulani pastoralist in Ewekoro (Ewekoro, Ogun). The victim's body was found in a grave on the assailant's farm.
On 12 March 2022, a Katsina militia killed two siblings and abducted five other persons in Hayin Labaran, Funtua LGA (Katsina).

On 12 March 2022, armed individuals opened fire against a passenger car in the Yantumaki/Danmusa road, near Yan Tumaki (Dan-Musam Katsina) after the driver refused to stop. The car hit a tree and capsized; no fewer than five people died and three were injured.
On 12 March 2022, a girl was kidnapped by armed individuals at her house at the Danjuma area of Oke-Aro, Ajure (Akure South, Ondo). The group also took her fathers mobile phone.

On 12 March 2022, police operatives clashed with armed individuals in Tugu Gari village, Matazu LGA (Katsina), coded to Matazu, as the group attacked the village, rustling cattle. One armed individual was killed and 32 cows and 23 sheep were recovered.
On 13 March 2022, Sokoto militiamen killed one trader and abducted several others when they blocked the Sokoto-Goronyo road (Goronyo, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 March 2022, an ethnic Hausa was assaulted and killed by four unidentified individuals at his farm in Giri village, in the outskirts of the Federal Capital Territory, coded to Abuja, Abuja Municipal. Other five people were also injured, three severely. Four suspects were arrested.

On 13 March 2022, a taxi driver (Okada) was killed by suspected cult militia members along a road in or around Jesse (Ethiope West, Delta). Rival cult militias have recently clashed in the area (coded separately).

On 13 March 2022, overnight, armed individuals kidnapped three Yorubas in Bokolo, Funtua LGA (Katsina), coded to Funtua. The victims are an electrician, an university student and his five year old sister. The group demanded N30 million naira for their release.
Around 14 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists kidnapped four people in Agadama (Ughelli North, Delta). The group demanded money and food items for their release.

Around 14 March 2022 (as reported), military forces clashed with militiamen in Mariga LGA (Niger), coded to Mariga, while the group was trying to move stolen cattle in the area. Scores of militiamen were killed; fatalities coded as 20.

On 14 March 2022, unidentified armed individuals clashed with Ogwashi-Uku local defense group in Aboh Ogwashi Ukwu (Aniocha South, Delta) within the context of a land dispute. The head of the defense group was killed and two other members of the group were injured.
Around 14 March 2022 (as reported), a hairdresser was kidnapped from his shop in Ore (Odigbo, Ondo). The man was rescued by the Amotekun Corps (no clash reported).

Around 14 March 2022, militiamen clashed with police officers and a local defense militia at their hideouts presumably around Nasko (Magama, Niger) during a police operation to recover cattle. An unspecified number of militiamen were killed and 800 cattle were recovered. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 14 March 2022, two unidentified cult militia clashed at the Polytechnic, Ibadan (Akinyele, Oyo). There were no fatalities.
On 14 March 2022, Eiye and Arobaga confraternities clashed in Jesse (Ethiope West, Delta). 4 suspected cultists were killed.

On 14 March 2022, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of persons, including a head teacher, in Sabon Garin Safana village (Dutsinma, Katsina), coded to Dutsin Ma. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 15 March 2022, Boko Haram militants (presumed JAS) attacked Lantewa community (Tarmua, Yobe). Casualties unknown.
On 15 March 2022, Boko Haram militants (presumed JAS) set up an illegal vehicle check point and killed two (presumed not armed) a local defense group in Kaliyari (Bursari, Yobe).

On 15 March 2022, the military clashed with armed individuals during an operation in Tse-Keji, around Gbise (Katsina Ala, Benue). 4 armed men were killed and their camp destroyed. Following the clash, the group threatened the area with retaliation.

On 15 March 2022, armed individuals clashed with NDLEA officers, backed up by police and military, during an attack to the NDLEA offices in Ntezi (Ishielu, Ebonyi). Four people were killed: two armed individuals, a NDLEA officer and a patient from the agency's rehabilitation center. Other armed individuals escaped with injuries.

On 15 March 2022, armed individuals clashed with police officers in Gafara, Ngaski LGA (Kebbi), coded to Wara, after crossing to the region from the Danko/Wasagu LGA (Kebbi). Four police officers and between 1 to 7 civilians were killed. The group of about 500 armed men took over a tomato company in the area.

On 15 March 2022, militiamen clashed with the police and local vigilantes during an attack in Nasko (Magama, Niger). Three police officers and four local defense militia members were killed, along with seven militiamen. The attack would be in retaliation to another clash which left several militiamen killed and 800 cattle recovered (coded separately).

On 15 March 2022, armed individuals killed four people and abducted four others, including the Maigemu village head, during attacks in Kwatan Nanido, Maigemu, Tinga, Kwamishina Maigemu villages in Gassol LGA (Taraba), coded to Mutum Biyu.

Around 15 March 2022 (between 14 - 16 March), four people, including two local defense militia members, were killed by suspected cult militia members at the Boboroku and Irodo communities of the Idjerhe kingdom in Jesse (Ethiope West, Delta). The event happens within the context of rivalry clashes between two cult militias.
On 15 March 2022, the police killed three suspected kidnappers at their hideout in Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta).

On 15 March 2022, suspected ISWAP members abducted a doctor in Gubio (Gubio, Borno). The group also seized food stuff and fuel from an humanitarian truck. The abductee was released around 18 February 2023, after he was forced to treat wounded militants and their families, there are no reports about ransom payment.
Around 15 March 2022 (as reported), Aro and Bobo cult militias clashed in Aba (Aba South, Abia) following the killing of an Aro member (details not specified). 3 people were killed.

On 15 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked civilians, killed three persons and abducted eight others along the Dogon Dawa- Zaria road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 15 March 2022, cult militia members attacked UNIZIK vigilante members at the Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The police arrested an unspecified number of cultist members.
On 15 March 2022, two bus drivers were killed by officers from the Lagos State Task Force in Isheri (Kosofe, Lagos). Circumstances for the deaths are unknown.

On 16 March 2022, a woman was kidnapped by three armed individuals from her house in Ishiagu (Aniocha South, Delta). She had been previously kidnapped in 2019, and released - at the time - after the payment of ransom.
On 16 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed a school teacher at Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 16 March 2022, joint security operatives comprised of military, police and Niger State Vigilante Group members clashed with militiamen at the group's hideouts in or around Bangi (Mariga, Niger). A police officer was killed and the state's Commissioner claimed that over 100 militiamen were killed and 50 motorcycles were seized from the group. The operation took place following a discovered plan to attack the village and after the Nasko clash (coded separately). Fatalities coded as 101.

On 16 March 2022, armed individuals abducted 8 persons, including 3 women APC ward leaders, travelling in separate buses between Araromi-Opin and Obbo Ile (Ekiti, Kwara). Five of the abductees escaped, the women leaders and three other men were held by the abductors who demanded a ransom of 20 million naira. The abductee were rescued by a local defense militia (coded separately).

On 16 March 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty policeman as he was returning home from work in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The abductee was rescued the following day at Umueze in Awkunanaw. There are no reports of a clash or ransom payment.
On 16 March 2022, a Zamfara militia raped women and rustled cattle when they invaded Dutsin Zai and Gamawa in Tofa district (Bungudu, Zamfara).
On 17 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted two men from Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 17 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed one man and abducted seven women at Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 17 March 2022 (as reported), Adadama militiamen killed a man in Ochanyim Amagu (Ikwo, Ebonyi) within the context of land disputes of the community with the Adadama community in Cross Rivers state.

On 17 March 2022, policemen and soldiers in collaboration with a local defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group at Dobi Kwalita, coded to Dobi (Gwagwalada, FCT). One abductee was rescued, and one of the assailants were arrested, two guns that were loaded with ammunition were recovered by the security operatives.

Around 17 March 2022 (between 10 - 24 March), soldiers engaged Kaduna militiamen in an armed clash after airstrikes by the air force in Magaba (Giwa, Kaduna), according to the Defence headquarters. 8 militiamen were killed, 7 were arrested.
On 17 March 2022, a pastoralist was killed by armed individuals presumably in Kaura LGA (Kaduna), coded to Kaura. 30 cows were also killed and 7 motorcycles were burnt.
On 17 March 2022, armed individuals shot and killed the vice chairman of the Borno chapter of Timber Shed Association in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 17 March 2022, ISWAP/Boko Haram members clashed with the military during an attack to a base in Bama (Bama, Borno). One soldier was killed, several were injured and a number of them are missing. The group took over the military base.
On 17 March 2022, militia members shot and injured one person and kidnapped between 48 to 57 people (including 32 women) in Agunu Dutse community (Kachia, Kaduna).

Around 17 March 2022 (as reported), NURTW member assaulted with cutglass and sticks, and injured Fire Service members in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) after arriving at their premises in three vehicles. 10 Fire Service staff were severely injured. Motivation for the attack is unknown.
On 17 March 2022, a Zamfara militia raped women and rustled cattle when they invaded Dan Daji and Dakace in Tofa district (Bungudu, Zamfara).

On 18 March 2022, a suspected members of an unidentified cult militia killed a man at Baruwa estate (Alimosho, Lagos). The victim's body was found with marks that indicated he was attacked with a cutlass, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 18 March 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with farmers at Magirami bush in Guri LGA (Jigawa). Two persons were killed and five others were wounded, other sources report at least 5 to 6 persons killed and many others wounded.

On 18 March 2022, armed individuals killed the step-brother of an aide to the Plateau state governor in Takas village, Pankshin LGA (Plateau). The aide's stepmother and a girl leaving with her were abducted, there are no reports of ransom demands.

On 18 March 2022, DSS operatives shot sporadically and killed one woman at Ologo, Coal Camp, (Enugu North, Enugu). The victim was pursued and shot by one of the operatives, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 18 March 2022 (as reported), the military claimed a clash with ISWAP/Boko Haram members around the Musiri and Ndufu villages, Ngala LGA (Borno). An unspecified number of ISWAP/Boko Haram members were killed and various camps were destroyed; 30 abductees were rescued. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals intercepted and abducted six travelers from a commercial bus at Ochaja (Dekina, Kogi). The abductees include (presumed not armed) NYSC members and a pregnant woman; the abductees were rescued and the abductors were arrested by Amotekun Corps, there are no reports of a clash.
On 19 March 2022, two Naval officers stabbed and shot a medical doctor in Lekki (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos) after a disagreement over a parking lot. The victim was wounded, and taken to the hospital.

On 19 March 2022, Ndaka and Ichen ethnic militias clashed in Bissaula (Kurmi, Taraba). Three policemen and one woman were killed as the policemen were deployed to the location and overpowered by one of the groups; properties were also destroyed.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals tied up and beat the gatekeeper of a politician's house in in Ondo (Ondo West, Ondo). The house was vandalized and set ablaze; there were no occupants of in the building during the attack, believed to be politically related. The politician family had suffered other attacks previously.

On 19 March 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons on their way to Idoani (Ose, Ondo). The abductees were a cocoa farmer, and a female and a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded, they escaped from the bush after their abductors fell asleep at night.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals on 10 motorcycles attacked members of Abba Vigilance Group and Abba Security Network in Nkwangele LGA (Imo), coded as Abba. The assailants, who attacked from Okwelle community, shot at the defense militiamen who fled, leaving their patrol van that was set ablaze by the assailants. There were no casualties.

On 19 March 2022, ISWAP militants clashed with the military as they attacked a military base and were repelled by soldiers in Doron Baga (Kukawa, Borno). Scores of militants were killed, several others were wounded. The group was armed with grenades and five gun trucks. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals abducted a university teacher, his wife and four others near Ewatto (Esan South East, Edo). The wife was released on the same day and asked to mobilize for ransom by the abductors, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.
On 19 March 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked a police station and killed two policemen at Umuoguma (Owerri West, Imo). Police sources claim that the attack was repelled.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals attacked a member of the PDP in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The victim was beaten, shot in the leg by the assailants and was later rescued and taken to the hospital; the reason for the attack is presumed to be political.

On 20 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists in large numbers attacked civilians and killed around 34 persons in Mararaban, Adan, Tsonje, Katanga, Kadarko, all in Kagoro chiefdom, Kaura LGA (Kaduna) [coded to Kagoro] and Agban (coded separately). Over 200 houses and 32 shops were set on fire, 17 motorcycles were vandalized. The attack would be a reprisal to the killing of one pastoralist on the previous week [coded separately]. Fatalities split into 2 events, coded as 17.

On 20 March 2022, Nigerian soldiers repelled an attack by Sokoto militiamen on traders along Sokoto-Goronyo road (Goronyo, Sokoto). The militiamen blocked the road with the intention of robbing and abducting traders; casualties unknown.
On 20 March 2022, a policeman killed a scrap collector in Agbor (Ika South, Delta) following the victim's refusal to pay a bribe of 1000 naira.

On 20 March 2022, a Zamfara militia killed between 16 to 20 civilians, including the village head, of Ganar-Kiywa (Bukkuyum, Zamfara), coded to Bukuyum. 62 persons were also abducted from the areas and Bungudu LGA [coded separately].

On 20 March 2022, an unidentified armed group of four abducted a man from Ozoro town (Isoko North, Delta). The abductee was rescued by policemen after the abductors abandoned him and fled because the policemen were on their trail.

On 20 March 2022, a local defense militia clash with an armed group presumably around Araromi-Opin (Ekiti, Kwara) while trying to rescue persons abducted on 16 March by the group (coded separately). One female abductee, who was a women leader of the APC, was killed during the clash; an unspecified number of the defense militia members were wounded, one in critical condition.

On 20 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists killed two military officers in Agban (Kaura, Kaduna) as the group attacked the village and Adan, Tsonje, Katanga, Kadarko, all in Kagoro chiefdom, Kaura LGA [coded separately]. Around 34 people were killed, over 200 houses and 32 shops were set on fire, 17 motorcycles were vandalized. The attack would be a reprisal to the killing of one pastoralist on the previous week [coded separately]. Fatalities split into 2 events, coded as 17.

On 20 March 2022, suspected IPOB militants in large numbers attacked a police divisional headquarters and clashed with policemen and DSS operatives in Omuma (Oru East, Imo). Four militants were killed, others fled and a number of them were wounded. Five different undetonated IEDs were recovered.

On 21 March 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted one 60 year old woman from Gambanda (Gummi, Zamfara). The victim was rescued by the police, her abductors were arrested. There are no reports about a clash during the rescue.
