One NSCDC operative was killed, the commandant was beaten up and arrested by the police officers.

On 25 April 2022, an armed group took over the streets and shot sporadically in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). Residents scampered for safety; officers of the custodial center barricaded the center to avoid an incursion. Casualties unknown.

On 26 April 2022, policemen responded to a distress call and repelled an attack by Katsina militiamen in Kadage village, Kurfi LGA (Katsina). One militiaman was killed, all the rustled animals were recovered; many militiamen fled with gunshot wounds.

On 26 April 2022, soldiers and Civilian JTF engaged Kaduna militiamen in an armed clash after the militiamen invaded Angwa Kadara in Juji (Chikun, Kaduna). Some unarmed youths in the area confronted and chased the militiamen before they were intercepted by soldiers and CJTF. One woman was killed and another was abducted. Three persons, including the commander of the Civilian JTF, sustained bullet wounds from the attack which lasted till the following morning.

On 26 April 2022, Nigerian troops in conjunction with the Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram fighters during a clearance operation at Kasha in Mafa LGA (Borno). Six militants were killed, weapons and ammunition, amongst others items were recovered.

On 26 April 2022, Nigerian troops on a clearance operation destroyed Boko Haram/ ISWAP enclaves around Merkas and Yarganari villages, coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed and abducted victims were rescued. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 26 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed a Fulani pastoralist who was tending to cows in Ogu community (Ogu, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 26 April 2022, Oyo State Park Management System clashed with Isota boys and Were boys at the Ali Iwo area of Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). Some sources claim the clash was a result of the sporadic shooting by members of the Park Management System which resulted in the death of one person hit by a stray bullet; some reports mentioned that the Isota and Were boys attacked passers-by, especially persons wearing cloths with the governor or PMS insignia. At least three persons were killed in total, scores were wounded and vehicles were vandalized.

On 27 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians in Kitakum, Ungwan Magaji and Ungwan Rimi in Kauru LGA (Kaduna). About 22 persons were killed, 19 of whom were from the Irigwe ethnic group, several others were injured and 60 houses were burnt.

On 27 April 2022, armed individuals killed a member of NNPP in Bayelsa state at his residence around Bay-Bridge road in Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The assailants shot the victim several times through the window of his bedroom after they scaled the perimeter fence of the house. The victim was a former APC chieftain before he defected to the NNPP.

On 27 April 2022, policemen and members of a local defense militia clashed with Katsina militiamen and repelled them from Marina village in Safana LGA (Katsina). One of the assailants were killed; a gun and two of their motorcycles were recovered.
On 27 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and wounded two Fulani pastoralists around Kpara village (Bassa, Plateau). Six cattle were shot dead, at least 113 others were rustled.
On 27 April 2022, a Kaduna militia shot and injured a doctor who attempted to escape abduction, together with other people, along the Kaduna-Abuja road, coded to Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna).

On 27 April 2022, an assumed Fulani militia, killed one person in the Hausa community of Gudum Hausawa (Bauchi, Bauchi) during the burial of two other people killed on the previous week (coded separately). 20 houses were burnt. The event happens within the context of communal clashes between Fulani and Hausa in the region and the attack was described as an reprisal attack to the previous week one.

On 27 April 2022, armed individuals suspected to be assassins attacked the residence of an APC chieftain, wounded a gatekeeper, and bound the others in the Nasarawa area of Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano). The assailants did not gain access into the house; the police were alerted by neighbors. The chieftain is also a gubernatorial aspirant in Jigawa state and he was not in the house at the time of the attack, other sources report that the gatekeeper was shot and wounded.

On 27 April 2022, MNJTF troops with air support clashed with ISWAP/Boko Haram militants at Tunbun Rago (Abadan, Borno) and killed at least 20 militants. 12 rifles, a large cache of ammunitions, 5 gun trucks laden with supplies and a MRAP were recovered by the troops.

Around 27 April 2022 (as reported), MNJTF troops from Cameroon on a clearance patrol came in contact with two Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] at the general area of Chikulgudu, coded to Wulgo (Ngala, Borno). The militants were killed and two motorcycles were recovered.

On 27 April 2022, suspected Ikot Ekwere militiamen raped women when they invaded Ikot Obio Offong community coded to Nung Udoe (Ibesikpo Asutan, Akwa Ibom). The assailants burnt a car, over 20 houses, wounded many people, looted household items, domestic animals and money from other houses. They chanted war songs and fired several gunshots; two persons were missing up till June, the attack was over a protracted land dispute.

On 28 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked two locals working on their farm and killed them at Tse Tume in Turan council ward (Logo, Benue). Other sources claim three victims, including one woman, was killed.

On 28 April 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted the village head of Rijana and an unspecified number of farmers at Kurmi community, coded to Rijana (Kachia, Kaduna). The abductors demanded for tramadol, gallons of petrol, engine oil, cigarettes, recharge cards and two new motorcycles as ransom.

On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops on a clearance operation killed several ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, including the spiritual head of Galta, around Manjo Ali Qere, Dikwa LGA (Borno). Arms and ammunition were also recovered; several fatalities coded as 3.

On 28 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed two loggers who were IDPs from the Mandarari camp, their bodies were found near Konduga LGA (Borno). The victims were assumed by the militants to be spies of the military.
On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops, after sighting ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, shelled around the Dalori area (Jere, Borno) and the Molai General area [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.
On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops, after sighting ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, shelled around Molai General area (Jere, Borno) and around Dalori [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.

On 28 April 2022, local defense militiamen from a community in Oyigbo LGA attacked locals from Oloko community working on a community farmland in Tai LGA (Rivers), on the boundary between Oloko and Afam and coded to Ogoni. The assailants killed a pastor, abducted an unspecified number of persons, burnt houses and the victim's motorcycle.

On 28 April 2022, soldiers responded to a distress call and repelled an attack on civilians by an armed group at Rikwe-Chongu village in Kwal district (Bassa, Plateau). Between 2 to 3 civilians and one soldier were killed; one person was wounded and several houses were burned, food barns were destroyed, food stuff and domestic animals were stolen.

On 28 April 2022, armed individuals with machetes attacked security guards and residents at 2/1 New Site in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Many residents and some guards were wounded and robbed. The assailants, whom arrived in motorcycles, were invited by a commercial tricycle rider in retaliation after he was beaten by a resident earlier.

On 28 April 2022, suspected cult militiamen attacked and injured a human right activist at the Alex Ekueme Square in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants, numbering about 11, wielded guns and other weapons and invaded the venue while tricycle operators were waiting to meet the governor; police operatives intervened and shot in the air before the assailants left.
On 28 April 2022, armed individuals ambushed, shot and wounded a pregnant woman between Kaseyo and Torkula villages (Guma, Benue). The victim was returning to Gbajimba when the attack took place.

On 29 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed five civilians at a bar at Obiofia village in Osumenyi (Nnewi South, Anambra). The owner of the joint and four customers were the victims, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno), as well as Dipchari, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Bula Musa, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, (Bama, Borno), Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, Bomari, as well as Dipchari, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, and Dar el Jamal [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Kote (Bama, Borno), as well as Jeree, Gargash, Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 4.

On 29 April 2022, Nigerian troops with air support repelled an attack by ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). The militants, in two groups, attacked the town from Magumeri road and Gubio road; many militants were killed and several others were wounded before they retreated. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 29 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with NSCDC operatives providing security coverage to the Livestock Guards at the Wadata axis of Makurdi LGA (Benue). Two NSCDC operatives and one livestock guard were killed, and one operative was wounded. The operatives had seized some cows violating the open grazing law before they were ambushed by the group.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Dipchari (Bama, Borno), as well as Dar el Jamal, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Gargash (Bama, Borno), as well as Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 4.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Jeree (Bama, Borno), as well as Gargash, Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

On 30 April 2022, policemen clashed with armed individuals who attempted to abduct an expatriate in Ovia North East LGA (Edo), coded to Okada. Five of the assailants were killed, others escaped with bullet wound, two guns and eight live cartridges were recovered.

On 30 April 2022, armed individuals ambushed and killed 5 commuters along the Sabon Gari-Kampani road, Wase LGA (Plateau). The victims include a member of a local defense militia (presumed unarmed) whose motorcycle was stolen after he was killed, and locals returning from the market. 20 other persons were abducted.

Around 30 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops from Benue and Taraba clashed with armed Fulani militiamen at Kashimbila (Takum, Tarab) during a patrol. One militiaman was killed, the others fled with varying degrees of wounds and left a teenager boy behind. The troops set the militia's makeshift camp ablaze and recovered 4 cutlasses, one knife and other weapons.

On 30 April 2022, suspected IPOB militants raped a woman, and killed her and her husband close to the Banana junction in Orlu (Orlu, Imo) as they were on their way to Imo for their wedding. The victims, both members of the military and presumed off-duty at the time of the event, were beheaded after they were killed. IPOB denied the being involved in the attack and claimed the Nigerian Army and DSS were responsible.

On 30 April 2022, suspected cult militiamen attacked and beat up a candidate for the PDP ad-hoc delegate election, who is also a lawyer, in Oduma Ward 4 (Aninri, Enugu). The assailants were led by the deputy ward chairman, a PDP member. An unspecified number of other persons were also attacked. The PDP claimed the ad-hoc delegate election was peaceful.

On 30 April 2022, suspected personnel of the Enugu State Government Neighbourhood Watch attacked and beat up a supporter of Ike Ekeweremadu (PDP) at Ugbaike in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu) during the ad-hoc delegate election of the party. The assailants inflicted the victim with deep machete cuts on his head. The PDP claimed the election was peaceful.
On 30 April 2022, ISWAP militants killed two civilians at an illegal vehicle checkpoint along Dikwa-Mafa road (Dikwa, Borno).

Around 30 April 2022 (as reported), two members of Aiye cult militia, also called Black Axe, shot and killed three persons at the Isale Aluko area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) while they were in search of a member of the Eiye cult militia. The victims answered a question asked by the assailants in a way which angered them, resulting in the attack.

Around 30 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a patrol clashed with suspected armed Fulani pastoralists at Hundo-Ado community in Mbatyula council ward (Katsina Ala, Benue) while responding to a distress call. Three of the pastoralists were killed and weapons were recovered by the troops.

On 30 April 2022, suspected IPOB militants clashed with soldiers at a military checkpoint at Agulu (Aniocha, Anambra). The soldiers fled from the checkpoint; the assailants, who were shouting and demanding for the release of Nnamdi Kanu, claimed soldiers were killed. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 1 May 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Whirl Stroke clashed with armed individuals at a forest in Sengev council ward, Guma LGA (Benue), coded to Gbajimba, while responding to a distress call. A couple who were abducted by the armed individuals were rescued after the assailants fled and left them behind. No fatalities.

Around 1 May 2022 (as reported), armed individuals on motorcycles killed over 40 persons, including policemen and soldiers, providing protection to a community in the southern part of Taraba state during the Sallah break, as claimed by the Senator representing the Taraba south senatorial district. Location coded to the southern town of Gembu (Sardauna, Taraba).

Around 1 May 2022 (as reported), suspected members of Aiye cult militia, also called Black Axe, killed one person in Ilaro (Egbado South, Ogun). The reason for the attack is unknown, the police claimed to have arrested four militiamen in connection with the attack.

On 1 May 2022, an unidentified rival cult militia clashed with another unidentified cult militia around Okesuna/ Oja Gboro area (Ilorin East, Kwara). One person, suspected to be a member of one of the militias, was killed.

On 1 May 2022, Awawa Boys members attacked residents and killed one person in Shaiba (Agege, Lagos). Residents were robbed of valuables and an unspecified number of others were wounded; the killed victim was attacked with what appeared like cutlasses and sticks.
On 1 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a pastor from his church in the Ajebandele area of Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). There are no report of ransom demands.
On 1 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a lecturer in Oturkpo (Otukpo, Benue), while three other persons escaped being abducted during the event. The abductee escaped from his abductors on 2 May.
On 2 May 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed a farmer on his cashew farm at Araromi village in Igbo Ora (Ibarapa Central, Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, joint task force operatives, presumed to comprise of soldiers, policemen and local defense militiamen, clashed with members of a Niger communal militia around Uregi and Kiribo villages (Rafi, Niger) while the group was attacking civilians. Ten assailants were killed, 14 abductees were rescued, seven motorcycles and arms were recovered.
On 2 May 2022, armed individuals killed two people, including a presumed off duty policeman, beside St Mary's Church in Ozubulu (Ekwusigwo, Anambra). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, armed individuals killed two brothers at Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra). One of the victims, who was a former youth leader, was killed in front of their residence, while the second was blind-folded and abducted by the assailants and later killed close to Utu junction; his corpse was dumped at the center of the road. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with the Civilian JTF, while on a clearance operation, clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in Kayamla village (Konduga, Borno). The militants were on a mission to rustle cattle from pastoralists; three of them were killed and one suspected female collaborator was arrested near the village.

On 2 May 2022, armed individuals suspected to be enforcing a sit in order attacked and beat up a shop owner for opening his shop in Uli (Ihiala, Anambra). The victim's generator set was set ablaze by the assailants.

On 3 May 2022, Yansakai militiamen from Tungar Bido village attacked residents with cutlasses, knives and other weapons and killed one person in Tungar Dutsi village of Gana district (Bukkuyum, Zamfara), coded to Bukuyum. The assailants invaded the village, claimed they were celebrating Sallah and shot sporadically; they attacked residents after they were cautioned against shooting. The leader of the group was arrested by the police, others fled.
On 3 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals abducted the three delegates of the PDP election committee near Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu) while they were enroute to Ebonyi.
On 3 May 2022, ISWAP fighters clashed with Nigerian troops at a forward operation base in Kada, 2 km from Kautakari (Chibok, Borno), dislodging the troops. who fled to Chibok town.

On 3 May 2022, ISWAP fighters attacked civilians in Kautakari (Chibok, Borno). Between 7 to 9 locals were killed; the group looted and set shops and houses ablaze. Hundreds of locals fled into the bush and many others were missing.

On 3 May 2022, suspected IPOB militants attacked policemen at a checkpoint in Obudi-Agwa (Oguta, Imo). One policemen was killed and between one and two others were injured; the assailants cut off the privates part of the killed officer and left with it. The police claimed to have clashed with the assailants at the spot immediately after and killed two armed men while the others escaped. 3 total fatalities.
On 4 May 2022, armed individuals abducted two passengers of a commercial vehicle along the Emohua-Kalabari axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 May 2022, Nigerian troops clashed and killed scores of ISWAP/ Boko Haram and cleared out 24 of their camps in the Bama LGA (Borno) axis. Adamu Ngulde, a commander of the militants, was one of the fatalities, dozens of militants surrendered and more than 900 women and children were rescued. Fatalities coded as 20.
On 4 May 2022, ISWAP militants traced and killed three of their members who were enroute to surrender to Nigerian troops close to Karetu (Mobbar, Borno).

On 4 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with soldiers at Uratta (Aba South, Abia) while they were spreading information about a sit in order slated for the next day. Four armed individuals, including the leader of the group, were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds; some charms and a live tortoise were recovered from the suspected leader.

On 5 May 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed a Fulani man, his wife and son while they were returning from Nguma (Biu, Borno) after some of their members were killed by an IED planted by the group itself [coded separately].
Around 5 May 2022 (as reported), members of a Sokoto militia abducted three residents from Takakume village (Goronyo, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 May 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked residents of Cinke and Zarama villages in Kwal (Bassa, Plateau) and killed eight persons. Two other persons were wounded; several goods were destroyed and stolen.

On 6 May 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a large number of members of a Zamfara militia when the militia men attacked civilians in Damri (Bakura, Zamfara). Four persons, including one policeman, a NSCDC operative and patients receiving treatment in a hospital were killed; one vehicle belonging to the police was set ablaze. The attack might be related to the clash the group had with the military in the region which killed 10 militiamen two weeks prior (coded separately).

On 6 May 2022, armed individuals enforcing a sit in order shot sporadically at residents when they attacked Ebebe junction of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One vehicle and a motorcycle were set ablaze by the assailants, there were no casualties. The sit in order was in response to President Buhari's visit to the state, IPOB has denied imposing the sit in order.

On 6 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Sabon Gari Damri and Kalahe in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). Between 40 to 56 bodies were recovered. The attack might be related to the clash the group had with the military in the region which killed 10 militiamen two weeks prior (coded separately).
On 6 May 2022, armed individuals suspected to be assassins shot and killed a photographer at his wife's store on Otomewo road in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 7 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked residents and shot sporadically in Faru, Faru Magami ward, location coded to known village on the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). One person was killed in Faru Magami, an unspecified number of persons are missing.

On 7 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals abducted a man at the Okada axis, in or around Okada (Ovia North East, Edo). The abductee was in the company of his son who he was taking to write JAMB examinations, the son was left behind by the abductors.

On 7 May 2022, military forces with local defense militiamen repelled an attack by gunmen in Gurbin Magarya, Jibia LGA (Katsina). Three residents were killed, three others were wounded and livestock belonging to residents were killed by the assailants before the arrival of security operatives.

On 7 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked residents and shot sporadically in Garin Minane village in Maradun LGA (Zamfara). Six persons, four of whom were returning from a farm were killed; an unspecified number of persons are missing.

On 8 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a catholic priest from the premises of his parish in Ikot Abasi Akpan, Mkpat Enin LGA (Akwa Ibom). The assailants invaded the area on a motorcycle and shot sporadically into the air to scare residents away. The abductee was released on 12 May, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 8 May 2022, members of a Sokoto militia clashed with members of a local defense militia as they attacked Takakume (Goronyo, Sokoto). The leader of the assailants was killed by the defense militia. One resident was killed and six others were abducted and later killed by the assailants as revenge for the killing of their leader. Fatalities coded as 8.

On 8 May 2022, armed individuals attacked a truck being driven by assumed Fulani, wounded the driver and set the truck ablaze on the Ezinifitte/ Uga road (Aguata, Anambra). The truck was conveying cattle to a market in the state. One person was rescued and 34 livestock were recovered by the police.

On 9 May 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed three persons in Num area of Sara village, coded to Tafawa-Balewa (Tafawa Balewa, Bauchi). Five persons were wounded by the assailants. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Gini (Muya, Niger), Dandaudu and Gidan Mangoro [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Gini; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 0.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Dandaudu (Muya, Niger), Gini and Gidan Mangoro [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Dandaudu; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 1.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Gidan Mangoro (Muya, Niger), Dandaudu and Gini [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Gidan Mangoro; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 0.

On 9 May 2022, a Joint Task Force presumed to comprise of the military, police and local defense militiamen repelled an attack by militants in Jellako community, coded to Kagara (Rafi, Niger). 15 abductees who were abducted from different locations were rescued, two motorcycles were abandoned by the assailants who fled with gunshot wounds.

On 9 May 2022, an armed group numbering up to 20 stabbed and wounded one resident and abducted 3 persons, including the deputy paramount ruler of Otuabula community (Ogbia, Bayelsa). The wounded victim escaped being abducted; there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 9 May 2022, Boko Haram/ISWAP militants killed a Boko Haram commander (who had paid allegiance to ISWAP) at Galta in Madagali LGA (Adamawa) after he was tried and found guilty of 'treasonable felony' over his plans to surrender to the Nigerian troops.
On 9 May 2022, a Katsina communal militia killed one person and stole valuables from Mai Gora (Faskari, Katsina).

On 10 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with Nigerian troops at Ananum village (Donga, Taraba). Two armed persons were killed, others fled with gunshot wounds; weapons, ammunition charms and some money were recovered by the troops.
On 10 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with soldiers after ambushing them in Mararraba (Donga, Taraba). The troops fought off the ambush; two armed men were killed and other were injured.

On 10 May 2022, suspected members of an unidentified cult militia attacked and killed three persons in Inen community, coded to Ikot Ibritam (Oruk Anam, Akwa Ibom). One motorcycle and a POS machine were stolen from the victims by the assailants whom other sources report came from neighboring communities.

On 10 May 2022, suspected sea pirates abducted seven passengers around the Yellow Channel axis between Bonny and Port Harcourt (Bonny, Rivers). The victims were rescued by the Nigerian Navy around 24 May and the Navy claimed no ransom was paid for the release.

On 10 May 2022, gunmen abducted three persons from Maji community (Suleja, Niger). The victims include one nursing mother, a teenage boy and another woman; a ransom of 5 million naira each has been demanded by the abductors.

On 10 May 2022, armed individuals suspected Fulani Ethnic militiamen ambushed the convoy of a commanding officer and clashed with soldiers and mobile police officers at Tati village in Takum LGA (Taraba). 7 security operatives were killed. The commanding officer and his orderly are missing. The police claimed the soldiers were caught in the clash between the Fulani and Kuteb militias.
On 10 May 2022, armed individuals attacked civilians and killed four persons in Ayilamo community (Logo, Benue). Several others persons were wounded.

On 11 May 2022, gunmen abducted scores of commuters, including from a commercial vehicle they ambushed in around the Evekwu and Rumuodogo communities (Emohua, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 May 2022, policemen and hunters clashed with armed individuals at Sara Kulinyi district (Hong, Adamawa) during an operation. Three armed men were killed, others fled with bullet wounds and one abductee was rescued.

On 11 May 2022, members of an unidentified cult militia attacked the home of a rival Aiye also known as Black Axe member and stabbed and injured his father in Badagry (Badagry, Lagos). The assailants were in search of their rival who was not at home when they arrived, his father was stabbed as a sign to show their presence.

On 11 May 2022, armed individuals numbering about five attacked a Muslim Cleric in a mosque at Kumo (Akko, Gombe) and set him ablaze. The assailants throw an explosive device at the cleric who was wounded along with some of his students. Some of the assailants were supporters of one of the aspirant for a legislative seats.

On 11 May 2022, policemen clashed with members of a Niger militia at Agigi/ Kpashimi forest in Lapai LGA (Niger). 15 abductees were freed, the militiamen fled into the bush with bullet wounds, two motorcycles were recovered and three militiamen were arrested by the policemen.

On 11 May 2022, armed individuals attacked a convoy of APC members, including a House of Assembly aspirant, at Italorun village on the Idanre-Akure road (Idanre, Ondo). The aspirant escaped unhurt, an unspecified number of others were wounded and taken to the hospital for treatment, vehicles were vandalized. The police claimed the attack was a result of a clash between two political aspirants in the area.

On 11 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia shot at a vehicle and caused it to crash along Gusau Dansadau road (Gusau, Zamfara) and abducted one of its occupants, who is a journalist. The second person in the car escaped, the abductee was released around 17 May, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 11 May 2022, policemen, together with members of a local defense militia, clashed with armed individuals suspected to be abductors in Uzea forest, Esan Central LGA (Edo), coded to Irrua. Six persons were killed: two armed men on the spot and four others who were previously arrested and led the police to the hideout sustained gunshot injuries and died in the hospital. Weapons and ammunition were recovered by the police.

On 11 May 2022, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants attacked civilians at Yadagungume and Limi village in Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). At least 3 people were killed, other sources report that the assailants are unidentified.

Around 12 May 2022 (between 11 - 17 May), two rival cult militias one of them presumed to be Aiye also called Black Axe clashed in Adaripon Ipage compound, Badagry (Badagry, Lagos). Three persons were killed within five days of the clash [one fatality coded separately], fatalities coded as 2.

On 12 May 2022, a joint security team presumed to comprise of soldiers, policemen and local defense militiamen, repelled an attack by members of a Niger militia who attempted to invade Maraban Dan-Daudu and Jiko villages via Gwada (Shiroro, Niger). On 6 June 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two farmers at Ikyungwa Tombo ward near Ayilamo (Logo, Benue). The victims were returning from their farm when they were attacked.

On 6 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted a former permanent commissioner of Zamfara Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) alongside his younger brother at Gidan-Giye, near Tsafe town (Zamfara). The abductees were trying to fix their car which developed a fault when they encountered the militiamen who were crossing. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 6 June 2022, members of Oruku communal militia attacked members of their community, killed one person, set the corpse ablaze, set two houses ablaze in Oruku (Nkanu East, Enugu). The victims were attacked for accepting to settle a dispute which the community had with their neighbors.

On 7 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen led by Dogo Gudale abducted about 23 persons from Gayawa, Takalafiya (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Kairu [coded separately]. The abductees were mostly between the ages of 19 to 35, many locals were displaced and there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen led by Dogo Gudale abducted about 23 persons from Kairu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Gayawa, Takalafiya [coded separately]. The abductees were mostly between the ages of 19 to 35, many locals were displaced and there are no reports about ransom demands.
Around 7 June 2022 (as reported), members of a Zamfara communal killed three residents of Gayawa village (Bukkuyum, Zamfara).

On 7 June 2022, ISWAP militants who rode on 6 motorcycles shot and killed between 12 to 25 scrap collectors who were mostly IDPs in Mukdula (Dikwa, Borno). The victims were part of a 50 strong group, 3 people escaped, 24 others are missing. ISWAP claimed the attack stating that the victims were 35 and members of militias loyal to the Nigerian army.
On 7 June 2022, suspected ISWAP/ Boko Harm militants abducted two women from Mairami village (Konduga, Borno).

On 7 June 2022, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a military barracks and killed four soldiers in Banki (Bama, Borno). They also claimed that one soldier was wounded and military operational vehicles were burnt. Other sources denied the attack, and claimed that the troops encountered a clash between Boko Haram and ISWAP fighters [coded separately] and proceeded to rescue some fleeing abductees who were wives of top Boko Haram commanders.

On 7 June 2022, policemen invaded the hideout of suspected Biafra militiamen and engaged them in an armed clash in Idemili South LGA (Anambra) coded to Ojoto. The leader of the armed group was killed, five others were arrested, guns, a Biafra flag and ESN uniforms were recovered by the policemen who were led to the hideout by a suspect the arrested after rescuing an abductee at Neni Anaocha.

On 7 June 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia attacked residents in Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara). At five residents were killed, several others were severely wounded. The attack took place a weeks after the predominantly Hausa community had a peace meeting with the militiamen.

On 8 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed an operative of Ebube Agu presumed to be off duty while he was returning from his duty post at Abofia in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The victim's body was found the following morning with several machete cuts.

On 8 June 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed two hunters who were serving as local defense militiamen in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). A private security guard was also killed by the assailants.

On 8 June 2022, an armed group abducted a photojournalist attached to the press unit of the Ebonyi state government house on the Okigwe-Aba-Enugu expressway (Aba South, Abia). The abductee was returning to Abakaliki from Aba, a ransom of 50 million naira has been demanded; the victim was released on 11 June after 300,000 Naira was paid as ransom

On 9 June 2022, a Bassa Kwomu militia suspected to have been hired from Agatu in Benue state killed three civilians when they attacked Baza and Anki villages, coded to Mozum (Bassa, Kogi). The assailants also burnt down the two villages.
On 9 June 2022, an armed group abducted a man from his residence in Nkwelle Ezunaka (Oyi, Anambra). The abductee was found dead and his body was abandoned on 13 June.

On 9 June 2022, an armed group abducted an APGA youth leader from his home in Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra). There were no reports for ransom demands, and the abductee was found dead two days later [coded separately].

On 9 June 2022, Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants around Lassa and Kelle villages (Askira Uba, Borno). Several militants were killed coded as 3, one gun truck, two civilian Hilux vehicles, arms and ammunition were recovered.

Around 9 June 2022 (as reported), a Niger communal militia attacked civilians and killed eight people in Gulbi, Unguwan-Jaye and Kusheriki (Rafi, Niger). 36 other people were abducted and one person was seriously injured.

On 10 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a staff of Alex Ekwueme Federal University Teaching Hospital in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The victim's body was found the following morning with several machete cuts.

On 10 June 2022, armed individuals abducted a youth president in Ihiala LGA when they invaded the secretariat in Ihiala (Ihiala, Anambra). The assailants also stole motorcycles worth millions of naira.

On 10 June 2022, troops of the MNJTF comprised of Nigerian and Chadian forces carried out clearance operation against ISWAP militants in Metele and Dogon Chuku (Abadan, Borno) and Kangarwa [coded separately]. Several militants were killed, one mortar, one gun and other logistics items were recovered.

On 10 June 2022, troops of the MNJTF comprised of Nigerian and Chadian forces carried out clearance operation against ISWAP militants in Kangarwa (Kukawa, Borno), Metele and Dogon Chuku [coded separately]. Several militants were killed, one mortar, one gun and other logistics items were recovered.

On 10 June 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a girl at her father's residence in Otukpo LGA (Benue) coded to Oturkpo. The victim was together with her younger sister who the assailants told that their father was the target and the murder was a message to him.

On 10 June 2022, an armed group comprised of Fulani pastoralists killed one student and left two others with varying degrees of injuries in Kuru (Jos South, Plateau). Some sources report that the assailants were sent by Fulani pastoralists who were sent away from the community, the police denied the reports of an attack on a school and insisted the attack happened in Riyom [coded separately].
On 10 June 2022, an armed group shot and killed one person along Mararaban Jama'a (Jos South, Plateau). Three other persons were wounded and taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 11 June 2022, masked an armed group abducted 15 young men, invaded the palace of the traditional ruler, shot sporadically and injured an unspecified number of persons in Ekwe (Isu, Imo). The abductees were excavating sand at the Njaba river, women and girls were not attacked by the assailants.

On 11 June 2022, a Sokoto communal militia abducted at least 40 wedding guests on the road between Tureta and Bakura (Tureta, Sokoto). 20 to 25 people escaped from the abductors and 30 others were left behind, the abductees who are telephone marketers were returning to Gusau after attending a wedding in Sokoto. A ransom of 145 million naira was demanded and later reduced to 60 million which is 5 million for each abductee. 29 abductees were released on 23 June, there are no reports about ransom payment.

Around 11 June 2022 (as reported), an armed group killed a youth leader of APGA whom they abducted two days earlier [coded separately] and the victim's body was found at Utuh junction (Nnewi South, Anambra).

On 12 June 2022, an armed group abducted a catholic priest from his house in Angware (Jos East, Plateau). The abductee is also the CAN chairman in the council area, youths in the area attempted to chase the abductors who began to shoot sporadically and took the priest away. 50 million naira was demanded as ransom; the abductee was released around 16 June, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 12 June 2022, an armed group abducted three pastors along the Ochadam-Okele-Ejule road (Ofu, Kogi). The abductees were on their way to a crusade when they were abducted, a ransom of 80 million naira was demanded.

On 12 June 2022, a local hunters militia joined by their counterparts from Idoani, Ipesi and Ifira clashed with an armed group composed of Fulani pastoralists near Idogun (Ose, Ondo). The ckash followed the abduction of three farmers [coded separately], casualties are unknown.

On 12 June 2022, an armed group abducted three farmers in Elegbeka community (Owo, Ondo). The abductees were on their way to the Akoko axis when they were abducted, a ransom of 4 million naira was demanded for each abductee.

On 12 June 2022, Nigerian troops conducted a clearance operation against a suspected Sokoto communal militia around Tureta LGA (Sokoto). Several militiamen were wounded and others were killed coded as 3 and over two thousand rustled cattle were recovered by the soldiers.

On 12 June 2022, an armed group abducted the wife of the APC chairman in Magama LGA from their residence in Tunga, Minna (Minna, Niger). The abductors requested for and collected a huge sum of money from the abductee; the abductee was found at a motor park in Maiduguri on 15 June.

On 12 June 2022, an armed group attacked and killed 11 to 37 civilians in Igama community (Ado, Benue) and set an unspecified number of buildings ablaze. The victims were all youths, women and the elderly were allowed to escape by the assailants. A lawmaker representing the constituency claimed 30 people were killed in two communities, split across two events and over 500 residents were displaced. Some sources report that the assailants included two naked women with pots on their heads making incantations, others report that they were Fulani pastoralists.

On 12 June 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF invaded a camp of Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in Gabchari, Mantari and Malam Masari (Bama, Borno) which was renamed Gazuwa/ Markas by the militants. 47 militants including top commanders and 2 Civilian JTF members were killed, other militants fled. The militants involved in the clash were in their hundreds on motorcycles with various weapons and the clash lasted for more than three hours.

On 12 June 2022, an armed group attacked civilians in Effeche (Okpokwu, Benue) and Igama community [coded separately]. A lawmaker representing the constituency claimed 30 people were killed in the attack, split across two events and coded as 10.

On 12 June 2022, Amotekun corps foiled an attack by an armed group on commuters who were traveling along the Old Ila Orangun-Ijabe road (Ila, Osun). Four of the commuters were wounded by the assailants before the arrival of the Amotekun operatives, one of the assailants was arrested.

On 13 June 2022, an armed group abducted the Anglican bishop of Jebba diocese, his wife and driver along the New Oyo-Ogbomosho expressway (Ogbomosho North, Oyo). The abductees were travelling from Ogun state to Jebba, the bishop's chaplain escaped into the bush, a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. The victims were rescued on 14 June by security operatives [no interaction reported].

On 13 June 2022, a suspected IPOB militia killed a man at Triangle axis in Nkwelle Ezunaka community (Oyi, Anambra) and drooped a note which said 'sit at home on Monday' on the corpse. The assailants wore masks, brought the victim out of the car, shot him and left.

On 13 June 2022, Black Axe cult militia also called Aiye cult militia and Buccaneers clashed with an Eiye cult militia at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun) resulting in one person killed. Other sources report that at least 10 people were killed while the police claims one person was killed and two militiamen were killed.

On 13 June 2022, an armed group comprised of Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two civilians in Ogbede-Mgbuji, coded to Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Many houses were destroyed, 14 farm settlements were sacked, an unspecified number of people were wounded and over 3000 residents were displaced.

On 13 June 2022, a local defense militia clashed with an armed group in Alor (Idemili South, Anambra) after they trailed them to a hotel. Two armed men were killed, one other person sustained burns, their female counterparts were arrested while their operational vehicle was burnt.

On 13 June 2022, Nigerian troops and Civilian JTF on an offensive clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Harm militants, destroyed over 700 makeshift houses and shelters, recovered weapons and motorcycles from them and arrested two militants. Location coded to Malam Masari (Bama, Borno) were the operation began the previous day.

On 13 June 2022, soldiers in collaboration with policemen while on a routine patrol foiled an attack and clashed with a Kaduna communal militia in Sabon Sara village, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). One militiaman was killed, one rifle was and nine motorcycles were recovered.
Around 14 June 2022 (as reported), Katsina militiamen abducted six civilians when they attacked Bakiyawa community (Batagarawa, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 14 June 2022, a Zamfara communal militia attacked and killed one person in Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). The assailants also rustled unspecified number of cattle.
On 14 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two women when they invaded Sapio village in Wase LGA (Plateau). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 14 June 2022, an armed group invaded a church and abducted two people at a vigil in a Celestial Church of Christ in Wasimi (Ewekoro, Ogun). One of the abductees is the assistant pastor and the other, a Sunday school teacher. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded and later reduced to 10 million, the abductors threatened to kill the victims if the ransom is not paid. The abductees were released on 18 June after 1 million naira was paid as ransom together with foodstuff, cigarette and gin.

On 14 June 2022, a Niger communal militia attacked civilians and killed five people when they raided Gidigore community, coded to Kagara (Rafi, Niger). Many other people were abducted by the assailants, several properties and houses were burnt and many people fled the area. The abductees were released on 17 and 18 June as part of a peace deal between the militiamen and the community, no ransom was paid.

On 14 June 2022, an unidentified armed group mounted on lorries and fired indiscriminately at civilians in Eke-Ozzi market, coded to Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). At least two people were killed and an unspecified number of others were wounded.
On 14 June 2022, two rival unidentified cult militias clashed at Balogun Agoro area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). Two people were killed and another was injured.

On 14 June 2022, an armed group wounded a former Adamawa state commissioner and some others around his household before abducting the commissioner from his home in Bajabure (Girei, Adamawa). Other sources report that two people were killed, a ransom of 30 million naira was demanded for his release.

On 14 June 2022, an armed group comprised of Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed three civilians in Ogbede-Mgbuji, coded to Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu) for the second day in a row. Many house were destroyed, 14 farm settlements were sacked, an unspecified number of people were wounded and over 3000 residents were displaced.

On 14 June 2022, an armed group abducted a journalist from his home in Umungasi Ohuhu (Aba North, Abia). The abductors scaled the fence of the victims house to gain entry and stole his car as well. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.

On 14 June 2022, a Katsina communal militia on motorcycles abducted six civilians from Shola community in Katsina (Katsina). The abductees include four men, one woman and her two year old baby, one of male the abductees escaped.

On 14 June 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF on an offensive clashed with ISWAP militants around Gurzum (Konduga, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed, coded as 3, their camps and markets were destroyed, weapons and other items were recovered.

On 14 June 2022, a Katsina communal militia attacked and killed one person and wounded another when they invaded Tafoki (Faskari, Katsina). The assailants had attacked Unguwar Sarkin Fulani community which was deserted before they conducted a house to house search killing the victim in the process, and stealing several cows and farming implements in the attack.

On 14 June 2022, an armed group clashed with soldiers, policemen and local defense militia at Yarkuka village, coded to Danko Maga ward (Danko, Kebbi). 23 dead bodies of the assailants were found by the bank of the Yarkuka river with gunshot wounds.

On 15 June 2022, some Kaduna communal militiamen engaged policemen in an armed clash along Saminaka-Jos expressway (Lere, Kaduna). Four militiamen were killed after they sustained serious injuries, two rifles and ammunitions were recovered by the police.

On 15 June 2022, a Niger communal militia ambushed soldiers in Rijiya Daji village in Mariga LGA (Niger). One soldier was killed, another was abducted, an operation vehicle was burnt while the assailants also stole guns.

On 15 June 2022, an armed group clashed with policemen who were on search operations in the forest, one assailant was killed after he sustained injuries and three other assailants were arrested. Location coded to Okpoga (Okpokwu, Benue).

On 15 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed five civilians in Shegyam and Dogon Ruwa in Wase LGA (Plateau). Hundreds of cattle were rustled, the police claim the casualty figure could not be ascertained, and one wounded victim was taken to the hospital.

On 15 June 2022, a Niger communal militia attacked civilians and killed three people in Maguzawa community coded to nearby Kagara (Rafi, Niger). An unspecified number of people including the chief imam were abducted and two houses were set ablaze. The abductees were released on 17 and 18 June as part of a peace deal between the militiamen and the community, no ransom was paid.

Around 15 June 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a former lawmaker in the Anambra state house of assembly. The victim was abducted on 9 June [coded separately] and a ransom of 15 million naira was paid for his release; his decomposing body was found without a head on the bank of the Ulasi river, between Uke and Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra) on 21 June.
On 15 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Udoda (Ahoada West, Rivers) and killed a chief, according to the Paramount Ruler of the community.
On 15 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted 50 farmers on the outskirts of Bama (Bama, Borno). The abductees were later released after they were robbed of their belongings.

Around 15 June 2022 (as reported), ISWAP claimed to have killed three soldiers and wounded others in an attack on a military barrack at Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The militants claimed to have carried out the attack with automatic weapons, burnt down a military operational vehicle and captured another.

Around 15 June 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted two men between Kabba and Okene (Kabba, Kogi). A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded and the abductees were released after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

Around 15 June 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted a pastor from Sabon Kurutu in Kachia LGA (Kaduna). The abductors refused to release him after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom and insisted on receiving motorcycles worth 800 thousand naira first. The abductee escaped around 26 August 2022.
On 15 June 2022, an armed group numbering about 200 attacked and killed over 30 people when they attacked nine settlements in Danko Maga ward (Danko, Kebbi).

On 16 June 2022, Nigerian troops repelled an attack by Boko Haram (JAS) militants in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The militants invaded the town through multiple folds in 4 gun trucks and ten motorcycles. Casualties are unknown.
On 16 June 2022, a Zamfara communal militia abducted an unspecified number of residents from Zurmi village (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 16 June 2022, an unidentified armed group shot at civilians when they invaded Tudun Wadan Jada, Old Jamari and Sabuwa Garin Jauro Bano in Alkaleri LGA (Bauchi). The assailants attempted to abduct a victim who raised an alarm that attracted youths that tried to prevent the abduction. The assailants shot at the people, killed four persons and wounded three others

On 16 June 2022, an unidentified armed group shot severally at five civilians who were meeting in front of their compound in Umuebele Okporo, coded to Orlu (Orlu, Imo). Three of the victims were killed, the other two sustained varying degrees of bullet wounds and the assailants who attacked them in an unregistered vehicle drove off.
On 16 June 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted a man while they were on their way to Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue).

On 16 June 2022, an armed group comprised of Fulani pastoralists clashed with a local hunter militia in Orokam community (Ogbadibo, Benue). The bodies of two hunters were found in the forest on 17 June without their heads and they were a councilor-elect and his cousin.
On 16 June 2022, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) militants targeted IDP camps with three mortar bombs in Banki (Bama, Borno). Eleven women and children were wounded.

On 17 June 2022, an armed group suspected to be comprised of armed pastoralists shot and killed a hunter in Ukwuani, coded to Obiaruku Quarters (Ukwuani, Delta). The victim was shot in the foot, and when he called his relatives to come and rescue him, the assailants assumed he was calling security agents and killed him.

Around 17 June 2022 (as reported), six members of a cult militia attacked a hospital in Uzabba (Owan West, Edo). 1 patient was killed. The militants had attacked the victim in January (coded as a separate event).

On 17 June 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with IPOB militants at Akwa village (Ihiala, Anambra). Five members of the armed group were killed and their corpses were paraded around the village in a Hilux vehicle by IPOB militants.

On 17 June 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with Ebube Agu operatives during a burial ceremony in Akwa village (Ihiala, Anambra). The clash was as a result of an argument by the armed group that Ebube Agu operatives ought not to enter Anambra state. There were no casualties.
On 17 June 2022, an armed group clashed with a team of policemen at a checkpoint and killed one policeman at Umanu junction in Nsukka (Nsukka, Enugu).
On 17 June 2022, operatives of the Enugu state neighborhood watch killed a hawker for obstructing traffic in Enugu East (Enugu) coded as Nkwo Nike.

On 17 June 2022, ISWAP militants killed three Civilian JTF members, wounded one other and abducted three humanitarian workers when they invaded the compound of a humanitarian organization in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The militants attempted to steal three vehicles but could not take them out of the compound. ISWAP claimed that the abductees were are staff of the Red Cross Society.
On 18 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a women leader in Isuokoma community at her farm near Onu Esu (Ohaozara, Ebonyi). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 18 June 2022, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants from Gazuwa town killed 13 metal scavengers made up of 11 males and 2 females in Goni Kurmi village (Bama, Borno). Dozens of other people including women fled the area to take refuge in Bama.

On 18 June 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be comprised of armed pastoralists attacked 30 civilians who were commuting to Atisbo from Itesiwaju at Alaga (Atisbo, Oyo). The victims were critically wounded.

Around 18 June 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted three locals of Ikaram-Akoko along Ayere-Ajowa Akunu axis (Ayere, Ijumu). The abductees were traveling to Ondo from Abuja, a ransom of 40 million naira was demanded.

On 18 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a village head and his son when they invaded Zira village in Toro LGA (Plateau). The abductees were released on 21 June, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 18 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted civilians who were returning from a burial ceremony along Auchi-Benin road (Etsako West, Edo). The abductees were in a bus which was attacked, 13 people including the driver were abducted and 10 escaped. A ransom of 20 million naira each was demanded for the release of the abductees.

On 18 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons who were returning from a wedding ceremony in Abuja around Akwanga (Akwanga, Nassarawa). Among the abductees were a former general secretary of the NFF and a former assistant coach of the super eagles. The abductees were released on 20 June after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom, one of the abductees claimed they were abducted by Fulani men less than 3 minutes after a checkpoint of the joint military.

Around 18 June 2022 (as reported), Nigerien troops of the MNJTF clashed with ISWAP militants when they invaded the militants' hideout in Ndaurori village, between Nigeria and Niger. An unspecified number of militants were killed, coded as 3 while others fled with bullet wounds, the surviving militants fled towards Bulabulin (Guzamala, Borno). Four motorcycles and dead bodies were littered in the area where the clash took place.

Around 18 June 2022 (between 17 - 18 June), Nigerian troops clashed with fleeing Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at Buduwa (Bama, Borno). Seven militants were killed, 14 rustled cattle and three bicycles were recovered.
On 18 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked and killed two farmers in the Iyatawa area of Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The victims had gone to their farm to plant crops, three others were abducted.

On 18 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians and killed one person in Mada community (Gusau, Zamfara). Six other people were abducted by the assailants who shot sporadically during the attack.
On 18 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed one civilian and abducted 14 others at Maraban Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 19 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one pastoralist and abducted another when they attacked Pai community in Kwali Area Council (FCT). The murdered victim attempted to resist the abduction of his kinsman which led to him being shot, there are no reports about ransom demands for the abductee

On 19 June 2022, policemen in collaboration with local self defense militias clashed with Zamfara militiamen who invaded Saran Gawama and Unguwar Mata villages in Gummi LGA (Zamfara). One of the assailants was seriously wounded, one rifle and 18 rounds of live ammunition were recovered while the rest fled with possible gunshot wounds in the clash which lasted for hours.

On 19 June 2022, suspected Fulani militiamen numbering about seven and wearing police uniforms abducted 6 Christian pilgrims when they invaded Ibite Awhum community in Udi LGA (Enugu). The abductees were praying on a hill near a monastery, before they were abducted. The victims were rescued by forest guards from Udi and Enugu East local government councils [there are no reports of an interaction].

On 19 June 2022, a group of unidentified armed men abducted the traditional ruler of Kalaba community from his palace in Kalaba, coded to Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The body of the abductee was found the next day [coded separately], the abduction was assumed to be in connection with the victim's rejection of plans by suspected crude oil thieves to set up illegal refineries in the community.

On 19 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen on motorcycles attacked and killed three worshippers at a catholic church in Rubu community, Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). 30 worshippers at a Baptist church were abducted [coded separately] and two people were wounded in the attack. 15 out of the 17 persons that were abducted from Unguwan Turawa were released after 4 million naira was paid, two girls were held back and one of them escaped and returned home on 20 December.

On 19 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted between 30 to 36 worshippers from a Baptist church in Rubu community, Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). The village head of Unguwan Fada was one of the abductees, he was released around 20 June to source for a ransom of 100 million naira to secure the release of about 36 other abductees. 15 out of the 17 persons that were abducted from Unguwan Turawa were released after 4 million naira was paid, two girls were held back and one of them escaped and returned home on 20 December.
On 19 June 2022, Fulani militiamen abducted two civilians from Ogbete-Mgbuji (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The spokesman of the community claimed that millions of naira was paid to secure their release.
Around 19 June 2022 (as reported), Fulani militiamen attacked and killed three civilians in Ogbete-Mgbuji (Isi Uzo, Enugu).

On 19 June 2022, ISWAP militants attacked commuters and detonated an IED along Gamboru-Ngala road (Ngala, Borno). Two drivers were shot and killed, two others died from the wounds sustained in the explosion, others were badly wounded, other sources report 6 killed and 2 wounded. The militants looted food items from the trailers and loaded the items into their Hilux, and set four vehicles ablaze. The assailants fled when they sighted Nigerian troops.

On 20 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the mother of the APC candidate for the Jigawa central senatorial district from her residence in Kiyawa town (Kiyawa, Jigawa). The victim was rescued in Kumbotso LGA Kano by security operatives on a joint operation [there are no reports of a clash].

Around 20 June 2022, Nigerian troops of Forward Operating Base Bakura clashed with Zamfara militiamen at Rafin Dakura in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). Two militiamen were killed and six abductees were rescued by the troops.

Around 20 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Kalaba community after he was abducted from his residence [coded separately]. The victim's body was found at Ikarama community (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The attack is assumed to be linked to the victim's refusal for an illegal oil refining camp to be set up in the community.

On 20 June 2022, suspected Fulani ethnic militiamen killed at least five persons from Udei and Yelwata at Mbagwen community, coded to Udei (Guma Benue). The victims were timber dealers who were returning the forest where they went to collect timber, they were 15 in number other sources report 16 all of whom were killed, five bodies were recovered and ten others are missing.

On 20 June 2022, an unidentified armed group of more than 20 shot sporadically to scare residents and abducted the district head of Panyam from his residence in Panyam (Mangu, Plateau). The abductors were heavily armed and they surrounded the palace, a ransom of 150 million naira was demanded. The abductee was released on 22 June, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 20 June 2022, a group of unidentified armed individuals ambushed the Kalaba community development chairman at his residence and killed him, coded to Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The victim and the traditional ruler of the community were opposed to the siting of an illegal oil refining camp in the community, which is assumed to be the reason for the attack, the body of the traditional ruler was also found after he had been abducted [coded separately].

On 20 June 2022, a soldier shot and killed a fuel attendant at a fuel station in Minna (Minna, Niger) after he was stabbed by the attendant. The incident was a result of an altercation between the station manager and the soldiers, other sources report that the victim slapped a soldier and chased him with a cutlass, which led to the shooting.

On 20 June 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF on a clearance patrol clashed with presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants along Bama-Pulka road (Bama, Borno). Two militants were killed, two locally made guns and ammunition were recovered.
On 20 June 2022, two rival unidentified cult militias clashed at Oyingbo market (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). At least one person was killed.

On 21 June 2022, heavily armed Katsina militiamen numbering about 15 attacked civilians, killed three people and wounded one other person when they attacked Bakiyawa (Batagarawa, Katsina). One married woman was also abducted; the youths of the community resisted the assailants and made it impossible for them to rob residents.

On 21 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians when they laid siege on the Geregu-Ajaokuta road (Ajaokuta, Kogi). Many commuters were wounded and seven persons including a lawyer and doctor were abducted by the assailants. Six vehicles were recovered from the scene. The doctor was released, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 21 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a retired chief pharmacist at the Ekiti state ministry of health from his farm located at Orin Ekiti (Ido-Osi, Ekiti). The abductee was released after 3 days, not less than 4.5 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 21 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen from Gando forest wounded many residents when they attacked Zugu community (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The assailants set a police outpost and three houses adjacent it ablaze, shops were looted and set ablaze and other residents sustained injuries as a result of a stampede while fleeing the assailants. The policemen had fled the outpost before the arrival of the militiamen who had passed the community but returned to attack the policemen and prevent them from foiling their invasion of other villages. An unspecified number of persons were displaced.

On 21 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted 6 residents from Keke A and Keke B areas on New Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna). One of the abductees is a soldier's wife, whose husband is presumed to have been a target but he was not at home when the abductors invaded the house.

On 21 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed three and wounded several others at a provision store by Ufoma Atose street in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). One of the murdered victims was the landlord of the building where the attack took place, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 21 June 2022, policemen in collaboration with a local self defense militia repelled an attack by Katsina communal militiamen in Sabon Dawa, Zakka district (Safana, Katsina). Two militiamen were killed.

Around 21 June 2022 (as reported), Kaduna militiamen received ransom from an abductee and informed the victim's family that he had been killed after. The victim was abducted along Kaduna-Abuja road, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna) in May [coded separately].

On 22 June 2022, policemen and members of a local self defense militia on a rescue mission clashed with Niger militiamen who abducted two farmers from Doma village, coded to Lapai (Lapai, Niger). One local self defense militiaman was killed, one of the abductees was killed during a rescue mission on a 24 June [coded separately]
On 22 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed two policemen when they invaded Yelwata, coded to Gbajimba (Guma, Benue).

On 22 June 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed the police DPO in charge of Nasarawa Eggon LGA who was on patrol and abducted him along Nasarawa Eggon-Arikia road (Lafia, Nassarawa). A ransom of 5 million naira was demanded.

On 22 June 2022, Nigerian army soldiers an unidentified armed group shot at civilians when they invaded Igbomotoru community, coded to Oporoma (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa) in gun boats and speed boats, as claimed by the community leaders. Many residents were wounded, buildings were burnt down and cash belonging to the building owners was stolen.
On 22 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Isuokoma community from his palace in Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). A ransom of 2 million naira was demanded.
On 22 June 2022, Katsina militiamen invaded a residence and abducted an 18-year old female at Sokoto Rima Quarters Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 22 June 2022, suspected ISWAP militants attacked Nigerian troops at a military base in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). The soldiers fled from the camp due to lack of ammunition and fighting equipment, the militants stole weapons and personal belongings from the camp. The attack lasted till the early hours of the following day.
Around 22 June 2022 (as reported), Nigerian soldiers clashed with Katsina militiamen at Mai Gora (Faskari, Katsina). Two militiamen were killed.

On 23 June 2022, three suspected members of an unidentified cult militia attacked civilians at a pub, killed two persons and shot one girl in the leg in Akwuke (Enugu South, Enugu). The murdered victims were the pregnant wife of the pub owner and a member of a local self defense militia (assumedly off duty), the assailants had visited the compound and demanded to see a young man who was not at home, they returned later for the pub owner who fled. The wounded girl was the help of the murdered woman.
On 23 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed three civilians including a university lecturer in Jootar (Wukari, Taraba).

On 23 June 2022, policemen engaged Kaduna militiamen in a clash along Galadimawa Kidandan road (Giwa, Kaduna). The militiamen fled into the forest with some of them sustaining bullet wounds, one other was killed, his rifle a revolver with cartridges and an operational motorcycle and were recovered.

On 23 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one tractor driver and abducted 22 people who were working on their farm in Rafin Daji, Gurdi ward (Abaji, FCT). Two tractors belonging to the owner of a farm were set ablaze, 13 out of the 22 abductees were members of the same family, other sources report 15 persons were abducted. The 15 abductees were released after 3 million naira was paid for each victim; items like rice, indian hemp, noodles, cigarettes and other hard drugs were also given to the abductors.

On 23 June 2022, security agents clashed with Katsina militiamen who abducted an unspecified number of residents from Rahamawa and Shagari-low cost housing estates in Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). It is unclear whether all the abductees were rescued, the militiamen were trailed by security agents, there are no further reports.
On 23 June 2022, hunters ambushed and clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Lawanti axis of Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). Four militants were killed while others escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 23 June 2022, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol ambushed and clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants on motorcycles around Gajiram general area (Nganzai, Borno). 6 militants were killed, three motorcycles and rifles were recovered.

On 23 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a Fulani pastoralist at a Fulani settlement in Rafin-Zurfi, coded to Gwagwalada (Gwagwalada, FCT). The assailants had targeted an unidentified person whom they missed and killed the victim instead.

On 24 June 2022, members of a local self defense militia on a search and rescue mission clashed with Niger militiamen who attacked and abducted scores of civilians in Kpada (Lapai, Niger). Three local self defense militiamen were killed, the assailants set one tractor ablaze.
On 24 June 2022, Nko communal militia and Onyadama communal militia clashed in Nko (Yakurr, Cross River ) over a disputed piece of land. Four people were killed and many sustained injuries.

On 24 June 2022, Niger militiamen ambushed members of a local self defense militia from Abaji and hunters who were on a rescue mission some kilometers from Lafia Kpada-Doma (Lapai, Niger). Two NSVC members, three self defense militiamen from FCT and one of farmers who was abducted from Doma [coded separately] were killed, six other self defense militiamen were wounded.

On 24 June 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Benue militiamen when they raided their hideout in Mbahuwuhe village, Utange council ward (Katsina Ala, Benue). Three militiamen were killed, one abductee with injuries was rescued, several items were recovered by the troops and the hideout was destroyed.

On 24 June 2022, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier and wounded the one other when they attacked soldiers and hunters in Boloko village (Fufore, Adamawa). Other sources report that 5 hunters and 1 soldier were killed.

On 24 June 2022, ISWAP militants attacked a police station and clashed with policemen at the Okehi area command, in Eika-Ohizenyi, coded to Obangede (Okehi, Kogi). One policeman was killed, a part of the police station was destroyed by explosives used by the assailants who fled before the reinforcement of soldiers and policemen arrived and two vehicles were destroyed.
On 25 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the transportation manager of a university in Yola at Fufore LGA (Adamawa). A ransom of 20 million naira was demanded for his release.

On 25 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked the residence of the district head in Rini (Bakura, Zamfara) and killed at least 2 persons. 4 others including the district head and his relatives were abducted.

On 25 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted many people including a medical doctor and two other health workers at Mashayar Zaki, along the Dan Sadau-Magami road (Maru, Zamfara). The doctor is also the Director-General of the Dansadau general hospital, a ransom of 20 million naira which was later to 5 million was demanded for the release of the medical doctor. The medical doctor and health workers were released after 5 million naira ransom was paid, the ransom was later returned to the abductees.
On 25 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked and killed a catholic priest when they raided the Prison farm at Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna).

On 25 June 2022, soldiers raped women and attacked civilians in Nko community (Yakurr, Cross River), shot sporadically and killed at least 5 to 10 persons. The soldiers, who were in the area to curb a communal clash, broke into shops and destroyed houses, searched for men and beat up the women when they did not find men. The attack lasted until the following day; the police claimed the soldiers' invasion was caused by shooting of an army major. The Nigerian Bar Association and the community claimed that the soldiers also raped women.

On 25 June 2022, suspected Nko militiamen attacked soldiers who were on a peace keeping mission in Nko community (Yakurr, Cross River), the soldiers in retaliation invaded the community [coded separately]. One soldier was killed and six others were wounded. The community denied attacking the soldiers.

Around 25 June 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted the immediate past secretary of Birnin Gwari local council and his younger brother from their farm. Location coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), the secretary was murdered after an undisclosed amount [coded separately] had been paid as ransom, while his brother escaped.

On 25 June 2022, soldiers in collaboration with policemen and DSS operatives clashed with IPOB militants in their camps at Idara Nnebo, Ihe Mbosi and Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra). The troops cleared the militants fire positions and IEDs and dislodged them from their camps.

On 25 June 2022, Nigerian troops raided a camp of IPOB militants which forced the militants to flee at Nkwerre-Inyi (Oji River, Enugu). The troops recovered two cars which had been snatched by the militants.

On 25 June 2022, members of a local self defense militia foiled an attempt by Sokoto militiamen to abduct farmers after the assailants killed 8 farmers in Kurya village (Rabah, Sokoto) and 3 others in Gandi district [coded separately].

On 25 June 2022, members of a local self defense militia foiled an attempt by Sokoto militiamen to abduct farmers after the assailants killed 3 farmers in their neighborhood in Gandi district (Rabah, Sokoto) and 8 others in Kurya [coded separately].

On 25 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen clashed with policemen who were part a convoy escorting a DPO at Corner Bolla, between Igabi and Chikun (Igabi, Kaduna). Several vehicles including those conveying civilian commuters were attacked, several people including the DPO were abducted. A ransom of 250 million naira which was later reduced to 80 million was demanded, the family of raised an unspecified amount which the abductors collected and refused to release him. The DPO was released on 5 October, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 25 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians and killed 15 people in Mada district (Gusau, Zamfara). An unspecified number of persons were abducted.

On 25 June 2022, Niger militiamen attacked civilians and killed three persons in Kombo village, coded to nearby Zara (Rafi, Niger). The assailants also abducted many residents from various communities, one person was seriously wounded, the attack started at night and ended the following morning.

On 25 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a man at Nwanchi village (Aniocha, Anambra) and put him in the trunk of his car which they took. The abductee was rescued on the same day by policemen [coded separately].
On 26 June 2022, members of KSVS and local hunters clashed with an unidentified armed group and killed two of them at Upogoro hills (Okene, Kogi). Two abductees were rescued.
On 26 June 2022, policemen on patrol clashed with an unidentified armed group and killed two of them at Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). The policemen recovered a car and two guns.

On 26 June 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to comprise of armed pastoralists killed a member of a local self defense militia and two civilians including a catholic priest whom they abducted from his residence at Ikabigbo community (Etsako West, Edo).

On 26 June 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be comprised of armed pastoralists killed a member of a search team and wounded two to three others. The search team was made up of security operatives, a local self defense militia and community youths who were searching for a catholic priest that was abducted from his residence in Ikabigbo community (Etsako West, Edo). Other sources report that two militiamen were killed.

On 26 June 2022, policemen repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group who were shooting sporadically at Uli (Ihiala, Anambra). The assailants fled and left behind the driver of their operational vehicle who was killed by the policemen, the car was recovered with charms in it.

On 26 June 2022, policemen on routine patrol engaged an unidentified armed group in a clash and foiled an attempted abduction by the group. One member of the group who had been on the police's wanted list was killed. Location coded to Benin City (Oredo, Edo).
