On 26 June 2022, a policeman shot and killed a truck assistant following an argument over an illegal levy at a checkpoint in Katsina-Ala (Katsina Ala, Benue). The victim had victim had paid 1500 naira instead of 3000 which was collected from loaded trucks and an argument.

On 27 June 2022, policemen shot and killed a truck driver and his motor boy at Itori (Ewekoro, Ogun) for driving against traffic while trying to avoid a bad portion of the road. The policemen and the driver had engaged in an argument after the policemen shot at the truck's tires.

On 27 June 2022, Agila and Ezza militiamen attacked Ngbo locals at Ojiogu and Okpochiri Ukwagba Ngbo, coded to Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) over a land dispute. Over 15 persons were killed, other sources report one killed, many were missing and injured and properties worth millions of Naira were destroyed. The chairman of Ngbo North Development Centre claimed the assailants were Agila militiamen.

On 27 June 2022, local self defense militiamen from Debogi, Zago and Ebbo carried out a reprisal attack on Niger militiamen in a forest which borders Lafia Kpada and Duma communities, coded to Lafia Kpada (Lapai, Niger). Five Niger militiamen were killed and six others escaped with bullet wounds.

Around 27 June 2022 (as reported), Ansaru militants beat up a commercial motorcyclist who lives in Unguwar Makera, Kazange ward, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) because he was seen with a sticker of a political aspirant.

On 27 June 2022, soldiers attached to the Forcados terminal shot and killed a civilian in Ogulagha community, coded to Forcados (Burutu, Delta). The victim was a snail hunter who went out in the company of 5 others to pick snails; they were intercepted by soldiers on the way back, the victim tried to flee and he was shot.

On 27 June 2022, soldiers dressed in plain clothes shot sporadically when they clashed with policemen at Edepie-Etegwe roundabout Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The soldiers were driving against traffic and were advised to take the proper lane by the policemen, which resulted in the clash; two persons were hit and wounded by stray bullets.
On 27 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians at Ayere (Ijumu, Kogi). The victims were from Ikaram Akoko. A ransom of 40 million naira was demanded.

On 27 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Udoda (Ahoada West, Rivers) and killed an unspecified number of person, coded as 3. The assailants broke doors and stole money worth 30 million naira and have killed over 30 people since 2019 [coded separately], according to the Paramount Ruler of the community.

On 27 June 2022, an operative of Amotekun shot and killed a student of Rufus Giwa Polytechnic Owo (Owo, Ondo) in front his parent's residence. The reason for the attack is unknown, the victim died from gunshot wounds ten days later.
On 28 June 2022, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed around the University of Port Harcourt, Choba (Obio, Rivers). An unspecified number of persons were killed, coded as 3.
On 28 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed five soldiers in villages neighboring Wase (Wase, Plateau).

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF ambushed suspected Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] in the axis of Gubio LGA (Borno). Three militants were killed, one bow and arrow, two rifles and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 28 June 2022, Fulani and Gbagyi ethnic militias clashed in Paikon Kore (Gwagwalada, FCT) following a disagreement over land for planting of pasture and food for consumption, many locals were wounded. Soldiers calmed the situation while policemen fired shots in the air.

Around 28 June 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed the immediate past secretary of Birnin Gwari local council whom they abducted together with and his younger brother from their farm [coded separately]. Location coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), the secretary was murdered after an undisclosed amount had been paid as ransom, while his brother escaped.

On 28 June 2022, Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] ambushed Nigerian troops after detonating an IED on the troops carrying out clearance operation along Miromti and Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed the Civilian JTF commander who attempted to repel their attack in Sabon Gero (Chikun, Kaduna). One resident was also killed, 17 residents including a medical doctor were abducted while six of the abductees escaped. The abductees were released on 13 August, the leader of the Civilian JTF claimed there was no ransom payment.

On 28 June 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted the wife of the chairman of the Zamfara state chapter of NULGE from their residence at Damba in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia was in search of the chairman who hid himself, and his wife pregnant wife was taken. The abductee gave birth in captivity, a ransom of 15 million was paid for the baby and mother's release.

On 28 June 2022, an unidentified armed group comprised of 5 masked men shot and killed a police officer who was returning home from work in Oboama community, Oyigbo (Oyigbo, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian soldiers from the navy and army killed scores of civilians when they invaded Ossomala, Umunankwo and Obeagwa communities, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra) as claimed by residents of the community. The soldiers were reported to be in search of unidentified armed group members, they destroyed traditional sanctuaries and claimed they were linked to IPOB activities. Scores of fatalities split across two events, coded as 10.

On 28 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in large numbers and a large convoy of vehicles attacked civilians in Lassa (Askira Uba, Borno). The militants shot sporadically and broke into stores, they invaded the village after coming from an area near Sambisa forest by Maikadiri and Utavu. Casualties unknown.

On 28 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in their large numbers clashed with Nigerian troops stationed at Maikadiri (Askira Uba, Borno) before they proceeded to attack Lassa town [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP militants on a troop's base in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The militants withdrew and fled through Dogsa. Casualties are unknown, ISWAP claimed to have fired three mortar at the barracks.

On 29 June 2022, members of the Enugu state vigilante group shot a 15 year old boy and killed him at his residence for resisting arrest in Nkpologwu community, coded to Umulokpa (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victim was confirmed dead the following day as a result of the injury from the shooting.

Around 29 June 2022 (as reported), soldiers in collaboration with members of a local self defense militia killed a member of an unidentified armed group at Kan Duniya, coded to Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau).

On 29 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted an unspecified number of persons from Gadar Zaima, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) on the village market day. The abductees include the village head, a political secretary of a political party from Kyaram ward, a local hunter and many visitors at the market.

Around 29 June 2022 (as reported), one of the abductees from the Kaduna train attack [coded separately] was shot by their abductors during a friendly exchange of fire between the abductors, as claimed by the negotiator who said the victim was in critical condition. Location coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna).

On 29 June 2022, Nigerian soldiers from the navy and army killed scores of civilians when they invaded Ossomala, Umunankwo and Obeagwa communities, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra) as claimed by residents of the community. The soldiers were reported to be in search of unidentified armed group members they destroyed traditional sanctuaries and claimed they were linked to IPOB activities. Scores of fatalities split across two events, coded as 10.

On 29 June 2022, a Niger militia clashed with policemen and ambushed soldiers providing reinforcement when they attacked a mining site at Ajata-Aboki, near Galapai (Shiroro, Niger). 35 soldiers, 7 mobile policemen, and 6 civilians were killed, several persons were wounded, between 2 and 4 Chinese nationals and other workers were abducted. Seven Chinese abductees were rescued by troops of the Nigerian Air Force on 17 December.

On 29 June 2022, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed and two people were killed in two separate attacks in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Other source report that 8 people were killed across Benin City as a result of a clash which was caused by one cult member who abandoned his group and joined a rival cult group.
On 29 June 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian troops at Mairami (Konduga, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 30 June 2022, about 300 members of a Zamfara communal militia including women dressed in military uniforms on motorcycles attacked civilians in Gadar Zaima, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). Two persons were killed and 12 others were abducted.

On 30 June 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with policemen who were on stop and search duty at a checkpoint in Gariki (Enugu South, Enugu). Two policemen were killed, other sources report that an unspecified number of persons were also killed.
On 30 June 2022, policemen raided a camp of IPOB militants and engaged in an armed clash at Oriuzor (Ezza North, Ebonyi). One militant was killed, six others fled with fled with bullet wounds.
On 30 June 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians, killed 20 people and abducted 25 women when they invaded three villages in Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 30 June 2022, a suspected Fulani militia dressed in military and police uniforms attacked civilians and killed two people in Mgbuji and Agu-Amede communities (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Two other persons were wounded.

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP fighters on 5 gun trucks attacked a camp of Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Gazuwa village, coded to near by Bama LGA (Borno). 18 ISWAP and 3 Boko Haram fighters were killed, three out of the five gun trucks were seized by the Boko Haram fighters, the other ISWAP fighters fled on motorcycles and two gun trucks.
On 30 June 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers on a patrol around Amdami forest, Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). Seven soldiers were killed.

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked civilians at Nchiha village in Korongilum ward (Chibok, Borno). Eight villagers including five members of the same family were killed, two other villagers drowned in a river while attempting to escape (total of 10 fatalities).

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired anti-aircraft rifles GPMG at an MNJTF helicopter in Borno, coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The pilot and co-pilot of landed the aircraft successfully and were unhurt.

On 1 July 2022, an Ezza militia killed a man from Ngbo at his house in Nkwuada, coded to Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) over a cow which the assailants claimed was found on his farm. Other sources report that the reason for the attack was anger by the Ezza people over the Ngbo people's refusal to allow them settle in the community.
On 1 July 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed two Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] and seized one motorcycle in the axis of Mafa LGA (Borno).
On 1 July 2022, Nigerian troops repelled an attempted attack by ISWAP fighters in Buni Gari (Gujba, Yobe). The militants fled.

Around 1 July 2022 (as reported), MNJTF troops on an offensive killed scores of ISWAP militants in armed clashes at Sabon Tumbum and Jibularam, Marte LGA (Borno). Top ISWAP leaders arrived in Sabon Tumbum from Kwalaram axis to evacuate the dead and wounded militants, scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 2 July 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) militants along Damaturu-Maiduguri road, coded to Ngamdu (Kaga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 2 July 2022, an unidentified armed group intercepted and abducted two catholic priests between Ehor and Iruekpen (Esan West, Edo). The abductees were on their way to Uromi from Benin City, the abductors fired several shots into the air which forced their car to stop. The abductees were rescued by policemen on 5 July there are no reports of a clash or ransom payment.

On 2 July 2022, a Ngbo militia attacked people from Ezza ethnic group at their settlement, coded to Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) in retaliation over the murder of one Ngbo local by Ezza militiamen. Casualties are unknown.

Around 2 July 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer from his residence at Eruku (Ekiti, Kwara). The abductee's body was found by vigilantes on a search and rescue mission after he was murdered over his family's inability to pay ransom [coded separately].

On 2 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia dressed in military and police uniforms abducted four persons who were returning from the farm at Mgbuji-Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 2 July 2022, a Sokoto militia attacked farmers on their farms at a community near Gandi district (Rabah, Sokoto) and killed four people. An 18 year old girl was abducted by the assailants.

On 2 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted one civilian from Kofar Gabas town coded to Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). The abductee was rescued by Nigerian troops at Maberiya village [no reports of a clash].

On 3 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman near his compound in Umuoma Nekede community (Owerri West, Imo). The abductee was trailed by the armed group from the Central primary school where he went to play football till he was abducted as he was alighting from his car. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 3 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a community leader and killed his son when they invaded his residence in Anguwan Baraye, Jannaret ward (Mangu, Nigeria). They kidnapped two women including the wife of the community leader.

On 3 July 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Boko Haram militants and killed five of them at Gamage village (Dikwa, Borno). Weapons and ammunitions were recovered by the troops, according to the Defense Headquarters.

Around 3 July 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted an Italian catholic priest along Ogunwenyi through Usen Community (Ovia South West, Edo). The abductee was rescued by policemen [coded separately].

On 3 July 2022, policemen invaded the camp of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash; three armed men were killed and the rest fled with gunshot injuries while an Italian priest who was abducted by the group [coded separately] was rescued. Location coded to Usen (Ovia South West, Edo) which is the area around where the abduction took place.

On 3 July 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with a local self defense militia in Zak community which is about 40km from Wase town (Wase, Plateau) Nine members of the armed group and 3 from the local defense militia were killed. The spokesperson of Operation Safe Haven claimed that the troops repelled the attack.
On 3 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two women at Washna village in Panyam district (Mangu, Plateau). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 3 July 2022, ISWAP claimed to have killed a policeman in Suleja (Suleja, Niger) and stole his gun.

On 3 July 2022, troops of MNJTF repelled an attack by ISWAP militants who invaded Monguno (Monguno, Borno) in gun trucks and motorcycles. The clash lasted for more than an hour and was reported to be a retaliation by the militants for the killing of some members by the MNJTF [coded separately]. Casualties are unknown.
On 4 July 2022, troops of Operation Safe Haven repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group on Gaji Bashar (Wase, Plateau). Casualties are unknown.
On 4 July 2022, an Ezza militia attacked Nkwuada locals and killed at least fifteen people, location coded to Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi).

On 4 July 2022, a large Kaduna militia attacked civilians in Iburu village (Kajuru, Kaduna), killed four persons and abducted 15 others . The fourth victim was killed on his way to offer assistance to other victims.

On 4 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked an off duty naval officer and cut off his hand before abducting him from his residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi) which they entered by destroying the windows and doors, a ransom of 3 million naira was demanded.

On 4 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife of the pastor in charge of ECWA church headquarters in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The abductee was taken away when the abductors invaded the church staff house and shot sporadically to scare people away; the pastor engaged the assailants [means not stated] before he escaped, there are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 4 July 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot at an aide of the Delta state governor at Ovwor, coded to Ovwodokpokpor (Ughelli South, Delta). The targeted victim was able to escape unhurt and he claimed that cash and other valuables worth millions of naira were stolen from his car.

On 4 July 2022, a Fulani militia attacked civilians, killed one person when they blocked Muji 1 route (Takum, Taraba) and killed another in Jenuwa Gida and Nyfiye communities [coded separately]. Five other people were wounded.

On 4 July 2022, a Fulani militia attacked civilians, killed a boy when they invaded Jenuwa Gida and Nyfiye communities coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba) and killed another person on the Muji 1 route [coded separately]. Five other people were wounded.

On 4 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted a catholic priest when they invaded the church rectory in Zambina (Kauru, Kaduna). The abductee was released barely 24 hours later, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 4 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a security guard of a petrol station and set the station ablaze at Igoba (Akure North, Ondo). The murdered victim was found tied up.
On 5 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked civilians and killed two people in Dogon Ruwa village (Dutsinma, Katsina). The assailants broke into many shops and stole valuables.
On 5 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a traditional ruler and his wife when they invaded Sabon Gari Bari village (Rogo, Kano). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Kunamawar Mai Awaki, Kunamwa Babba (Safana, Katsina), Unguwar Gurbai, Doguwar Dankwambo and Unguwar Ido [coded separately] killed eighteen people.
Around 5 July 2022 (between 3 - 6 July), two unidentified cult militias clashed around Apete, Fajol and other communities in Obantoko (Odedah, Ogun). Four persons were killed.
On 5 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman during an attempt to assassinate the deputy governorship candidate of the APC at the GRA axis of Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers).

On 5 July 2022, a Katsina militia numbering over 300 ambushed a police team that was on clearance patrol in Zakka forest (Safana, Katsina). The Katsina militia were on motorcycles shot sporadically with AK47 rifles and GPMGs, two police men including one assistant commissioner of police were killed, others sources report 3 fatalities.

On 5 July 2022, Nigerian troops repelled an attack by ISWAP militants who invaded the area in large numbers at Khaddamari (Jere, Borno) and attempted to attack a military formation. Casualties are unknown.

On 5 July 2022, ISWAP militants numbering over 200 attacked the medium security prison with explosives and clashed with security personnel at Kuje (Kuje, FCT). One NSCDC operative, two militants and four to ten inmates who attempted to escape were killed; 16 others were wounded, about 879 inmates escaped and 443 were rearrested, the Minister of Defense stated that all 64 Boko Haram/ ISWAP inmates had escaped. ISWAP claimed the attack and stated that its fighters who launched the attack were divided into 3 groups, the militants also gave the inmates a quaranic lecture in Fulani, Ebira and Hausa.
On 5 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked civilians, killed three persons at Buturkai village and rustled some animals at Marke village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 5 July 2022, a Katsina militia numbering up to 300 clashed with a local self defense militia at Kwanar Dtse, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). Three local defense militiamen and unspecified number of the assailants were killed, many other victims were wounded, cattle were rustled by the assailants who left with the dead bodies of their members. Fatalities coded as 6.

On 5 July 2022, presidential guards comprised of military, police forces and DSS operatives repelled an attack by a Katsina militia who ambushed them at Turare village near Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). Two members of the team sustained minor injuries, the guards and other members of the team were part of the president's advance team. Other sources report that there was no clash between the operatives and the militiamen; the operative waited till the militiamen left the area before proceeding and then shot into the air.
On 5 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted one man from Jangebe (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). 37 cows were also rustled from the village by the militia, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 6 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people from Dunwawa and Alawa villages, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 6 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted at least four commuters along Oke Ako-Irele road (Ikole, Ekiti). The victims were abducted on the road that links Ekiti and the Kogi border, a ransom of 20 million has been demanded. The abductees were released after a ransom of 1 million naira was paid.

Around 6 July 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a farmer whom they abducted from his residence [coded separately] after he was unable to pay the ransom. Location coded to Eruku (Ekiti, Kwara) where the victim was abducted, the victim's body was found by a search party of youths and vigilantes in the bush, three suspects were arrested and handed over to the police.
On 6 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a vice principal of a school in Iseyin (Iseyin, Oyo). The victim was released after a ransom of 2 million naira was paid.
On 6 July 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded a pharmacy and abducted a pharmacist in Kokori (Ethiope East, Delta). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 6 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked the residence of a pastor in Njairi (Mubi South, Adamawa) and killed two of his sons. The pastor was shot in the leg, his 13 year old daughter was abducted and his wife was left unconscious. The girl was released on 9 July after an huge ransom was paid.
On 6 July 2022, ISWAP claimed to have attacked and killed three Nigerian soldiers at Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Other sources report that 8 militants were killed.

On 6 July 2022, a Zamfara militia killed two commuters and wounded four others along Kaura Namoda-Shinkafi highway (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara) when they shot at a car driving towards Shinkafi. The assailants blocked the road for an hour.

On 6 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed and abducted a catholic priest along Oturkpo-Ugbokolo road (Otukpo, Benue). The abductee was released on 8 July, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 7 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted six farmers from Falam Tsibiri, Gabtu and Kairu villages, two of the abductees were taken to a new militia camp in Tabarga forest, Gabtu village coded to Gummi (Gummi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a quarry site, killed one policeman, injured one other and abducted a Chinese citizen in Shao (Moro, Kwara). The abductee was rescued by the police after the abductors abandoned him and fled.

On 7 July 2022, the Nigerian army headquarters claimed a clash between Nigerian troops on a clearance patrol and ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants around Dikwa-Gamboru highway (Dikwa, Borno). Scores of militants including top commanders were killed, coded as 20, several weapons and ammunition were recovered.
On 8 July 2022, a militia comprised of suspected Fulani ambushed and killed a civilian at Kwi (Riyom, Plateau). The victim was on his way home from work.

On 8 July 2022, a local self defense militia repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group presumed to be made up of armed pastoralists who attempted to attack the railway station in Abraka (Ethiope East, Delta). There were no casualties.

On 8 July 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted the head teacher of Shuwari primary school when they invaded Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The school and the teachers' quarters were set ablaze by the militants.

On 9 July 2022, pirates numbering over 700 abducted 5 civilians when they invaded Ibaka fishing community (Mbo, Akwa Ibom). The abductors shot sporadically to scare residents away, nine boats and outboard engines were stolen. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 9 July 2022, Biramafu and Evungi militias clashed in Biramafu (Gbako, Niger) and two people from Evungi were killed. The clash was over high speed breakers which were set up by residents of Biramafu on the road connecting their village to villages which residents Evungi attempted to remove.
On 9 July 2022, Nigerian troops responded to a distress call and rescued nine passengers who were abducted by an unidentified armed group at Dogon Filli village, coded to Jemaa (Jema'a, Kaduna).

On 9 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from his residence at Idare quarters in Okene (Okene, Kogi). The abductors posed as business associates of the victim whom they took away in his car; after burning their car at his residence, other sources report that the victim was beaten up and tied before he was taken away. The abductee was released on 15 September, after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.
On 9 July 2022, policemen on patrol clashed with an unidentified armed group suspected to be abductors at Iyuku (Etsako West, Edo). One of the assailants were killed.

On 10 July 2022, a Zamfara militia loyal to Damina attacked and killed 13 people on their farms in Dan Gulbi (Maru, Zamfara). Six people were killed outside the community and the other seven were killed inside the main village, several residents fled and unspecified number were missing.

On 10 July 2022, a policeman shot at a student of federal polytechnic Nekede at the entrance of his hostel in Umuokomoche, coded to Nekede (Owerri West, Imo). The student dodged the bullet and was not wounded, the reason for the attack is unknown and the policeman fled.

On 10 July 2022, Biramafu and Evungi militias clashed at Biramafu (Gbako, Niger) after two people were killed the previous day [coded previously]. One person was killed, soldiers and mobile policeman were deployed to the area.

On 10 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically and abducted the wife of the general manager of Imo state zoo from the car park of a church in Nekede (Owerri West, Imo). The abductors had tried to pick a different woman before a member of the group insisted saying ''its not this one''. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, the victim was released on 19 July, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 10 July 2022, an unidentified armed group who were 3 in number, wearing military uniforms killed a former militant leader at a hotel in Okutukutu (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The victim was the head of operations at Darlon oil and gas servicing limited, the attack is assumed to be an assassination.
On 10 July 2022, a Zamfara militia loyal to Damina shot and killed 5 people in Kango village, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). Several residents fled and unspecified number were missing.

On 10 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted one person in Awka South LGA (Awka South, Anambra) coded to Awka. The victim was released by the abductors in Amawbia area, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 10 July 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with a Katsina militia at Sambo village in Dandume LGA (Katsina). Two from the militia were killed, arms and ammunition were recovered; the clash took happened the following day also [coded separately]. 2 fatalities split across two events coded as 1.
On 11 July 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering about six abducted a businessman from his residence at Ugbokolo (Okpokwu, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of persons including the wife of the traditional ruler and nursing mothers when they attacked Kurfa community (Gummi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked civilians, killed one and abducted three people at Kwarare, coded to Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). The victims who were traveling from Jibia to Katsina drove into a roadblock which the militia set up using fire wood, the murdered victim was a student.

On 11 July 2022, security operatives (assumed Police forces) repelled an unidentified armed group that invaded the residence of the gubernatorial candidate of Labor party in the Osun state elections at Oke Ima, Ilobu (Irepodun, Osun) and shot sporadically. The LP candidate claimed that the assailants were supporters of the state governor. There were no casualties.

On 11 July 2022, an Iwo militia beat up a farmer from Odo Ekun community and almost lynched him before the victim was saved by his kinsmen. The victim had gone to a land which is currently in dispute between the two communities. Location coded to Iwo (Osin, Kwara).

On 11 July 2022, an Iwo militia killed one civilian, destroyed vehicles and houses when they invaded Odo Ekun community coded to Iwo (Osin, Kwara). The militia had previously attacked and beat up a farmer [coded separately].

On 11 July 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with a Katsina militia at Sambo village in Dandume LGA (Katsina). Two from the militia were killed, arms and ammunition were recovered; the clash took happened the previous day also [coded separately]. 2 fatalities split across two events coded as 1.
On 12 July 2022, policemen attached to a convoy killed two passengers of a tricycle and wounded the rider for attempting to overtake their convoy at Effurun (Uvwie, Delta).

On 12 July 2022, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a student when they invaded his residence at Akerebiata (Ilorin East, Kwara). The victim was hot in the chest, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 12 July 2022, a militia comprised of suspected Fulani attacked and killed five civilians at Anter community, Mbalagh council ward (Makurdi, Benue). The state governor's special adviser on security matters claimed to have received reports of two fatalities, other sources claim some persons were seriously wounded while others fled from their homes.

On 12 July 2022, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group that attacked Abuja quarters in Ugbor GRA, Benin City (Oredo, Edo). One member of the group was shot and killed and weapons were recovered.

On 12 July 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and killed ten militants around Titiwa village (Magumeri, Borno). The militants had set a checkpoint and abducted scores of civilians before the soldiers engaged them in a clash; some militants escaped with bullet wound and two stolen vehicle were recovered and returned to the owners.

On 13 July 2022, Ansaru militants repelled an attack by a Kaduna militia on civilians in Damari, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia attacked while Ansaru militants were preaching and were engaged in a clash, two locals were killed, shops, vehicles and a private hospital were burnt in the clash which lasted for more than two hours before the militia fled.

Around 13 July 2022 (between 13 - 20 July), an unidentified armed group killed over 30 civilians and displaced over 20,000 others when they attacked communities in Ussa LGA (Taraba) (coded to Lissam) and Takum, as claimed by the lawmaker representing the area in the House of Representatives. 30 fatalities split across two events; coded as 15.

Around 13 July 2022 (between 13 - 20 July), an unidentified armed group killed over 30 civilians and displaced over 20,000 others when they attacked communities in Takum and Ussa LGA (Taraba), as claimed by the lawmaker representing the area in the House of Representatives. 30 fatalities split across two events; coded as 15.
Around 13 July 2022, a Katsina militia killed two men and abducted one woman when they invaded Gangdun Sarki, a Fulani settlement in Bakori LGA (Katsina).

On 13 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted three others at Boto village (Tafawa Balewa, Bauchi). Two victims were relatives of a former governor who was the target of the assailants. A ransom of 600 million naira was demanded and later reduced to 6 million. Policemen reached the village after the assailants left. One of the abductees who is a female was released after 6 days, the other abductees were released around 26 July, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 13 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked officials of INEC at a voter registration center in Umuopu (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). Two voter registration machines were damaged by the assailants who shot sporadically into the air and caused a stampede which led to the injury of at least two persons, other personal items like mobile phones were lost. The attack led to the suspension of voter registration in the area.

On 14 July 2022, pirates abducted 28 people when they attacked a boat conveying fish traders along Uruan water channel, coded to Idu (Uruan, Akwa Ibom). The abductees were rescued by policemen who conducted a search.

On 14 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed two persons, wounded two others and abducted one person at Garun Gabas village (Malam Madori, Jigawa). The four victims attempted to foil an abduction by the assailants before they were attacked.
On 14 July 2022, Ezillo and Ishielu militias clashed in Ishielu (Ishielu, Ebonyi). The reason for the clash and casualties are unknown.

On 14 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a lecturer when they invaded his residence at Bajabure, coded to Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The victim who was a lecturer at the Adamawa state polytechnic was killed in the presence of his wife, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 14 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two expatriates in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The abductors arrived at the location in two SUVs and one Hummer bus and the occupants of the bus were dressed in military camouflage.

On 15 July 2022, pirates wounded two persons out of the 28 persons whom they abducted the previous day [coded separately] along the Uruan water channel, coded to Idu (Uruan, Akwa Ibom). The abductees were robbed, the engine of one of their boat was burnt by the assailants and they rescued by policemen after the pirates fled.
On 15 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man at a burial ceremony in Atta (Ikeduru, Imo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 15 July 2022, policemen on an offensive operation raided 3 hideouts of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Achalla (Awka North, Anambra). Over 10 members of the armed group were killed, weapons, ammunitions, cars and other items including a police uniform were recovered.
On 15 July 2022, a Kaduna militia killed two health ad hoc staff and wounded another while they were returning from duty in Zangang community in Kaura LGA (Kaduna).

On 15 July 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted two girls when they attacked Gidan Liman village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The police claimed to have rescued the abductees unconditionally at Nya Mango, around 21 August.

Around 15 July 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted about 40 villagers when they invaded Gidan-Dogo and Gidna villages, coded to nearby Ida (Kagarko, Kaduna). The assailants disrupted a burial ceremony in Gidan-Dogo and stole cooked food some of which they ate at the scene of the attack, many of the abductees were women and visitors. About 25 abductees were released, at least 12 others are yet to be released.

On 15 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Paikon Basa community in Gurdi ward (Abaji, FCT) and killed a seven year old boy. Four others were abducted; two of whom later escaped, a couple were hit by stray bullets where the assailants raided some shops and stole food stuff.

On 15 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed policemen on a car recovery mission at Oye-Agu Abagana coded to Abagana (Njikoka, Anambra) and abducted two policemen and one civilian. The abductees were killed and their bodies were set ablaze.
On 15 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 6 people from Mawogi community in Abaji area council (FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 15 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted two catholic priests on their way to perform pastoral duties at the rectory of a church in Yadin Garu (Kauru, Kaduna). One of the abductees was released after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom, the decomposing body of the second abductee was found by security operatives [coded separately].

Around 15 July 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed one of the two catholic priests whom they abducted from Yadin Garu (Kauru, Kaduna) [coded separately] and his decomposing body was found by security operatives. The second victim was released after an undisclosed amount of ransom was paid.

On 15 July 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with Nigerian soldiers who raided their hideout in an armed clash at Chito (Ukum, Benue). Three members of the group were killed, others fled, 18 motorcycles were recovered after the soldiers searched the hideout.

On 16 July 2022, a mob suspected to have been hired by land grabbers invaded Yegunda, Abomiti and Eyin-Osa areas coded to Epe (Epe, Lagos) and set several buildings ablaze. Some residents were wounded, rams, motorcycles, and money were also stolen by the assailants.
On 16 July 2022, a Kaduna militia ambushed Boko Haram militants outside of a community controlled by the militants in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). 17 militants were killed.
On 16 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a PDP party supporter at Ikire (Irewole, Osun) during the gubernatorial election.
On 16 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civilian at Amaraka (Isiala Mbano, Imo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 16 July 2022, pirates abducted an unspecified number of male passengers when they attacked and robbed a passenger boat going to Oron from Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductees except two persons were rescued after the abductors fled when they sighted Nigerian navy gunboats.

On 16 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an NDDC official after they trailed him to his community in Umuadara Umulogho (Obowo, Imo). The abductee's car was left behind by the assailants who demanded for a ransom of 10 million naira. The abductee was released around 17 July, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 16 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a farm supervisor on the farm of a former governor of Oyo state at Jabata (Surulere, Oyo). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded and the victim was released after 5 million naira was paid.
On 16 July 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked and killed two commuters at an illegal vehicle checkpoint which they mounted in Mafa LGA (Borno).
On 17 July 2022, a Kaduna militia killed one teenager and rustled several cows and looted food stuff from Dawakin Bassa community (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted about four commuters at Nise market, coded to Amawbia (Awka South, Anambra) which is a few kilometers away. The victims' car was set ablaze by the assailants who robbed some other persons, the attack lasted for about 30 minutes.

On 17 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted 8 civilians including a pregnant woman and her mother when they invaded the community and shot sporadically at Lema, coded to nearby Afaka (Igabi, Kaduna). 50 million naira ransom was demanded for the pregnant woman who delivered her baby in captivity and her sisters.

On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers who were on a patrol at Kampani in Wase LGA (Plateau). Two civilians were killed and one other was wounded by stray bullets, other sources report that additionally one soldier was killed and one other was wounded. The soldiers repelled the attack and denied that any solider was killed.

On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group riding on motorcycles abducted one person and beat up an unspecified number of others in Alor Agu (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The abductee was released after the assailants took him away and robbed him.

Around 17 July 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group shot at a commercial bus and wounded the driver at Isreal-Ama, coded to Abonnema (Akukutoru, Rivers) in an attempt to abduct the occupants. All the occupants of the bus including the driver who was wounded escaped.
On 17 July 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Ganun-Gari community in Randangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). One person was killed and three others were wounded.

On 17 July 2022, Nigerian soldiers conducted an operation and clashed with a Katsina militia at Palale-Jaja village, coded to Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). Two militia members were killed; weapons, ammunitions, motorcycles and other items were recovered by the soldiers.

On 17 July 2022, Ebube Agu operatives shot and killed between 7 to 14 civilians from Otulu community, who were returning from a wedding ceremony which held at Awomama. Location coded to Mgbidi (Oru West, Imo) which is near both communities, five other persons were missing, two were critically wounded and one sustained minor injuries. The State Governor and the DSS claimed that the murdered persons were IPOB militants who engaged in an armed clash with a joint security team.
On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians and wounded one person at Orie Akpanya (Olamaboro, Kogi). There was no reason for the attack.

On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the village head of Kuchibuyi community from his residence, coded to Bwari (Bwari, FCT) and fled with him through the road leading to Bwari town. The assailants fired gunshots to scare residents and local self defense militias away, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 17 July 2022, the Nigerian police claimed to have foiled an attack on civilians by a Katsina militia with assailants numbering over 100 at Shema and KTARDA quarters in Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The assailants abducted 9 persons including four women, shot sporadically and stole valuables from residents before the arrival of the policemen.

On 17 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 10 policemen who are assumed to be off duty at Obajana (Lokoja, Kogi). The policemen who were from the Nassarawa state command were returning from election duty in Osun state. The police claimed that the policemen were not abducted, as they all fled into the bush when their convoy was attacked by the assailants.

On 17 July 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked a position of Nigeria troops and engaged them in an armed clash at Abari axis of Monguno (Monguno, Borno). A military reinforcement was deployed and the militants were engaged till they retreated. Casualties are unknown.
Around 17 July 2022 (as reported), unidentified people invaded a polling station in Atakumosa (Atakumosa West, Osun), coded to Osu, and injured an INEC ad-hoc staff member during a voting exercise.

On 18 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a bread seller while he was distributing bread to his customers in his car at Ifewara (Atakumosa West, Osun). A ransom of 5 million naira which was later reduced to 500 thousand was demanded; the victim was released on 19 July after 150 thousand naira was paid as ransom.
On 18 July 2022, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian at Gidan Shaho in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara).

On 18 July 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be loyalists to the APC attacked the home of the Osun state commissioner for lands and physical planning, who is also an APC member, and wounded some of his aides who attempted to resist the attack in Erinmo-Ijesha (Efon, Ekiti). Properties and many cars were vandalized, other sources report that the attack maybe connected to the commissioner failing to acknowledge their help in recent elections or the victory of the PDP in the just concluded gubernatorial election.

On 18 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the APC chairman in ward 9 Orhionwon LGA when he was returning to his village from the farm. Location coded to Abudu (Orhionwon, Edo), the abductee was abandoned by the assailants after policemen chased them.
Around 18 July 2022 (as reported), a Sokoto militia killed one person at Dangawo and abducted 22 others from Dangawo and Unguwar Lalle (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).

On 18 July 2022, Nigerian soldiers clashed with a Niger militia at Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). The assailants who invaded communities in their hundreds were repelled, many of them were killed, other sources reported that at least 23 militiamen were killed and some of them escaped with bullet wounds.

On 18 July 2022, a Fulani militia abducted at least 15 residents who were on the way to their farm within Mgbuji town (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Some of the abductees were picked up from their farms. A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

Around 18 July 2022 (as reported), a joint team of policemen and a local self defense militia clashed with a Kaduna militia around Tudun Wada bridge. The assailants had attacked residents, killed two persons, abducted an unspecified number and rustled cattle in Ganun-Gari community, Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The abductees were rescued and the rustled cattle were recovered.
On 18 July 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two civilians on their farms at Ganun-Gari community in Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 18 July 2022, a Fulani militia attacked residents of a Fulani settlement in Gibob, Lusa ward (Bogoro, Bauchi). The assailants shot sporadically, abducted a 25 year old woman, broke her father's legs and wounded an unspecified number of persons. There are no reports about ransom demands.
Around 18 July 2022 (as reported), a Sokoto militia killed one person and abducted 41 farmers from Mashaya village (Sabon Birni, Sokoto) and Tsamaye [coded separately.
Around 18 July 2022 (as reported), a Sokoto militia abducted 15 persons from Katume, Garki and Yaradua villages, coded to Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).

On 18 July 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted passengers on a bus except a two year old girl along Sabon Birni-Goronyo road (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). The passengers were mostly women and were returning from a wedding ceremony.

On 18 July 2022, a local self defense militia repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group who invaded Nyifiye community in Takum LGA (Taraba). The assailants destroyed properties in the attack, there were no casualties.

On 18 July 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants ambushed a Nigerian troops and Civilian JTF and engaged them in an armed clash in Gubio LGA (Borno). 5 Civilian JTF operatives, including their chairman, and many militants were killed, coded as 3. Some sources report that soldiers were among the 5 fatalities, others report that an unspecified number of soldiers were killed, several were missing, at least one military vehicle, several weapons and ammunition were stolen and burnt by the militants.

On 19 July 2022, an unidentified armed group wounded one student with a knife and abducted another from their university in Akpabuyo LGA (Cross River) coded to Ikot Nakanda. Other sources report unspecified number of students were wounded while trying to escape the assailants who shot sporadically, the abductee was rescued by policemen who raided their hideout [coded separately].

On 19 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked and killed five civilians in Ruwan Godiya (Faskari, Katsina). Scores were wounded, several cattle and other domestic animals were rustled, the assailants also attacked Kwai village [coded separately]. Other sources report that six people were killed.

On 19 July 2022, suspected unidentified cult militia killed a member of a local self defense militia in Elibrada, coded to Emohua (Emohua, Riveres). One EMOLVICE was also shot and killed by his colleague in the crossfire.The police claimed to have arrested three person in connection with the attack.
On 19 July 2022, an unidentified cult militia attacked and wounded a man at Bolorunduro community in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 19 July 2022, a Katsina militia killed one person in Kwai village, Faskari LGA (Katsina). Scores were wounded, several cattle and other domestic animals were rustled, the assailants also attacked Ruwan Godiya village [coded separately].
On 19 July 2022, a Katsina militia killed one civilian when they attacked Kadirawa (Faskari, Katsina). The assailants also rustled an unspecified number of cattle and stole two motorcycles.

On 19 July 2022, security operatives (assumed military) clashed with a Kaduna militia at Kidunu in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, two rifles, motorcycles, charms and amulets were recovered.

On 20 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of passengers from a bus at Ochonyi-Omoko village along Lokoja-Abuja highway (Lokoja, Kogi). The assailants shot at the moving vehicle and deflated the back tires which forced it to stop.

On 20 July 2022, policemen at a checkpoint shot at a civilian at Independence Layout (Enugu North, Enugu), some sources report that the attack was over the victim' refusal to give bribe to policemen and that the victim and his girlfriend were killed. The police claimed that the victim refused to stop at a checkpoint and he hit and wounded a policeman before he was forces to stop and shot in the thigh.

On 20 July 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked the house of the Taraba state NMA chairman in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). Two local defense militia members were killed.

On 20 July 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a business man at a drinking spot in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The assailants traced the victim to the spot on a motorbike, some sources report that the victim was killed by his business rivals.

On 20 July 2022, policemen repelled an attack by a Katsina militia on the residence of a civilian at Jabiri, coded to Funtua (Funtua, Katsina). The assailants forced their way into the house and spent over one hour before the police intervention.

On 20 July 2022, a Katsina militia suspected to be from the camp of Ado Aleru numbering between 200 to 400 killed five policemen at a checkpoint in Gatakawa village (Kankara, Katsina). 3 civilians were also killed by the assailants who invaded the village on over 200 motorcycles and conducted a house to house search; money, food items, cattle and other valuables were stolen, many residents who attempted to escape sustained injuries in the attack which lasted for more than an hour. The policemen were from Kano command on special duties in the area.

Around 20 July 2022, (between 14 - 28 July), the Defense Headquarters claimed Nigerian troops repelled an attack by Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at Gwalaram village, coded to Gwalaram Ganya B (Magumeri, Borno). There are no further details.

Around 21 July 2022 (as reported), policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group in Iyuku community, coded to Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). One abductee was rescued, the assailants fled with gunshot injuries, weapons and ammunition were recovered by the policemen.

On 21 July 2022, policemen repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group on Igbo-Eze North police division headquarters within Nsukka axis (Nsukka, Enugu). The assailants fled and many of them were suspected to have sustained gunshot wounds.

On 21 July 2022, operatives of OP MESA who were chasing after suspected internet fraudsters killed a student who was hit by a stray bullet at Ago Ika area in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The police claimed the operatives were chasing a wanted cult militia member.

On 21 July 2022, a Katsina militia led by Bauche attacked Ansaru militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Damari forest (Sabuwa, Katsina). The clash lasted for several hours, three persons were killed including a top Ansaru commander.

On 21 July 2022, a Niger militia abducted a veterinary doctor who was returning to Kotangora (Kontagora, Niger) from some villages where he went to vaccinate some animals. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 21 July 2022, an unidentified armed group who were in their numbers and well armed abducted 10 cattle traders and rustled 250 cows at Andami town (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). The traders had bought the cows from the market.
On 21 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three commuters who were traveling along Ogbemudia farms, coded to Benin City (Oredo, Edo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 22 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed five civilians at different spots in Fobur community (Jos East, Plateau). One other person was abducted by the assailants, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 22 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted six people when they invaded Tabanni village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The abductees included a seven month old baby, a teenage girl and three married women, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 22 July 2022, policemen raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group who abducted a student [coded separately] and engaged them in an armed clash in Akpabuyo creek, coded to Ikot Nakanda (Akpabuyo, Cross River). Two members of the group were killed, one was arrested with injuries and the abductee was rescued.

On 22 July 2022, policemen beat up, shot and wounded a personnel of the Nigerian legion on the thigh in Lekki Scheme II estate (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos) after the policemen tried to gain access into the estate without proper clearance.

On 22 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a medical doctor along Ogbmosho-Ilorin road (Ogbomosho North, Oyo). Other sources report that he was abducted from his clinic. The Oyo state chairman of the Nigerian Medical Association claimed that the abductee is a medical doctor, a ransom of 30 million naira was demanded and the victim was released on 26 July after 3 million naira was paid as ransom.
On 22 July 2022, policemen foiled an attack by an unidentified armed group that invaded the residence of a civilian in Bassa LGA (Plateau). The assailants fled from the scene with bullet wounds.

On 22 July 2022, a Niger militia abducted at least fifty residents in Kuchi (Muya, Niger) when they invaded the area and conducted a house to house search. 20 persons escaped, while 29 others were rescued by the defense militia. The police claimed nine persons were abducted.

On 22 July 2022, a local self defense militia and hunter group clashed a Niger militia at Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger) and Galkogo. The assailants had abducted 22 persons from Kuchi [coded separately] and the abductees were rescued by the defense militia. Casualties are unknown.

On 22 July 2022, an unidentified armed group wearing masks and military camouflage killed a PDP member in Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). Sources report that the attack is connected to a communal crisis in the victim's community where the paramount ruler and community development chairman were also assassinated [coded separately]. The youths of area attempted to create a blockade to slow down the escape of the assailants and it resulted in pandemonium, the assailants fled.

On 22 July 2022, a Niger militia abducted the director of personnel management in Kontogora LGA and some laborers from his farm along Kontagora-Mariga road (Kontagora, Niger). A ransom of 15 million naira was demanded.

On 22 July 2022, a local self defense militia and hunter group clashed a Niger militia at Galkogo (Shiroro, Niger) and Sarkin Pawa. The assailants had abducted 22 persons from Kuchi [coded separately] and the abductees were rescued by the defense militia. Casualties are unknown.

On 22 July 2022, Yan Babeli militia abducted 13 Fulani pastoralists and killed 6 of them in Mongi and Langai communities (Mangu, Plateau). The victims were arrested by the militia who claimed to be searching for criminals, 7 persons were declared missing.

On 23 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed three persons, wounded many others when they attacked civilians in Pinau village (Wase, Plateau). Three other persons were abducted by the assailants who carried out the attack after soldiers guarding the village were withdrawn the previous day.

On 23 July 2022, a joint security team comprised of policemen and soldiers clashed with an unidentified armed group at Nkwo market in Okija [Orkija] (Ihiala, Anambra). One of the assailants was killed, others fled, two guns and one machete were recovered by the security operatives.

On 23 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed at least two people including a mobile policeman who was assumed to be off duty at Lasandi, BabaYau and Sabongari in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba).

On 23 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a businessman, killed him and abducted his son around Usiefurun in Orhuwhorum community (Udu, Delta). The attack lasted for the 30 minutes, the police claimed that the son was not abducted and the assailants came to rob the victim.

On 23 July 2022, policemen clashed with a Kaduna militia that attacked and abducted an unspecified number of farmers in Timburku village in Galadimawa (Giwa, Kaduna). Two of the assailants were killed, the abductees were rescued, one rifle and a motorcycle were recovered.

Around 23 July 2022 (between 23 - 24 July), an unidentified armed group shot and killed a member of the APC who is also an aide of the deputy senate president at his residence in Decima area of Sapele (Sapele, Delta). Some sources claim that the assailants were suspected assassins, others report that they were possibly armed robbers who had invaded the area

On 23 July 2022, a joint security team comprised of policemen and soldiers clashed with an unidentified armed group that blocked the road to rob and extort commuters along Onitsha-Owerri expressway (Onisha North, Anambra). One of the assailants was killed and others fled the scene with gunshot wounds.

Around 24 July 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia killed three civilians, wounded two and displaced others when they attacked 11 villages in Bardoki district (Gummi, Zamfara). The villages that were attacked include; Gwalli, Karaye, Barikin-Daji, Loni, Lanke, Duddai, Gidan-Illo, Marina, Kwado, Sagon Garbe and Makaranta, the assailants looted shops and houses and stole many valuables.

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters at Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia). The abduction took place near a military checkpoint and the soldiers could not rescue the victims.

On 24 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked and killed a farmer who was working on his farm and stole his motorcycle at Kore village in Bakiyawa ward (Batagarawa, Katsina). The assailants attacked in a large number seeking for whom to abduct, two of them approached the victim while others kept watch.

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed policemen on patrol duty who were responding to a distress call at Okpanam (Oshimili North, Delta). Three policemen were killed on the spot, one was wounded and two of their rifles were stolen.

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a couple when they invaded their residence at Sheda (Kwali, FCT). The abductors positioned themselves at strategic spots and shot sporadically during the abduction, the woman was released to go and source for ransom; there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 24 July 2022, a hunter from Bela village in Toungo LGA shot and killed his son for selling illicit drugs. Location coded to Toungo (Toungo, Adamawa).

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to comprise of Fulani attacked a police vehicle conveying expatriates and engaged policemen in an armed clash in Aruwa village, coded to nearby Ifewara (Atakumosa West, Osun). One of the assailants and one policeman were killed; the murdered policeman's rifle and ammunition were stolen by the assailants, one magazine, live ammunition and two mobile phones were recovered from the murdered assailant.

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a councilor and deputy leader of Song LGA few hours after he was abducted from his residence in Bannga, coded to Song (Song, Adamawa). The victim's son was shot and wounded by the assailants, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 24 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked commuters around Mil Takwas and Farun Bala villages, Coded to Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). The driver of one bus and two passengers were killed, an unspecified number of passengers were abducted and the passengers were robbed. Some sources reported that one person was killed and there were no abductees, other sources report that soldiers rescued the abductees after the assailants fled when the soldiers arrived [no interaction reported].

Around 24 July 2022 (between 23 - 25 July), a suspected unidentified cult militia shot an killed the son of a traditional chief at his residence in Ofatedo (Egbedore, Osun) and wounded 4 others. The victim was called out of his room by the assailants and was shot in the chest. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 24 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers on a patrol and engaged them in an armed clash along Kubwa-Bwari road (Bwari, FCT). Three soldiers were wounded, between 3 and 6 others were killed, the Nigerian Defense headquarters claimed to have killed 30 of the assailants.

On 25 July 2022, a Kaduna militia in large number on motorcycles killed three civilians when they attacked Damari in Kazage ward, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birin Gwari, Kaduna). The attack lasted for about one hour.

On 25 July 2022, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group that was responsible for the abduction of a student of Arthur Jarvis university [coded separately]. Six of the armed group members were killed according to the public relations officer of the police in Cross River state. Location coded to Ikot Nakanda (Akpabuyo, Cross River).
On 25 July 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted a catholic parishioner from his residence in Tambuwal (Tambuwal, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife of a Fulani leader from their residence in Anguwar Tudan Fulani at Yangoji (Kwali, FCT). The woman who was abducted for the second time, was abducted alongside three of their children. A ransom of 20 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded, 5 million was paid to the abductors who demanded for additional 2 million.

On 25 July 2022, Nigerian army soldiers beat up a retired policeman who is also a town union president in Imufu community at their office. The victim claimed that he was attacked after the soldiers asked him to provide the list of IPOB members in the community which he insisted he did not have. Location coded to Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu).
On 25 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted six persons in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The abductees consisted of five girls and the leader of a self defense militia.

On 25 July 2022, two unidentified cult militias clashed over a battle for territory control at Arietalin axis in Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). One civilian who was a mechanic was killed, it is unknown whether the victim was a member of one of the militias.

On 25 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a 17 year old girl in Agbegbor village in Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). Some sources reported that the assailants were armed Fulani pastoralists, the state government denied the claims and insisted that there are no pastoralists camp in the area.

On 25 July 2022, a suspected Black Axe militia also called Aiye attacked a team of policemen and engaged them in an armed clash at Mile 2 area of Lafenwa in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The clash lasted for over 30 minutes, a patrol vehicle was destroyed and one of the assailants who was initially arrested by the police escaped.

On 25 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted up to 36 residents from Keke B area in Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna). The victims except one person were released after 2.5 million naira was paid as ransom, the abductors demanded for two motorcycles as ransom for the last victim.

On 25 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three traditional worshippers who had gone to the river for prayers along Benin-Abraka road, coded to Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The abductors abandoned the victims and fled after policemen pursued them in a bid to rescue the abductees.

On 25 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a police station and clashed with policemen at Okuta Elerinla division in Akure (Akure South, Ondo). The assailants scaled through the fence to gain access into the premises, one policeman was shot and killed.

On 25 July 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a suspected member of a Zamfara militia while commuting on a motorcycle along bush paths in Gidan Garba, Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). 1 rifle and 2 pairs of woodland camouflage were recovered.

On 26 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted 13 persons and looted many shops at Hayin Gada in Damari town, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The assailants were on their way to the forest when they invaded the area after they attack civilians the previous day [coded separately].
On 26 July 2022, a local self defense militia foiled an attack by a Katsina militia along Jibia-Katsina road (Jibia, Katsina). There are no further details.
On 26 July 2022, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians, killed 4 persons and abducted up to 30 others in Morai (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). An unspecified number of abductees escaped.

On 26 July 2022, a Katsina militia attacked and killed three civilians in Yartafki, Unguwar Isyiaka and Company Daudawa communities in Funtua LGA (Katsina). Several other persons including a school principal were abducted, a nursing mother and a ward head.

On 26 July 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed a commander of a local self defense militia when they attacked his house and clashed with his security guards in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The assailants who invaded the town on motorcycles headed straight to the commander's house.

On 27 July 2022, a suspected Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Yan-Kukoki and Danbanda communities in Gummi LGA (Zamfara). About 20 persons were killed and their bodies were found around a stream the following day.

On 27 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed six persons, wounded many others and stole food stuff when they attacked civilians in Pinau village (Wase, Plateau) and shot sporadically. Four more bodies were later found in the bush, hundreds of residents fled the area after soldiers deployed to the area were withdrawn five days before the attack.

On 27 July 2022, Oyo state park management system attacked a transport company, wounded the manager and vandalized properties along New Ife road in Egbeda LGA (Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 27 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and shot at civilians and detonated explosives at a construction site in Owo (Owo, Ondo). Two gate keepers were wounded and some equipment were damaged, the state governor claimed that the assailants only intended to damage the company's equipment and not kill any person.

On 27 July 2022, Nigeria troops responded to a distress call and clashed with a Zamfara militia that attack Bayi village in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara). One of the assailants was killed, guns, ammunition, marijuana and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 27 July 2022, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians and killed 28 persons in Duma village (Tureta, Sokoto) when they invaded the community an rustled livestock. An unspecified number of person drowned in a nearby river while fleeing the attack, some others mostly youths were abducted and forced by the assailants to drive the rustled cattle out of the town. Large quantities of petrol was demanded as ransom.
On 27 July 2022, suspected Boko Haram/ ISWAP ambushed the convoy of the chairman of Nganzai LGA along Gajiram and Gajigana (Nganzai, Borno). One policeman in the convoy was killed.

On 28 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a bus driver and his conductor from a farm at Chida community in Kwali (FCT). The abductee went to load charcoal from a farm when they were abducted, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 28 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia numbering 10 abducted three persons from Abaa community coded to Iresa Pa (Surulere, Oyo). The abductees include a hotelier and one of his staff, other sources report that only the hotelier and his staff were taken. A ransom of 5 million naira was paid, the abductees were murdered by the abductors [coded separately].

On 28 July 2022, policemen on a night patrol clashed with an unidentified armed group in their hideout in Ogwueka forest along Benin-Auchi expressway (Etsako West, Edo). Two of the group's members were killed and two others were arrested, weapons and ammunitions were recovered by the policemen.

On 28 July 2022, ISWAP militants in large numbers attacked soldiers at a checkpoint close to Zuma military barracks and engaged them in an armed clash in Zuba (Gwagwalada, FCT). Policemen were also to deployed to support the soldiers, the assailants were later repelled, at least 3 soldiers were killed and a number of other were wounded, other sources report one soldier and two of the assailants were killed, and two soldiers were wounded. ISWAP claimed responsibility for the attack.
On 28 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of persons from Dakwa in Bwari (FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 28 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed the traditional ruler of Yukuben chiefdom and his son who was also his driver when they were returning from Takum (Takum, Taraba). The victim's bodies were discovered in the bush at another community far from the attack scene, the police claimed to have arrested some suspects in connection with the attack.

On 28 July 2022, NDLEA operatives clashed with NURTW in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) after the operatives traced a vehicle suspected to be conveying consignment to Lagos motor park. The NURTW claimed the clash resulted from an attempt to resist the NDLEA after they wounded four persons, and prevent more injuries while the NDLEA claimed that four persons were wounded due to a conflict which resulted when the operative attempted to arrest a driver.

Around 29 July 2022 (between 25 - 31 July), a Zamfara militia abducted many residents including 29 women and children from about 16 communities including Ruwan-Rana and Ruwan-Jema in Bukkuyum LGA (Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. Two abductees from Ruwan-Rana were released on 30 July after providing 8 jerrycans of petrol and 5000 naira worth of phone recharge cards to the militia as ransom.
On 29 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and wounded three others in Garin Sambo village, Alkaleri LGA (Bauchi).

On 29 July 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted scores of civilians from Damari town, in Kazage ward coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The assailants rustled cattle, seized motorcycles and snatched money from traders, other sources report that at least 50 people were abducted and one pregnant woman died while fleeing the attack. Hundreds of residents fled the area.

On 29 July 2022, a local self defense militia engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash after the Kaduna militia abducted one woman and three of her children in Shika village (Giwa, Kaduna). The assailants fled and abandoned one of the abductees.

On 29 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia shot a man and wounded him, abducted his three year old nephew and a lecturer from their neighborhood in Offa Meta, coded to Ofe (Atiba, Oyo). The victims were released around 31 July after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 29 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a gold miner and his driver along Ilesa-Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded for the miner, the victims were released around 8 August after 20 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 29 July 2022, a Katsina militia abducted six persons from Tashan Buja in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees included a house wife and her child for whom the militia demanded for 6060 million naira ransom.

On 29 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a retired policeman who is the father of a journalist after they scaled the fence of his compound and shot him at close range in Okporo (Orlu, Imo). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 29 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia abducted two persons after shooting sporadically for 30 minutes in Aguamede community (Isi Uzo, Enugu). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 29 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two actors who were returning from a movie location in Ozalla town (Nkanu West, Enugu). A ransom of 100,000 dollars was demanded, the abductees were released on 3 August, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 30 July 2022, policemen and hunters clashed with an unidentified armed group at Damara Hills in Maiha LGA (Adamawa). Three members of the armed group were killed, others escaped with bullet wounds and four abductees were rescued.

On 30 July 2022, different local self defense militias engaged in armed clash with an unidentified armed group that invaded Bangalala community in Wase LGA (Plateau). 16 of the assailants and two defense militiamen were killed, other assailants escaped with injuries. Other sources report that the defense militia engaged the armed group who had taken control of the community for a while.

On 30 July 2022, an unidentified armed group on motorcycles attacked civilians, killed 3 to 4 persons and wounded others in Jauro Manu, coded to Garin Jauro Manu (Gassol, Taraba). Some other persons were abducted, the assailants raided shops, stole money and other valuables from traders. The Nigerian civil defense corps claimed 5 persons were killed, 6 wounded and scores were abducted.

On 30 July 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed policemen and a local defense militia who were responding to a distress call at Jidda-Basssa in Ajaokuta (Ajaokuta, Kogi). 3 policemen and 5 defense militiamen were killed.

On 30 July 2022, suspected IPOB militants abducted a policeman [presumed to be on duty], who was serving in Igbo Eze North divisional headquarters. Location coded to Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The corpse of the policeman was found in a shallow grave around 12 August.
On 30 July 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one abductee by throwing him and one other victim off a bridge in Alor (Idemili South, Anambra). The victims were abducted along Nnobi-Nnewi road.

Around 30 July 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia abducted 12 persons including a baby from Rungawa village in Talata Mafara LGA (Zamfara) and took them to the camp of Bello Maibille in Kare Kukanka forest. The abductees were rescued by police operatives and a local defense militia [no reports of a clash] without payment of ransom

On 30 July 2022, a suspected Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters along Sokoto-Shinkafi road (Sokoto North, Sokoto). One of the abductees is a student of the Sokoto state school of midwifery; a ransom of 30 million naira which was later reduced to 3 million was demanded for the release of the student.

On 30 July 2022, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye/ Eiye cult militias shot and killed a man at Osogun area, coded to Alapere (Kosofe, Lagos). The attack was a result of an ongoing clash between Eiye and Black Axe militias, two other person were killed on different days [coded separately], the police claimed only 2 persons were killed and some persons were abducted in connection with the attack.
On 30 July 2022, a Fulani militia killed one civilian when they attacked Aguamede community (Isi Uzo, Enugu). One house and a car were set ablaze by the militia.

On 31 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons from Rafin Ciyawa (Ningi, Bauchi). The abductees included a nursing mother, her baby and two others, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.

Around 31 July 2022 (as reported), the Kaduna state government claimed that Ansaru militants set up permanent operational bases and created parallel governments in some parts of the state. The militants have occupied large space of land, gone into farming and hired locals as free laborer's in Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Other sources report that the locals claim to prefer working as free labourers than to be murdered or abducted.
On 31 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a former member of the Anambra state house of assembly from his house at Ihiala (Ihiala, Anambra). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 31 July 2022, an unidentified armed group operating on motorcycles blocked the road and abducted 14 travelers at Benbel village along Mutum Biyu-Wukari road (Gassol, Taraba). The property of the travelers were stolen, one of the abductees was a truck driver whose family claimed that a ransom of 30 million naira was demanded for his release.

On 31 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted six travelers on the Ibillo-Ikiran-Ore road (Akoko Edo, Edo). Three of the abductees were rescued by the police and a local self defense militia [there are no reports of a clash].

On 31 July 2022, a suspected unidentified cult militia attacked a police patrol team and engaged the policemen in an armed clash at Banga camps coded to nearby Swali (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The assailants also detonated explosive devices, the attack was repelled, one policeman was killed, another policeman and a child were wounded, the assailants fled with bullet injuries and were pursued by the policemen.

On 31 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia numbering over 30 blocked the road and clashed with soldiers that responded to a distress call on the road between Leru junction and Ihube (Nneochi, Abia). Two soldiers were wounded, a military van was set ablaze and scores of commuters from three buses were abducted.
