On 31 July 2022, a Katsina militia numbering about 30 abducted two persons from Babbar Ruga community (Batagarawa, Katsina). One of the abductees escaped, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 31 July 2022, a Katsina militia killed two civilians and abducted 8 others when they attacked Kwarin Maikotso and Kore villages, coded to Katsina (Katsina). An unspecified number of animals were also rustled by the militia.
On 31 July 2022, ISWAP militants attacked and killed a retired soldier on his farm around Ngwom and Mafa (Mafa, Borno).

On 31 July 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians and killed seven persons in Chugwi (Jos South, Plateau). Several other persons were wounded, other sources report that 8 members of the same family were killed, gunshot wounds and machete cuts were inflicted on women and children.

On 31 July 2022, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye/ Eiye cult militias shot and killed a man outside of his wife's shop around Agboyi junction, Alapere (Kosofe, Lagos). The assailants used machetes to cut the victim's body after shooting him and then they fled the area. The attack was a result of an ongoing clash between Eiye and Black Axe militias, two other person were killed on different days [coded separately], the police claimed only 2 persons were killed and some persons were abducted in connection with the attack.

On 1 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 5 persons on a farm in Yumoa (Toto, Nassarawa). The abductees included a former director of research in the Nassarawa state ministry of education who owned the farm and four timber workers. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 August 2022, suspected IPOB militia attacked a police patrol team and engaged them in an armed clash at Ogbada quarters coded to Illah (Oshimili North, Delta). One of the militants was killed, the others fled with gunshot wounds, one rifle and six rounds of ammunition were recovered. The recovered rifle was stolen form policemen who were attacked previously [coded separately].

On 1 August 2022, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a woman on her farm at Fadahunsi area of Ilesa (Ilesha West, Osun). One of the victims eyes were removed, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 1 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted seven persons from Vinkilang community in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). Six of the abductees were released after 400 thousand naira was paid as ransom for each of them, the seventh abductee was murdered after a ransom of 500 thousand was paid [coded separately].

On 1 August 2022, suspected IPOB militants attacked civilians, killed seven persons and wounded others when they invaded Umuafom community in Orogwe (Owerri West, Imo). The attack was as a result of the arrest of a youth in the community by suspected Ebube Agu operatives. Other sources report that the victims were security guards and the building that was attacked was inhabited by Hausa migrants and civilians from Niger Republic. IPOB denied responsibility for the attack and claimed that security agencies are complict in attacks within the south east.

On 2 August 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed commuters and abducted 4 persons at Aloma junction in Otukpa (Ogbadibo, Benue). Security forces were deployed to the location to rescue the abductees, there are no further details.
On 2 August 2022, Boko Haram militants ambushed Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai in Firgi, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). Two soldiers were killed.

On 2 August 2022, a Fulani militia killed two persons whom they previously abducted [coded separately], shot and wounded the person who delivered the ransom around Igbon area of Ogbomosho-Ilorin expressway (Ogbomosho North, Oyo). The abductors killed the victims after receiving 5 million naira ransom and discovered that there were soldiers around the area.

On 2 August 2022, Nigerian troops and the Civilian JTF invaded a Boko Haram (JAS) camp and engaged the militants in an armed clash at Gazuwa village, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). One soldier and many militants were killed, the other militants fled. Many fatalities coded as 3.
On 2 August 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked the convoy of an assistant inspector general of police between Barde and Jagindi (Jema'a, Kaduna). The AIG was wounded and his orderly was killed.
On 2 August 2022, a local self defense militia clashed with Boko Haram militants who attacked and attempted to rustle cattle from Kuda village (Nganzai, Borno). Two militants were killed.

On 2 August 2022, a Niger militia clashed with security agents when they attacked civilians in Lanta and Makuna villages in Irina (Shiroro, Niger). The militia invaded the area in large numbers and operated till the following morning. Three civilians were killed, two others were wounded, one of the assailants was wounded and taken away on a motorcycle.

On 2 August 2022, a Fulani militia killed one person and abducted 2 other people in Manchok (Kaura, Kaduna). The assailants shot sporadically before abducting people; the abductees were the rector of the federal school of statistics, and the grand daughter of the murdered victim, they were released after 1 million naira was paid for the rector and 150 thousand naira was paid for the girl. The abductee claimed the assailants were young Fulani men.

On 2 August 2022, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye/ Eiye cult militias killed a commercial tricycle operator whom they trailed to where he went to eat in Agboyi area of Alapere (Kosofe, Lagos). The victim was shot in the head, before his body was cut machete, the assailants cut his hand and took it away. The attack was a result of an ongoing clash between Eiye and Black Axe militias. The assailants covered their faces with handkerchiefs and escaped, residents claim that the police arrested innocent persons in connection with the attack. Two other person were killed on different days [coded separately], the police claimed only 2 persons were killed and some persons were abducted in connection with the attack.

On 3 August 2022, a local self defense militia clashed with Boko Haram militants who invaded Kakari village, Gudumbali (Guzamala, Borno) on a reprisal attack. The militants attacked on 7 motorcycles and 9 of them were killed by the local militia using bow and arrows.

On 3 August 2022, Nigerian troops responded to a distress call and clashed with an unidentified armed group in Quan-Pan LGA (Plateau) coded to Baap. One of the assailants was killed while others escaped with gunshot wounds, one rifle, rounds of ammunition and other items were seized.

On 3 August 2022, Boko Haram (JAS) militants attacked and kill three farmers on their farms in Gujeri (Konduga, Borno). The assailants invaded the area from Gazuwa and demanded for food items from the victims and shot at them when they could not meet the demands. Two of the victims who survived the gunshots were cut and killed with cutlasses, one farmer escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 3 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three children from Kaduna estate in Ajaokuta steel complex (Ajaokuta, Kogi). The abductors invaded the area in their numbers and shot sporadically to scare neighbors and security agents from the area, a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.

On 3 August 2022, Nigerian army soldiers numbering over 30 beat up 2 policemen and killed one of them near the Ojo military cantonment (Ojo, Lagos). The soldiers road lane was stopped by the victims who were conducting traffic, they demanded to pass and were refused which resulted in the beating. Other sources report that the victims were taken to the barracks by the soldiers who later attempted to the corpse in a drainage before they were caught by authorities in charge of the barracks.

On 3 August 2022, a Katsina militia killed three civilians when they attacked Dantsauni village in Batagarawa LGA (Katsina). Dozens of people most of whom were women and children were abducted, hundreds fled toward the nearby Katsina city. The police claimed one person was killed and two others were wounded.
On 3 August 2022, a Katsina militia fired some shots along Katsina ring road near Katsina city (Katsina, Katsina). There are no further details.

On 3 August 2022, a Katsina militia who left their motorcycles at Dutsin Lema community abducted 15 persons from Natsinta community, coded to Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). 26 person were initially abducted, 15 persons who comprised of four women, two girls and seven men were taken away and the others were released.

On 3 August 2022, ISWAP militants abducted three civilians between Maiduguri and Gajiram (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The abductees included a medical doctor working with a humanitarian agency. The abductees escaped on 30 December 2022, when the militants were engaged in a clash with rival Boko Haram [JAS] fighters [coded separately].

Around 3 August 2022 (as reported), a policeman flogged a civilian with a cutlass in Cross River state, coded to Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The IGP ordered for the trial of the policeman.
On 3 August 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted a medical doctor on official duty along Nganzai-Monguno road (Monguno, Borno).
On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot at motorists at Lomara, coded to Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia). The victims' car was riddled with bullets and damaged, casualties are unknown.
On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman at Ime-Obi in Agbor (Ika South, Delta).

On 4 August 2022, a Kaduna militia adducted a sick woman after her husband who was their target escaped from their house in Kakeyi (Zaria, Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically while taking the abductee away, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a man whom they abducted alongside 6 other victims [coded separately] and took to the bush. The abductees were taken from Vinkilang community in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa); six of them were released, while the seventh one was shot in the back and killed after 500 thousand naira was paid as ransom and he had started walking way.
On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed abducted an pastor from his residence in Ufuma (Orumba North, Anambra). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 4 August 2022, a Fulani militia clashed with security agents around Ihube cashew plantation (Okigwe, Imo). The clash resulted in a stampede and at least one civilian was wounded.

On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a driver then abducted the occupants of the vehicle along Owo-Ikare road (Akoko North East, Ondo). The abductees included the traditional head of Iku quarters, an APC chieftain, a community leader and one other person. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded, the victims were released on 6 August, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 August 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants who attempted to attack a formation of the troops in Abbari Kasuwan, Shani LGA (Borno). Six militants and one soldier were killed, other militants fled with bullet wounds.

Around 4 August 2022 (between 28 July - 11 August), troops of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants along Uzoro-Gadamayo road. Coded to Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). One militant was killed, others fled, two rifles, ammunitions and a phone were recovered as claimed by the Defence Headquarters.

On 4 August 2022, an unidentified armed group in their numbers invaded the house of a police officer who engaged them in armed clash at Orogwe (Owerri West, Imo). The assailants fled and were chased by the police officer who killed two of them while the others fled with bullet wounds.
On 5 August 2022, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group along Chevron clinic road (Warri North, Delta) coded to Koko. One of the assailants was killed and weapons were recovered.

On 5 August 2022, suspected members of Black Axe militia also called Aiye shot and killed a member of Eiye cult militia [presumed to be unarmed] and his daughter at Ilesa garage area of Osogbo (Oshogbo, Osun). The daughter died at the hospital as a result of wounds she sustained in the attack, the victim was an ally of the Oshogbo NURTW chairman and his second in command.
On 5 August 2022, Boko Haram and ISWAP militants clashed at Gazuwa, coded to Bama which is 8km away (Bama, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 5 August 2022, ISWAP militants attacked policemen and expatriates in Ajaokuta (Ajaokuta, Kogi). Two policemen, two drivers and two expatriates were killed, three other expatriates were abducted. Other sources report that 5 persons were killed, the militants also claimed to have carried out the attack.

On 5 August 2022, a policeman shot and killed a man in Ede (Ede North, Osun), some sources report that the victim engaged in an altercation with the policeman and attempted to snatch his gun; others refuted the claim and reported that the victim asked why the policeman was trying to arrest his sister, the Osun state house of assembly minority leader was also reported to have ordered the shooting, he denied being in the area at the time of the incident.

On 5 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a woman who was a member of the PDP at Alapa area of Ede (Ede North, Osun) following a quarrel among members of the party. Other sources report that the APC claimed that the woman and one other victim [coded separately] were members of the APC and they were killed by assailants from other political parties.

On 5 August 2022, suspected IPOB militants invaded a police station and engaged policemen in an armed clash at Obudi-Agwa (Oguta, Imo). Two male police officers were shot and killed, two female officers were burnt to death, two suspects in detention were released, one civilian who was a commercial motorcyclist was shot and killed in his residence by the assailants who also burnt vehicles at the police station and a part of the building.

On 5 August 2022, presumed ISWAP or Boko Haram (JAS) militants abducted about fifty pastoralists in Yomongo, location coded as Ngawama (Abadan, Borno). The abducted were taken to Tcharikari (Bosso, Diffa) in Niger.

On 5 August 2022, Nigerian troops repelled and attack by large numbers ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The militants invaded the area in trucks, motorcycles and weapons with which they shot sporadically, scores of militants were killed while the others fled. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 6 August 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a man, wounded him and abducted his son along Itaji-Ijelu Ekiti (Oye, Ekiti). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 6 August 2022, an unidentified armed group in large numbers killed one Fulani pastoralist and abducted one other person when they invaded a Fulani settlement in Gwombe village (Kuje, FCT). The victim who was killed was shot when he attempted to flee.

On 6 August 2022, Nigerian troops in a joint operation with a local self defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group in Sabon Gari and regained Zurak and Yaddi villages which served as the group's base. Location coded to New Zurak (Wase, Plateau). 8 of the assailants were killed, the others fled and their base was burnt in the clash which lasted till the following day.

Around 6 August 2022 (as reported), suspected IPOB militants killed a policeman whom they abducted on 30 July. The victim's corpse was discovered in a shallow grave when policemen raided a forest in (Igbo Eze North, Enugu) coded to Enugu-Ezike.

Around 6 August 2022 (as reported), ISWAP ambushed and clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) who were on their way to rustle cattle from civilians at Jilli (Gubio, Borno). 8 Boko Haram fighters were killed, their weapons and motorcycles were seized by ISWAP fighters.
On 6 August 2022, a Nigerian navy personnel stabbed a civilian for stepping on his shoes in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The victim was seriously wounded.

On 6 August 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed Ebube Agu operatives and engaged them in an armed clash which lasted for two hours between Izombe and Agwa communities (Oguta, Imo). The Ebube Agu operatives abandoned their vehicle and fled, two of them were also captured.

On 7 August 2022, a Niger militia killed the FIRS coordinator in charge of Zamfara, Sokoto and Kebbi states at Saminaka community (Lapai, Niger). The vehicle in which the victim and three other were travelling in was shot at and he was hit by a stray bullet, three women from the community were abducted by the assailants and two tankers conveying petrol were hit by bullets which caused an explosion. Other sources report that one other FIRS staff was wounded.

On 7 August 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked residents, killed three persons and abducted several persons from Bali town (Bali, Taraba). The assailants invaded the area on motorcycles, shot sporadically one member of the Taraba marshall was one of the killed victims, two other persons were badly wounded.

On 7 August 2022, soldiers shot and killed a man at a checkpoint in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The victim was mistakenly shot by the soldiers who were trying to deflate another person's tyres.
On 7 August 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a So Safe Corps official and abducted a woman from a bar at Soyoye (Obafemi, Ogun).

On 7 August 2022, a Katsina militia clashed with a local self defense militia when they invaded civilians at Shola quarters in Katsina metropolis (Katsina, Katsina). Several residents including a newly married couple; two members of the local defense militia were killed, two others were wounded and the others retreated. Other sources report that one local defense militia man was killed, the assailants infiltrated the commuity the previous day and mingled with residents, security operatives arrived after the assailants had left.

On 7 August 2022, a Katsina militia shot and killed a man who resisted being abducted along Funtua road (Funtua, Katsina). The victim insisted that his family could not afford to pay ransom and preferred to be shot, at least ten other persons were abducted by the assailants.
On 7 August 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a convoy of civilian vehicles and shot at their cars along Owerri-Onitsha expressway (Onisha North, Anambra). There were no casualties.

On 7 August 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and repelled an attack on Bama town (Bama, Borno). The militants fled and were pursued by the troops, there are no further details.

On 7 August 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants armed and dressed in uniform abducted one person when they approached Gamboru market (Ngala, Borno). A ransom of 2 million naira was demanded, after the victim's family raised 1.5 million the abductors promised to release the victim.
On 7 August 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram and repelled an attack on Goniri (Gujba, Yobe). There are no further details.
On 7 August 2022, a Katsina militia killed the head of a local self defense militia in Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina).
On 8 August 2022, a Katsina militia abducted two women and two children and beat up one woman who attempted to escape in Kankia (Kankia, Katsina). There are reports about ransom demands.
On 8 August 2022, the IMN claimed that a combined team of security operatives shot, killed 6 members of the group who were on a procession in Zaria (Zaria, Kaduna) and wounded 40 others.

On 8 August 2022, policemen responded to a distress call and clashed with IPOB militants who invaded and razed the house of a local defense militia operative in Oduma (Aninri, Enugu). The police claimed to have recovered weapons from the assailants, casualties are unknown.

On 8 August 2022, two policemen engaged ISWAP militants who attacked a checkpoint at Auno (Konduga, Borno). One policeman was killed, a reinforcement of policemen repelled the attack and others sustained injuries while the militants fled.

On 8 August 2022, two unidentified cult militias celebrating the August 8 founders day clashed at Olunlade area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). Residents claimed that four persons were killed, while the police claimed two persons were killed. Some sources report that the assailants trailed a target to a gin bar, killed him and two others while others report two killed and two wounded.

On 8 August 2022, Nigerian troops on clearance operations clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at an iilegal market established by the militants at Dambia, also called Markas (Bama, Borno). Four militants were killed, others fled and four women suspected to be the wives of the militants were wounded and evacuated to the hospital for treatment.

On 9 August 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and shot at commuters at Okpara Inland (Ethiope East, Delta). The driver of the vehicle was wounded, while the passengers fled into the bush, the victims were returning from the train station which is at the outskirts of the community.

On 9 August 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering about five attacked police NIS officials who were on a patrol and engaged them in an armed clash along Galadi-Birniwa axis (Maigatari, Jigawa) and killed one official. Two others were wounded, the assailants fled to the forest in Niger Republic after the clash and left their motorcycles and a phone.

On 9 August 2022, a Sokoto militia wounded and abducted an unspecified number of residents from Damba (Illela, Sokoto) and Buwadi [coded separately]. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area.

On 9 August 2022, policemen and a local self defense militia foiled an attempt by an unidentified armed group to abduct the village head at Garun Babba (Garun Mallam, Kano). The assailants fled and left the victim, three of their motorcycles were recovered.

On 9 August 2022, a Kaduna militia killed one local self defense militia guard who was on patrol, wounded three people and abducted an unspecified number of others in Yakawada (Giwa, Kaduna). The abductees included the wife and children of the village head, two other nursing mothers and their babies.
On 9 August 2022, a Katsina militia attacked commuters along Katsina-Jibia road (Katsina, Katsina). Security operatives were deployed to the location, there are no further details.
On 9 August 2022, ISWAP militants clashed with Nigerian soldiers as they charged through two ambushes in Karetu (Mobbar, Borno). A few soldiers were wounded.

On 9 August 2022, a Sokoto militia killed 11 persons and wounded several others at Buwadi (Illela, Sokoto). Several others were also abducted from Damba [coded separately] when the assailants invaded the areas and shot sporadically.

On 9 August 2022, a man engaged an unidentified armed group who invaded his house in an armed clash and killed one of the assailants in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). Other members of the group broke into the house and killed the man.
On 10 August 2022, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of people from Birchi village (Kurfi, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 10 August 2022, an unidentified cult militia clashed with a local self defense militia during a reprisal attack in Ohwase (Udu, Delta). The attack was caused by the arrest of some cult militia members which was aided by the local defense militia, two defense militia members were killed.

On 10 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man on his farmland at Oduegbala, coded to nearby Ogume (Ndokwa West, Delta). The victim was shot several times, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 10 August 2022, ISWAP militants abducted the Bulama of Goni Kakari village (Magumeri, Borno) when they invaded the area.

On 10 August 2022, a Fulani militia carried out simultaneous attacks on civilians at Tse Ngojov and Tse Valem Yaweh communities in Tombo council ward (Logo, Benue). Six persons were killed and several others sustained gunshot and machete wounds. Other sources report that 12 persons were wounded, and the assailants invaded the area from Taraba state. The executive secretary of the state emergency management board said that 463 persons were displaced as a result of the attack.

On 10 August 2022, a policeman shot at an unmarked vehicle that had four policemen who were assumed to be off duty and one civilian along Obudi-Agwa/Ejemekuru road (Oguta, Imo). One of the victims was killed, the others were wounded; the offensive team mistook the victims to be an armed group on their way to attack a police station.

Around 10 August 2022 (as reported), suspected IPOB militants killed the Imo state commander of Ebube Agu Corps who is assumed to be off duty. The victim was found hiding in the forest before he was shot. Location coded to Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). IPOB denied involment in the attack adding that the victim was not a member of Ebube Agu and he was killed for refusing to join Ebube Agu Corps.

On 11 August 2022, a Zamfara militia led by the camp of Dogo Gudale who were estimated to be 200 conveyed on 100 motorcycles attacked civilians and killed three farmers in Tungar Wakaso village (Gummi, Zamfara) and Birnin Tudu [coded separately]. 17 others including 15 women and a chief imam were abducted in the attack which lasted for four hours which the intervention of security operatives.
Around 11 August 2022 (as reported), a presumed Niger Militia abducted a farmer from his farm in Gasakba (Abaji, FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 August 2022, a Niger militia ambushed a local self defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Gasakba (Abaji, FCT). The defense militia mobilized into the forest to rescue an abductee, two of them were killed and four others were wounded.

Around 11 August 2022 (as reported), policemen raided a camp of suspected IPOB who engaged them in an armed clash at a forest in Agu-Ibeje, Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). One of the suspected militants was killed, several others escaped with varying degrees of gunshots. The body of a policeman was exhumed from a shallow grave, several arms and ammunition and vehicles were recovered.

On 11 August 2022, an unidentified cult militia killed two members of a rival unidentified cult militia [presumed to be unarmed] in their appartement at Ogbogboro community, Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa).

On 11 August 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a commercial motorcyclist along Ilemeso/ Isan-Ekiti road (Oye, Ekiti). The attack resulted from the victim's refusal to carry the assailants to a forest, he escaped with gunshot wounds to Isan Ekiti where he died.

On 11 August 2022, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash when they invaded Mbala Divisional police headquarters at Isuochi (Nneochi, Abia). One policeman was who is the divisional crime officer at the station was abducted, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 11 August 2022, an unidentified armed group raped and killed a female student who they abducted while she was on her way to Ipara (Remo North, Ogun). The victim's phone was taken away by the assailants.
On 11 August 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 11 August 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted the DPO of Magami division who was presumed to be off duty, in Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). He was released on 16 August after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom by his family and friends, others sources reports that the state government claimed to have secured his release.

On 12 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest and a seminarian along Umunneochi-Ihube road, coded to Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia). A ransom of 50 million was demanded for the two abductees, who were released at a location not far from where they were abducted around 14 August. There are no reports about ransom payment.

On 12 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 38 persons who were travelling at Oronigbe community, coded to Igbanke (Orhionwon, Edo). The police rescued 33 of the abductees [no clash mentioned]. A ransom of 5 million was demanded for each abductees who were all female footballers, they were released on 17 August, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 12 August 2022, Nigerian troops foiled an ambush that was staged by ISWAP militants at Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). An unspecified number of soldiers were wounded.

On 12 August 2022, a Zamfara militia led by Bello Turji invaded the camps of rival militias and engaged them in an armed clash between Kaura Namoda and Maradun forest, coded to Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). Many militiamen were wounded, sheep and cattle belonging to the rival militia were stolen.
On 12 August 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted one civilian from Dalori community (Jere, Borno) and demanded for a ransom of 2 million naira.
On 13 August 2022, a Katsina militia abducted three women from Gora village (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 August 2022, an unidentified armed group in their numbers on motorcycles clashed with a local self defense militia when they attacked civilians in Garin Kuka (Gassol, Taraba) and Garin Gidado [coded separately]. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area, wounded several others and abducted an unspecified number. Other sources report that at least 6 local militiamen and 6 assailants were killed.

On 13 August 2022, an unidentified armed group in their numbers on motorcycles attacked civilians and killed no fewer than 16 people in Garin Gidado (Gassol, Taraba) and Garin Kuka were they clashed with a local defense militia[coded separately]. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area, wounded several others and abducted an unspecified number. Some sources report that the community was empty when the assailants arrived from Garin Kuka where at least 12 persons were killed, fatalities coded as 4.
On 13 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civilian in front of his house in Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). The victim was a tanker driver, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 13 August 2022, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of passengers when they ambushed passengers in two commercial buses near Kurmayai village (Batsari, Katsina). There are reports about ransom demands.

On 13 August 2022, soldiers and policemen clashed and exchanged gunshots at Ajegunle area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) following a disagreement over right of way. The soldiers and the policeman who later called a police station were dressed in mufti, three other personnel also joined the soldiers.

On 13 August 2022, soldiers beat up a trailer driver and his conductor who were heading towards Gwagwalada from Zuba (Gwagwalada, FCT) and forced them to lay in muddy water for driving against traffic. The victims fled and the soldiers punctured the 12 tires of the trailer.
On 13 August 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with security operatives, presumed to be policemen at Ukpo-Akpu axis (Dunukofia, Anambra). There are no further details.

On 13 August 2022, a local defense militia tortured and killed a wheel barrow pusher who was reported to them by a trader over missing goods in Suleja market (Suleja, Niger). The members of the militia unit were arrested by the police.
On 13 August 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted a woman her two children from their residence in Yarima quarters, Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 August 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted a man from his farm in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Kaduna). A ransom of 5 million was demanded, the family offered 3 million which the abductors rejected and asked the family to pick up his corpse. The attack is coded separately

On 13 August 2022, Nigerian troops during a clearance operation intercepted and clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at Ngwom (Mafa, Borno). The militants were enroute to rustle cattle from pastoralists in the general area, three militants were killed.

On 13 August 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Forest Sanity supported by Nigerian Air Force carried out a clearance operation against a Kaduna militia in Galibi area (Chikun, Kaduna). Scores of militiamen were killed; coded as 20, two GPMG, three rifles and seven motorcycles were recovered in the offensive which included land and air operations.
On 13 August 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with security operatives, presumed to be policemen at Ezinifite axis, Aguata LGA (Anambra). There are no further details.

On 14 August 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a catechist from a catholic church which they invaded in Dinya, Gassol LGA (Taraba). The abductors shot sporadically and hit objects on the door of the parish priest before taking the abductee. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 14 August 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a man who was returning from church in Borno-Kurku, Bali LGA (Taraba). The victim was rescued and taken to the hospital.

Around 14 August 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed one civilian who they shot at his residence in Rundele (Emohua, Rivers). The militants detonated an IED which destroyed some shops in the market, two militants were killed in the clash, the troops recovered rocket launchers and several IEDs that were planted along the road as claimed by the Nigerian Army. Other sources report that the troops attacked and killed three civilians instead of a clash with militants.
On 31 August 2022, an armed group of suspected PDP loyalists attacked members of Labor Party at Nenwe (Aninri, Enugu). There are no further details.

On 31 August 2022, a Katsina militia ambushed soldiers who were escorting a group of locals at Shimfida (Jibia, Katsina). The assailants detonated an IED on an armored personnel carrier; two soldiers were killed, four others were wounded and one was missing, other sources report that 4 civilians were also killed, the assailants fled after the soldiers returned fire and engaged them in a clash.

Around 31 August 2022 (as reported), an official of NSCDC punched a man on the face after the man stopped him from taking money from his car at Iloro (Ijero, Ekiti). The man sustained an injury on his lip as a result of the punch.

On 31 August 2022, an unidentified armed group beat up a man, wounded him and abducted his daughter from their residence in Ikot Ansa (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 September 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering at least 100 and mounted on motorcycles attacked civilians in Lambar Agwad community in Jega LGA (Kebbi). Four people were killed and an unspecified number of others were abducted.
On 1 September 2022, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Farin-Ruwa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed while the others withdrew and fled.

On 1 September 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians when they blocked the Birnin Gwari-Funtua highway (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and trapped several vehicles. One driver was killed and scores of travelers were abducted, the assailants asked the vehicle owners to pay between N300,000 to 1 million naira to retrieve their vehicle.
On 1 September 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one soldier and set an operational vehicle ablaze when they attacked soldiers at a checkpoint in Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu).

Around 1 September 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a director in the Ondo state teaching service commission in Akure (Akure South, Ondo). The mutilated body of the victim was found without his head and intestines and with a hole in his chest; he had been declared missing on 1 September and his body was discovered on 4 September.

Around 1 September 2022 (between 1 - 2 September), soldiers in collaboration with a local self defense militia and volunteers clashed with ISWAP/Boko Haram militants at Gabchari, Sheruri and Mantari , coded to Bama (Bama, Borno) and Malam Masari [coded separately]. The fleeing militants were bombed by the air force in an offensive which lasted for over 48 hours, over 200 militants were killed including some high ranking commanders and 70 others who were fleeing drowned. 200 fatalities split across two events coded as 100.

Around 1 September 2022, (between 1 - 2 September), soldiers in collaboration with a local self defense militia and volunteers clashed with ISWAP/Boko Haram militants at Malam Masari (Bama, Borno), Gabchari, Sheruri and Mantari [coded separately]. The fleeing militants were bombed by the air force in an offensive which lasted for over 48 hours, over 200 militants were killed including some high ranking commanders and 70 others who were fleeing drowned. 200 fatalities split across two events coded as 100.

On 1 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked residents and killed 6 persons at Umella village in Mbawa ward (Guma, Benue). The assailants invaded the area and shot sporadically, the corpses were recovered after they left and one corpse was macheted while two other persons were wounded.

On 2 September 2022, pirates attacked a military gunboat at a checkpoint and clashed with soldiers after they attacked a passenger boat along the Bille waterways (Degema, Rivers). One civilian and two soldiers were killed, one other person was rescued and one was wounded according to the police. Other sources report an unspecified number of civilians were killed and wounded in the attack and the soldiers' weapons were stolen.

On 2 September 2022, a Zamfara militia shot and wounded one person who attempted to escape being abducted at a mosque in Zugu community (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). 44 persons were abducted by the assailants who invaded the mosque before the Jumaat prayers began and operated for over one hour. Other sources reported that the abductees were subjected to physical labor on the millet and sorghum plantation of the abductors. 43 of the abductees were released on 6 September after 5 million naira and other items were paid as ransom, one abductee died as a result of torture [coded separately].

On 2 September 2022, a Katsina militia in large numbers abducted four civilians when they invaded Dutsen Reme in Bakori LGA (Katsina). The abductees included one student, a staff of High Court Funtua and a woman whose husband fled and her stepdaughter. The assailants had requested for the wives of the abductees and took the men away when they did not see the women. There are no reports about ransom payment.

On 2 September 2022, an NSCDC operative beat up a woman at Abbatoir area, coded to Bukuru (Jos South, Plateau) following a disagreement over parking lot. The operative and his colleague were both armed which made onlookers scared to intervene.

On 2 September 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants numbering about 20 attacked worshippers at a mosque in Ngulde (Askira Uba, Borno). The chief imam of Gima and three others were killed; one of the victims sustained injuries and died in the hospital (total of 5 fatalities), livestock and foodstuff were looted from the community, and two vehicles were set ablaze.
On 3 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians and killed three persons in their homes at Tse Numgbera, coded to Gbajimba (Guma, Benue).
On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group killed an off-duty soldier after they ambushed a commercial bus. The soldier was on his way to Zuru (Zuru, Kebbi) to visit his parents.

On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted between 11 to 40 commuters at Ifon (Ose, Ondo) while they were on their way to Benin from Akure. One of the abductees was rescued by the police and soldiers [no clash reported], a ransom of between 3 to 10 million naira was demanded for each of the victims.

On 3 September 2022, two unidentified rival cult groups were engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Gboko town (Gboko, Benue). Three persons were killed and some others sustained varying degrees of injuries, security agents intervened and brought the situation under control. 3 fatalities split across two events coded as 2. The police claimed that 30 persons were arrested in connection with the clash.

On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one a drivers and abducted 8 travelers along Emohua-Kalabari road (Emohua, Rivers). The assailants shot at the vehicle conveying the abductees who were going to Kalabari from Port Harcourt, one of the abductees was released after a ransom of 150 thousand naira was paid.
On 3 September 2022, a Kaduna militia killed one person and looted several shops when they attacked civilians at Damari in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna).

On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one and abducted 13 farmers from Gasakba (Abaji, FCT). 12 of the abductees were released, one was later killed [coded separately] after 8 million naira, two bags of rice, wine and drugs were provided as ransom.

On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group beat up a school principal who resisted being abducted when they invaded his compound Udianga Enem, coded to Utu Etim Ekpo (Etim Ekpo, Akwa Ibom). The victim was abducted, his SUV and motorcycle were also taken away after the attack which lasted for about two hours. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded, the abductee was released on 18 September after 4.2 million naira was paid.

On 3 September 2022, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Sabon Birni (Igabi, Kaduna), Dogon Dawa-Kuyelo and Farin Ruwa [coded separately]. Three militiamen were killed, two rifles, nine magazines, seven Boafeng communication radio and other items were recovered by the troops. 3 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 3 September 2022, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Dogon Dawa-Kuyelo coded to Sabon Kuyelo, (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) Sabon Birni and Farin Ruwa [coded separately]. Three militiamen were killed, two rifles, nine magazines, seven Boafeng communication radio and other items were recovered by the troops. 3 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 3 September 2022, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Farin-Ruwa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), Dogon Dawa-Kuyelo and Sabon Birni [coded separately]. Three militiamen were killed, two rifles, nine magazines, seven Boafeng communication radio and other items were recovered by the troops. 3 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 3 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an NSCDC operative [presumed to be off-duty] and abducted three persons from the vehicle they were traveling in one the Oke Ako- Irele road (Ikole, Ekiti). The assailants shot at the vehicle during the attack, a ransom of 30 million naira has been demanded for the abductees' release. The abductees were released after 5 million naira and 100 thousand naira worth of recharge cards were provided, the police denied any ransom payment and claimed to have rescued them.

On 3 September 2022, policemen clashed with a Katsina militia who abducted three people in Katsina metropolis (Katsina, Katsina). One of the abductees was the candidate for the Kankia zone state house of assembly from the PDP, his wife and the registrar of Isa Kaita college of education. The two men were rescued by the police.

On 4 September 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted a man from Barde village in Ikara LGA (Kaduna). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded; the victim was rescued around 12 September by policemen on a patrol after the abductors abandoned him and fled when they sighted the policemen.

On 4 September 2022, an armed group suspected to be loyal to the PDP shot sporadically at the venue of a Labor Party meeting in Awgu (Agwu, Enugu). The meeting was disrupted; chairs and canopies were destroyed, the members fled, some of them were wounded and the windshield of one person's car was shattered.

On 4 September 2022, policemen engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Juga village in Kankia LGA (Katsina) after the assailants abducted a man from his residence. The abductee was rescued, two of the assailants were killed and one of their motorcycles was recovered.

On 4 September 2022, two unidentified rival cult groups were engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Gboko town (Gboko, Benue). Three persons were killed and some others sustained varying degrees of injuries, security agents intervened and brought the situation under control. 3 fatalities split across two events coded as 1. The police claimed that 30 persons were arrested in connection with the clash.

On 4 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a Muslim cleric at his residence in Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The victim died the following day after he was shot, the reason for the attack is unknown. IPOB denied responsibility for the attack and accused security agencies of stage managing confessions from criminals to indict them.

Around 4 September 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia tortured and killed a civilian who was abducted from a mosque in Zugu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abduction was coded separately, the other abductees were released.
On 4 September 2022, a Katsina militia killed one man after a failed attempt to steal his motorcycle at Unguwar Katoge quarters in Batsari town (Batsari, Katsina).
On 4 September 2022, a Katsina militia shot at motorists and killed one person near Tsabawa village in Batsari LGA (Katsina). An unspecified number of people were abducted and wounded.
On 4 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted around 11 bus passengers at Ganmo area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 September 2022, a presumed faction of Igbide communal militia killed one person and wounded the vice president of a faction of the community at Igbide (Isoko South, Delta). The two victims were driving together when they were shot by the assailants, soldiers were deployed to the area to restore calm.
On 5 September 2022, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians when they blocked the Birnin Gwari-Funtua road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). An unspecified number of others were abducted.

Around 5 September 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted a man who was sent to deliver the ransom that was demanded for the release of a police DPO that was previously abducted [coded separately] around Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a traditional ruler from his palace in Pinau (Wase, Plateau). Other sources report that the traditional ruler and his driver were abducted while on their way to Wase town, they were rescued by soldiers who clashed with the abductees [coded separately].

On 5 September 2022, troops of Operation Safe Haven clashed with an unidentified armed group and rescued the traditional ruler of Pinau and his driver who were earlier abducted [coded separately]. Two guns and three motorcycles were recovered by the troops, location coded to Pinau (Wase, Plateau) where the abductees were taken from.

On 5 September 2022, suspected soldiers of the Nigerian army attacked civilians in Tuoma community, coded to nearby Bille (Degema, Rivers), used machetes to break into houses and attempted to arrest some residents after they clashed with pirates at Bille as a result of which two soldiers died [coded separately].

On 5 September 2022, a local defense militia foiled an attack on civilians by a suspected Fulani militia that was disguised in military uniform at Isuochi (Nneochi, Abia). An unspecified number of the passengers sustained bullet wounds, there were no fatalities and the assailants fled after they were overpowered.
Around 5 September 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed one of the farmers whom they abducted from Kuntunku and Gasakpa communities in Gurdi ward (Abaji, FCT) [coded separately].

Around 5 September 2022, policemen who were part of the Green Sheriff beat up a petty trader and her daughter in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The daughter who was accused of attempting to attack the policemen with a knife, was arrested and released on 6 September, the woman's wares were scattered on the road and she claimed the policemen took away 250,000 naira from her. The policemen claimed that the women had been warned severally to not sell along the roadside.
On 5 September 2022, a Zamfara militia attacked a motorcycle rider, wounded him and stole his motorcycle at Malamai village, Maradun LGA (Zamfara).
On 6 September 2022, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed in Jibowu area (Ifako, Lagos). Policemen were deployed to the area, normalcy was restored and one person was arrested.

On 6 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot an policeman who was off duty and traveling in a commercial bus with civilians around Orsu-Nkwerre-Orsu (Orlu, Imo). The victim who was enroute to Lagos on an official trip was shot in his hand and leg when the assailants found his ID card, the bus was ordered to leave without him and his whereabouts are unknown.

On 6 September 2022, a Katsina militia ambushed soldiers on patrol and engaged them in an armed clash in Kaiga (Dan-Musa, Katsina). Two soldiers were killed, and unspecified number of others were wounded.

On 6 September 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians when they invaded Katun Gida in Idon (Kajuru, Kaduna) and shot sporadically. Two persons who were siblings were killed, 13 others were abducted; three of whom escaped, one other man was released by the abductors to tend to his sick wife.

On 6 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians and killed many people [coded as 3] in Kukawa, Gyanbahu, Dungur and Keram, coded to Dengi (Kanam, Plateau). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area; many other persons were wounded, houses were set ablaze and hundred fled their homes.

On 6 September 2022, suspected soldiers of the Nigerian army attacked civilians in Bille (Degema, Rivers), beat up and arrested some residents after they clashed with pirates in the area as a result of which two soldiers died [coded separately].

On 6 September 2022, ISWAP fighters occupying Cingori and Yuwe shot at Boko Haram militants who sought refuge at Cina village in Bama LGA (Borno). The Boko Haram militants were fleeing from a military bombardment [coded separately] and the ISWAP fighters stopped shooting at the Boko Haram fighters when they noticed that there were women and children in their midst, they were allowed to pass including an unspecified number of wounded fighters.

On 6 September 2022, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with soldiers at a checkpoint in Monguno (Monguno, Borno) and killed four soldiers while others were wounded. Other sources report that no soldiers were killed, one militant was killed and their gun truck was seized by the soldiers.
On 6 September 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP militants at Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). There are no further details.
On 6 September 2022, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and stole his motorcycle when they attacked Kwantarawa village in Maradun LGA (Zamfara).

Around 7 September 2022 (as reported), soldiers and mobile policemen clashed with a Kaduna militia after they invaded their hideouts in Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), Rijana and Niger state [coded separately]. The security agents were led to the hideouts by volunteers, over 30 militiamen were killed and 15 informants were arrested. 30 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 10.

Around 7 September 2022 (as reported), soldiers and mobile policemen clashed with a Kaduna militia after they invaded their hideouts in Rijana (Kachia, Kaduna), Birnin Gwari and Niger state [coded separately]. The security agents were led to the hideouts by volunteers, over 30 militiamen were killed and 15 informants were arrested. 30 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 10.

Around 7 September 2022 (as reported), soldiers and mobile policemen clashed with a Kaduna militia after they invaded their hideouts in Kagara (Rafi, Niger) and Kaduna state [coded separately]. The security agents were led to the hideouts by volunteers, over 30 militiamen were killed and 15 informants were arrested. 30 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 10.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the chairman of Kanke LGA from his residence in Kwang (Quan-Pan, Plateau). The abductors shot sporadically to scare away other residents before abducting the victim. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering up to four abducted a woman at the entrance of her residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded, the abductors threatened to increase the amount if it is not paid by 11 September.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the former chairman of Alieru LGA together with his wife from their residence in Aliero town (Alieru, Kebbi). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons when they intercepted a hearse around Umunneochi-Ihube-Okigwe axis, coded to Isuochi (Nneochi, Abia). One of the abductees escaped, there are no reports about ransom demands for the other two persons.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash at New Haven area (Enugu North, Enugu). Three policemen were killed and one was declared missing, they were on their way back to the police station when they assailants attacked them. Other sources report that two civilians were killed, the weapons of the policemen were stolen and one person was abducted.

On 7 September 2022, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a military checkpoint and caused the withdrawal of soldiers at Bama (Bama, Borno). Other sources report that the militants were repelled when they attempted to infiltrate the location. Casualties are unknown.

On 7 September 2022, Nigerian troops ambushed a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash around Fondisho area in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed and others escaped with bullet wounds.
On 7 September 2022, a Sokoto militia conducted a house to house search and abducted 11 persons from Gurami (Tangaza, Sokoto). The abductors also stole valuables.

On 7 September 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed and abducted seven civilians at Nrobo (Uzo Uwani, Enugu) while they were traveling from Nsukka to Abbi. The abductees were released on 9 September after a ransom of 500 thousand naira was paid, the initial ransom demand was 30 million naira which was later reduced.

On 8 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Ofeapo, coded to Bugana (Omala, Kogi), killed four persons and wounded two others. The dead victims consist of two females and two males.
On 8 September 2022, a Katsina militia shot indiscriminately at residents in Yar Santa village in Kankara LGA (Katsina). Houses and properties were set ablaze and casualties are unknown.
On 8 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Eika-Ohizenyi police station in Okehi LGA (Kogi) coded to Obangede and killed one person before the attack was repelled.
On 9 September 2022, Ebube Agu operatives shot and killed a civilian in Orlu (Orlu, Imo). The victim was killed over an accident scar on his shoulder.
On 9 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians and killed three persons in Yogbo community (Guma, Benue). Two of the victims were women.

On 9 September 2022, policemen on patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia along Zaria-Kano expressway (Zaria, Kaduna) and rescued two female abductees while the militiamen abandoned the vehicle they were in and fled with varying degrees of bullet wounds. A gun loaded with 30 live rounds of ammunition was recovered.

On 9 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the wife of an operative of Enugu state neighbourhood watch when they invaded their residence in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The assailants were in search of the victim's husband who fled earlier.

On 9 September 2022, soldiers attached to the pipeline surveillance team of Nigerian Agip Oil Company attacked civilians, killed two people and burnt three houses when they invaded Okobe community (Ahoada West, Rivers). Ten other persons were arrested, the cause of the attack is unknown while some sources report oil companies and security agencies in the area had previously accused residents of engaging in oil theft.

On 9 September 2022, the air component of operation Hadarin Daji carried out airstrikes using bombs, rockets and cannons and dislodged a Katsina militia led by Babaru that had occupied Gidan Guga village in Faskari LGA (Katsina). Babaru was killed in the airstrike.

On 9 September 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP militants at Waijroko (Damboa, Borno). The militants invaded the area on 40 motorcycles and shot sporadically, two of them were killed, four were wounded while the others were forced to withdraw in two groups towards Kilgori and Yagiwa.

On 9 September 2022, ISWAP militants attacked a refugee camp and were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers in Banki (Bama, Borno). Two militants were killed, the soldiers did not record any fatalities; the militants claimed to have attacked a military checkpoint, killed one, caused the withdrawal of the rest and seized ammunition and other items.

On 9 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditonal ruler of Umudi community from the front of his office at Tetlow road in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The abductors demanded for a ransom of 200 million naira which was later reduced to 12 million, the victim escaped from the abductors hideout on 13 September.

On 10 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the brother of the PDP governorship aspirant when they attacked Rin community, coded to Baap (Quan-Pan, Plateau). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded by the abductors.

On 10 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians and killed one person in Ukohol community coded to Gbajimba (Guma, Benue). Several houses were set ablaze by the assailants, other locals fled the area.
On 10 September 2022, a Niger militia killed at least one person when they attacked Kpada and Yabo communities (Lapai, Niger). Several other residents fled the area.
On 10 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civilian at Eyoabasi in Oron LGA (Akwa Ibom). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 10 September 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted an aid worker from his residence in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 10 September 2022, ISWAP militants claimed an attack on a police checkpoint at Garingada in Geidam LGA (Yobe). One policeman who was attached to a border patrol was killed.

On 10 September 2022, a private security guard shot an killed a man at Ibuowo estate in Okinni (Egbedore, Osun). The reason for the attack is unknown, the police claimed to have arrested 3 private security men in connection with the attack.

On 10 September 2022, soldiers and policemen shot sporadically while dispersing civilians who gathered at the palace of a rival traditional ruler to celebrate new yam festival in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Five persons were wounded as a result of a stampede which occurred, teargas was fied at the person who initially refused to leave the venue which they sealed.

On 10 September 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia at Tollgate area and Sabon Gida (Chikun, Kaduna). Many militiamen were killed, coded as 10; a militia commander Boderi Ishaya escaped, while another leader called Musti was killed, other sources report scores of fatalities as claimed by the Kaduna state government.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers when the assailants invaded the road around the Obosi end of the 2nd Niger bridge (Idemili South, Anambra). There are no further details.

On 11 September 2022, Nigerian troops ambushed and clashed with Boko Haram militants at the Kasuwan Daula axis, killed 7 and repelled an attempted reprisal by the militants who were heading to Bama town (Bama, Borno). The militants fled from the secon clash.

On 11 September 2022, policemen on a routine ambush operation clashed with an unidentified armed group at Ughiole forest, coded to nearby Aviele (Etsako West, Edo). One of the assailants was killed, others fled with bullet wounds; one gun, amulets, charms and 240,000 naira were recovered.

On 11 September 2022, policemen who repsonded to a distress call were engaged in an armed clash by Eiye confraternity at Gbokoto (Egbado North, Ogun). The assailants who had attempetd to kill the traditional ruler over a misunderstanding he had with his wife were contracted by the ruler's son. Six of the assailants were arrested, one locally made gun, two live and one expended catridge were recovered.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the vice chairman of Isoko North LGA who is also a PDP chieftain from Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta) while he was returning home from a night club. A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded; other sources report that he was abducted in Ogor town when he was enroute to Patani. The abductee was released on 14 September after 7 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group armed with cutlasses and knives attacked residents, stabbed two persons robbed others in Ikwa (Gwagwalada, FCT). The victims tried to prevent the assailants from robbing members of their household which led to their stabbing.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one civilian when they invaded Tekpeshe community, coded to Gurdi ward (Abaji, FCT). The former ward councilor, six of his family members and eleven others including the son of the village chief were abducted by the assailants. The former councilor and four others were released on 12 September and given a motorcycle to go and source for 8 million naira and food stuff as ransom. The abductees except the son of the village chief were released after over 5 million naira was paid as ransom, an additional 8 million was demanded for the remaining abductee who was released on 4 October after a solar panel, drugs and foodstuff worth 436,700 was given as ransom.

On 11 September 2022, Civilian JTF operatives clashed with a Katsina militia that invaded Batsari town (Batsari, Katsina) on 10 motorcycles. Nine of the assailants were killed, five were arrested, nine of their motorcycles were seized while one escaped.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Kunga A community. Coded to nearby Jos (Jos North, Plateau) and wounded two persons before the police prevented them the abduction of any persons [means not stated]. Sources report that the policemen responded to the distress call late.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civilian at the Oruku market square (Nkanu East, Enugu). Some sources report that the attack was connected to a communal conflict, and the assailants were working for some persons involved in the conflict.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of a senator at Enugu-Ukwu (Njikoka, Anambra) and killed between 5 to 7 persons. The fatalities included the senator's aides and security aides, the senator escaped unhurt; the police claimed two policemen were wounded, two others and three civilians were killed.

On 11 September 2022, an unidentified armed group forcefully entered the residence of a pastor, shot his wife in the leg, abducted him and one other person from Ganawuri community, coded to Ganawuri Hills (Riyom, Plateau) when they invaded they area and shot sporadically for several hours. The second abductee was a school principal who was rescued by a local defense militia [no clash was reported], a ransom of 20 million was demanded for the pastor's release.
On 12 September 2022, Nigerian troops on clearance patrols clashed with a Kaduna militia around Kangon Kadi, coded to Damba (Chikun, Kaduna) and rescued 6 abductees. The militiamen fled.

On 12 September 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted six persons from Unguwan Fada in Kasuwan Magani (Kajuru, Kaduna) during a night raid. About 40 others were abducted the following day [coded separately] a ransom of 200 million naira was demanded for 45 abductees from the two events according to SOKAPU.

Around 13 September 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Apewohe (Chikun, Kaduna) an extended to Dakwala and Kunai hills. An unspecified number of militiamen were killed, coded as 3.

On 13 September 2022, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who responded to a distress call in an armed clash after the assailants abducted a baby from Achigbor community, coded to Ehor (Uhunmwode, Edo). Three of the assailants were killed, three others fled, the baby was rescued, one gun, a cutlass and an axe were recovered by the policemen.

On 13 September 2022, an unidentified armed group wounded an APC party candidate in the forthcoming election and abducted his wife and child from their residence in Shao (Moro, Kwara). The man escaped abduction; an unspecified amount was paid as ransom, policemen rescued the victims while the abductors were sharing the ransom [coded separately].

On 13 September 2022, policemen on a patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia that they intercepted at Galadimawa district (Giwa, Kaduna). The militiamen fled and left two abductees behind who were rescued by the policemen.

Around 13 September 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Daban Lawal Kwalba and Rafin Gwaska in Igabi (Kaduna) and cleared out the hideout of the militia. 10 abductees were rescued, and the militiamen fled in the first location while guns, ammunition, military uniforms and other items were recovered from the second location.

On 13 September 2022, a Kaduna militia invaded a church and abducted about more than 60 people including children and old people at Bayan Kasuwa quarters, another six people were abducted from Janwuriya village, a few kilometers from Kasuwan Magani (Kajuru, Kaduna). The abductors abducted six people the previous day [coded separately] and demanded for a ransom of 200 million naira for abductees from the two events whom they claimed were 40 while 5 persons were declared missing according to SOKAPU.

On 14 September 2022, a Katsina militia attacked residents at Bakiyawa community (Batagarawa, Katsina), killed one person, injured four others and abducted an unspecified number of people, other sources report that between 43 to 50 people were abducted. The assailants also rustled many animals. A ransom of 250 million naira was demanded for the 43 abductees
On 14 September 2022, a Niger militia abducted five civilians when they raided Angwan Dajin Gomna in Kpada (Lapai, Niger). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 14 September 2022, a Niger militia abducted five civilians when they raided Zago and Lafiyan Zago (Agaie, Niger). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 14 September 2022, policemen in collaboration with a local self defense militia and local hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash. The group had abducted two persons the previous day from Shao (Moro, Kwara) [coded separately] and were sharing the ransom that was paid. Two of the abductors were killed, the others fled, one car, a gun and an unspecified amount of money were recovered by the operatives.

On 14 September 2022, policemen clashed with a Katsina militia who were not fewer than 30 that attempted to rob civilians and blocked the Sabuwa-Mararabar Yakawada road (Sabuwa, Katsina). One of the assailants was killed, one rifle and four motorcycles were recovered from the scene by policemen.

On 14 September 2022, scores of a Niger militia attacked the office of a local defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Ebbo (Lapai, Niger). One local defense militiaman was killed, another was wounded and the attack was repelled.

Around 15 September 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians when they invaded Birnin Tudu (Gummi, Zamfara). A ransom of 9 million naira and a motorcycle was demanded, the abductees were released after the demands were met.

On 15 September 2022, officials of Yakurr LGA task force beat up a civilian and caused him some burns on his body in Ugep (Yakurr, Cross River) following the victim's refusal to hand over his car keys to the officials who were dressed in mufti. The assailants fled after the victim was wounded.

On 15 September 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted three civilians from farms in Kurgin Gabas community, Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). Other sources report that five persons were abducted, the abductees escaped around 30 September.
On 15 September 2022, Nigeria Customs operatives who were pursuing suspected smugglers shot and wounded a driver at Garki motor park (Garki, Jigawa). The victim was a member of NURTW.

On 15 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked policemen at a checkpoint and engaged them in an armed clash at the boundary between Agba and Ndiagu Ogboji (Ezza North, Ebonyi). Two policemen were killed, others sustained injuries and one operational vehicle was set ablaze. The police claimed that no policeman was killed.

On 15 September 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded the home of a senior special assistant to the Bauchi state governor in Bauchi (Bauchi, Bauchi). One person was injured, the assailants fled when policemen arrived and three empty shell of ammunition were recovered.

On 15 September 2022, ISWAP fighters clashed with Boko Haram fighters led by Kundu who were on a robbery mission between Dikwa and Bama (Dikwa, Borno). 8 militants from the both sided were killed, the Boko Haram fighters fled and left their motorcycles.
On 15 September 2022, ISWAP invaded a camp of rival Boko Haram and engaged them in an armed clash between Bama and Konduga (Bama, Borno). At least 23 Boko Haram fighters were killed.

On 15 September 2022, a task force comprised of soldiers and policemen clashed with local hunters that attacked them and attempted to prevent the seizure of commercial motorcycles at Sabon Lugbe, coded to Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Four suspected hunters were arrested, two weapons and 72 motorcycles were seized.
On 15 September 2022, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a student in Yabatech, Yaba (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 16 September 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed an operative of Ebube Agu Corps at his duty post in Mkpuma Ekwa-Oku, coded to Izi (Izzi, Ebonyi).
On 16 September 2022, a Kaduna militia killed a farmer and snatched his motorcycle at Kurgin Gabas community in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna).

On 16 September 2022, an Ogbe-Ijoh militia were repelled by an Aladja militia when they attempted to invade Aladja community (Warri South, Delta). Two persons were killed before the arrival of soldiers, other sources report that there were no casualties, and the Ogbe-Ijoh militia shot indiscriminately and left, the police claimed that one person was killed. The clash was over a boundary dispute.
On 16 September 2022, an unidentified armed group wounded an unspecified number of persons and abducted two others in Rumde Alkali, coded to Tongare (Yola-South, Adamawa).

On 16 September 2022, ISWAP fighters led by Ba'ana Chigori attacked the camp of rival Boko Haram fighters and engaged them in an armed clash in Malam Masari (Bama, Borno) as known as Gabchari, Gaizuwa and Mantari. 29 Boko Haram fighters including a top commander were killed, the surviving militants fled, ISWAP spared women and children.

On 16 September 2022, soldiers and Ebube Agu operatives attacked civilians when they invaded Awo-Idemili and Eziawa (Orsu, Imo), Orsu Ihiteukwu communities [coded separately]. At least one person was killed, several houses and business premises were destroyed, as claimed by IPOB. The chief press secretary of the state governor denied claims, the governor claimed that materials used in the manufacture of explosives were found in some of the shops which led security agents to set them ablaze.

On 16 September 2022, soldiers and Ebube Agu operatives attacked civilians when they invaded Orsu Ihiteukwa (Orsu, Imo), Awo Idemili and Eziawa communities [coded separately]. At least one person was killed, several houses and business premises were destroyed, as claimed by IPOB. The chief press secretary of the state governor denied claims.

On 17 September 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted five passengers of a commercial vehicle at Choba junction (Obio, Rivers) along Emohua-Kalabari road. The driver was later released, there are no reports about ransom demands for the other abductees; four abductees were rescued by policemen on 20 September [no interaction was reported].
Around 17 September 2022, armed individuals abducted five passengers of a commercial bus along the Emohua-Kalabari road (Emohua, Rivers). No further details.

On 17 September 2022, an unidentified armed group fired indiscriminately at the residence of an Islamic cleric at Iseyin town (Iseyin, Oyo). One person sustained gunshot wounds, the cleric was abducted.

On 17 September 2022, troops of Operation Forest Sanity engaged a Kaduna militia in armed clash on the fringes of Bwari Jere forest, coded to Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). At least 48 of the militiamen were killed.

On 17 September 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted two persons along Abuja-Kaduna road, coded to Katari (Kachia, Kaduna). The victims included the nephew of Bishop Kukah and a driver, the abductee's mother was allowed to go after the abductors saw a stomp on her leg. A ransom of 50 million naira, later reduced to 30 million was demanded.

On 17 September 2022, ISWAP fighters killed two Boko Haram officials when they invaded their camp at Gazuwa, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). The officials were Abou Hamza (Munzir) and Abou Ibrahim (Nakib), they were silently killed and their bodies were found in their homes early the following morning.

On 17 September 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted and clashed with ISWAP militants in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). One militant was killed; weapons, a magazine, drugs, phones and other items were recovered.
On 17 September 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed ISWAP militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Karetu (Mobbar, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 17 September 2022, a Niger militia clashed with a local self defense militia when they invaded Japap area in Suleja (Suleja, Niger). The local defense militia was overpowered an fled, the assailants abducted two civilians including the pastor of a church that was having a vigil nearby, they fled with the abductees when soldiers arrived the area. The abductees were released on 20 September after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 17 September 2022, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a local self defense militia called Youth Initiative of Operation Self-Defense when the assailants attacked Dutsin Ma community (Dutsinma, Katsina). Two self defense militiamen were killed, residents fled the area due to fear of being attacked.
On 18 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia in their numbers attacked and killed three civilians when they invaded Ngban community in Nyiev council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 18 September 2022, a Niger militia in their numbers attacked and killed four civilians and wounded 8 others when they invaded Fapo village in Lapai LGA (Niger). The assailants shot sporadically during the attack, 15 persons were also abducted.

On 18 September 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man along the Okpolu-Rumuigbo (Obio, Rivers). The assailants had intercepted the victim and shot him after an altercation between them, they fled immediately after.

Around 18 September 2022 (as reported), policemen from the anti-cultism and kidnapping squad engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and killed two of them while the third one escaped with bullet wounds at Creek Town (Odukpani, Cross River). The police claimed that the assailants were responsible for the abduction of four clergymen [coded separately].
On 18 September 2022, a Zamfara militia in large number, riding motorcycles attacked civilians at Guawa village in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). There are no further details.
On 18 September 2022, a Zamfara militia attacked commuters along Tsafe-Funtua highway (Tsafe, Zamfara). Security operatives were deployed to the area, there are no further details.

On 18 September 2022, a Katsina militia shot indiscriminately at passengers at Kwanar Gamji along Funtua-Dandume road (Dandume, Katsina). A commercial driver was shot and killed and unspecified number of passengers were abducted.

Around 18 September 2022 (between 8 September - 22 September), the Nigerian Defense Headquarters claimed to have killed two ISWAP/ Boko Haram commanders at Parisu and Sheruri general area in Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). The commanders were Abu Asiya and Abu Ubaida (A Qaid).

On 19 September 2022, an armed Fulani pastoralists militia invaded a residence at Kwarra (Wamba, Nassarawa) where they forcefully took away a 14-year old girl into the bush, stabbed and raped her into a coma. The police claimed that two persons were arrested in connection with the incident. It is unclear if the victim died.

On 19 September 2022, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier when they attacked a checkpoint manned by the Civilian JTF in Jakana (Bama, Borno). Other sources report one Civilian JTF member and not a soldier was killed.
On 19 September 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people including the secretary of the Moriki emirate in Moriki (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 September 2022, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a Togolese security guard (off duty) and shot and injured youths who tried to rescue him at Gbede (Ori Ire, Oyo). The kidnappers demanded a ransom of 10 million naira, but the victim was released on 21 September after an undisclosed ransom was paid.
On 19 September 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters from 2 vehicles when they blocked the Shinkafi-Gusau (Shinkafi, Zamfara).
On 20 September 2022, armed individuals abducted two occupants of a private car along the Emohua-Kalabari road (Emohua, Rivers). The abductors demanded a ransom of 50 million Naira.

On 20 September 2022, a Niger militia mounted on motorcycles fired indiscriminately at civilians in Kpampo village, coded to nearby Gulu (Lapai, Niger). 5 people were killed, 4 others were injured, 8 others were abducted and food supplies were looted.
On 20 September 2022, a Katsina militia wounded one person when they attacked Dangaje village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).
