On 28 October 2022, a Niger militia killed two civilians in Iku forest (Tafa, Niger) after they went into the forest in search of their stolen cattle. The victims were part of five villagers from Bamburu community in Gwagwalada who embarked on the search.

On 28 October 2022, Boko Haram militants killed one driver when they attacked and robbed commuters in Yuwe axis, along Banki road (Bama, Borno). The militants stole food, clothes and other items and fled.
On 28 October 2022, a Katsina militia abducted 4 people from Funtua in the vicinity of Jabiri (Funtua, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 28 October 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Umuanunu community in Obinze (Owerri West, Imo). There are no further details.

On 28 October 2022, policemen in collaboration with hunters clashed with an unidentified armed group dressed in military camouflage, who attacked civilians at Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). One policemen was killed another was wounded, three civilians including one university professor, the daughter of a traditional ruler and two female students were abducted. A ransom of 50 million was demanded for the professor, and 10 million each for the students, 2.2 million naira was paid as ransom for the students, who was released on 30 October together with the monarch's daughter and the professor, whose ransom amounts were undisclosed.

On 28 October 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted one civilian at an illegal vehicle checkpoint which they set up at Kinjimiram (Magumeri, Borno). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 28 October 2022, policemen engaged a Katsina militia that had attacked civilians in an armed clash at Gandun Sarki village in Matazu LGA (Katsina). 21 abductees were rescued, 20 rustled cattle were recovered, many militiamen were killed by the police and some escaped with gunshot wounds. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 29 October 2022, a Zamfara militia set a couple and their home ablaze at Gayari community (Gummi, Zamfara). The victims were rescued and taken to the hospital.
On 29 October 2022, a Katsina militia shot indiscriminately and abducted a woman and her son in Ingawa LGA (Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 29 October 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and shot at civilians in Tse Ikyem community, coded to Ugba (Logo, Benue). Three persons were killed and several others were wounded, other sources report that the scene of the attack was the same as the previous attack of 23 October [coded separately].

On 29 October 2022, Kubdiya and Tarbuwa communal militias clashed using arrows and dane guns during a reprisal attack at Kubdiya (Gamawa, Bauchi). 3 people were wounded and 10 others were wounded. The clash was over an attack on Kudiya locals by a Tarbuwa militia the previous day [coded separately].
On 29 October 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a policemen and stole his rifle at Edgerton street in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River).

On 29 October 2022, Sara-Suka militia attacked and killed one person at Yan Doya market in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The victim was returning home when he was attacked and killed with knives, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 29 October 2022, a Katsina militia abducted 10 persons from a residence which they invaded in Dajin Mare, Dandume LGA (Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 29 October 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering about 10 invaded Ogbaku motor park (Mbaitoli, Imo), killed one soya seller and wounded a trader in the shoulder. The victims are suspected to be from the Hausa ethnic group.

On 29 October 2022, Boko Haram/ ISWAP fighters in large numbers were engaged in an armed clash with soldiers when they attempted to invade the military barracks of Wawa cantonment, New Bussa (Borgu, Niger) and free militants that were in detention there. The soldiers received reinforcement from the air force base in the area and repelled the militants; 8 militants were killed, 3 to 18 others were arrested and an unspecified number were wounded.

On 31 October 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted 4 civilians from Dogondaji and 6 others from Kazauda villages in Wanke district (Gusau, Zamfara). A ransom of 2 million naira each was demanded.

On 31 October 2022, an unidentified armed group trailed and abducted a man who was returning home from church in Abak (Abak, Akwa Ibom). On 31 October 2022, a Zamfara militia shot indiscriminately at civilians in Yankaba (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara) and killed 4 persons.

On 31 October 2022, a Katsina militia killed one civilian in Shanga, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The victim was killed for pointing a torch light in the direction of the assailants while they were heading to an destination.

On 9 November 2022, soldiers beat up a policeman and an official of Lagos traffic management agency on Eko bridge in Lagos (Lagos Island, Lagos) after they reprimanded the soldiers for following the wrong traffic lane. Another set of soldiers who were on the right lane also joined their colleagues to beat up the victims who were later hospitalized.

On 9 November 2022, a Benue militia suspected to be linked with Gana killed five people and wounded several others at a pub in Pevya, coded to Katsina-Ala (Katsina Ala, Benue). One of the victims was a member of a local defense militia who was trailed to the spot and killed alongside his friends, he was suspected by the assailants to be an informant for security operatives.

Around 9 November 2022 (as reported), Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] abducted about 40 women from Gwoza community (Gwoza, Borno). 20 of them were murdered in two separate events after they were accused of witchcraft by the militants [coded separately].
On 10 November 2022, a Niger militia attacked civilians at a village near Kafin Koro (Paikoro, Niger). There are no further details.

On 10 November 2022, troops of Operation Forest Sanity on a fighting patrol clashed with a Zamfara militia at Danmarke in Gummi LGA (Zamfara). Several militia men fled with bullet wounds, three abductees were rescued, 5 rifles, 30 motorcycles and other items were recovered.
On 10 November 2022, soldiers shot two tanker drivers around Ejule-Ochadam junction (Ofu, Kogi). It is unclear whether the victims died, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 10 November 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia that had come to evacuate the remains of their colleagues that were killed the previous day [coded separately] at Gando forest, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). Hundreds of militia members were killed, coded as 100.

On 10 November 2022, Nigerian troops ambushed a Kaduna militia led by Dogo Maikasuwa and engaged them in an armed clash at a forest in the Gengere-Kaso general area, coded to nearby Kaku (Chikun, Kaduna). The militia leader and another militiaman were killed, some fled with bullet wounds weapons, ammunition, and other items were recovered.

On 10 November 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP fighters who invaded a humanitarian transport hub in Monguno (Monguno, Borno) and attempted to steal vehicles. The militants were repelled, they set vehicles ablaze before they fled. ISWAP claimed the attack was at the ICRC compound and that 25 vehicles were set ablaze. Other sources report that the attack was at a transportation agency and 22 vehicles were destroyed.
On 10 November 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired indiscriminately and abducted two women in the vicinity Dusuman (Jere, Borno). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 10 November 2022, Boko Haram [JAS faction] commander Ali Ngulde killed 10 women at Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno) after they were accused of witchcraft. The victims whose throats were slit were abducted alongside 30 others [coded separately] and were accused of being responsible for the death of the commander's children. Other sources report that 15-17 women were killed, 10 of whom were accused of witchcraft, the 5 others were members of the group that attempted to surrender to the military.

Around 11 November 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group affiliated to the governor of Rivers state abducted a supporter of the PDP presidential candidate in Ikwerre LGA (Rivers) coded to Isiokpo. The abductee was made to denounce his support for the PDP's candidate until the governor gave to do otherwise.

On 11 November 2022, the Defense Headquarters claimed that troops of Operation Forest Sanity on a fighting patrol attacked camps of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash in Lanke and Danmarke villages in Gummi LGA (Zamfara). At least 8 militiamen were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds and four abductees were rescued. Arms, ammunition and motorcycles were also recovered by the troops.

On 11 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 16 persons who were returning to Gwombe (Kuje, FCT) after attending a wedding in Abaji. 15 of the abductees were released after foodstuff, drugs and wine worth 437,000 naira were received by the abductors around 3 January 2023. The last abductee was murdered [coded separately] over claims of refusal to cooperate by the abductors.
On 11 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Ufuma (Orumba North, Anambra) supposedly killing 3, yet to be confirmed by the police. The attackers also stole a bullion van.

On 11 November 2022, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a patrol of Nigerian soldiers between Katafila and Mararaba towns, coded to Biu (Biu, Borno). The soldiers fled and one of their vehicles was seized by the militants.

On 11 November 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a polytechnic deputy rector after they flagged down his vehicle along Otukpo-Eke-Ugbokolo-Otukpa road, coded to Oturkpo (Otukpo, Benue). The victim was traveling with his wife whom the assailants attempted to abduct but later abandoned when they sighted soldiers who responded to the sounds of their gunshots.

On 12 November 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the information officer of Ukum LGA at his residence in Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). The victim was trailed by the assailants who shot him in the stomach, he was taken to the hospital where he died. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 12 November 2022, Ebube Agu operatives attacked LP supporters and wounded an unspecified number of supporters at Mgbom Okposi (Ohaozara, Ebonyi). Some of the victims were missing, the LP house of assembly candidate for Ohaozara East constituency claimed that the attack was led by LGA chairman. The chairman claimed that the operatives were at the venue to ensure the supporters did not block the road and no one was attacked, the Ebube Agu commander claimed the operatives were not in the area and that the victims may have been attacked by fellow members following a disagreement while the police denied knowledge of the incident.

On 12 November 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to assassins attacked civilians at a chemist in Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta). The assailants shot sporadically, and two persons were confirmed to have been killed, one other person who was a businessman was taken away and later confirmed killed. The police confirmed that one person was killed.

On 12 November 2022, over 50 members of a local defense militia who were armed with machetes and dane guns attacked and wounded members of the APC in Oturkpo (Otukpo, Benue). The victims claimed that the assailants were led by the chairman of Ado LGA and his deputy, the victims were taken to another location where they were tortured and handed over to the police. They were later released after the intervention of the commissioner of police in the state.

On 12 November 2022, the Defense Headquarters claimed that Nigerian troops clashed with IPOB militants in Isuofia (Aguata, Anambra). 13 militants were killed, 6 others including a herbalist were arrested, arms, ammunition and military camouflage uniforms were recovered by the troops.

On 12 November 2022, an unidentified armed group in large numbers attacked an army checkpoint and clashed with soldiers at Isuofia (Aguata, Anambra). The assailants gained entrance through a neighboring community, at least two soldiers were killed, other sources report that four assailants were also killed and two soldiers were wounded.

On 12 November 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to have been recruited by the national secretary of the PDP attacked the party members at the party's secretariat in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) and disrupted the inauguration of the presidential campaign council. Office equipment were damaged and officials were manhandled, other sources report that the attack was over the national secretary's claim that he did not make any input in the selection of PCC members in the state.

On 12 November 2022, Boko Haram [JAS faction] commander Ali Ngulde killed 10 women at Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno) after they were accused of witchcraft. The victims whose throats were slit were abducted alongside 30 others [coded separately] and were accused of being responsible for the death of the commander's children. 10 other victims were previously killed by the militants [coded separately]. Other sources report that 15-17 women were killed, 10 of whom were accused of witchcraft, the 5 others were members of the group that attempted to surrender to the military.

Around 13 November 2022 (between 11 November - 14 November), police forces responded to a distress call and clashed with a Zamfara militia at Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara). The militiamen fled with possible gunshot wounds, two rifles, 35 rounds of ammunition and some charms were recovered by the police.

On 13 November 2022, a Kaduna militia that attempted to infiltrate the housing location of Nigerian troops were engaged in an armed clash at Kankomi (Chikun, Kaduna). One of the assailants who was wearing military camouflage was killed, others fled with bullet wounds, the fleeing assailants killed 3 civilians. Other sources report more than one of the assailants were killed, including the militia leader Kachalla Gudau and his aide Rigimamme. One rifle, ammunition and locally made grenades were recovered by the troops.
On 13 November 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed 1 person at Tudun Mare in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). The victim was a teacher.

On 13 November 2022, policemen beat up the secretary of Ifa Ikot Akpan, attacked and wounded him with a machete at Ifa Ikot Akpan, coded to Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). The victim claimed that the attacked was based on the orders of the state's commissioner for environment, due to his support for the gubernatorial of the Young Progressives Party.
On 13 November 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed 3 persons in Gefe (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 13 November 2022, IPOB militants abducted an off duty soldier after they intercepted the vehicle he was traveling in and searched it along a road in Anambra, coded to Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The abductee's uniform and boots were found in a bag and pictures of him in uniform were found on his phone. The Nigerian Navy confirmed the abduction and claimed that a search for the abductee had commenced.
On 13 November 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia at Kafaiyo in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed and one rifle was recovered.

On 14 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted 8 IDPs from Dangurunfa community, coded to Dan Garamfa (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abductees consisted of 6 women and two men, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 14 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted 3 men from Sadawa community (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 14 November 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai together with Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants who had set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint to rob civilians at Ngwom (Mafa, Borno). Two civilians were killed, the troops recovered four of the militants' motorcycles.
On 14 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Ariaria community (Uruan, Akwa Ibom) coded to Idu. Two persons were killed and about two shops were set ablaze.
On 14 November 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai clashed with Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] at Mafa axis (Mafa, Borno). 14 militants including one commander were killed.

On 14 November 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to have been sponsored by the PDP attacked the SDP gubernatorial candidate in Egberu Ndoki (Oyigbo, Rivers). The SDP candidate claimed that the assailants were sponsored by the Rivers state PDP chairman. There are no further details.

On 14 November 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a business woman along Lafia-Shendam road (Lafia, Nassarawa). The victim who was the wife of a former LGA chairman in the state was on her way to a market and was shot by the assailants who were targeting the driver of the vehicle she was in.
On 14 November 2022, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted at least 20 housewives from Bagege village in Mayanchi (Maru, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 14 November 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two persons at Mgbala community, coded to nearby Mgbele (Oguta, Imo). The victims were a pregnant woman and a local defense militia member who is presumed to have been unarmed.

On 14 November 2022, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Obudi Agwa and two chiefs when they invaded the palace at Obudi-Agwa (Oguta, Imo). the victims were in a cabinet meeting when the assailants attacked. Other sources report that 5 were killed and others including the traditional prime minister were wounded. IPOB denied involvement in the attack, and claimed that Ebube Agu operatives were responsible, the spokesperson of the group claimed that the state governor recruited criminals and Niger Delta militants to kill and destroy the property of persons against the Fulanization of Imo state.

On 15 November 2022, an unidentified armed group shot a businessman in the thigh and abducted his in-law at the latter's residence in Imeko (Imeko-Afon, Ogun). The abductee was taken away in his car which was later abandoned in the town, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 15 November 2022, a joint patrol of soldiers, policemen and a local defense militia responded to a distress call and clashed with an unidentified armed group that had ambushed a commercial bus and abducted civilians near Otukpa (Ogbadibo, Benue). The assailants abandoned the abductees, and killed one member of a local defense militia whom they encountered while fleeing.
On 15 November 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded a court, overpowered the policemen there and set four suspects free in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta).

On 15 November 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists numbering about 15 and armed with machetes and guns shot at vehicles and abducted nine passengers along Akampka-Biase, coded to Akankpa (Akamkpa, Cross River). There are no reports about ransom demands, 8 of the abductees were released, the police claimed that the abductees were not pastoralists.

On 15 November 2022, a local defense militia attempted to repel an attack by suspected armed Fulani pastoralists in Maikatako community in Batura district (Bokkos, Plateau). The assailants overwhelmed the local defense militia and killed between 9 to 11 civilians, including 9 family members, wounded 6 others and burnt 4 houses.

On 15 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest from Igbo-Ukwu (Aguata, Anambra). The abducted was found and rescued in Umueri community by a local self defense militia after he was abandoned there by the abductors.

On 16 November 2022, DSS officials averted the attempted abduction of an LP senatorial candidate by suspected Ebube Agu operatives in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The targeted person was being returned to a correctional center when the vehicle conveying him was intercepted.
On 16 November 2022, officials of the Lagos state task force attacked residents of Yegunda, Abomiti and Eyin-Osa in Epe (Epe, Lagos) when they invaded the area.
On 16 November 2022, a Katsina militia attacked and wounded an unspecified number of civilians when they invaded a residence in Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). Phones were also stolen by the assailants.

Around 16 November 2022 (as reported), suspected armed pastoralists armed with spears, arrows and other weapons attacked and killed a farmer at Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). Many other persons were wounded by the assailants, residents claimed that the assailants were supported by MACBAN.
On 16 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Maikatako 1 and Maikatako 2, coded to Batura (Bokkos). Residents fled from the community when they sighted the assailants.

On 16 November 2022, suspected soldiers attacked civilians when they invaded Bodo community (Gonaka, Rivers) and shot sporadically in the air for several hours. The assailants invaded the regent's residence and beat up his wife after they meet his absence and took about 25 people away.

On 16 November 2022, policemen in collaboration with a local defense militia clashed with a Niger militia at Kumbashi (Mariga, Niger). 7 militiamen were killed, others fled with bullet wounds and two local defense militiamen were wounded and taken to the hospital.

On 17 November 2022, a soldier shot and killed another soldier and a humanitarian worker in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The assailant also stabbed one helicopter pilot before he was shot and killed by other soldiers.

On 17 November 2022, a Zamfara militia suspected to be led by Dankarami abducted more than 40 people from Kanwa village (Zurmi, Zamfara). The abductors conducted a house to house search in the area and most of the abductees were women and children, five of the abductees escaped. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 17 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons from Ibeagwa, coded to Nkwo Nike (Enugu East, Enugu). The abductees consisted of a shop owner, a commercial tricyclist and a third person who was caught filming the abduction of the other two persons. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 18 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons including two medical doctors at the Ikomita section of the Calabar-Ikom highway (Ikom, Cross River). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded for the release of the doctors, the victims were released on 22 November and the chairman of the Nigerian medical association claimed that no ransom was paid.

On 18 November 2022, a group of hunters and a local self defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group that attacked a Fulani settlement between Gorgor and Liya communities (Biu, Borno). The assailants wounded the son of the Fulani leader when they did not meet his father, and collected one million naira from the victim's family. They were overpowered by the hunters who arrested the leader of the group, seized his rifle while the others fled.
On 18 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a trader from Anyiin (Logo, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 18 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Ebube Agu operatives and killed two of them at a checkpoint in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). Many residents of the area sustained varying degrees of injuries while trying to flee from the attack.

On 18 November 2022, soldiers and policemen clashed with a Kaduna militia that attacked travelers at Gulbala (Giwa, Kaduna). The roadblock set up by the assailants was dismantled and 76 abductees were rescued by the troops while three travelers were missing [presumed abducted].

On 18 November 2022, a Kaduna militia killed a policeman when they attacked a convoy of the managing director of the Railway Management Company Limited at Goni Gora (Chikun, Kaduna). The other occupants of the car escaped unharmed.

On 18 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a former Enugu state commissioner and his brother at Nkpokolo, Achi (Oji River, Enugu). The former commissioner was also a former local government chairman. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 18 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an architect at the residence of his boss in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductors took the abductee and his car away, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 18 November 2022, a local defense militia invaded the hideout of a Niger militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Dogon Ruwa in Shiroro LGA ( Nigeria). One abductee was killed, an unspecified number of others were rescued.

On 18 November 2022, a suspected Oruku militia attacked and killed two civilians at Aguikpa community, coded to nearby Oruku (Nkanu East, Enugu). One of the victims was a former president general of Oruku community.

On 18 November 2022, ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters clashed with the police and military forces near Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). 11 fatalities, including 9 soldiers and 2 mobile police officers were recorded.

On 19 November 2022, a suspected member of the Oyo state park management system clashed with a commercial motorcyclist which resulted in the killing of a boy who was hit by a stray bullet at Igbo Ora (Ibarapa Central, Oyo). Two other persons were wounded, the PMS denied any connection with the assailant who was later killed by a mob [coded separately].

On 19 November 2022, a local self defense militia ambushed and clashed with a Zamfara militia in Birnin Magaji (Gummi, Zamfara). The assailants had attempted to kill the leader of the self defense militia, 18 of the assailants were killed.

On 19 November 2022, Ebube Agu operatives attacked and shot at the convoy of a PDP chieftain at Ekoli (Afikpo South, Ebonyi). The assailants mounted a roadblock and shot two supporters who were critically wounded.

On 19 November 2022, a Sokoto militia ambushed and killed two civilians who were mounted on motorcycles and carrying petrol at Lomedai village in Illela LGA (Sokoto). The assailants stole their motorcycles and petrol.

On 19 November 2022, some soldiers attacked civilians at a burial ceremony in Ogombo (Eti-Osa, Lagos), killed one person and wounded another. The soldiers were invited by a member of the family to disrupt the ceremony following a family feud.
On 19 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted 19 to 37 people in Kobre village, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 November 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded a catholic church and abducted a priest in Ibegwa-Aka (Igbo Eze South, Enugu). The assailants trailed the priest to the parish house, shot sporadically and threatened to burn it down if the priest did not come out. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 November 2022, an unidentified armed group numbering 6 abducted a man from his residence at Igbekebo (Ese-Edo, Ondo). The victim was a former aide to the state governor, policemen arrived after the abductors left with the victim. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.

On 19 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Oko-Olowo (Ilorin West, Kwara). One person was shot at and macheted, two others were abducted and there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 November 2022, a Katsina militia shot at security (assumed Police) operatives who attempted to foil the militia's attack on commuters at Magama Jibia in Jibia LGA (Katsina). Two civilians were killed, three others were abducted and an unspecified number of persons were wounded.

On 19 November 2022, ISWAP fighters ambushed a convoy of Boko Haram [JAS] fighters and engaged them in an armed clash which lasted about 40 minutes at Chillaria axis of Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). An unspecified number of Boko Haram fighters were killed. One Hilux, several motorcycles and weapons were seized by ISWAP. Unknown casualties coded as 3.

On 19 November 2022, suspected armed pastoralists killed a farmer following a disagreement over grazing on his farm at Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The victim was shot with and arrow and macheted by the assailants, other workers on the farm fled and the assailants also set the tricycles used by the farmers ablaze. Other sources report that the residents tried to repel the attack before policemen escorted MACBAN leaders who rescued the assailants.

On 19 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 20 persons, most of whom were women from Daura town (Daura Katsina), and proceeded to rob other persons in Baichin Daura. The abductees including twin 4-day old babies were taken away during a house to house search. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 November 2022, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Aguamede community (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and killed four people, many others were wounded and houses were burnt, 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.
On 19 November 2022, suspected IPOB militants attacked policemen at a checkpoint at Agbani (Nkanu West, Enugu). The assailants shot sporadically and killed three policemen.
On 20 November 2022, a local defense militia ambushed Boko Haram militants in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). Three militants were killed.

On 20 November 2022, a suspected unidentified cult militia were engaged in an armed clash with policemen after the militia invaded Aguleri (Anambra East, Anambra). The clash lasted for about one hour, there was an unspecified number of injuries on both sides and the police claimed to have arrested 15 assailants. Some sources report that the clash started between two rival cult militias and the police engaged the attacking group in an armed clash, others report that the assailants were heading towards the police station in the area before they were repelled by the policemen.

On 20 November 2022, a local defense militia ambushed and clashed with Boko Haram fighters [JAS] in the axis of Konduga LGA (Borno). Four militants were killed, the fourth person was fatally wounded and the body was later found, the militants were intercepted on their way to receive ransom payment for an abductee.

On 20 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 38 people while they were working on their farms in Gidan Goga (Maradun, Zamfara) and Yankaba [coded separately]. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 20 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a police surveillance team and engaged them in an armed clash at Eha-Alumona (Nsukka, Enugu). One policeman was killed.
On 20 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two people while they were jogging in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). One of the abductees escaped, there are no further details.

On 20 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 20 travelers between Ugbowo and Ohosu communities (Egor, Edo) after they shot sporadically at vehicles on the road. 17 of the abductees were rescued by the police [no clash was reported], the police claimed to be combing the bush in search of the remaining 3 persons.

On 20 November 2022, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians and killed two persons when they invaded Agbeta II Tuabom community (Eleme, Rivers). Many people were also wounded by the assailants, other members of the community fled the area due to fear of being attacked.

On 20 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 38 people while they were working on their farms in Yankaba (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara) and Gidan Goga [coded separately]. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 20 November 2022, armed pastoralists attacked and wounded an unspecified number of civilians at Hayin Dogo ward, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). There are no further details.

On 21 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons along Oke Ako-Irele road (Ikole, Ekiti). The victims consisted of a school principal, two teachers and one nurse who were returning home from work. The principal escaped the following day, while the remaining 3 abductees were released after an unspecified amount was paid as ransom, two of the abductors were arrested by the joint task force [no clash was reported].

On 21 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from Kwadabe village in Kiyawa LGA (Jigawa). The victim was release around 23 November, there are no reports about ransom demands or payment.

On 21 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a PDP member and his older brother from Boi (Bogoro, Bauchi). The older brother was abandoned in the bush and later rescued while the politician was taken away and a ransom of 100 million was demanded. The abductee was released on 4 December, there are no reports about ransom payment.

Around 21 November 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia abducted four persons from Guidan Kolo (Gusau, Zamfara). A ransom of 10 million naira which was later reduced to 5 million was demanded, before the abductors demanded that the ransom be paid in the yet to be launched naira notes. They insisted on keeping the abductees till December when the notes will be in circulation.

On 21 November 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted four passengers on the road between Kwanar Maharba and Yar Butu in Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto). The abductees comprised of two men and two women, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 21 November 2022, a Katsina militia abducted two farmers near Turare coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 21 November 2022, a Katsina militia invaded a Fulani settlement in Badole, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina) and killed one person.

On 21 November 2022, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Aguamede community (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and killed 8 people who were returning from their farms or in their houses. About 25 others were wounded, the victims included women and children, houses were destroyed and the murdered victims had their throats slit and machete cuts on their heads, 5 more bodies were found the following day, 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 22 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the APGA candidate for the Ahiazu constituency in Imo state while he was on his way to Ahiazu, coded to Oru (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo). The abductee was released on the same day after the abductors took the valuables which he had with him as at the time he was abducted.

On 22 November 2022, a Zamfara militia led by Bello Turji abducted 5 elders from Moriki who went to deliver the protection levy which was imposed on their community at the militia's hideout in Jirari, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). The victims were abducted because they delivered 10.5 million naira out of the 20 million that was demanded and insisted on keeping 5 out of the 7 of them in order to ensure that the balance is paid.

On 22 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor and his son when they invaded his residence at Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). The son was released unhurt, there are no reports about ransom demands for the doctor.
On 22 November 2022, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Eha Amufu communities (Isi Uzo, Enugu), killing one person and leaving 3 others critically wounded.
On 22 November 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two civilians at an unspecified community in Billiri LGA (Gombe).

On 22 November 2022, and unidentified armed group attacked and killed 8 civilians when they invaded Kwatas (Bokkos, Plateau). An unspecified number of others were also wounded by the assailants who shot sporadically during the attack.
On 22 November 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian soldiers in the vicinity of Goneri Kadauye in Konduga LGA (Borno). There are no further details.
On 22 November 2022, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Banga (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Two persons were killed and two others were abducted.
Around 23 November 2022, unidentified armed group raped and killed a woman in Onicha (Onicha, Ebonyi).

On 23 November 2022, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Riyoji village in Dauran Birnin Tsaba (Zurmi, Zamfara) and killed 19 people. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded they area, and the victims were shot while they were trying to escape.
On 23 November 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP militants on Goniri (Gujba, Yobe) until they fled. There are no further details.
On 23 November 2022, a security agent presumed to be a policeman killed a truck driver at checkpoint along Oturkpo-Enugu expressway (Otukpo, Benue). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 24 November 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed 11 persons at Rafin Sarki in Giwa LGA (Kaduna). Several other persons sustained gunshot wounds.
On 24 November 2022, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian at Karamai (Kajuru, Kaduna).
On 24 November 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians in Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 24 November 2022, Nigerian troops ambushed Boko Haram fighters [JAS] and engaged them in an armed clash towards Mafa axis (Mafa, Borno). 5 militants were killed, one of them was captured alive by the troops.

On 24 November 2022, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform clashed with policemen who were on escort duty at Rumuokoro (Obio, Rivers). Three policemen were killed, others sources report four policemen killed, valuables were stolen by the assailants who also abducted an oil and gas executive. The abductee was released around 8 December, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 24 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest alongside several church members at an unspecified location in Nassarawa state, coded to Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The abductees were en route to Abuja, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 24 November 2022, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians at Damari villlage (Sabuwa, Katsina).
On 24 November 2022, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian at Chibiya (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 24 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 17 travelers along Okene-Ibilo road (Okene, Kogi). The abductees were on their way to Ilorin to attend a wedding, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 25 November 2022, a Katsina militia killed two civilians when they attacked Yan Ukku in Safana LGA (Katsina). Five other persons sustained gunshot wounds.

On 25 November 2022, MACBAN leadership claimed that a local defense militia attacked and killed 13 pastoralists in Jatau and Japan communities (Bali, Taraba). 270 cows and several motorcycles were also stolen by the assailants.

On 25 November 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two residents at Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The victims were keeping watch at the exit routes of the community, the third person who was able to escape returned and informed the community.

On 26 November 2022, Nigerian troops repelled Boko Haram militants that attempted to attack Dikwa town (Dikwa, Borno) until they fled. The militants had tried to invade the town from the southern and western axes of Gulumba Gana and Maiduguri road.

On 26 November 2022, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked a predominantly Christian village at Maikadiri (Askira Uba, Borno). The militia fled; one motorcycle, ammunition and other property were seized by the militants.
On 26 November 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted two civilians along Isa-Modaci road (Isa, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 26 November 2022, suspected army personnel with an NSCDC official flogged civilians with their belts when they invaded a sanitation court in Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia). The assailants released 51 offenders including one woman of theirs, they scattered all record books and documents except one, court officials, ministry staff and other security personnel fled.

On 26 November 2022, two unidentified cult militias clashed and shot sporadically during a supremacy battle in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Six persons were killed, other sources report that the murdered victims were presumed to be passers-by who were hit by stray bullets.

Around 27 November 2022 (as reported), a suspected Fulani militia abducted and later killed a couple whose corpse was found at a forest in Ukpata community (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The corpses were found decomposing with some body parts missing.

On 27 November 2022, troops of Operation Forest Sanity who were on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia in Kaso, coded to Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna) and Bawa Rikasa Hill. The militiamen fled; nine abductees were rescued, 90 cattle were recovered and four motorcycles belonging to the militiamen were recovered from the second location.
On 27 November 2022, presumed soldiers clashed with a Sokoto militia that attacked civilians in Kalmalo (Illela, Sokoto). Two people including one militiaman were killed, 16 others were wounded.

On 27 November 2022, troops of Operation Forest Sanity on a clearance operation clashed with a Kaduna militia at Tsohon Gaya, coded to nearby Sabon Gaya (Chikun, Kaduna) after the troops identified the militia's hideout. Four militiamen were killed; two instantly and the other two later died from gunshot wounds, one rifle, ammunition and one motorcycle were recovered by the troops.

On 27 November 2022, MNJTF troops repelled an attempt by ISWAP militants led by Abu Ubaida to infiltrate Monguno town (Monguno, Borno) through Charly 6. 7 militants were killed, the others fled and were chased by the troops.

On 27 November 2022, a DSS operative attacked and wounded the director general of the PDP gubernatorial campaign in Abia state at Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia) after the victim bashed the car of the DSS operative. The assailant was arrested by the police.
On 27 November 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a man at Umubere in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 27 November 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked a man and his son on their way to their farm in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The man was killed and his son sustained machete cuts

On 28 November 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 18 passengers at Ochadam (Ofu, Kogi). The bus was heading to Abuja from the eastern region when it was flagged down by the abductors, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 28 November 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a member of a local defense militia [presumed to be unarmed] at Abejukolo (Omala, Kogi). The victim's wife and one other woman were abducted and a ransom of 8 million naira was demanded.

On 28 November 2022, a local defense militia engaged a Katsina militia that attacked civilians and rustled cattle in an armed clash at Unguwar Korau, Safana LGA (Katsina). The assailants fled, one of them was arrested and the rustled cattle were recovered.

Around 28 November 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed intercepted and abducted the leader of a local self defense militia while he was returning from church in Ukwulu (Dunukofia, Anambra). The abductee was released around 28 December after 5 million naira was paid as ransom, he had been abducted and released previously [coded separately].
On 28 November 2022, an unidentified armed group killed the Kaura area women leader of LP when they invaded her residence in Kaura (Kaura, Kaduna). Her husband also sustained gunshot injuries.

On 28 November 2022, policemen attached to Ughelli Division A attacked and beat up three journalists in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta). The journalists claimed that they tried to control traffic congestion in the area when they were kicked and hit with the butt of guns by the policemen.

On 28 November 2022, a Black Axe militia attacked a member of the group on the campus of University of Cross River in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River) over his refusal to relinquish a position within the confraternity. The police claimed that the victim was shot in the leg and receiving treatment, other sources report that he died.

On 28 November 2022, suspected security operatives dressed in military uniforms shot the security officers (presumed Military forces) guarding an oil well in Izombe (Oguta, Imo). The assailants invaded the area in armored cars, there are no further details.

On 28 November 2022, a faction of NURTW which is loyal to the PDP attacked members of another faction which is loyal to the APC at four different motor parks in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The parks which were dominated by APC loyalists were attacked simultaneously by PDP loyalists who claimed the NURTW worked against the new governor's election; one union member sustained machete cuts and his car was set on fire and gunshots were fired indiscriminately. The APC claimed that over 500 of its members were wounded in the incidents, and a number of properties including campaign billboards were destroyed, other sources report that ten persons were wounded.
On 29 November 2022, a Katsina militia killed the mother and brother of a divisional police officer at their residence in Dan Musa town (Dan-Musa, Katsina).

On 29 November 2022, suspected members of an unidentified cult militia abducted a PDP chieftain at Ikot Akpa Ntuen in Ukanafun LGA (Akwa Ibom). The abductee who was a former party executive in the LGA was ambushed and abducted at his business premises, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 29 November 2022, a Zamfara militia killed two people and wounded two others when they attacked Dankoto village in Talata Mafara LGA (Zamfara). The village head was also abducted by the assailants and there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 30 November 2022, an unidentified group of farmers killed a pastoralist in Bayo LGA (Borno) following an argument over land encroachment by cattle.

On 30 November 2022, an unidentified group of pastoralists carried out a reprisal attack and killed eight persons in Bayo LGA (Borno) following an argument over land encroachment by cattle which led to the killing of one pastoralist [coded separately]. The assailants also set many houses ablaze.

On 30 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted at least seven commuters along Zurmi-Jibia highway, Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). The abductees included six APC members and one driver, other sources report that the abductees filled three cars, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 30 November 2022, an unidentified armed group of six who were suspected to be PDP members stabbed a Labor Party chieftain at Atakumosa East LGA (Osun) coded to Iperindo. The victim and an unspecified number of others were attacked while they were pasting posters of a House of Representatives candidate in the area.
On 30 November 2022, a Sokoto militia killed 6 civilians when they attacked Bari (Goronyo, Sokoto). The assailants invaded shops and looted goods, several livestock were also rustled.
On 30 November 2022, a Sokoto militia killed 1 civilian when they attacked Kagara (Goronyo, Sokoto). The assailants invaded shops and looted goods, several livestock were also rustled.
On 30 November 2022, a Sokoto militia killed 1 civilian when they attacked Kojiyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). The assailants invaded shops and looted goods, several livestock were also rustled.

On 30 November 2022, an unidentified armed group killed a couple and their daughter at Yelwata, coded to Gbajimba (Guma, Benue). One the second daughter sustained machete cuts and was critically wounded. The victims were attacked on their farm.
Around 30 November 2022 (as reported), ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS] fighters engaged in an armed clash at Mutakinti general area in Bama LGA (Borno). 11 fighters loyal to JAS were killed.
On 30 November 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted 5 civilians from Faji village in Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto). The abductees included a man and his two wives, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 30 November 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted one person at Mareri quarters (Gusau, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 30 November 2022 (as reported), troops of Operation Forest Sanity engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kwanti and Kuzo in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). Three abductees were rescued, two unidentified dead victims were discovered, the militiamen fled and dozens of their camps were destroyed by the troops who also recovered 4 motorcycles that were left behind.

On 30 November 2022, suspected members of an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a former student of Yabatech in the school premises in Yaba (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). Other sources report that the victim was also a member of an unidentified cult militia and the attack is related to an ongoing cult clash that began in July.

On 1 December 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from her place of work, the abductee was rescued by a local defense militia that intercepted the abductors on the Ozubulu (Ekwusigwo, Anambra). There are no reports of a clash.
On 1 December 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked Kainya village (Danko, Kebbi). There are no further details.
On 1 December 2022, an unidentified armed group killed one person in Onikerosine community, coded to Bolorunduro (Ondo East, Ondo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 1 December 2022, security operatives assumed to be comprised of soldiers, policemen and a local defense militia were ambushed by a Niger militia and engaged them in an armed clash around Unguwan Aboki and another militia hideout around Katarma (Chikun, Niger). The militiamen fled, five abductees were rescued and over 300 cattle were recovered from different locations [coded separately].

On 1 December 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked the residence of Oso Adowa-Akoko traditional ruler in Ajowa-Akoko (Akoko North West, Ondo). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the residence and destroyed the main entrance into the residential building of the palace, and kidnapped the traditional ruler. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, it was later reduced to 10 million and the abductee was released around 8 December after it was paid.

On 1 December 2022, policemen guarding an INEC office repelled suspected IPOB militants that attempted to burn the office in Orlu (Orlu, Imo). The assailants invaded the area, shot sporadically and threw an IED which damaged the security post of the office before they were chased by the policemen. The police claimed that many of the assailants sustained serious wounds. IPOB denied any links to the attack and claimed that the government and police were trying to blackmail it by linking the groups with attacks.

On 1 December 2022, operatives of a joint task force presumed to be comprised of soldiers, policemen and a local defense militia clashed with a Niger militia working for a militia leader called Alhaji Leyi at Gaskiya Bana, coded to Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). 20 militiamen were killed and five abductees were rescued by the security operatives, over 300 cattle were recovered from different locations [coded separately].

Around 1 December 2022 (as reported), ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS] fighters engaged in an armed clash at Mantari area in Bama LGA (Borno). ISWAP outnumbered and overpowered JAS and 11 fighters were killed.

On 1 December 2022, the Nigerian Army claimed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai with air support, clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants around Waijroko-Damboa road (Damboa, Borno). Several militants were killed, coded as 10, several weapons and gun trucks were recovered from the militants.

On 2 December 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a commercial motorcyclist at Obelle (Emohua, Rivers) in retaliation for some of their cows that were killed due to an argument over grazing on people's farms in the area.

On 2 December 2022, a Zamfara militia killed 12 persons including one farmer in simultaneous attacks in Manya, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Nasarawa-Burkullu [coded separately]. Eleven persons including six farmers and five women were abducted, soldiers were seen rushing to the area to repel the attack but were unsuccessful. 12 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 6.

Around 2 December 2022 (as reported), troops of Operation Forest Sanity who were on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia along Gyam-Manini-Kuriga-Udawa-Bukuru road (Chikun, Kaduna). The clash lasted for 25 minutes, the militiamen fled while the troops dislodged their camp, recovered one rifle, seven motorcycles, nine rounds of ammunition and one Boafeng radio charger.
On 2 December 2022, an unidentified armed group dressed in police and army uniforms abducted a man from his residence in Igbo-Ekhe (Etche, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 2 December 2022, suspected armed pastoralists in their numbers attacked worshippers at a mosque in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta). 11 persons were critically wounded, 3 worshippers were abducted, the police confirmed the attack and not the abduction.

On 2 December 2022, Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash after the militants invaded Waijroko (Damboa, Borno) in two MRAPs, six Hilux vehicles mounted with anti aircraft guns and fired multiple mortar bombs from the Gubub axis of the town. The troops also ambushed the militants who were fleeing, scores of militants were killed, coded as 20 in the gun battle which lasted for about 40 minutes.
On 2 December 2022, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a patrol of soldiers that attacked their position in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). One soldier was killed, the others fled.

On 2 December 2022, a Zamfara militia killed 12 persons including one farmer in simultaneous attacks in Nasarawa-Burkullu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Manya [coded separately]. Eleven persons including six farmers and five women were abducted, soldiers were seen rushing to the area to repel the attack but were unsuccessful. 12 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 6.
On 2 December 2022, a suspected Fulani militia killed two people when they attacked a farm in Gahweton (Takum, Taraba). One of the victims was a former councilor.

On 2 December 2022, a Sokoto militia abducted a six year old boy from Arkilla (Wamakko, Sokoto). The abductors demanded for the ransom in bitcoin, the abductee was released on 6 December, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons in Bom village, coded to nearby Rafin Kada (Wukari, Taraba). The abductees were rescued by troops of Operation Whirl Stroke, there are no reports of a clash.

On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Abule-Oke, Agbado, Olaogun and Ijoko communities in Ifo LGA (Ogun). At least three persons were shot and wounded, the commander of So-Safe corps claimed that three of the assailants were later arrested.

On 3 December 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai and Civilian JTF who were on a fighting patrol clashed with Boko Haram fighters [JAS] at Limanti, Loskori and Gaza villages (Mafa, Borno), Bulakulari and Gwari-Gwazo [coded separately]. 24 militants were killed, split across two events and coded as 12, 40 bicycles and other weapons used in attacking soldiers and civilians were recovered.

On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be loyalists of the Osun state governor attacked civilians when they invaded the house of a member of the PDP in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The house and three shops near the building were demolished, the owner of the house claimed that he was attacked over a petition he wrote to the screening committee of the PDP concerning the governor's certificate before the governorship primary elections.

On 3 December 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai and Civilian JTF who were on a fighting patrol clashed with Boko Haram fighters [JAS] at Bulakulari and Gwari-Gwazo coded to Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno), Limanti, Loskori and Gaza villages [coded separately]. 24 militants were killed, split across two events and coded as 12, 40 bicycles and other weapons used in attacking soldiers and civilians were recovered.

On 3 December 2022, some naval officers clashed with policemen in Satellite town (Amowo-Odofin, Lagos) following an argument which ensued after the policemen on patrol duty flagged down the soldiers who were dressed in plain clothes. One policeman was stabbed and killed by the soldiers, many passers-by who attempted to intervene and an unspecified number of policemen were also wounded by the soldiers. The navy claimed that the policeman was not stabbed to death, and that it was the policemen and a mob who started hitting the soldiers before a policeman shot in the air and dispersed the crowd.

On 3 December 2022, security operatives together with a reinforcement team from a police station clashed with an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins numbering 9 who attacked the house of a senator in Minna (Minna, Niger). The senator was not in the house, assailants were arrested and they claimed to have been informed that arms and foreign currency were in the house hence the invasion, other sources report that the arrested assailants claimed to have been sebt to abduct the senator.

On 3 December 2022, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians at Natsinta in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees incuded women and children, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted 8 residents of Anguwan Hausawa in Kwakwu community, coded to Kuje (Kuje, FCT). The abductors shot sporadically to scare of policemen from a police outpost, a ransom of 25 million naira was demanded.

On 3 December 2022, a Katsina militia numbering about 40 and riding on motorcycles attacked civilians and killed one person at Karare (Batsari, Katsina). 28 persons most of whom were students were abducted; one escaped, four others including 3 students were released and sent to inform the community that the ransom would be accepted in the new naira notes. Some sources report up to 30 abductees, others report less and two fatalities.

On 3 December 2022, hundreds of Boko Haram [JAS] fighters led by Ali Ngulde attacked and clashed with ISWAP fighters in the camp of Yuwe coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). At least 12 ISWAP fighters were killed and their weapons were seized. Other sources report that the JAS fighters ambushed ISWAP after a failed negotiation that was initiated by JAS.
On 3 December 2022, ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS] fighters clashed at Dollar land in Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). Dozens of fighters including women were killed, fatalities coded as 12.

On 3 December 2022, a Kaduna miitia killed two abductees out of the scores of travellers they abducted when they hijacked four vehicles along Kiyaya-Kititi road, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). The abductees were selected from the vehicles, one of the abductees who was a nursing mother was released, one escaped, ransom amounts within the range of 10 to 50 million naira have been demanded.

On 3 December 2022, a Katsina militia attacked worshippers at a mosque in Maigamji (Funtua, Katsina). Two worshippers including the chief imam were shot and wounded, 19 others were abducted; between 4 to 6 of the abductees were rescued between the night of 3 December and the morning of 4 December by policemen [no clash was reported].

On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be loyalists of the Kogi state governor and the APC, armed with guns machetes and sticks attacked the supporters of the PDP senatorial candidate of Kogi central senatorial district during a campaign rally. One person was shot, many others were wounded before the police intervened. The campaign began in Okene and ended at Adavi, coded to Ogaminana (Adavi, Okene).
On 3 December 2022, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a comedian along Ring Road, coded to Oke Ado (Ibadan South West, Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 3 December 2022, a Katsina militia killed one person in Sayaya (Matazu, Katsina) for resisting abduction.

Around 4 December 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a man at Serafu village, coded to Iseyin (Iseyin, Oyo). The abductee was released after a ransom of two million naira was paid.

On 4 December 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the Benue state commissioner for housing and urban development at Adankari (Ohimini, Benue) while he was en route Utonkon. The commissioner was abducted together with one of his in-laws and his driver and a ransom of 5 million naira was demanded. The commissioner was released on 6 December, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 4 December 2022, a suspected Katsina militia killed one person when they blocked the entrance to Wagini and Garin Ajiya villages (Batsari, Katsina).

On 4 December 2022, Boko Haram fighters divided themselves into two groups and raided ISWAP positions where they engaged them in armed clashes at Arra, Ukuba and Sabil Huda (Gwoza, Borno). More than 23 ISWAP fighters were killed, their weapons, motorcycles and bicycles were seized.

On 4 December 2022, security operatives [presumed to be policemen] killed a tricycle rider in Dutse Uku area, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau) following an altercation that started when the victim was stooped and questioned for riding his tricycle past the permitted hours.

Around 5 December 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia fleeing from a military operation in Zamfara killed two farmers in Shirkai village and abducted 19 persons from Warkata and Kairu, location coded to Wasagu (Danko, Kebbi). An estimated 6000 residents from different villages fled.

On 5 December 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai and Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] militants in Koshebe (Mafa, Borno) and Karkut [coded separately]. 4 militants were killed; split across two events and coded as 2, others fled, 6 newly established camps of the militants were destroyed, grenade, weapons and handsets were recovered by the troops.

On 5 December 2022, an unidentified armed group on a motorcycle attacked a checkpoint and clashed with policemen and Ebube Agu operatives in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One policeman and one of the assailants were killed, other sources report that two Ebube Agu operatives were also killed.

On 5 December 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai and Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] militants in Kurkut, Mafa LGA (Borno) and Koshebe [coded separately]. 4 militants were killed; split across two events and coded as 2, others fled, 6 newly established camps of the militants were destroyed, grenade, weapons and handsets were recovered by the troops.

On 5 December 2022, Boko Haram [JAS] fighters attacked and killed 33 wives of ISWAP militants as a reprisal following a number of clashes between the groups. ISWAP fighters had laid an ambush for the JAS fighters who made a detour an attacked the women instead. Location coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno).
On 5 December 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP militants in the vicinity of Konduga town (Konduga, Borno). Casualties unknown.

On 5 December 2022, a Sokoto militia numbering about 90 killed three policemen guarding a market and three civilians when they attacked Yar Bulutu market in Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto) and shot sporadically. The assailants set one of the policemen's vehicle ablaze and threw the body of one policeman into the fire, several other civilians sustained varying bullet wounds.

On 5 December 2022, ISWAP fighters led by Ba'ana Chigori attacked and clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] fighters at their position in Farisu, coded to Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). 15 JAS fighters including a unit commander Malam Aboubakar also were killed, and seven motorcycles were seized from them.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group shot at travelers at Uyanga Okpo Usun axis (Akamkpa, Cross River). One person was wounded, four other persons including a former accountant general of the state were abducted.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group shot at the bus conveying Kaduna state athletes to their hostel in Issele-Uku (Aniocha North, Delta). The assailants fled when they realized there were security operatives on board. There were no casualties.

On 6 December 2022, Nigerian army soldiers on clearance patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Fatika and Makera (Giwa, Kaduna), Idasu [coded separately]. Several militiamen were killed, coded as 3 and others fled to the Hayin Siddi area.

On 6 December 2022, policemen who were shooting sporadically killed a civilian that was hit by a stray bullet at Aja (Eti-Osa, Lagos). The policemen were raiding black market fuel seller in the area, the police command in the state claimed that the assailant was disarmed and arrested.

On 6 December 2022, a Taraba militia wounded one local and abducted 20 commuters along Kente-Chinkai road (Wukari, Taraba). The victims were rescued by troops of Operation Whirl Stroke after the militia abandoned them while they were being pursued.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group in large numbers raped women and stole farm produce which they harvested from farms in Chakumi (Gwagwalada, FCT). Six women were raped in attacks which lasted for 3 days. Residents fled the community.
Around 6 December 2022 (as reported), two unidentified cult militias clashed during a cult war at Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). At least three persons were killed.

On 6 December 2022, Nigerian army soldiers on clearance patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Idasu (Giwa, Kaduna), Fatika and Makera [coded separately]. Several militiamen were killed, coded as 3 and others fled to the Hayin Siddi area.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group raped women and stole farm produce which they harvested from farms at Tuduru in Gurdi ward (Abaji, FCT). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area.

On 6 December 2022, troops of Operation Hadin Kai on a fighting patrol intercepted ISWAP militants and engaged them in an armed clash at a crossing point in the Mainok axis (Kaga, Borno). 8 militants were killed, four motorcycles and other items including medicines and food stuff were recovered by the troops.
On 6 December 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in the vicinity of Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Casualties unknown.
On 6 December 2022, Nigerian troops shot at presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in the vicinity of Muna Dalti (Jere, Borno). Casualties unknown.
Around 6 December 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group raped women and stole farm produce which they harvested from farms in Paikon-Bassa and Kutura, coded to Abaji LGA (FCT).

On 6 December 2022, police forces repelled a Katsina militia when they blocked a cattle route along Tashar Maje in Kankara LGA (Katsina). Abductees and rustled cattle that were taken away from their village by the militia members [coded separately] were recovered.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT) and killed one person. One other person sustained gunshot wounds, between 9 and 10 persons including one NYSC member were abducted, two abductees later escaped and the assailants fled through a nearby hill, other sources reported that the assailants were robbers. The abducted NYSC corps member was released around 12 December after an undisclosed amount of ransom was paid.

On 6 December 2022, a Katsina militia abducted five villagers from Karo village (Musawa, Katsina). The militiamen also stole 43 cows, 86 sheep, two donkeys and three motorcycles which were all recovered by policemen who intercepted the militia [coded separately]. The abductees were also rescued.

On 6 December 2022, an unidentified armed group invaded a hospital and abducted four newly born babies at Nkpologwu (Aguata, Anambra). The reason for the abduction is unknown, the President-General of the community denied the report and insisted that it did not happen.

On 7 December 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two women along Ibillo-Igarra-Auchi road (Akoko Edo, Edo). The abductees were rescued on 12 December as a result of a rescue mission carried out by a team of policemen, soldiers, local defense militia and hunters [there are no reports of a clash].
On 7 December 2022, a Sokoto militia attacked commuters at Dogon Karfe village in Illela LGA (Sokoto) for plegding allegiance to another militia group. One driver was killed and another was abducted.
On 7 December 2022, Kashimbila and Kwande communal militias clashed at Kashimbila (Takum, Taraba). Five persons from Kwande were killed and five others from Kashimbila were wounded.

On 7 December 2022, an unidentified armed group in large numbers raped women and stole farm produce which they harvested from farms in Chakumi (Gwagwalada, FCT). Six women were raped in attacks which lasted for 3 days. Residents fled the community.

On 7 December 2022, soldiers and policemen clashed IPOB/ESN militants at Umuhu-Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu) following an attempt by the soldiers to allow a truck that local defense militiamen claimed was intercepted with armed Fulani pastoralists pass through the community. One ESN fighter was killed.

On 7 December 2022, soldiers and policemen wounded and arrested an unspecified number of civilians in Bodo (Gonaka, Rivers) as claimed by the residents of the area. The state police commissioner had earlier announced that operatives were drafted to the area to mop up arms which they had information were being stored in the community.
On 7 December 2022, a local defense militia clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists until they retreated at Isiado, coded to nearby Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). There are no further details.

Around 8 December 2022 (as reported), troops of the Nigerian army clashed with a Kaduna militia at a militia camp around Rafin Sarki in Giwa LGA (Giwa). Five militiamen were killed, many others fled and the camp was cleared by the troops.

On 8 December 2022, an unidentified armed group in large numbers raped women and stole farm produce which they harvested from farms in Chakumi (Gwagwalada, FCT). Six women were raped in attacks which lasted for 3 days. Residents fled the community.

On 8 December 2022, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Moroma hill in Mboi district (Song, Adamawa). On 31 December 2022, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen on patrol in an armed clash on the road by Okuvo and Eborede communities (Okpe, Delta). The assailants had abducted three civilians who they abandoned and fled.
On 31 December 2022, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with soldiers at a military checkpoint in Ubomiri (Mbaitoli, Imo). One student who was commuting was killed by stray bullet.

On 1 January 2023, troops of 222 batallion Konduga in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives intercepted and clashed Boko Haram [JAS] militants at Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Two militants were killed.

On 1 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with hunters clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] militants who abducted two civilians in the axis of Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The militants abandoned the abductees and fled.

On 1 January 2023, a Kaduna militia that attacked residents were engaged in an armed clash by a local defense militia in Anguwar Salanke, Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). On 1 January 2023, a policeman shot and killed two civilians at Filin Canada in Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). Three teenagers sustained gunshot wounds, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a woman in Owutu (Afikpo South, Ebonyi). On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a permanent secretary of Plateau state ministry of works from the entrance of his residence in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The abductee was rescued by policemen in Bassa LGA after the abductors abandoned him and his vehicle.

On 1 January 2023, a Zamfara militia in large numbers abducted 15 civilians who were traveling along Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara). The abductees were rescued after the militiamen abandoned them following a search and rescue operation by security operatives.

On 1 January 2023, a Zamfara militia in large numbers abducted a retired colonel, two of his children and two other persons near Yan Doton Daji (Tsafe, Zamfara). The abductors shot sporadically and scared people, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one man, abducted him and three other men at Baipe community in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 January 2023, policemen on patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along Gusau-Magami-Dansadau road (Gusau, Zamfara). One militia member was killed and the others fled, guns, ammunition and charms were recovered by the policemen.
On 2 January 2023, Waja and Lunguda militias clashed in Lafia (Lamurde, Adamawa). Over 4 houses and 11 shops were set ablaze, there were no fatalities.

On 2 January 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed the president-general of Obosi community in the community (Idemili South, Anambra). On 2 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a truck driver, wounded three labourers and abducted six other persons at Rudu village (Toto, Nassarawa). The driver had attempted to run away before he was killed, a ransom of 20 million has been demanded for the abductees' release.

On 2 January 2023, a Kaduna militia was engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops who responded to a distress call at Rafin Sarki village in Giwa LGA (Kaduna) for the second day in a row. Two militiamen were killed, split across two events coded as 1, and one rifle was recovered.

On 2 January 2023, Black Axe cult militia also known as Aiye and Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shibiri, Igbede and Imude areas of Ajangbadi (Ojo, Lagos). On 2 January 2023, a soldier shot and killed a civilian at Asokoro (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The soldier had tried to halt the motorcyclist's movement and shot at them which resulted in the death of the victim who was the passenger. The soldiers fled and abandoned the corpse.

On 2 January 2023, policemen repelled a Katsina militia in their numbers that attacked a police nipping point along Jibia-Katsina road (Jibia, Katsina). On 2 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed four persons at Okpuno (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants had pursued someone into the compound where the victims were and shot them, one of the victims was a PDP chairman in the area.
On 2 January 2023, Boko Haram [JAS] fighters clashed with ISWAP fighters at Garin Ba'aba in Bama LGA (Borno). An unspecified number of fighters were killed, coded as 3.
On 2 January 2023, Zamfara Communal militia attacked commuters around Kucheri, along the Funtua- Tsafe Road, coded to Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara) and abducted many people.
On 2 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed two persons at Ekeh Awka in Awka (Awka South, Anambra) during a cult related reprisal attack and battle for supremacy.

On 3 January 2023, the Nigerian military clashed with Kaduna Communal Militia around Tungan Rafin Toba village in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troop killed two militia members and recovered several weapons, including 2 AK47 rifles, 51 rounds of 7.62mm special, 4 AK47 riles magazines, five mobile phones, motorcycles and the sum of Two Hundred and Six thousand Naira (N206,000). 2 fatalities reported.

Around 3 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed one of the persons among the 16 others that were abducted on 11 November 2022 [coded separately] as they were returning to Gwombe (Kuje, FCT). The victim was killed over claims of non-cooperation by the abductors, the other abductees were relased after ransom.

On 3 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked residents in Nagi village at Gaambe-Ushin ward (Gwer West, Benue). Several people were injured by the assailants. Other sources report that two persons were wounded.

On 3 January 2023, Black Axe cult militia (also known as Aiye) and Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shibiri, Igbede and Imude areas of Ajangbadi (Ojo, Lagos). Two other militia members were killed, split across 7 events and coded as 0.

On 3 January 2023, Nigerian troops carried out an ambush operation against a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Rafin Taba (Giwa, Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed, two rifles, ammunition, money and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 3 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people around Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). 3 fatalities reported.

On 3 January 2023, ISWAP claimed its fighters attacked the JTF base in Shara, coded to Biu (Biu, Borno) with machine guns. They killed two JTF fighters, burnt houses and went away with some properties. 2 fatalities reported

On 3 January 2023, Hausa and Fulani ethnic militias clashed in a market at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo) following a fight between a Hausa and Fulani in the market. On 3 January 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia who rode on a motorcycle killed two commercial tricycle riders in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Other sources report one fatality and that the attack is cult related.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a hotelier at his farm in Serafu village, coded to Iseyin (Iseyin, Oyo). The commandant of Amotekun claimed that the abductee was released.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five family members along the Ochadamu- Ajaokuta road, coded to Ofu (Ofu, Kogi).
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who were on patrol in an armed clash in Nunku town (Akwanga, Nassarawa). Two of the assailants and one policeman were killed.

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed four persons in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The victims included a legislative leader in the area, two businessmen and one of their staff. The reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 4 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed two boys and dumped their bodies in a river in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The victims had been declared missing two days earlier, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Some sources report that the attack is a result of reprisal attacks between cult militias.
On 4 January 2023, Katsina Communal Militia abducted a woman along Wagini-Garin Dodo Road, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). No further details

On 4 January 2023, ISWAP claimed to have raided the headquarters of a local defense militia and killed two operatives in Chara, coded to Damaturu (Damaturu, Yobe). The militants also claimed to have set a number of houses ablaze.

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 25 invaded the office of the Anambra vigilante service and killed one operative at Ndikokwu village in Uli (Ihiala, Anambra).
