On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group of eight shot at communter in a vehicle around Kabba junction (Kabba, Kogi). Some of the bullets hit the car and tyres, the commuters were able to escape.

On 4 January 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Karfi (Malumfashi, Katsina) after the militia had abducted one civilian from his residence in the area. On 4 January 2023, Hausa and Fulani ethnic militias clashed in a market at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo) for the second day in a row, following a fight between a Hausa and Fulani in the market. On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man and abandoned his body in his car in Nawfia (Njikoka, Anambra). The victim was discovered with marks of violence and a suspected gunshot injury.

On 5 January 2023, Sokoto Communal Militia attacked Gidan Altine village, coded to Illela (Illela, Sokoto) and shot indiscriminately at the people; One person was shot dead in the attack. 1 fatality reported.
On 5 January 2023, the Obudu Communal group and the Tiv ethnic militia clashed along the Vande Ikya - Obudu road, coded to VandeIkya (VandeIkya, Benue). Casualties unknown.

On 5 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked residents in Tse-Girgi Dajo village at Gaambe-Ushin ward (Gwer West, Benue). One person was injured by the assailants. Other sources report that two persons were wounded.
On 5 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man in Ukpor town (Nnewi South, Anambra). There are no further details.
On 5 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted another at Mosogar (Ethiope West, Delta). The murdered victim was shot when he resisted being abducted.

On 5 January 2023, Sokoto Communal militias abducted two commuters at Isa Junction, Isa (Isa, Sokoto).

On 5 January 2023, a suspect unidentified cult militia killed one person and dumped the body in Akure metropolis (Akure South, Ondo). The victim's body was burnt and put in a metal box, his identity is unknown. Other sources report that the attack was a result of an ongoing cult war.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man in Chigari, Fufore (Fufore, Adamawa), when resisting abduction. A five-member armed group attempted to abduct the man but later shot him when he resisted. 1 fatality reported.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a girl in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano) and demanded a ransom of two million naira for her release. The police arrested three teenagers of 19 years old as suspects of abduction.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the police at the residence of the Plateau State House of Assembly's speaker in the Federal Low-Cost Housing, coded to Riyom (Jos South, Plateau). On 7 January 2023, the Nigerian troops raided the enclaves of the Zamfara communal militia in Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Anka LGA, coded separately. The military recovered weapons and ammunition from the militiamen.

On 7 January 2023, the Zamfara communal militia abducted an unspecified number of people, including the former District Head of Birnin Tsaba village, along Birnin Tsaba- Daura Road, coded to Dauran Birnin Tsaba (Zurmi, Zamfara).

On 7 January 2023, the Deebam Cult militia set fire to a house in Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers) and killed the occupant. On 7 January 2023, the Nigerian troops raided the enclaves of the Zamfara communal militia in Anka (Anka, Zamfara) and Bukkuyum LGA, coded separately. The military recovered weapons and ammunition from the militiamen. Casualties unknown.

On 7 January 2023, Zamfara communal militia attacked Duhuwar Saulawa, coded to Anka (Anka, Zamfara) and killed an unspecified number of people (coded as 3). Many people were also injured in the attack.

On 7 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked INEC PVC collection centers in Ikpoba Okha LG, coded to Idogbo (Ikpoba Okha, Edo) for the second day. On 8 January 2023, the Nigerian Police shot and killed a member for a Zamfara militia in Maradun LGA, coded to LGA HQ, Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The police recovered some weapons from the militia. 1 fatality reported.

Around 8 January 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) abducted four teenage girls suspected to be wives of the ISWAP at Kaula village, Kaula (Abadan, Borno). The girls fled after ISWAP fighters were defeated in the North of Kayowa and Tumbun Gini.

On 8 January 2023, Fulani herders attacked and killed a farmer in Eshijiko, Pada or Kpada (Pategi, Kwara) during an altercation. On 8 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the Chief of Staff to the Osun State House of Assembly Speaker at the Ifofin area of Ilesa (Ilesha West, Osun). The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment.
On 8 January 2023, Zamfara communal militia invaded Marakaye Village, coded to Kanwa (Zurmi, Zamfara) and shot an unspecified number of people dead. Unspecified fatality coded as 3.
On 8 January 2023, Zamfara communal militia shot and killed one person and abducted three others in Bola village, Gusau LGA, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). 1 fatality reported.

On 9 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a 70-year-old man in Dan village, Dan (Alkaleri, Bauchi). The armed group invaded the community, shot the victim repeatedly and fled on sighting the police. 1 fatality reported.

On 9 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the President of Igueben Area Customary Court in Ugoneki (Igueben, Edo) on her way to court.

On 9 January 2023, Katsina communal militia indiscriminately shot and injured an unspecified number of people in Sabon Garin Bilbis village, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). No casualty was reported.

On 9 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a former Edo State House of Assembly member at Ubiaja (Esan South East, Edo) while travelling to Abuja.

On 10 January 2023, the Nigerian Police, supported by the local hunters, clashed with unidentified armed group around Dajin Madam and Yankari National Park ( Alkaleri, Bauchi). On 10 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted about 15 people, including the community leader from the Oluwalose community, Oko-Olowo (Ilorin West, Kwara). The kidnappers invaded the community on motorcycles and took their victims away.

On 10 January 2023, Katsina Communal Militia abducted a woman in Dustin Ma quarters in Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). The militiamen also went away with a motorcycle and mobile phones. An unspecified number of domestic animals were rustled. No casualty reported.

On 11 January 2023, Zamfara Communal Militia shot and killed a man and injured two others in Kanoma (Maru, Zamfara). No further details. 1 fatality reported.

The police recovered two locally made pistols, live ammunition, and one motorcycle. 1 fatality reported.

On 11 January 2023, the Kaduna Communal militia shot and killed a Chairman of Fityanul Islam First Aid group and his nephew in Unguwar Mai Awo village, coded to Turunku (Igabi, Kaduna). The militia also abducted four women, including a nursing mother. 2 fatalities reported.
On 11 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two farmers in Ileogbo (Aiyedire, Osun) while returning from the farm. The abductors demanded a ransom of N10 million.
On 11 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person at Orie Utuh (Nnewi South, Anambra). No further details.
On 11 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person along the Amichi-Ekwulumili-Okigwe Road, coded to Amichi (Nnewi South, Anambra). No further details.

On 11 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man in Ushapa (Bwari, FCT) and abducted his family members. The victim was reported to have wrestled with the assailants before he was shot. 1 fatality reported.

The assailants dismantled the canopies and the public address system arranged by the party. Many NNPP members fled the scene.

On 12 January 2023, the Nigerian police clashed with Niger Communal Militia in Maje Village, coded to Nasko (Magama, Niger). The police shot and killed one of the militia members and recovered his AK-49 rifle. Others escaped with gun wounds. 1 fatality reported.

On 12 January 2023, the Nigerian police clashed with Niger Communal militia in New Bussa (Borgu, Niger). The militiamen were trying to collect a ransom to release some hostages in their captivity when the police engaged them. The police killed three militiamen and freed the hostages unharmed. They also recovered one pump action rifle with four cartridges and two single-barrel guns. 3 fatalities reported.

On 12 January 2023, the Nigerian Police clashed with an unidentified armed group in Ihiala (Ihiala, Anambra) while responding to a distress call over the attack on the community. The assailants had killed four members of the state vigilante group and burnt many houses, coded separately, before the police engaged them in an arms fight. The police killed one of the assailants and recovered two locally-made IED launchers, seven undetonated IEDs, 40 pieces of live cartridges, 15 live 7.62MM AK-47 ammunition, knives, charms, and other weapons. 1 fatality reported.

On 12 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and abducted the Divisional Police Officer in charge of the Pankshin Division in Pankshin (Pankshin, Plateau). He was attacked in his hotel room before they took him away.

On 12 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed 4 members of the Anambra Vigilante group in Ihiala (Ihiala, Anambra). The assailants beheaded one of the corpses and went away with the head. They burnt five buildings with an IED. The affected buildings included the Local Government headquarters and the Independent Electoral Commission's (INEC) building. 4 fatalities reported.

On 12 January 2023, the Nigerian security forces clashed with unidentified armed men in Ugoneki (Igueben, Edo) while trying to rescue the President of the Igueben Area Customary Court abducted by the militiamen. The President of the Customary Court was rescued with gun wounds, and the armed men shot a police officer dead in the operation. 1 fatality reported.

Around 12 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group suspected of being soldiers attacked PDP members in Idanre (Idanre, Ondo). Casualties unknown. Shops were destroyed. PDP accused the attackers of being APC supporters.
On 12 January 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with a local defense militia, shooting and killing two militia members in Amukpe (Sapele, Delta). No further details. 2 fatalities reported.
On 12 January 2023, the Islamic State fighters attacked and killed four members of the Civilian JTF with machine guns in Marte (Marte, Borno). 4 fatalities reported.
On 13 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and stole valuables when they attacked Ubiaji community, coded to Ajaka (Igalamela, Kogi).

On 13 January 2023, the Nigerian police raided an enclave of the Kaduna Communal Militia in the Warsa Piti Area of Saminaka Lere LGA, coded to Mariri (Lere, Kaduna). The police arrested two militiamen and recovered a locally fabricated GPMG Rifle with six rounds of live ammunition and a Dane gun. No casualty was reported.

On 13 January 2023, the Nigerian troop of the Guard Brigade and the JTF raided enclaves of militias in Idu Chikara, along the boundaries of Toto Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, Abaji FCT and Koton Karfe in Kogi, coded to Umaish (Toto, Nassarawa). Two militias were killed, and 30 abductees were rescued in the operation. The troop recovered one Rapid Propelled Grenade Tube and several military uniforms. 2 fatalities reported.
On 13 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at her residence at Technical College Area in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). No further details.

On 13 January 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops of 25 brigades of Operation Hadin Kai in Azir OR Ajir (Damboa, Borno) with three mine-resistant ambush-protected (MRAP) vehicles and four gun trucks. The troops, supported by air components, repelled the attack and engaged the militia in a heavy gun battle that killed many ISWAP fighters. Unknown casualties codes as 3.

On 13 January 2023, the Islamic State fighters attacked the Nigerian Army headquarters in Azare (Hawul, Borno). IS claimed to have killed and wounded many soldiers and destroyed an armoured vehicle. The also seized some weapons and ammunition from the Nigerian troops. Unknown casualties coded as 3.

On 13 January 2023, the Nigerian Police exchanged gunshots with an unidentified armed group around the Unukpo - Orogun palm tree plantation, Orogun (Ughelli North, Delta). The armed group, suspected of being armed robbers, gathered in their enclave. The gunfight ensued when the police invaded their enclave in the palm tree plantation. The police killed one of them, and others fled. 1 fatality reported.

On 14 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the Parish Priest of St. George's Catholic Church, Omu Ekiti, between Itaji-Ekiti and Ijelu-Ekiti, coded to Itaji (Oye, Ekiti). Reverend Father was returning from the state Capital when he was abducted. The abductee was released around 17 January, there are no details about ransom payment.

On 14 January 2023, a militia from Lambada killed the District Head of the Lambata community, headquarters of Gurara LGA, in Lambata (Gurara, Niger) over a chieftaincy tussle among some royal houses and villages in the LGA. 1 fatality reported.

On 14 January 2023, an unidentified armed group in military uniform abducted four tipper truck drivers in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The victims are members of the Oyun Garage branch of the Association of Quarry and Sand dealers who went to convey sand for construction work.

On 14 January 2023, an unidentified armed group invaded the residence of the CUPP 's spokesperson in the Umukegwu community, Akokwa (Ideato North, Imo), when he was meeting with some of his supporters. The armed group shot and killed four persons, including the PDP's candidate for Ideato north and south constituency for the Federal House of Representatives. They also burnt some vehicles. 4 fatalities reported.
On 14 January 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked commuters, wounded two people and abducted three others along Kaura Namoda-Birnin Magaji road (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara).

On 14 January 2023, the Nigerian Police, supported by the KADVS local vigilance group clashed with Kaduna Communal Militia in Amana Maimadachi village, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). The police responded to a distress call from the village and thwarted the kidnapping attempt by the militiamen. A militiaman in a military camouflage uniform was shot dead, and the rest escaped with gun wounds. The police recovered an AK47 Rifle with four rounds of live ammunition from the militia. 1 fatality reported

On 14 January 2023, a Kaduna militia invaded a residence and were engaged in an armed clash by Nigerian troops who mobilized to the scene at Amana Madachi village in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds.

On 14 January 2023, policemen of Surulere Area C command killed a tricycle rider in Surulere (Surulere, Lagos) following the victim's refusal to pay them a bribe. The victim was with his girlfriend and they were both assaulted before the victim passed out and eventually died.

On 15 January 2023, Niger Communal Militia attacked a Reverend Father of Saint Peter and Paul Catholic Church in his house in Kafin Koro (Paikoro, Niger). The militiamen set the house on fire and burnt the Reverend Father alive when they couldn't access his house. A colleague of the father was shot in the shoulder when trying to escape from the scene. It was reported that the militia members divided themselves into two; a group went to the father's residence, and the other stood guard in town to prevent interference. 1 fatality reported.

On 15 January 2023, MNJTF troops repelled the Boko Haram (JAS) fighters' attack on their base in the Bakassi area, Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The troops engaged the militia in gun fights and killed scores of their fighters. An AK-47 rifle with two loaded magazines, including mobile phones and five new motorcycles, were recovered from the Militia. Scores fatalities coded as 20.

On 15 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a policeman and injured another during an attack on the INEC office in Amechi Awkunanaw, Amechi (Enugu South, Enugu). The armed group razed the gatehouse of the office when they failed to access the building. 1 fatality reported.

Around 15 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group, numbering about twenty men, shot and killed a security guard as they attacked the INEC office in Oru (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo). The armed group suspected to be Eastern Security Network (ESN), dressed in the ESN uniform, invaded the INEC office in search of the officers distributing the permanent cards. The assailants were heard shouting, 'No elections in Biafra Land.' 1 fatality reported.

On 15 January 2023, Zamfara Militia abducted four Tsafe College of Health Technology students along Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji roads, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The students were abducted when returning from their wedding ceremony. The abductees were rescued around 28 July as claimed by the state police command.

On 15 January 2023, Nigeria security forces clashed with an unidentified armed group in Akokwa (Ideato North, Imo). The Nigeria military invaded the camp of the armed group and engaged them in gun fights. The clash resulted in the death of some of the armed group members and the arrest of others. Unknown casualties coded as 3.
On 15 January 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one person and rustled livestock when they attacked Yarbarde and Joddo communities in Kware LGA (Sokoto).

On 15 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of persons including a naval officer [presumed to be off-duty] at Upper Iweka, coded to Fegge (Onisha South, Anambra). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 15 January 2023, Katsina Communal Militia attacked a church (New Life for All) in Jan Tsauri, Gidan Haruna, Kankara LGA, coded to Kankara (Kankara, Katsina). The militiamen shot and injured the pastor and abducted five women from the church.

On 15 January 2023, the Eiye cult militia and Aro Bagger or Arobaga clashed around the Ekosodin Area of Benin City (Oredo, Edo) and killed four militiamen from both sides. The clash broke out when the Aro Bagger mistakenly shot and killed an Eiye member over a conflicting issue between them and the Black Axe. 4 fatalities reported.

On 15 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a woman along the Oda road, coded to Akure (Akure South, Ondo). The victim was trailed and stabbed to death by the assailants, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 15 January 2023, troops of the Nigerian Army raided hideouts of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash in the vicinity of Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). An unspecified number of militiamen and their leader were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons in Kogi State, coded to Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The three men took a ransom to the armed group to release two persons earlier abducted in Osun State. They released the first two hostages and held the ransom bearers. One of the ransom-bearers was released on Tuesday.
On 16 January 2023, an unidentified armed group fired indiscriminately along Onitsha-Owerri road in Ihiala LGA (Anambra). No fatality reported.

On 16 January 2023, Kaduna militia abducted eight persons including 6 women in Unguwar Alkasim village along Kaduna-Zaria in Igabi LGA, coded to Birnin Yero (Iagbi, Kaduna). The militiamen invaded the community and shot sporadically before abducting eleven people but released 3 of them later. They went away with six women and two men.

Around 16 January 2023 (week of), Sokoto militia attacked seventeen villages in Rabah LGA, Rabah (Rabah, Sokoto) and Kware LGA, coded separately. Three persons were killed, and many domestic animals were rustled. 3 fatalities were shared within two events. 2 fatalities reported.

Around 16 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a Keke rider around Ujevwu Junction in Ujevwu (Udu, Delta). His body was found by residents who called the police.
On 16 January 2023, a Katsina militia abducted a Local Government Vice Chairman from his residence at Kira village (Musawa, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom payment.

Around 16 January 2023 (week of), Sokoto militia attacked seventeen villages in Kware LGA, Rabah (Kware, Sokoto) and Rabah LGA, coded separately. Three persons were killed, and many domestic animals were rustled. 3 fatalities were shared within two events. 1 fatality reported.

On 16 January 2023, Katsina militia abducted the Vice Chairman of Musawa Local Government in his village in Paiki, coded to Dangani (Musawa, Katsina). The militia abducted a man with him and released the man later but declined to release the Vice Chairman.

On 16 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at civilians in a car at Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The victims escaped, one of them sustained gunshot wounds and was taken to the hospital while their car was riddled with bullets. The assailants proceeded to abduct 2 commercial motorcyclists and robbed houses around before they fled into the bush.
On 17 January 2023, a Katsina militia abducted five persons from Dogon Ruwa village (Dutsinma, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 17 January 2023 (week of), the Nigerian troops raided the Kaduna militia's camps in the Kutura-Rijana area, coded to Rijana (Kachia, Kaduna). The troops destroyed the camps and recovered three motorcycles and many sets of military uniforms after the militiamen had fled. No casualty reported.

On 17 January 2023, the Nigerian troops of Operation Forest Sanity clashed with the Katsina Militia along Maidabino-Danmusa Road, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). Two militiamen were shot and killed during the gunfights. 2 fatalities reported.

On 17 January 2023, the Nigerian police shot and killed a trader at Alaba Rago Market, Alaba (Ojo, Lagos), when trying to arrest a suspect. Some traders prevented the police from arresting the suspect and threw different objects at them. In response, a police officer opened fire and killed one of them. 1 fatality reported.

On 17 January 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed a farmer and abducted eight others in Makilwe village, coded to Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). The militiamen contacted the victims' families and asked for millions of naira as a ransom. 1 fatality reported.

On 17 January 2023, Katsina militia shot and killed three people in Jajar Kanwa village, coded to Jibia (Jibia, Katsina) and abducted six others, including a pregnant woman. The militiamen were armed with AK-47 rifles and arrived at the community at 2 am on motorcycles. They rustled domestic animals, stole money and handsets, and gave the villagers a seven-day ultimatum to contribute twenty thousand naira each. 3 fatalities reported.
On 17 January 2023, a Katsina militia abducted the APC ward chairman of Faskari ward from his residence in Faskari town (Faskari, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 17 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an inspector of police while patrolling Iheorji Ohanku Road, Aba (Aba South, Abia). The police shot and killed two militiamen and others escaped with gun wounds. The militiamen carted away an AK-47 rifle belonging to the deceased officer. 3 fatalities reported.

On 17 January 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with Kaduna Militia along the Kaboresha-Rijana Forest-Kuzo-Kujeni-Gwanto-Kachia axis, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). The army ambushed the militia in a clearance operation and killed two militiamen. Three motorcycles were recovered. 2 fatalities reported.

On 17 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons from Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The victims were a landlord and his tenant who is a member of the NYSC. There are no ransom demands yet.

On 18 January 2023, suspected herdsmen killed three persons and abducted 13 others in Emokpae, coded to Egbeta (Ovia North East, Edo). Some of the victims were women. Some children returning from school were also abducted. The abduction provoked a peaceful protest by the community, coded separately. 3 fatalities reported.

On 18 January 2023, a Kaduna militia killed six persons and wounded an unspecified number of others when they fired indiscriminately in Zonkwa community (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). One other person was abducted.

Around 18 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked and tortured a man in Orifite (Ekwusigwo, Anambra). They also riddled the man's car with bullets for wearing a campaign T-shirt of the Labour Party. The armed group were heard saying that anyone caught wearing or putting on any campaign material of politicians would be severely dealt with.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with a militia from Kebbi state, during a clearance operation in Munhaye, Awala, Mairairai and Kabari villages in Danko- Wasagu, coded to Wasgu (Wasagu, Danko) and Maru LGA, coded separately. The troop destroyed four vehicles and eight motorcycles and recovered three AK 47 rifles, one SMG, 32 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, and other items. 7 militiamen were killed in the clash. 7 fatalities shared between the events, coded to 4.
On 18 January 2023, IPOB's military wing, the Eastern Security Network, attacked the Agwa Central Vigilante group in Agwa, Oguta (Oguta, Imo) and burned down their facilities. No fatality reported.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigerian Police repelled IPOB's attack on their station in Agwa, Oguta (Oguta, Imo). IPOB proceeded to the station after attacking the Agwa Central Vigilante group, coded separately. The police shot and killed three IPOB fighters. 3 fatalities reported.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigeria Police shot and killed two members of an armed group along Ughelli/Patani expressway, coded to Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta) and arrested another. The armed group had abducted a man before the police clashed with them. The police rescued the victim and recovered two locally made guns and three live cartridges. 2 fatalities reported.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Katsina militia in Dangeza, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina) and killed a militiaman. The troops recovered an AK 47 rifle mounted on a motorcycle with two magazines and one Baofeng HHR. 1 fatality reported.

On 18 January 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with a militia from Zamfara state during a clearance operation in Munhaye, Awala, Mairairai and Kabari villages in Maru, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara) and Danko- Wasagu LGA, coded separately. The troop destroyed four vehicles and eight motorcycles and recovered three AK 47 rifles, one SMG, 32 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, and other items. 7 militiamen were killed in the clash. 7 fatalities shared between the events. 3 fatalities reported.

On 19 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and abducted the Sole Administrator of the Ideato North Local Government Area of Imo State with two others in the Imoko community, Arondizuogu or Ndizuogu (Ideato North, Imo). The administrator was shot in the leg and was abducted after setting his house on fire. Another source reported that the APC party chairman of the area was abducted together with the sole Administrator.

On 19 January 2023, IPOB militants clashed with policemen when they attempted to attack the Njaba divisional police headquarters in Umuaka (Njaba, Imo). The police repelled the attack, one of the militants was killed, an unspecified number of others were shot and wounded and weapons were recovered.

On 19 January 2023, an unidentified armed group fired shots during the PDP political campaign, coded to Ewu (Esan Central, Edo). Casualties unknown. The Speaker of Edo State House of Assembly and other PDP leaders were evacuated to safety.

On 19 January 2023, Kaduna militia abducted the Catechist of St. Monica Catholic Church, Ikulu-Pari, in Chawai, Fadan Chawai (Kauru, Kaduna). The armed group targeted the Reverend Father but picked up the catchiest when the father could not be found. The abductee was released on 21 January, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 19 January 2023, suspected Fulani herdsmen shot and killed eight persons in the Abagana community, Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). The victims, including a family of six members, were wiped out in the attack. Another source reported that some victims were beheaded, and the assailants went away with their heads. Two victims were IDPs, as the community is opposite the IDP camp. 8 fatalities reported.

On 19 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at one person and kidnapped three others at Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu). It is unclear whether the one that was shot at died or was wounded, he was shot for confronting the assailants.
On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a first-class traditional ruler in Plateau State in Shere (Jos East, Plateau). The police rescued the monarch a few hours after his abduction.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two members of APC in Mkpuma Akataka, Izi LGA, coded to Izi (Izzi, Ebonyi). The party members were holding a meeting in the community when two members of the armed group arrived on motorcycles and opened fire on them. The wounded ones were taken to the hospital. 2 fatalities reported.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the returning Internally Displaced Persons of Tiv origin in Tor-lorlumun Rafin Kada (Wukari, Taraba). The attackers macheted the IDPs and destroyed their belongings.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a traditional ruler with his two wives and six children in Mutum Biyu (Gassol, Taraba). The armed group shot sporadically to scare away the community's people and successfully took away the monarch and his family members. One of the abductees escaped, the decomposing bodies of the other 7 were found [coded separately]

On 20 January 2023, The Niger Militia shot and killed the Allawa Ward Councillor in Shiroro LGA on his way from Kuta to Allawa coded to Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). The councillor was with another person on a motorcycle when they encountered the militia who shot them dead. 2 fatalities reported.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group raped nine female students when they invaded their hostel in Awka North (Awka North, Anambra) coded to Awba. The assailants also robbed the students of valuables.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted six pupils of the LGEA Primary School, Alwaza, in Doma (Doma, Nasarawa). The pupils were kidnapped as they arrived at the school premises early in the morning. Two female pupils among the abductees were rescued around 21 January, in Obi LGA after pressure was mounted on the abductors; the remaining four abductees were rescued around 3 February, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 20 January 2023, the Nigerian police clashed with an unidentified armed group in Shere (Jos East, Plateau). The armed group abducted the paramount traditional ruler of Izere, Plateau State, and opened fire on the police attempting to rescue the monarch. A civilian guard was shot dead, and a police officer sustained a gun injury during the rescue operation. 1 fatality reported.

On 20 January 2023, the Nigerian police engaged an unidentified cult militia in a gun battle in the Oke Baale, Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The cult militias had engaged each other in gunfights before the police intervened. On sighting the policemen, one of the groups opened fire on them. The police responded with superior firepower, and the militia fled. No fatality reported.

On 20 January 2023, two unidentified rival cult groups clashed in Oke Baale, Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The clash ensued when one of the militia groups abducted a member of the other group leading to an exchange of gunshots. Two passer-bys were hit and died. 2 fatalities reported.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three farmers on their farm at Ologun area in Iwo (Iwo, Osun). The abductees who are Fulani were abducted after the target of the abduction was not found, a ransom of 5 million naira was demanded.

On 20 January 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash when they invaded Oguta police station (Oguta, Imo) and threw explosives at the facility. One policeman was killed, some of the assailants escaped with gunshot wounds.
On 20 January 2023, a policeman shot and killed a civilian at his home in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano) following a misunderstanding between the victim and the policeman the previous day.

On 20 January 2023, troops of sector 3 of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with the MNJTF clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Monguno (Monguno, Borno) and foiled the militants attack. Two militants were killed while some others fled with gunshot wounds, five abductees were rescued, a rifle, two loaded magazines and other items were recovered.

On 20 January 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity engaged Jukun and Tiv ethnic militia in an armed clash at Fiindi area of Makurdi LGA (Benue) in an attempt to stop a clash that was going on between the two groups [coded separately]. The clash lasted for about one hour and the militiamen fled through River Benue on canoes, there were no fatalities.

On 20 January 2023, Tiv and Jukun ethnic militias engaged in an armed clash over a fish pond and a parcel of land in the Fiidi area of Makurdi LGA (Benue). Three persons from the two ethnic groups were wounded, one house was set ablaze before the militiamen fled after soldiers reached the location and engaged them in a clash [coded separately].

On 21 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed Ebubeagu's Commander (Southeast Security Network) at his home in Ogboji, Ezza North LGA., coded to Okposi (Ezza North, Ebonyi). The armed group took away his gun and motorcycle. 1 fatality reported.

On 21 January 2023, APC loyalists attacked a musician at a burial ceremony at the lodge of the Chairman of Ohaozara LGA in Obiozara (Ohaozara, Ebonyi). The victim was beaten and wounded for refusing to sing a campaign song for the APC presidential candidate at the request of APC supporters.

On 21 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three persons including a Ebube Agu commander who was at his home and presumed to be unarmed in Mkpuma Akataka (Izzi, Ebonyi) and stole his gun and motorcycle. The assailants invaded the area on a motorcycle and shot sporadically, the police insisted that there was no proof of political motivation in the attack. Other sources report that the other two victims were APC members who were in a party meeting.

On 21 January 2023, policemen in collaboration with soldiers and hunters trailed and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash following the abduction of two civilians by the group on their way from Garkida (Gombi, Adamawa). One of the abductors was killed, others fled with bullet wounds and one locally made rifle was recovered.

On 21 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed five civilians including the hamlet head when they invaded Gwadar Sabon Layi, coded to Tafawa-Balewa (Tafawa Balewa, Bauchi). One other person was abducted by the assailants who shot sporadically into the air to scare residents, other sources report four fatalities.

On 21 January 2023, suspected armed PDP loyalists attacked the secretariat of Accord Party at Igbo-Ekhe (Etche, Rivers) as claimed by the party's gubernatorial candidate who also insisted that the assailants were organized by the council chairman.

On 21 January 2023, suspected armed PDP loyalists attacked the convoy of the gubernatorial candidate of Accord Party in Etche, coded to Igbo-Ekhe (Etche, Rivers). The candidate was visiting the area following an attack on the party's secretariat which he claimed was carried out by the same assailants [coded separately] who were organized by the council chairman. There were no fatalities, vehicles were damaged.

On 21 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives intercepted and killed one Boko Haram [JAS faction] militant between the border between Nigeria and Cameroon, coded to Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno) where the militants were headed. One other militant was arrested, some food items that they had purchased were recovered by the troops.

On 21 January 2023, policemen beat up some students when they invaded a private hostel at Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The policemen were armed, broke down some doors of student's rooms and claimed to be in search of internet fraudsters. The victims were beaten after they claimed to not know any fraudsters.

On 21 January 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants ambushed Nigerian military forces that were escorting a civilian convoy at Nyaleri village (Damboa, Borno). The troops engaged the militants in an armed clash until they fled, casualties are unknown.

On 22 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted Fulani pastoralist when they invaded a ranching settlement at Awba-Ofemili (Awka North, Anambra). 15 cows were killed by the assailants in the attack, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 22 January 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Daddara community (Jibia, Katsina). Casualties are unknown.

Around 22 January 2023 (as reported), policemen and a local defense militia clashed with a Fulani militia that invaded Mkpunando-Aguleri, coded to Aguleri (Anambra East, Anambra) and repelled them. The assailants fled, their cattle also destroyed farms in the area. There were no casualties.

On 22 January 2023, a Niger militia attacked civilians at Kuta town (Shiroro, Niger), killed three persons and abducted three others. The car of the local council chairman was shot at and damaged with bullets, he and the other occupants of the car escaped, the assailants also rustled cattle at Egwa village [coded separately].

On 22 January 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about four killed one civilian at Nkpikpa, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra). The assailants who were in a tricycle took away the victim's belongings and shot sporadically, one of the assailants was hit by a bullet and died. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 22 January 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person when they invaded a residence at Unguwar Dutsin Ma Quarters in Batsari town (Batsari, Katsina). The victim sustained machete cuts from an attempt to disarm one of the assailants, his motorcycle and an unspecified number of cattle were rustled.

On 22 January 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked positions of Boko Haram [JAS faction] and engaged them in an armed clash during a reprisal attack at Mantari and Maimusari also called Gaizuwa in Bama LGA (Borno). Several fighters were killed and their makeshift homes were destroyed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 22 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the sole administrator of Ideato North LGA of Imo state, who was abducted alongside two others [coded separately] at Imoko community, Arondizuogu or Ndizuogu (Ideato North, Imo). The victim was beheaded by the assailants after they collected 6 million naira as ransom, location coded to where he was abducted from.

On 22 January 2023, a Niger militia clashed with soldiers when they invaded about seven communities including Kadna, Chiri, Vemu and Kam in Shiroro LGA (Niger). Many civilians were wounded, the state commissioner for internal security and humanitarian affairs claimed that some soldiers were also wounded and two civilians were killed. One person was abducted from Kadna and the assailants also raided food barns and stole cattle in large numbers.
On 22 January 2023, a Nigerien militia killed one civilian and abducted eleven others from Abaga village in Irina ward (Shiroro, Niger). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 23 January 2023, a policeman hit and wounded a pap trader following a confrontation over a traffic accident in Owode area of Oyo town (Oyo West, Oyo).

On 23 January 2023, policemen in collaboration with local hunters and a local defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group at a forest in Bode Saadu (Moro, Kwara) based on intelligence gathered about the group's activities. Three members of the armed group were killed, two others were arrested with locally made guns.

On 23 January 2023, policemen on a routine check engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash along Eyenkorin, coded to Oko-Olowo (Ilorin West, Kwara). Some members of the armed group escaped with bullet wounds, one of them was later found with wounds and was arrested.

On 23 January 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with Anambra state vigilante service operatives along Ifite road, Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The clash led to a heavy presence of security operatives in the area, there were no fatalities.

On 23 January 2023, ISWAP fighters ambushed troops of the 25th Task Force Brigade, Operation Hadin Kai who were on a fighting patrol and engaged them in an armed clash at Komala in Damboa LGA (Borno). The air task force supported the troops; sources report 23 - 33 fatalities, others fled with gunshot wounds and the troops recovered one gun truck, an MRAP, three motorcycles, medical supplies and other items.

On 23 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP fighters in Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The militants fired a few shots and fled after the troops responded. Casualties are unknown.
On 23 January 2023, Nigerian military forces killed two suspected IPOB militants at the border between Orsu Ihiteukwa (Orsu, Imo) and Orsumoghu in Anambra state.

Around 23 January 2023 (as reported), Supreme Vikings and Ciao-Sons cult militias clashed in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). There were no fatalities but 6 were injured. The clashes are reprisal attacks Mafia following the death of a Vikings member in December 2022.

On 23 January 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two farmers on their farms in Toru-Angiama (Patani, Delta). The bodies of the victims were discovered on their farm, other sources report that the victims who were a father and son met the pastoralists destroying their crops, one member of the community was wounded and several others were abducted.

On 24 January 2023, a Zamfara militia clashed with a local defense militia at Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara) after the local militia chased them following a failed attack on farmers. The Zamfara militia called for reinforcement that arrived and fired grenades, there were no fatalities and the assailants fled. The undetonated grenades were recovered the following day and handed over to the appropriate authorities.

On 24 January 2023, PDP and APC supporters clashed in Ikire (Isokan, Osun) after the parties' senatorial candidates for Osun West senatorial district set their campaign rallies on the same day. The APC candidate claimed that the assailants were led by his PDP opponent, the PDP candidate claimed that two of his supporters were killed and others were wounded, the police confirmed the clash and one fatality and that some others were wounded.

On 24 January 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity clashed with a Kaduna militia and foiled their attack around the Udawa-Manini axis (Chikun, Kaduna). 15 civilians were rescued, some of whom were wounded and taken to the hospital.

On 24 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her daughter around Otaefun/Kobongboe axis of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) while they were returning home from her shop. A ransom of 5 million naira was demanded to be paid via the abductee's bank account. The abductees were rescued in Ibadan, where their abductors abandoned them because they were being trailed by security agents.
On 24 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a female APC member in Okwelle (Onuimo, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 24 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed an APC ward chairman when they invaded his residence at Umuchoke Okwe, coded to Okwe (Onuimo, Imo). The victim was an aide of a former organizing secretary of the APC, five other chieftains of the party were abducted by the assailants who shot in the air to scare residents away.

On 24 January 2023, ISWAP militants abducted at least 71 fishers around the axis of Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). The abductees were released the following day, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 24 January 2023, Nigerian soldiers repelled an attack by ISWAP around Komala (Konduga, Borno). One MRAP, a gun truck and three motorbikes were recovered.

On 24 January 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity ambushed and clashed with a Kaduna militia at Maraban Huda village in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, a civilian who was wounded by the militia was rescued and a motorcycle was recovered by the troop. The ambush in response to a distress call over the militia's attack at Gonan Doctor village.
On 24 January 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted the district head of Chawai from his residence in Zambina (Kauru, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.
Around 24 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted two community leaders in Ogbaku (Mbaitoli, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 24 January 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity ambushed and clashed with a Kaduna militia around Mangoro general area of Chikun-Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna), on the boundary with Shiroro LGA in Niger state. Two militiamen were killed, one rifle, one gun, one IED, a Boafeng radio and 10 motorcycles.

On 25 January 2023, suspected loyalists of the APC and the Kogi state governor attacked members of the PDP and vandalized the party's offices in Ajaka (Igalamela, Kogi) and Aloma. Vehicles and other properties were damaged and at least one person sustained machete cuts.

On 25 January 2023, suspected loyalists of the APC and the Kogi state governor attacked members of the PDP and vandalized the party's offices in Aloma (Ofu, Kogi) and Ajaka. Vehicles and other properties were damaged and at least one person sustained machete cuts.

On 25 January 2023, a Niger militia numbering about 100 attacked and killed three miners at a mining site in Dami Dami (Muya, Niger). Three other victims drowned while trying to escape, the assailants demanded for money, gold and other items from the miners and shot 3 persons who were uncooperative.

On 25 January 2023, PDP loyalists attacked the APC candidate for Osun West senatorial district and his supporters at Ikire Ward 9 (Irewole, Osun) as claimed by APC presidential campaign council in the state. A number of the senatorial candidate's supporters were wounded.
On 25 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at a campaign rally of the PDP in Awgu ward one, coded to Awgu (Agwu, Enugu). One person was killed and several others were wounded.

On 25 January 2023, suspected IPOB militants attacked a police checkpoint and clashed with police officers at Ihitte junction (Ngor Okpala, Imo) coded to Umuneke Ngor. A police woman and a civilian were killed, the police claimed that the assailants were from the ESN/ IPOB, other sources report that 2 police officers and one vehicle inspection officer were killed.
On 25 January 2023, a Kaduna militia killed five local miners at a mining site in Hayin Udawa, coded to Udawa (Chikun, Kaduna). Some others sustained gunshot wounds.

On 25 January 2023, a Niger militia were repelled and engaged in an armed clash by operatives of the joint task force, presumed to be a local defense militia in Kuchi town (Muya, Niger). Casualties are unknown.

On 25 January 2023, policemen shot and killed a tailor after he tried to escape arrest when the policemen invaded his residence in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The victim's family claimed that the policemen took his corpse and dumped it at a morgue, then shot in the air to disperse them when they went to the Osun police anti-cultism unit.

On 25 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a pastor after they broke into his residence in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The victim's body was found the following day around Malkohi IDP camp.
On 25 January 2023, a soldier killed one civilian at Owaza (Ukwa West, Abia) coded to Oke-Ikpe. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 26 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a local defense militia at a checkpoint in Uburu (Ohaozara, Ebonyi). Two local defense militiamen were killed, while some others sustained gunshot injuries.

Around 26 January 2023 (as reported), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed 6 farmers when they invaded and annexed Elerinla (Ose, Ondo), Molege, Ugboruwen, and Adedigba [coded separately]. The assailants uprooted cassava from farms and fed it to their cattle, set houses, cars and motorcycles ablaze, other sources report that at least 8 persons were killed and 40 hectares of farmland were destroyed. Six fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

Around 26 January 2023 (as reported), suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed 6 farmers when they invaded Molege, Ugboruwen, Adedigba (Ose, Ondo), coded to Ifon and Elerinla [coded separately]. The assailants uprooted cassava from farms and fed it to their cattle, set houses, cars and motorcycles ablaze. Six fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 26 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a pastor an dumped his corpse near Malkohi IDP camp in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The victim was abducted the previous day from his house, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 26 January 2023, ISWAP claimed to have fired two mortar shells that were targeted at a military base in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Other sources claim that the mortars landed in the bush without any impact.

On 26 January 2023, suspected APC members attacked the convoy of the deputy governorship candidate of the PDP and other PDP supporters who were returning from the party's campaign's rally in Igbesa (Ado-Odo, Ogun). Some party supporters sustained varying degrees of injuries and vehicles were destroyed. The media aide of the deputy governorship candidate claimed that APC loyalists laid ambush and carried out the attack.

On 27 January 2023, Zamfara state anti-thuggery committee operatives attacked supporters of the PDP at Gusau central motor park (Gusau, Zamfara) and killed one person while others sustained bullet wounds as claimed by the PDP gubernatorial candidate in the state. The assailants numbering over 20 shot sporadically, vandalized vehicles and stole some items.

On 27 January 2023, suspected APC loyalists attacked the convoy of the Lagos PDP gubernatorial candidate in Coker-Aguda (Surulere, Lagos). Three persons were wounded and vehicles on the convoy were destroyed, other sources report that assailants who were armed with guns and machetes damaged the canopies set up by the PDP and shot randomly in the area. The Lagos APC spokesperson claimed that the PDP loyalists were the aggressors and 3 persons were killed, while the claimed that the attack was sponsored by APC.

On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two soldiers when they attacked an army checkpoint at Idodo (Nkanu East, Enugu). The assailants who invaded the checkpoint in a Sienna bus shot sporadically before attacking policemen at two checkpoints [coded separately].

On 28 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai on fighting patrols clashed with Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Kayamari, Habasha and Yuwe in Konduga LGA (Borno). 32 militants including one commander were killed, the others fled and abandoned their weapons and properties. 50 bicycles were recovered and destroyed by the troops.

On 28 January 2023, a member of Ebube Agu corps killed his colleague in Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi) following a disagreement over 1000 naira and the sharing formula of money given to them during a campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress. The victim had attempted to shoot the assailant first but the assailant was quicker to act. Other sources report that the altercation was over other reasons while the state Ebube Agu commander claimed that the assailant was not a member of the corps but a member of an unidentified armed group.

On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at a former local government chairman and commissioner and his friend while they were traveling on the Calabar-Ikom highway (Ikom, Cross River). They were both wounded and taken to the hospital for treatment.
On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a civilian at his village of Mbapa (Gwer West, Benue).

On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked, shot sporadically and killed two persons at Enyiogugu (Aboh Mbaise, Imo). One of the victims suspected to be a northerner was shot, while the second person was beheaded.

On 28 January 2023, soldiers numbering five attacked civilians at their house during a wedding celebration in Rafin Guza (Kaduna North, Kaduna) coded to Kaduna following an altercation with a commercial tricycle rider and soldiers earlier that day due to traffic congestion that was caused by the wedding celebration. One person was killed, three others were shot and beaten by the soldiers.

On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked policemen at a mobile checkpoint at Enugu-Ebonyi states boundary, coded to Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). Three policemen were killed, one other policeman was shot in the leg. The assailants had attacked soldiers and policemen at two other checkpoints [coded separately].
On 28 January 2023, a Katsina militia killed a 'suya' seller who resisted abduction in Dutiinma community of Batsari LGA (Katsina). The assailants also rustled an unspecified number of cattle.

On 28 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked policemen at a checkpoint at Owo/Idodo junction (Nkanu East, Enugu). The policemen fled and the assailants moved to a mobile police checkpoint [coded separately].

On 29 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the wife of the Ebube Agu commander in Afikpo South LGA at their house in Owutu (Afikpo South, Ebonyi). The assailants also set the commander's house ablaze.

On 29 January 2023, Black Axe militia (also called Aiye confraternity) and Red Axe cult militia clashed at Ikpayongo (Gwer East, Benue). One person was killed, while the assailants sang boastful cult-related songs.

On 29 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed six civilians at Tse-mkem Mbashimbe Mbabuande and Babowa (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka. Two of the victims were killed in the bush while they were sawing wood.

On 30 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons on the highway around Toro general area (Toro, Bauchi). One of the abductees is a journalist, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released on 1 February, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 30 January 2023, suspected PDP members attacked and wounded APC supporters at Okerewe area (Ife East, Osun) coded to Ife-Ife. The assailants who wounded many people proceeded to destroy properties at secretariats of the APC at Ife Central LGA and Ife East LGA [coded separately] after they tore down APC banners in the area. A member of the PDP claimed that the attack was triggered by APC members who attacked a PDP member.

On 30 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the Rivers APC gubernatorial candidate in Opobo town (Opobo, Rivers). An APC member was also abducted and later released, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 30 January 2023, security operatives on the convoy of the Bauchi APC governorship candidate repelled an attack by unidentified armed group on the convoy at Akuyam town (Misau, Bauchi). One person was killed and another was injured by the security operatives, the candidate's media aide claimed that the opposition were responsible for the attack and that 15 - 20 cars were destroyed during the clash.
On 30 January 2023, a Katsina militia abducted five women from Daddara Liman village, coded to Daddara (Jibia, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 30 January 2023, OSPAC operatives killed a man while he was on his way to Ipo (Ikwerre, Rivers). The victim was ambushed shortly after he was bailed from OSPAC custody.

On 30 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and inflicted machete cuts on three APC members in Omumma LGA (Omumma, Rivers) coded to Eberi. The victims were on a door to door campaign for their party, when they were attacked and threatened that the party would not be allowed to carry out their scheduled campaign rally in the area.

On 30 January 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians and abducted the daughter of the village head at Kukar Babangida village in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The assailants also set the village ablaze after the attack. There are no reports about ransom demands for the abductee.

On 30 January 2023, supporters of the APC clashed and shot sporadically in Ikoro (Ijero, Ekiti) following a disagreement over money. One person was killed and a few others were wounded. The PDP House of Representatives candidate for Ekiti Federal Constituency claimed that the security operatives attached to the convoy of his APC opponent were responsible for the attack.

On 30 January 2023, a Niger militia attacked civilians at Hayin Magaji village, few kilometers away from Kontagora town (Kontagora, Niger) and killed one person. Four others sustained various degrees of bullet wounds and 16 women including 4 nursing mothers were abducted together with their babies.

On 30 January 2023, Nigerian troops carried out an offensive operation and clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at villages in Bama LGA (Borno) and Mafa LGA [coded separately]. Three militants were killed and 10 abductees were rescued. 3 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 30 January 2023, Nigerian troops carried out an offensive operation and clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at villages in Mafa LGA (Borno) and Bama LGA [coded separately]. Three militants were killed and 10 abductees were rescued. 3 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 1.
On 31 January 2023, an unidentified armed group of three killed the Madaki Jannaret at his residence in Jannaret (Mangu, Plateau). The victim was shot severally on his chest and stomach.

On 31 January 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the security operatives attacked to the convoy of the Rivers state SDP candidate when they attacked his convoy at Akinima (Ahoada West, Rivers) while they were going to attend a statewide campaign rally. Casualties are unknown.

On 31 January 2023, Nigerian troops raided an IPOB militants' camp and engaged them in an armed clash at Ovuru community forest (Uzo Uwani, Enugu) coded to Umulokpa. 4 militants were killed, weapons, ammunition, an IED and other items were recovered.
On 31 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed a civilian when they attacked his community of Mbadyugh Tse-uhon in Sengev council ward (Gwer West, Benue).

On 31 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the aide of a federal lawmaker and one other person at Iwuru-Turunkekpem axis (Biase, Cross River) of Calabar-Ikom highway. The abductees were on their way to Boki for the funeral of the aide's father, a ransom of 60 million naira was demanded.

Around 31 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked the APGA governorship candidate in Ebonyi state at Iboko community (Izzi, Ebonyi) when he went to commission a campaign office in the area. Casualties are unknown.

On 31 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed a police DPO [presumed to have been off-duty] a few kilometers to Naka town (Gwer West, Benue). Some sources report that the assailants blocked the road for hours before the attack, others report that the victim was going to pick his men that were posted the road on routine duty.

On 1 February 2023, Black Axe militia [also called Aye militia] members clashed with Eiye militia at Etegbin (Ojo, Lagos) after the Aye members trailed an Eiye member who they accused of killing one of their members to a drinking joint. The clash escalated towards Ajangbadi and several persons were wounded.

On 1 February 2023, an unidentified armed group in their numbers armed with IEDs, petrol bombs and other explosives attacked a police station and a residential building within the same premises at Nnobi (Idemili South, Anambra). The assailants killed a 16 year old male civilian and wounded another girl, both victims were related to policemen.

On 1 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the commissioner for women's affairs in Cross River state along Mayne avenue (Calabar South, Cross River) coded to Anantigha. There are no reports about ransom demands, other sources report that she was abducted alongside an unidentified woman and that the abductors had pretended to be soldiers who demanded for why the abductee was driving a car with covered number plates. The abductee was rescued around 8 March by soldiers who raided the abductor's hideout [coded separately].

On 2 February 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with operatives of the Anambra vigilante service who were on a routine patrol in Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). The clash lasted for several minutes and one vigilante member was killed.

On 2 February 2023, troops of 1 Division of the Nigerian army on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Manini village (Chikun, Kaduna). 30 abductees were rescued by the troops who also recovered two motorcycles, casualties are unknown.

On 2 February 2023, an unidentified armed group invaded a police anti-cult unit and were engaged in an armed clash by policemen on duty at Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). The assailants who threw petrol bombs into the police station were repelled, one policeman was killed, some were fatally wounded and the assailants' bombs destroyed some building in the station.

On 2 February 2023, suspected Ebube Agu operatives ambushed the convoy of the APGA gubernatorial candidate, wounded his police orderly who later died and two others at Okpoto (Ishielu, Ebonyi). The driver of the APGA candidate was killed, his backup Hilux van was set ablaze and at least five persons were missing. The state commander of Ebube Agu denied the attack.

On 2 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and wounded a farmer on his farm near Oloke village in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). The victim was attacked with a machete and was asked by the assailants to inform the other residents of their coming.

On 2 February 2023, soldiers beat up security officers on night duty at the main campus of the University of Benin at Ugbowo (Egor, Edo) after they scaled the perimeter fence to gain entrance. The attack was a reprisal following a clash between the soldiers and students earlier [coded separately]; scores of civilians including students were wounded and several vehicles on the campus were destroyed.

On 2 February 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed a local defense militia that was pursuing them at Mji community in Kankara LGA (Katsina). The assailants received information about the local defense militia's movement from informants, residents claimed that at least 30 local militiamen were killed and several others were wounded. The police area command disputed the fatality figures.

On 2 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a judge while he was presiding over a court sitting in Ejemekwuru (Oguta, Imo). The assailants who operated on motorcycles dragged the victim out of the court, shot him and left.

On 2 February 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed Yansakai militia from 11 villages who trailed them to a location at Yargoje forest (Kankara, Katsina) and attempted to recover cattle that were stolen the previous day by the Katsina militia [coded separately]. 41 Yansakai militiamen were killed; and later increased to between 72 and 102, two others were wounded, some sources report unspecified number of wounded persons, others report that the clash lasted for over 48 hours. 72 fatalities split across two events coded as 36.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering five beat up a community bank CEO whom they abducted alongside two other persons at Nnobi (Idemili South, Anambra). The CEO was escaped from the abductors who fired shots at his car windshield and tires before taking him away.
On 3 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two civilians in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). Two other persons were missing.
On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two travelers along Iwuru-Turunkekpem (Biase, Cross River). An unspecified number of other travelers were abducted.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with policemen at a police station in Abagana (Njikoka, Anambra) and killed three operatives of the Anambra vigilante service who were on patrol before arriving at the police station. The policemen repelled the assailants who threw petrol bombs, destroyed some structures in the police station and set inmates free. Other sources report that two vigilante operatives were killed.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed two persons when they attacked the residence of LP House of Representatives candidate for Lere federal constituency at Gure village (Lere, Kaduna). The candidate was away from his house.

On 3 February 2023, a Katsina militia clashed with Yansakai militia from 11 villages who trailed them to a location at Yargoje forest (Kankara, Katsina) and attempted to recover cattle that were stolen by the Katsina militia [coded separately]. Some sources report that the clash lasted for over 48 hours; 41 Yansakai militiamen were killed; and later increased to between 72 and 102, two others were wounded, other sources report unspecified number of wounded persons. 72 fatalities split across two events coded as 36.

On 4 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife, two sons of the traditional ruler of Bukpe and three other residents from their houses at Bukpe, Kwali Area Council (FCT). The wife and one of the ruler's sons were released after 2.5 million naira foodstuff, hard drugs and other items were paid as ransom around 27 March, a ransom of 3 million naira was demanded for the release of the remaining abductees.

Around 4 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed 7 members of the family of the district head of Mutum Biyu who were abducted [coded separately] from Mutum Biyu (Gassol, Taraba). 8 persons including the head's two wives and six children were abducted, one of them escaped and the rest were killed and their decomposing bodies were found.
On 4 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed three farmers when they attacked Ikobi (Apa, Benue). Other sources report that 4 persons were killed.

On 4 February 2023, a Fulani militia ambushed troops of Operation Whirl Stroke and engaged them in an armed clash at Mbapa (Gwer West, Benue). Three soldiers sustained various degrees of injuries, the troops overpowered the militiamen.

On 4 February 2023, suspected Kalare Boys Gang members attacked the residence of a PDP chieftain at Gombe (Gombe, Gombe) where he had arranged a meeting with women and youths. Five persons were wounded and the house was vandalized before policemen intervened, the chieftain claimed that the attack was related to his defection from APC to PDP.
On 4 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an NGO intern around Jahi axis (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductee was released on 8 February, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 February 2023, Nigerian troops raided the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Balange village, on the fringes of the Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). Five militants were killed and 55 abductees were rescued.

Around 5 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer from his farm at Oko Oparun village (Ondo East, Ondo) coded to Bolorunduro. A ransom of 700 hundred thousand naira was demanded, the body of the victim was discovered four days later following the family's failure to pay the ransom.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins invaded the house of a PDP chieftain at (Akpabuyo, Cross River) coded to Ikot Nakanda. The chieftain and his family were not at home, the gate keeper was beat up and stabbed multiple times, the assailants who were armed with machetes, sticks and firearms also vandalized properties. The PDP claimed that the APC was responsible for the attack.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed the convoy of the PRP governorship candidate in Cross River at Betem axis (Biase, Cross River). Two persons were killed and four others were wounded, the candidate who is also a former minister survived. Some sources report that 3 persons were killed, a large number of others were abducted and the car of murdered victims was mistaken to have been that of the governorship candidate, others report that four persons were also abducted and several others were wounded.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted nine locals in Monu village, coded to Rubochi (Kuje, FCT) while they were loading logs of wood into a truck in the forest. Eight of the abductees were released after the abductors asked them to return, claiming that they had found their target. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians and killed three persons at Maiyanga, Bokkos LGA (Plateau). The assailants shot sporadically during the attack, two other persons sustained gunshot wounds.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku and Omor militias clashed over a suspected boundary dispute at Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra) and Omor [coded separately]. Five persons were killed, some sources report that at least 10 persons were killed, others report that one to six others were abducted, houses were set ablaze and IEDs were planted and yet to be detonated. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku and Omor militias clashed over a suspected boundary dispute at Omor (Ayamelum, Anambra) and Anaku [coded separately]. Five persons were killed, some sources report that at least 10 persons were killed, others report that one to six others were abducted, houses were set ablaze and IEDs were planted and yet to be detonated. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 6 February 2023, Amasiri and Nde Ndukwe residents attacked farm settlements in Oso (Afikpo South, Ebonyi) and killed one person during the attacks which lasted for 3 days before the intervention of security operatives. Houses, farm produce and properties were destroyed, four others were abducted and later released after a peace meeting organized by council chairmen and monarchs. The murdered victim was behead, his head was taken away by the assailants. Fatality split accross 3 events, coded as 1.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku militia clashed with soldiers who were sent to enforce peace in Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra). One soldier was abducted and his rifle was stolen, the soldiers retaliated and raided the community [coded separately].
On 6 February 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked and clashed with Boko Haram fighters who were moving towards the axis of Tumbun Gini (Abadan, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 6 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed one man while he was fishing and also attacked his brother at Ugboanyim-Aniyi in Amagunze (Nkanu East, Enugu). The murdered victim's body was found the following day with machete cuts, residents of the community fled the area due to fear.

On 6 February 2023, Nigerian conducted several artillery fire missions against ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at Tumbun Barebare, Tumbun Mata, Kaye Kura, Kwatan Yobe, and Dumba in Kukawa LGA (Borno). 42 militants were killed.

On 7 February 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji invaded the hideout of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Danmarke forest (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. Scores of militiamen were killed in the clash that lasted overnight [coded separately]. 20 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 10.

On 7 February 2023, Amasiri and Nde Ndukwe attacked farm settlements in Oso (Afikpo South, Ebonyi) and killed one person during the attacks which started the previous day and lasted for 3 days before the intervention of security operatives. Houses, farm produce and properties were destroyed, four others were abducted and later released after a peace meeting organized by council chairmen and monarchs.
