On 7 March 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted five people when they attacked Takatsaba village (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 7 March 2023, ISWAP militants killed a civilian when they blocked the road along Gajiram-Monguno (Nganzai, Borno).
On 7 March 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed an unspecified number of civilians in Tse-Jor (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 8 March 2023, APC and PDP supporters clashed during a campaign rally of the APC at Duguri town (Alkaleri , Bauchi) coded to Buren Duguri. One person was shot and killed, 14 to 15 others sustained machete wounds, The PDP claimed that several others sustained varying degrees of injuries including bystanders, their billboards were destroyed, their offices and tricycles were set ablaze. Both parties accused the other for being responsible for the attack.

On 8 March 2023, a Niger militia abducted a businesswoman and two of her daughters from their home in Beji town (Bosso, Niger). To other tenants of the woman were abducted but later escaped, the assailants shot sporadically in the town to scare residents away. Sources claim that the abduction was connected to the woman's refusal to allow a petrol station to serve as a fuel dump to the militiamen.

On 8 March 2023, soldiers engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash and repelled an attack on civilians in Wushishi LGA (Niger) and Rafi LGA [coded separately]. The militiamen shot sporadically at the civilians; killed 5 persons including a pregnant woman, wounded others before the soldiers arrived and fled with more than 50 people whom they abducted. Other sources report that NAF fighter jets engaged the militiamen who also attacked Rafi LGA, fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 8 March 2023, soldiers engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash and repelled an attack on civilians in Agwa community (Rafi, Niger) coded to Kagara. The militiamen shot sporadically at the civilians; killed 5 persons including a pregnant woman, wounded others before the soldiers arrived and fled with more than 50 people whom they abducted. Other sources report that NAF fighter jets engaged the militiamen who also attacked Wushishi LGA, fatalities split across two events coded as 3.

On 8 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and beat up a journalist in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The assailants demanded for a particular gadget from the victim and when he was unable to provide it, they pushed him out of a moving tricycle and assumed he was dead.

On 8 March 2023, ISWAP militants attacked IDPs who were fishing and shot sporadically at them in Mukdolo village (Ngala, Borno) coded to Gamboru. Between 26 to 35 persons were killed, nine others escaped, three among them sustained bullet wounds. Some sources report that the militants had severally warned the victims to stay away from their zone, other sources report that the victims were also tortured by the militants. The police claimed that 29 persons were killed and nine were seriously wounded.

On 8 March 2023, troops of 13 Brigade Nigerian Army who were deployed to Operation Akpakwu ambushed an unidentified armed group at their hideout and engaged them in an armed clash around Peter Effiong Creek. The troops rescued the Cross River state commissioner for women affairs who was abducted by the group at Mayne Avenue [coded separately], while the members of the group fled. Location coded to Anantigha (Calabar South, Cross River) where the abduction was coded to.

On 8 March 2023, policemen engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash and repelled the militia's attack on Jabiri area of Funtua LGA (Katsina). One militiaman was killed, another was arrested and one rifle was recovered.
On 8 March 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted three people who were traveling from Garki to Masawa village in Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 8 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed 8 persons in Tse-Jor (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka. The victims were at the burial of victims of a previous attack, several persons sustained varying degrees of injuries, the assailants who invaded the area from Nassarawa state also set the village ablaze and fled before soldiers arrived.
On 8 March 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked farmers and fishers in Mugdala village, also spelled Mukdula (Dikwa, Borno), killing 16 boys aged between 13 and 17 years.

On 9 March 2023, an unidentified armed group of locals killed a Fulani pastoralist at Unguwan Juju (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). The victim was tied to a tree and cut to death with a machete, the attack led to reprisals in the area (coded separately).

On 9 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the Taraba state chairman of CCSON from his residence at Magami (Jalingo, Taraba). The abductors demanded for a ransom of 100 million naira and later reduced it to 25 million.

On 9 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a journalist in Mobalufon area of Ijebu-Ode (Ijebu Ode, Ogun). A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded, the abductee was rescued by policemen around 13 March (coded separately).

Around 9 March 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in police uniform attacked the president of Ogoni Youth Federation (OYF) in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) attempting to assassinate him. Unknown if the attackers were police officers. No fatalities.
On 9 March 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person and abducted an unspecified number of others when they attacked a commuter bus that was heading to Batsari market (Batsari, Katsina).

On 9 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be APC supporters shot and killed a presumed OPC member and two other persons at Akere spare parts market in Ajegunle (Ajeromi, Lagos). The assailants also set the market ablaze and destroyed properties worth millions of naira, the attack is suspected to have been politically motivated against Igbo traders due to their assumed preference for the LP gubernatorial candidate.

On 9 March 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram fighters invaded a police formation and clashed with policemen at Magumeri (Magumeri, Borno). The militants snuck in from two directions, at least one policeman was killed in the clash which lasted for about 30 and one police vehicle was taken away by the militants. Other sources report that seven villagers were abducted by the militants.

On 10 March 2023, a Kaduna militia killed one person and abducted four members of his family when they invaded his residence at Karimbu-Kahugu (Lere, Kaduna) coded to Saminaka. The murdered victim was the son of a pastor who attempted to resist the militiamen, his wife and three others were the abductees.

On 10 March 2023, a soldier shot and killed his colleague at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno) following an argument. Other sources report that the assailant was suffering from a mental illness and possessed by a spirit.

On 10 March 2023, Nigerian Navy personnel beat up a policeman when they invaded the Enerhe divisional police station (Uvwie, Delta). There were sporadic gunshots in the area, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 10 March 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 20 abducted nine persons from Kuchibiyi in the Kubwa area (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductees include a pastor, his wife and children. Some of the abductees were released, at least 11 others were still held and 50 million naira was demanded as ransom.

On 10 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a businessman at Agbariko area of Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). The assailants were two and trailed the victim from his shop on a motorcycle.

On 11 March 2023, a Fulani militia attacked a group of youths who went fishing and killed one of them at Unguwan Wakili (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zangon Katab. The attack was a reprisal for the killing of a pastoralist (coded separately), the victim was cut to death with a machete.

On 11 March 2023, a Fulani militia attacked a checkpoint and clashed with soldiers at Unguwan Wakili junction (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zangon Katab. The attack was a reprisal over a clash between policemen and some Fulani pastoralists earlier that day, over 10 persons were killed and four others sustained injuries.

On 11 March 2023, a policeman shot and killed a Fulani pastoralist at Unguwan Wakili (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zangon Katab following an altercation between the policemen and some pastoralists. Another policeman was killed after he was accidentally hit by his colleague.

On 11 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the councilor representing Echara Ward 2 at Okposi (Ezza North, Ebonyi). The victim was attacked as he was returning from his shop, the assailants shot him and set his body ablaze together with his car. Both the APC and PDP accused one another of being responsible for the attack.
On 11 March 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Kinfau village in Safana LGA (Katsina) and escaped through the Rugu Forest. Casualties are unknown.

On 11 March 2023, a Katsina militia clashed with a local defense militia at Makera (Kankara, Katsina), Majifa, Gidan Jifau and Gurbi (coded separately). 21 persons including 21 males and two females were killed across the locations, 5 of which were in Gurbi and 13 others across 3 locations, 13 fatalities spilt across 2 events coded as 6. Other sources report that 18 others were wounded and the clash started when the defense militia clashed with the militiamen including those from Zamfara that were attending a wedding ceremony at Majifa.

On 11 March 2023, policemen and a local defense militia clashed with a Zamfara militia when they conducted clearance operations in Munhaye forest (Tsafe, Zamfara). 14 abductees were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 11 March 2023, a Katsina militia clashed with a local defense militia at Gurbi (Kankara, Katsina), Makera, Majifa and Gidan Jifau (coded separately). 21 persons including 21 males and two females were killed across the locations, 5 of which were in Gurbi. Other sources report that 18 others were wounded and the clash started when the defense militia clashed with the militiamen including those from Zamfara that were attending a wedding ceremony at Majifa.

On 11 March 2023, a Katsina militia clashed with a local defense militia at Majifa, Gidan Jifau (Kankara, Katsina), Makera and Gurbi (coded separately). 21 persons including 21 males and two females were killed across the locations, 5 of which were in Gurbi and 13 others across 3 locations, 13 fatalities spilt across 2 events coded as 7. Other sources report that 18 others were wounded and the clash started when the defense militia clashed with the militiamen including those from Zamfara that were attending a wedding ceremony at Majifa.

Around 11 March 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at a location in Askira LGA (Askira Uba, Borno) coded Askira, Kukawa, Gwoza and Damboa [coded separately]. 7 militants were killed; split across 4 locations and coded as 2, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

Around 11 March 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at locations in Damboa LGA (Borno), Askira Uba, Kukawa and Gwoza [coded separately]. 7 militants were killed; split across 4 locations and coded as 1, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

Around 11 March 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at locations in Kukawa LGA (Borno), Askira Uba, Gwoza and Damboa [coded separately]. 7 militants were killed; split across 4 locations and coded as 2, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

Around 11 March 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at locations in Gwoza LGA (Borno), Askira Uba, Kukawa and Damboa [coded separately]. 7 militants were killed; split across 4 locations and coded as 2, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

Around 12 March 2023 (as reported), a local defense militia killed a boy in Deba Kowa (Yamaltu, Gombe). The victim was taken away by the militiamen at midnight, his body was found at Tunga covered with grass, he was abducted after he stabbed a member of the militia with a knife.

On 12 March 2023, an unidentified armed group of two clashed with the security operatives attached to the campaign entourage of the LP Lagos state gubernatorial candidate at Epe (Epe, Lagos) during a campaign walk in the area. The PDP House of Representatives candidate for Epe was part of the campaign entourage. Casualties are unknown.

On 12 March 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Idimu area (Alimosho, Lagos) and rescued a journalist that was abducted by the group (coded separately). The members of the group fled with varying degrees of gunshot wounds following the clash which lasted for about 45 minutes.

On 12 March 2023, members of the Rivers state task force killed a commercial bus driver around Rumuokoro (Obio, Rivers). The officials beat up the victim and hit him on the head with a stick, he was taken to the hospital and confirmed dead.

On 12 March 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji and a local defense militia repelled an attack by a Zamfara militia on Bula village in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). Two women and a baby who were abducted from the village were rescued after the troops blocked the exit route of the militia as claimed by the commander of 1 Brigade Gusau.

On 12 March 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded four persons at the Bori area (Khana, Rivers). The assailants were riding on a motorcycle and shot sporadically at the private car, all the occupants sustained bullet wound, the victims included the national leader of Conscience of Ogoni People.

On 12 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the Delta state PDP gubernatorial candidate between Elume junction and Okuabude (Okpe, Delta) as he was returning from a political meeting in Sapele. The candidate survived the attack, one security man was wounded and there were no fatalities.
On 13 March 2023, suspected armed pastoralists (suspected Fulani) killed a man whom they beheaded in Zarama-Yambiri (Yenagoa, Bayelsa).

Around 13 March 2023 (as reported), a suspected unidentified cult militia abducted a student from his residence at Uwelu (Egor, Edo). The abductee was taken in the presence of his family members, he was taken in place of his brother who the abductors were looking for because he offended a member of the gang. The victim's body was later found at Oluku (coded separately).

On 13 March 2023, policemen attached to Operation Whirl Punch engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash, after the militia blocked the Galadimawa-Tumbruku road (Giwa, Kaduna). One militia member was killed, others fled with bullet wounds and the policemen recovered one rifle and two live rounds of ammunition.

On 13 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the AP house of assembly candidate for Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA constituency 2 at Rumuigbo (Obio, Rivers). The abductee was taken away in his car, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 March 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a man and his four children from their residence at Saminaka in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Soldiers trailed the abductors and rescued two out of the abducted children [no reports of a clash].
On 13 March 2023, a Zamfara militia shot at passengers along Kaura Namoda- Shinkafi road (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Casualties are unknown.

On 13 March 2023, Ijegwu and Ojantele militias engaged in an armed clash over disconnected electricity supply around Ojantele (Otukpo, Benue). Three persons were killed and many houses in both communities were set ablaze while a few other sustained gunshot wounds.
On 14 March 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians in Langson (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa. 10 persons were killed and many others sustained injuries.

On 14 March 2023, policemen killed a civilian after he was arrested detained and tortured in Ore (Odigbo, Ondo). The victim was a guest at a hotel that was raided by policemen, he died as a result of the torture was released on a bail of 5000 naira. The police denied the claims insisted that the persons who were arrested and screen were suspected to be political thugs.
On 14 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two farmers who were on their way to a farm in Oiji (Apa, Benue).

Around 14 March 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted the Accord party candidate for Rivers State House Assembly Onelga Constituency, coded to Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers).

Around 14 March 2023 (as reported), a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a student whose body was found at a dumpsite in Oluku (Ovia North East, Edo). The victim was abducted from his residence (coded separately) by the assailants who were looking for his brother that was reported to have wronged a member of the gang. One person was arrested in connection with the attack as claimed by the police.

On 14 March 2023, Nigerian troops conducted clearance operations to the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash within Ngala LGA (Borno). 6 militants were killed, weapons, ammunition, dummy rifles, livestock and other items were recovered by the troops, 49 abductees comprising of 29 adults and 23 children were rescued.

On 14 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with the APC attacked the LP house of assembly candidate for Surulere 1 constituency and his supporters and disrupted their campaign rally at Iponri (Surulere, Lagos). A member of the team was wounded, one woman was robbed by the assailants and the police claimed to have recovered one tricycle belonging to that assailants. Other sources report that some people were stabbed, one was shot and persons were robbed, the assailants also said 'no Labor Party, except APC, Sanwo-Olu for governor'.

On 15 March 2023, a Niger militia ambushed and clashed with the joint task force that was comprised of the army and a local defense militia at Igu village (Muya, Niger). Four soldiers and four defense militiamen were killed, the task force were attacked twice by the militiamen. Other sources report that one defense militiaman and an unspecified number of the assailants were killed and two task force patrol vehicles were vandalized with bullets.

On 15 March 2023, a Niger militia killed a medical practitioner who attempted to escape an attack in Adunu (Paikoro, Niger). More than 40 persons including women, children and a retired police officer were abducted. Some residents claimed that abductees who could afford between 10 to 20 thousand naira in old or new currency notes were released. 56 people were abducted from the community and one other community, a ransom of 200 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released around 24 August 2023 after the militia became tired of feeding them without receiving ransom.

On 15 March 2023, a Niger militia killed a village head when they attacked civilians at Beni village (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The assailants abducted about 20 persons, conducted house to house searches, stole money, foodstuff and other valuables. 56 people were abducted from the community and one other community, a ransom of 200 million naira was demanded. Three of the abductees were killed to serve as a warning, other sources report 5 persons were killed. The abductees were released around 24 August 2023 after the militia became tired of feeding them without receiving ransom.

On 15 March 2023, a Niger militia killed the village head of Gusasai (Bosso, Niger) coded to Maikonkele when they invaded the community. The victim's wife, two daughters and one other male from the family were abducted and there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 15 March 2023, Nigerian army troops of sector 3 of the MNJTF, Operation Hadin Kai and the special forces of sector 4 MNJTF Niger Republic clashed with ISWAP militants at Kusuma, Jibularam and Kwalaram in Marte LGA (Borno). The troops also conducted multiple airstrikes and killed more that 70 militants including high ranking commander, foot-soldiers and Hisbah police from ISWAP. Several vehicles and weapons were destroyed, hundreds of fighters also fled to safe locations within the Marte general area.

On 15 March 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Sokoto militia in an armed clash when they conducted clearance operations on the militia camps at Malawa, Gangara and Bafarawa villages in Sabon BirniLGA (Sokoto). An unspecified number of militiamen were killed and multiple motorcycles were recovered. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the LP house of assembly candidate for Aniocha South Constituency at Ewulu (Aniocha South, Delta) coded to Ogwashi-Uku. Casualties are unknown.
On 16 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to have political affiliation shot and killed a PDP supporter at (Ife South, Osun) coded to Ifetedo.

On 16 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted the deputy governorship candidate for YPP in Cross River state along the Calabar-Ogoja highway (Ogaja, Cross River). Three others including an immigration official (presumed off-duty) were also abducted and a ransom of 60 million which was later reduced to 40 million was demanded for the abductees' release. The abductees were released around 21 March after a ransom of 2 million naira was paid.

On 16 March 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in police uniforms abducted an APC chieftain from his Aluu community (Ikwerre, Rivers). The abductee was also the party's secretary in the LGA, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 16 March 2023, the Zamfara anti-thuggery committee wounded scores of policemen when they ambushed the convoy of the Zamfara state PDP gubernatorial candidate in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The wounded policemen were escorts on the convoy; other sources report that one policeman was wounded, the candidate's media office claimed that the attack was unprovoked and an assassination attempt.

On 16 March 2023, an official of the DSS shot and killed a suspected cultist in his compound at Ogidi (Idemili North, Anambra) after the official pursued the suspected cultist who ran into the compound. Other sources report that the victim was killed by a local defense militia member.

On 16 March 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 30 in a motorcade of 10 vehicles and dressed in black attacked the home of the Oyo state APC gubernatorial candidate in Oja'gbo (Ibadan South East, Oyo) coded to Mapo. The assailants wounded many of his supporters, dispersed hundreds of them and screamed in Yoruba 'it is your turn to die' while looking for the candidate who was not at home at the time. Other sources report that the attack was a reprisal for the murder of 3 PDP supporters earlier that day (coded separately).

On 16 March 2023, PDP and APC members engaged in an armed clash at Ile-Tuntun (Ibadan South East, Oyo) coded to Mapo. The clash occurred at the meeting venue of the APC, when PDP members threw objects at them; they retaliated and a leading PDP member and a member of the House of Representatives shot at the APC members. 3 persons were killed, 13 others were wounded and a number of vehicles and motorcycles were destroyed. Other sources claim that the victims included a PDP councilor, the PDP claimed that the APC were the aggressors.

On 16 March 2023, presumed Black Axe militia killed a presumed member of SEC at Bariga (Somolu, Lagos) in a reprisal attack over the killing of their member by the other group earlier on the same day [coded separately].

On 16 March 2023, SEC militia killed the brother of a member of a rival group at Somolu (Somolu, Lagos) and cut off his left hand. The cut hand was taken away by the assailants, the brother of the victim was the 'hitman' of the Black Axe militia.
On 17 March 2023, a Sokot militia shot indiscriminately at Kojiyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). Casualties are unknown.

On 17 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two passengers and abducted an unspecified number of others when they blocked the road around Ganmi junction near Bwari town (Bwari, FCT) and shot sporadically. The attack went on for about one hour, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 17 March 2023, policemen killed two persons when they invaded the INEC office in Oko Ita (Ibiono Ibom, Akwa Ibom) and shot sporadically. The assailants invaded the place in 5 white Hilux vehicles, took the corpses away and wounded at least one person. Other sources report that 3 persons were killed and the victims were suspected supporters of YPP who were trying to block PDP supporters from stealing election materials.

On 18 March 2023, APC supporters beat up a female voter for not voting for the APC at a polling unit and threatened to murder her when they see her in town. Location coded to Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi).
On 18 March 2023, PDP agents beat up and chased away agents of other political parties including AAC agents in Mbadwem, Mbabai and Mbawa council wards (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the campaign director of the APC in Ahoada West LGA after he was abducted while casting his vote at Ibagwa polling unit 2, ward 10 (Ahoada West, Rivers) coded to Akinima. The persons who abducted the victim were dressed in police uniforms and he was abducted for attempting to stop the assailants from snatching election materials, his body was found later that day riddled with bullets.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up the cameraman of a TV station who was covering the gubernatorial elections in the Elegushi palace at Ikate (Eti-Osa, Lagos). The assailants also seized the cameras and drones that were used for the coverage.
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a polling unit and chased voters away at Awoyaya (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos).
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group invaded Elibrada community in Emohua LGA (Rivers) and shot sporadically. Casualties are unknown.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the APC House of Assembly candidate for Ahoada East constituency 2 at Obelle community (Emohua, Rivers). The abductee was on his way to his polling unit, the abductors shot sporadically to disperse people, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 18 March 2023, IPOB members attacked voters and disrupted the electoral process in Amaowele (Agwu, Enugu). Casualties are unknown.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked polling unit 027 in Sade (Darazo, Bauchi) and disrupted the voting process. Security agents were deployed to the location and normalcy was restored.

Around 18 March 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted the gate keeper of a newly elected House of Representatives member at Erawhe-Owhe (Isoko North, Delta) coded to Ozoro. Ten cows and other livestock belonging to the lawmaker were stolen, the decomposing body of the abductee who was from the Hausa ethnic group was found after days of intensive search [coded separately].

On 18 March 2023, policemen killed a member of an unidentified armed group who attempted to snatch ballot boxes in Gboko South (Gboko, Benue) and several others sustained injuries. Other sources report that at least six persons were killed at different locations across the LGA.

On 18 March 2023, a presumed member of an identified armed group was killed by security agents when he attempted to disrupt the voting process in Mbube (Ogaja, Cross River) coded to Bansan Mbube. Other sources report that the murdered person was a party official for the APC and he was killed by soldiers.

On 18 March 2023, troops of Operation Desert Sanity ambushed and clashed with Boko Haram militants in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 18 March 2023, PDP agents fought civilians at their polling unit of 006 Otoro Ward 06 (Abak, Akwa Ibom) coded to Abia Okpo Otoro as claimed by a civilian. Casualties are unknown.

On 18 March 2023, soldiers of 401 special forces brigade beat up a serving member of the House of Representatives when they invaded his hotel in Gboko (Gboko, Benue) and wounded him. Some sources report that the lawmaker was accused of planning to rig elections, which prompted the attack, he denied the claims and insisted that he was beaten without any provocation, despite that he identified himself to the soldiers, and that the attack happened around 2am.

On 18 March 2023, APC supporters numbering up to 20 wounded a voter after they flogged him when they attacked polling units 108, 007 and 028 in the Ajiran area of Lekki (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos). The assailants consisted of females and males and insisted that only persons voting APC would be allowed to vote.
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a polling unit, chased voters away and vandalized voting materials at Ward 2, Unit 6 in Bonny LGA (Rivers).
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a PDP chieftain when they attacked a polling unit in Onicha LGA (Ebonyi).
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person at Oghara (Isoko North, Delta) during the gubernatorial election.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be have a political affiliation attacked and wounded two persons at Abule Ado (Amowo-Odofin, Lagos). The police spokesperson in the state claimed that there was an intra-community fight in the area which resulted in the destruction of property.

On 18 March 2023, two unidentified armed groups with political affiliation to the two leading political parties in the community clashed at Ogbokiri (Emohua, Rivers) and three persons were killed. Some sources report that the persons were killed when they attempted to snatch ballot boxes, and that they were with a serving lawmaker, other sources report that the clash was between a joint task force comprised of the army and police and a cult militia.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group beat and wounded a retired soldier at her polling unit in Dikenafai (Ideato South, Imo) for attempting to prevent them from rigging an election as claimed by the victim.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a polling unit and disrupted the electoral process around Yankaba Kawaji-Jigirya (Nassarawa, Kano). Security operatives were deployed to the area and normalcy was restored.
On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her daughter along Garrison in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with security operatives at Mosogar (Ethiope West, Delta). Four persons were killed, the house of a supporter of the APC who is also a former President-General of the Urhobo Progress Union was set ablaze.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with PDP wounded a commissioner of workers at his polling unit in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) following an argument. The victim was hit on the head with a stick and was rushed to a nearby clinic.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with politicians attacked a state commissioner at his polling unit of Birnin Ruwa, Ramayana in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The commissioner escaped being lynched, voters were chased away and ballot papers were snatched by the assailants.

On 18 March 2023, a Katsina militia attacked the convoy of the Katsina state gubernatorial candidate of the NNPP while he was enroute to his hometown , Kandawa in Bakori LGA (Katsina). The candidate escaped, casualties are unknown.
On 18 March 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person and wounded one other person when they attacked Kagara village coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 18 March 2023, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group that had attempted to snatch ballot boxes and voters' phones in Odoakpu area of Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). The group fled the area, casualties are unknown.

On 18 March 2023, an unidentified armed group was repelled by security operatives (assumed Police forces) when they attempted to steal ballot boxes at a polling unit along Sama road in Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto).
On 18 March 2023, two unidentified armed groups suspected to be political party supporters clashed at polling unit 030 in Tudun Wada ward (Sokoto South, Sokoto) coded to Tudun Wada A.

On 2 April 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked Christians at a vigil ground where they were worshipping at Akenawe (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba. One person was killed, five persons sustained varying degrees of machete wounds and four others including the resident pastor were abducted. Other sources report that three persons were abducted and two people sustained machete cuts.

On 2 April 2023, an unidentified armed group in their hundreds attacked civilians in Oganenigu (Dekina, Kogi) and killed 10 persons including the APC ward chairman of Oganenigu and a pastor who initially fled but went back to the church when he thought the assailants had left. Hundreds of houses were also set ablaze, other sources report that at least 50 houses were burnt by the assailants who shot people on sight when they arrived.

On 2 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife and son of the village head of Nasarawa village in Tsanyawa LGA (Kano) from their residence in the village. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 2 April 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted two female students of Federal University Gusau from a private hostel at Sabon Gida, coded to nearby Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). The assailants tied up two gatekeepers at the hostel and stole their phones before abducting the victims. There are no reports about ransom demands, the abductees were released on 14 April, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 2 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three residents in Dabna (Hong, Adamawa) when they invaded the community. The assailants shot sporadically during the attack, looted medicine and food stores, they also set vehicles and other valuables ablaze. Other sources report that 4 persons were killed.

On 3 April 2023, hunters and an unidentified communal militia clashed at the Sabon Gari-Trikaniya area (Chikun, Kaduna). The clash started the previous day [coded separately], two people were killed and six others were wounded, 2 fatalities split across two events coded as 1. The state government imposed a curfew in the area to curtail further attacks.

On 3 April 2023, a local defense militia numbering over 60 killed one person and wounded several others at Dugwer community in Bali LGA (Taraba) while trying to eject them from a land. The assailants also looted farm products, motorcycles and personal belongings. Residents claimed that the state governor had indicted interest to take over the land and the assailants were working on the orders of the Chief of Jibu.

On 3 April 2023, an unidentified armed group affiliated with a PDP chieftain, Chief Kevwe Edoja attacked a chieftain of the APC at his residence in Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta). Casualties are unknown.

On 3 April 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed three persons in Igbobi community (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo. The traditional ruler of the community was one of the victims, he was abducted and later killed.
On 3 April 2023, suspected armed pastoralists in their numbers attacked civilians in Kwesati (Ussa, Taraba). At least 10 people were killed and houses were set ablaze by the assailants.

On 3 April 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted at least 10 students of government secondary school Awon (Kachia, Kaduna). The state government confirmed the abduction and added that 8 students and an unspecified number of residents were abducted and that the students were not abducted on the school premises but on their way home from school. There are no reports about ransom demands, the government claimed that 8 students were abducted and they escaped back home around 18 April.

On 3 April 2023, a policeman shot and killed two civilians in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The victims were a trader and a commercial tricycle rider, other sources report that the second victim was an okada rider who was wounded and that the trader was hit by a stray bullet as a result of sporadic shooting by policemen who invaded the market and attempted to arrest commercial okada riders.

On 3 April 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a staunch Islamic faithful along the Atundaolu area of Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). The victim was hit in the head with a stick after the assailants noticed that the bullets shot at him did not have any effect. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 3 April 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a student of University of Benin in his hostel in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Other sources report that the victim was the school's chief of Kegite, students chased away security operatives who arrived the scene after and also chased away other students who were in class.

Around 3 April 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a bouncer at a joint in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) for preventing them from smoking Indian hemp inside the joint. Another person at the place was also hit by a stray bullet, the assailants fled from the scene.

On 4 April 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected killed a member of MACBAN at Obioma (Udi, Enugu) and killed other persons at different locations [coded separately] as claimed by MACBAN. An unspecified number of cattle were also killed during the attacks.

On 4 April 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] suspected to be from the camp of Ali Ngulde were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by Nigerian troops and Civilian JTF at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno) when they attempted to invade civilian quarters. Five militants were killed while the others fled.

On 4 April 2023, an Ofatura communal militia killed three civilians when they attacked Ovonum community (Obubra, Cross River) following a dispute over a piece of land. Several houses were also set ablaze by the assailants.

On 4 April 2023, troops of 21 brigade of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF clashed with Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants when they conducted clearance patrols at Garin Ba'aba on the fringes of Sambisa forest in Bama LGA (Borno). The troops outran the militants' camp and killed 18 of them.
On 4 April 2023, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically when they invaded Igbobi community (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo. Casualties are unknown.

On 4 April 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians in Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue) and killed three persons. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the community and residents fled, the chairman of Otukpo LGA claimed that the assailants came in from Apa through Agatu.
On 4 April 2023, a Kaduna militia who were about six in number killed 4 civilians at Dutsin Bako (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). The victims consisted of three Nigerien native medicine sellers and one local.

On 4 April 2023, ISWAP militants in large numbers were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by Nigerian troops when they attacked a location of the troops at Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 4 April 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by Nigerian troops of 73 battalion when they attempted to attack them at Njimtilo (Magumeri, Borno). The militants fled with gunshot wounds.

On 5 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three persons after they invaded Gowon estate in Ipaja (Alimosho, Lagos). One survivor was admitted at the hospital where he was receiving treatment, the police arrived the scene after the attack and claimed to have recovered nine expended cartridges and a bunch of keys.

On 5 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the district head of Chip community (Pankshin, Plateau) from his palace. The abductors forced their way into the abductee's palace and also shot sporadically to scare other people away, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 April 2023, a policeman shot and killed a civilian along Ugbolu-Illah road (Oshimili North, Delta) following a disagreement over bribe payment when the victim was stopped at a checkpoint for a search. The police claimed that the assailant policeman was arrested.

On 5 April 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians during a funeral in Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue). 43 to 46 persons which later increased to 51 were killed by the assailants who shot sporadically, when they invaded the funeral of persons who were killed the previous day [coded separately].

On 5 April 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked travelers between Ndemili and Oliogo communities (Ndokwa West, Delta). One passenger in the vehicle was shot and killed and an unspecified number of others were abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 5 April 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked and engaged policemen in an armed clash along Igarra-Auchi road (Akoko Edo, Edo). Three policemen were killed, their rifles were stolen, and other sources report that one was seriously wounded. The assailants were trailed into the bush; one of them died in the bush from bullet wounds, the second was wounded and arrested by local defense militiamen who recovered six rifles and claimed that the assailants came from Okenne in Kogi state. ISWAP claimed the attack.

On 6 April 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] killed a pastor and wounded his wife when they invaded Madthaw village coded to Miringa (Biu, Borno) which is 9km away. Some other persons were wounded, buildings were destroyed, foodstuff and livestock were looted by the militants.

Around 6 April 2023 (as reported), a Sokoto militia killed an abductee they abducted from his hometown in Rabah LGA (Sokoto) a few weeks earlier. The victim's family paid a ransom of 2 million naira for his release.

On 6 April 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one person and abducted 14 persons from Chida community in Kwali Area Council (FCT). The wounded victim was shot when he attempted to flee, the community's traditional chief was one of the abductees. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 6 April 2023, Kutep and Fulani militias clashed at Kwesati and Fikye (Ussa, Taraba) after the Kutep militia attacked pastoralists as reprisal over an attack by a suspected Fulani militia [coded separately]. Many persons were killed and many residential buildings were set ablaze including the house of the paramount ruler of Lisam Kwe who was accused by youths of taking sides with the Fulanis. Unknown fatalities coded as 10.

On 6 April 2023, PDP members abducted the state legal adviser of the APC at the headquarters of INEC in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) after he received some election documents from INEC. The abductee was released the following day, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 6 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a retired immigration officer whom they abducted around Ombi II in Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa) where they mounted a roadblock. The victim's body was found in the area the following morning.

On 6 April 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia dressed in black clothes trailed and killed a motorist at Irona area of Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). The victim was shot and his body was macheted by the assailants who took a bag from his car and fled.

On 6 April 2023, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group when they raided the group's hideout in Ikorodu (Ikorodu, Lagos). One member of the group was killed and two abductees were rescued.
On 6 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three girls as they were returning from school in Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos). The reason for the attack is unknown and there are no ransom demands.

On 7 April 2023, SEC and Black Axe militias clashed at Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos). One person was killed, several others sustained machete cuts in the a series of clashes [coded separately]. Other sources claimed that four persons were killed in the different events, the police claimed that two persons were killed. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 7 April 2023, policemen engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified cult militia suspected to be affiliated with land grabbers when they invaded the militia's hideout at Emuren (Shagamu, Ogun). One policeman was killed and his rifle was taken away by the militia, three other policemen were wounded, other sources report that the policemen were on a routine patrol.

On 7 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a former Nassarawa state deputy governor when they invaded Gwagi village in Wamba LGA (Nassarawa) and shot sporadically before taking the abductee away. The abductors fled with the victim before the arrival of policemen, the abductee was released on 9 April after a ransom of 4 million naira was paid.

On 7 April 2023, an unidentified armed group of five abducted a businesswoman from her husband's shop at Ata-Idung Afaha Eket (Eket, Akwa Ibom). The abductee was taken away in the presence of her husband after the abductors shot sporadically to scare people away. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 7 April 2023, suspected Boko Haram militants [JAS Faction] killed 10 civilians when they attacked an enclave of ISWAP fighters in Kainuwa near Gashigar (Mobbar, Borno). The victims were attacked because of locals' cooperation with ISWAP, one gun truck and six motorcycles belonging to ISWAP were captured, several makeshift houses were also burnt.

On 7 April 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over rivalry in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta). One person was killed and residents fled for fear of indiscriminate arrests by the police.
On 7 April 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at policemen at a checkpoint along Marine Base in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). One policeman was killed and the assailants drove away.
On 7 April 2023, troops of sector 3 MNJTF repelled and engaged ISWAP militants who attempted to infiltrate Monguno (Monguno, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 7 April 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 80 children from Wanzamai village in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara). The abductees who were between 12 - 17 were collecting firewood in the bush, other sources report that the abductees were 85 while the police claimed 9 persons were abducted. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded and later 1.7 million naira at the rate of 20,000 per abductee was paid, an additional 850 thousand was demanded by the militia as money to replace two of their motorcycles that were destroyed by soldiers. 74 abductees were released around 4 may after 6 million naira was paid in two installments, one of the remaining 12 abductees was murdered [coded separately] while the others were released on 10 May after an additional 500 thousand naira was paid.

On 7 April 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians in an IDP camp at Mgbam, Nyiev council ward (Guma, Benue). Between 30 - 38 persons most of whom were women were killed and 39 others were seriously wounded, an undisclosed number of houses and barns of yam seedlings were burnt. The state police spokesperson claimed that only 28 corpses were recovered.

On 8 April 2023, SEC and Black Axe militias clashed at Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos). One person was killed, several others sustained machete cuts in the a series of clashes [coded separately]. Other sources claimed that four persons were killed in the different events, the police claimed that two persons were killed. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 8 April 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji conducted offensive operations and clashed with a Zamfara militia at their hideouts in Yartasha and Chabi (Maru, Zamfara). Two militiamen were killed, one was arrested.

On 8 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed an off-duty policeman whose body was found at Mbutu (Aboh Mbaise, Imo) after he was abducted from his home in Umuoshike Ogbor. The victim visited his family to spend the Easter holiday with them.

On 8 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a Fulani cattle dealer and his daughter after they were abducted from their residence at Chitumu in Gwagwalada Area Council (FCT). One other person sustained a gunshot wound, other sources report that two persons; the father and uncle of the male abductee were killed, two others sustained gunshot wounds. A ransom of 30 million was demanded.

On 8 April 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed and clashed with a Katsina militia at Dan Marke in Kankara LGA (Katsina). The militia was intercepted while conveying a large quantity of rustled cattle; one militiaman was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, two rifles, 150 rustled cattle and 40 sheep amongst other items were recovered.
On 9 April 2023, a Kaduna militia killed three civilians at Kankomi (Chikun, Kaduna). The bodies were found by soldiers who repelled the militia's attack on a military post (coded separately).

On 9 April 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked a military post and were repelled by Nigerian army soldiers at Kankomi (Chikun, Kaduna). One militiaman was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, one rifle and ammunition was discovered.

On 9 April 2023, two local defense militias collaborated and engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash when they invaded their camp at Kainji Lake National Park (Borgu, Niger). The clash lasted for 4 days [coded separately], at least 50 Niger militiamen and two local defense militiamen were killed, 9 out of 12 abductees including the registrar of the sharia court in Ibbi town were killed by the Niger militia in retaliation for the murder of their colleagues and destruction of their camp, the other 3 abductees escaped. 61 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 16.

On 9 April 2023, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group when they came to receive ransom at Toungo LGA (Adamawa). One member of the group was killed, the others fled with bullet wounds, two abductees were rescued.

On 9 April 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants when they raided their hideouts at (Askira Uba, Borno) coded to Askira, Gwoza and Damboa [coded separately]. 4 militants were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, their camps were destroyed and 136 civilians comprising of 46 adult females and 90 children were rescued. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 9 April 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants when they raided their hideouts in Damboa LGA (Borno), Askira Uba and Gwoza [coded separately]. 4 militants were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, their camps were destroyed and 136 civilians comprising of 46 adult females and 90 children were rescued. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 9 April 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity on a clearance patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia on a high ground ahead of Kafaiyo in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, a rifle and two motorcycles were recovered. Several militia camps near Kafaiyo, Dafako, Kopi and Gadani were dismantled.

On 9 April 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants when they raided their hideouts in Gwoza LGA (Borno), Askira Uba and Damboa [coded separately]. 4 militants were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, their camps were destroyed and 136 civilians comprising of 46 adult females and 90 children were rescued. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 10 April 2023, SEC militia wounded scores of people and vandalized properties at Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun). The reason for the attack is unknown, the police intervened and arrested the assailants [coded separately].
On 10 April 2023, a Niger militia abducted an unspecified number of people when they attacked Kasuwan-Garba in Mashegu LGA (Niger). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 10 April 2023, two local defense militias collaborated and engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash when they invaded their camp at Kainji Lake National Park (Borgu, Niger). The clash lasted for 4 days [coded separately], at least 50 Niger militiamen and two local defense militiamen were killed, 9 out of 12 abductees including the registrar of the sharia court in Ibbi town were killed in by the Niger militia in retaliation for the murder of their colleagues and destruction of their camp, the other 3 abductees escaped. 61 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 15.

Around 10 April 2023 (as reported), an Ezeke-Amasiri militia attacked residents of Amata-Akpoha in Akpoha (Afikpo North, Ebonyi) on their farmlands following a land dispute. Seven people were wounded, three of them were in critical conditions.

On 10 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and injured another at Gangarbi village (Rogo, Kano) coded to Rogo Sabon Gari when they went to abduct a popular businessman from the village. The assailants shot sporadically to scare people which hit the victims.

On 10 April 2023, a Zamfara militia was engaged in an armed clash with policemen in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara) when they attempted to attack a community. The militiamen were repelled, at least two of them were killed and the others fled with possible gunshot wounds.

On 11 April 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed a Kaduna militia during a strategic operation and engaged them in an armed clash at Sabon Birni area (Igabi, Kaduna). One militia leader, Isiya Danwasa and an unspecified number of militiamen were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 11 April 2023, two local defense militias collaborated and engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash when they invaded their camp at Kainji Lake National Park (Borgu, Niger). The clash lasted for 4 days [coded separately], at least 50 Niger militiamen and two local defense militiamen were killed, 9 out of 12 abductees including the registrar of the sharia court in Ibbi town were killed in by the Niger militia in retaliation for the murder of their colleagues and destruction of their camp, the other 3 abductees escaped. 61 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 15.

Around 11 April 2023 (as reported), SEC and Black Axe militias clashed at Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos). Several persons sustained machete cuts in the a series of clashes [coded separately]. Some sources claimed that four persons were killed in the different events, the police claimed that two persons were killed. 4 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 11 April 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a chieftain of the APC at his country home in Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta). The victim was the chairman of an APC support group called the Achievers Group, other sources report that he was killed due to his support for the APC presidential candidate.
On 11 April 2023, two factions of Deebam militia engaged in an armed clash over following a supremacy war at Elechi Beach in Mile 1, Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). Two persons were killed.
On 11 April 2023, ISWAP claimed to have fired two mortar shells at a Nigerian army base in Goniri (Gujba, Yobe). Other sources claimed that the mortar shells landed on the outskirts of town.
On 11 April 2023, an unidentified cult militia abducted two shop owners in Ubeta community (Ahoada West, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a domestic worker at the palace of the traditional ruler of Oghara in Kabba LGA (Kogi). The traditional ruler and two chiefs were abducted, one of the chiefs escaped, the assailants shot sporadically before gaining access into the palace. A ransom of 60 million naira which was later reduced to 2 million naira was demanded, the traditional died from torture while the second abductee was released.

On 11 April 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted nine people from Kutcheri (Tsafe, Zamfara). The abductees consisted of nine females and two males, they were rescued by policemen on 13 April [there are no reports on a clash].
On 11 April 2023, two unidentified armed groups clashed at Magodo (Kosofe, Lagos) over the enforcement of a court judgement. The police was invited to quell the tension, casualties are unknown

On 12 April 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji in collaboration with a local defense militia engaged a Zamfara militia and repelled them in around Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara). The militia had planned to attack Gidan Danjimma and Kirifada before they were repelled, 15 militants were killed including their leader Dankarami also known as Jarfa, an unspecified number of others sustained various degrees of injuries and fled into the forest. Two soldiers and four local militiamen were wounded.

On 12 April 2023, Nigerian troops engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along Dambisa-Bini road (Maru, Zamfara). The militiamen had blocked the road to abduct commuters, before they were repelled, two of them were killed while the troops recovered one rifle, and a motorcycle.

On 12 April 2023, two local defense militias collaborated and engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash when they invaded their camp at Kainji Lake National Park (Borgu, Niger). The clash lasted for 4 days [coded separately], at least 50 Niger militiamen and two local defense militiamen were killed, 9 out of 12 abductees including the registrar of the sharia court in Ibbi town were killed in by the Niger militia in retaliation for the murder of their colleagues and destruction of their camp, the other 3 abductees escaped. 61 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 15.
On 12 April 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians in Ruji and Atak'Njeh villages (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zangon Katab. Nine persons were killed and three others were wounded.

Around 12 April 2023 (as reported), Hausa and Fulani ethnic militias clashed in Gwadabawa LGA (Sokoto) and killed scores of persons. Soldiers intervened in the clash and one soldier was killed. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 12 April 2023, a Fulani militia numbering eight clashed with policemen when they invaded a Fulani settlement at Ago-Igbira (Odo-Otin, Osun) coded to Okuku. One person was injured a pastoralist was abducted by the assailants, the abductee was rescued by Amotekun operatives after the abductors abandoned him on sighting the operatives in a forest boundary between Osun and Kwara.

On 12 April 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed three persons two of whom are presumed to be unarmed members of a cult militia at Ubeta (Ahoada West, Rivers). Sources report that the attack appeared to be a reprisal.

On 12 April 2023, a Kaduna militia clashed with a local defense militia at Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and killed 4 four local defense militiamen and 9 residents. 25 others were abducted by the assailants who shot indiscriminately, looted shops and rustled cattle. NAF carried out an airstrike on the militia as they were fleeing [coded separately].
On 13 April 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted and killed one Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighter at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). One AK-47 rifle was recovered.

On 13 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person when they blocked Assakio-Sabon Gida road (Lafia, Nassarawa). The abductee was rescued by policemen the following day [coded separately].

Around 13 April 2023 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia killed a police constabulary who is presumed to have been off-duty in his community, Ikot Abasi Akpan in Mkpat Enin (Akwa Ibom). The victim who was behead and his body dumped inside a well, was attacked over claims that he was working as police informant.

On 13 April 2023, ISWAP militants killed 10 civilians in Buni Gari (Gujba, Yobe). The first victim was abducted and killed while the others were ambushed and killed when they went to search for the first victim. ISWAP claimed the attack, stating that it had captured and killed 13 militia members loyal to the Nigerian Army. Other sources report that the victims were civilians.
On 13 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilian men from Igoba (Akure North, Ondo). The abductees were four and one of them escaped, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 14 April 2023, a Katsina militia in their numbers were engaged in an armed cash by policemen who responded to a distress call at Agarwal village in Kurfi LGA (Katsina). Two militiamen were killed, many others fled with bullet wounds.

On 14 April 2023, policemen clashed with an unidentified armed group after they abducted a man the previous day [coded separately] from along Assakio-Sabon Gida road (Lafia, Nassarawa). Three members of the group were killed, one was arrested, a weapon and seven rounds of ammunition were recovered and the abductee was rescued.

On 14 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a couple along Oshogbo-Iragbiji road in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The victims ran into an ambush that was mounted by the abductors, there are no reports about ransom demands. The abductees were rescued by policemen after a clash with their abductors [coded separately].

On 14 April 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked commuters on the Yankara-Tsafe road (Tsafe, Zamfara). An unspecified number of persons were wounded and abducted, some vehicles also crashed and resulted in fatalities.

On 15 April 2023, a local defense militia engaged a Zamfara militia that came to provide reinforcement to a Niger militia for a reprisal attack in Mashegu LGA (Niger). The Zamfara militiamen numbered up to 100, over 50 of them were killed, others fled with bullet wounds and an unspecified number of local defense militiamen were also killed. Unknown self defense militia fatalities coded as 3.

On 15 April 2023, a Kaduna militia were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers and a local defense militia when they attacked civilians at Runji village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zangon Katab. 33 civilians were killed, 7 others were wounded and 40 houses were burnt during the attack that was launched by the assailants who split themselves into three group. Some sources report that an unspecified number of assailants were killed, others report that the assailants were a suspected Fulani militia, unknown assailants fatalities coded as 3.

On 15 April 2023, a Yansakai militia operative was shot and killed by soldiers at Bajida polling unit 001 (Fakai, Kebbi). The Yansakai operative was also a PDP agent who attempted to snatch a soldier's gun and a ballot box together with his group.

Around 15 April 2023 (as reported), a local defense militia beat up a man in Jengere (Bassa, Plateau) following a misunderstanding. The victim who was a youth leader in Jengere was arrested and tortured, which resulted in his death [coded separately].

On 15 April 2023, an unidentified armed group affiliated with politicians attacked civilians at a polling unit in Utai village (Wudil, Kano) during supplementary elections. Six persons were killed, other sources report that three wounded persons died while receiving treatment and that the assailants were brought from else.

On 15 April 2023, unidentified armed groups that were sympathetic to rival political parties clashed and blocked the main road in Jaba area of Ungogo LGA (Kano) during supplementary elections in the state. Casualties are unknown.
On 15 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest along Oriagu-Obowo road, coded to Otoko (Obowo, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 15 April 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked polling units where supplementary elections were taking place in Ikono/Ini federal constituency, coded to Ibiaku Ntok Okpo (Ikono, Akwa Ibom). Election materials were snatched and one NYSC member on election duty was shot and wounded in the leg at a polling unit, the elections were cancelled.

On 15 April 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked polling units where supplementary elections were taking place in Ikono/Ini federal constituency, coded to Odoro Ikpe (Ini, Akwa Ibom). Election materials were snatched and one NYSC member on election duty was shot and wounded in the leg at a polling unit, the elections were cancelled.

Around 16 April 2023 (as reported), armed Fulani pastoralists killed a farmer on his farm in (Kokona, Nassarawa) coded to Kokouna following a quarrel that ensued between them when the farmer arrived at his farm and met his the pastoralists destroying it. The victim was macheted to death.

On 16 April 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a community leader and abducted several residents from Unguwan Liman community in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The abductees comprised of males and females, and the assailants threatened to attack the community again soon.

On 16 April 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Tunkuda, Mashayawo and Mazauda (Kiyawa, Zamfara) coded to Birnin Magaji. 8 persons were killed across the villages by the militiamen who insisted on continuing the attacks in the area until the unit of soldiers stationed in the area is withdrawn.

On 16 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 8 civilians along Atampka-Uggugbu road (Ogbadibo, Benue) coded to Otukpa. The abductees were returning from a local market in Ahor-Ogbo ransom of 500 thousand naira each was demanded and one of the abductees was released due to health challenges. On 30 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one soldier who was dressed in plain clothes and abducted his colleague [both presumed to be unarmed] along Ibbadu-Idadu in Doma LGA (Nassarawa). On 30 April 2023, suspected Fulani armed pastoralists killed two farmers on their farm in Udei community (Guma, Benue). The victims were shot to death.

On 30 April 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two pastoralists at Dong Kassa village in Bassa LGA (Plateau). The state chairman of MACBAN claimed that the victims were killed on their father's farm.

On 30 April 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a lawyer from his chamber near Warri Main Market in Warri (Warri South, Delta). The abductee was released the following day after a presumed ransom amount which was undisclosed was paid.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person in Eku community (Ethiope East, Delta). Two houses and other properties were set ablaze and destroyed, other sources report that the attack may have been as a result of suspected cultists and youths of the community.

On 2 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted a lady from her residence in Fadan Ikulu (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) after shooting sporadically for almost two hours. The abductors arrived in vehicles and motorcycles, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three local defense militia operatives at Etiti Ohazu area of Aba (Aba South, Abia).

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two staff of the federal ministry of works and a contractor at Tse-Agbete village in Kendev ward (Ukum, Benue). The abductee was taken from a construction site in the area, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 2 May 2023, troops of Sector 1 of the MNJTF conducted Operation Scorpion and killed some Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants around Kirta Wulgo (Monguno, Borno). 8 repentant militants were also received, fatalities coded as 3.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons at Hoss (Riyom, Plateau). Two other persons who sustained injuries died on 4 May, residents who protested the against the attack the following day claimed that the victims were killed a few meters from a military checkpoint.
On 3 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer who was working on his farm along Ise-Emure road, coded to Emure-Ekiti (Emure, Ekiti). A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 3 May 2023, policemen beat up a man at Oko-Oba abattoir, coded to Agege (Agege, Lagos) over his refusal to submit his phone for a search. The policemen were attached to the Agege Abattoir police station.

On 3 May 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed the youth leader of Abarikpo community (Ahoada, Rivers) in his fathers compound in the same community. Some sources report that the victim's stance against cultism and insecurity in the area may have been the reason for the attack.

On 4 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia clashed with soldiers who were keeping surveillance in Bafai Gora village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). Two persons were killed, one soldier and one civilian were wounded.

The abductees who were abducted on 2 May [coded separately] were released and the militiamen fled from the area.

Around 4 May 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a woman whom they had abducted on 27 April [coded separately] after a part payment of 6 million naira was paid as ransom. On 4 May 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Yardadi village, coded to Rini district (Bakura, Zamfara). Around 4 May 2023 (as reported), troops of 21 armored brigade in Bama engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash at the Banki axis (Bama, Borno). Two out of the three aid workers who were abducted on 26 April [coded separately] were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 5 May 2023, Black Axe also known as Aiye confraternity and SEC members engaged in an armed clash following a battle for supremacy at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). One person was killed, several other persons were wounded in the clash which started on 2 May [coded separately].
On 5 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian in Gbajimba (Guma, Benue).

On 6 May 2023, an Ezza militia attacked Effium communities and were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers and policemen who repelled them in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The clash started on 5 May and lasted for three days [coded separately], casualties are unknown.

On 7 May 2023, policemen on routine patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia who were dressed in military camouflage at Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). One militia member was killed and an operation motorcycle was recovered.

On 7 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a pastoralist in Kuchimi village (Kagarko, Kaduna).

On 7 May 2023, Black Axe militia and Klansmen Konfraternity engaged in an armed clash in parts of Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom) and Idu [coded separately], over control of minibus parks and toll collection. On 8 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the front of his residence at Eket LGA (Akwa Ibom). The abductee was a staff of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.

On 9 May 2023, suspected IPOB militants ambushed and killed a member of the Imo state's APC presidential campaign council of Oru-East LGA around Awo-Omamma technical school (Oru East, Imo). On 9 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed eight civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 10 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a local politician and his son at Bureh village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The victim's wife was wounded by the assailants.

On 10 May 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted a chieftain of the APC from his residence at Umuarugo village in Umueze II (Ehime Mbano, Imo). On 10 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed seven civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 12 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians when they attacked Mawofi village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa in large numbers.
