The militia leader, Yellow was killed together with an unspecified number of his group members. Unknown fatalities coded as 3 + one militia leader fatality, total 4 fatality coded.
On 12 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 21 persons from Kago, Tsauni-Abe, Doguwa and Akoti in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). One of the abductees was a pastor, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman at a checkpoint around the Emohua axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers). The assailants arrived and shot sporadically, a civilian who was driving in a private vehicle was hit by a stray bullet.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group led by a faction of the Obubu community leaders attacked and wounded five members of the community (Udu, Delta) over a leadership tussle. An unknown number of houses were also destroyed.

Around 13 May 2023 (between 13 May - 14 May), a suspected Fulani killed three civilians when they attacked Ijaha village (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo and set two other villages ablaze [coded separately].

Around 13 May 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from her store in Rumu-Olumene community (Obio, Rivers). The abductee was released around 20 May after a ransom of 200,000 thousand was paid, the initial amount demanded was 15 million naira.

On 13 May 2023, soldiers of 21 armored brigade of Operation Hadin Kai killed one ISWAP militant at Ukuba in Bama LGA (Borno). The troops recovered a large cache of weapons which included submachine guns, hand grenades, mortar bombs, shika rounds among others.

On 13 May 2023, ISWAP militants were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by troops of Operation Hadin Kai when they attacked Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). The militants withdrew and casualties are unknown.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor who was heading to work in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). An undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom, the abductee was rescued when security agents raided their hideout [coded separately].

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer along Otu-Alaga road (Itesiwaju, Oyo) after they ambushed him and shot sporadically into the air to scare away other motorists and passers-by. The abductee is also a cattle dealer and a ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a businessman at Oba (Idemili South, Anambra) as he was driving from a meeting. The assailants shot the victim and ensured that he died without stealing any valuables from him.

On 14 May 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Katoge, Matsematsi, Tabanni villages and Matankari town (Maru, Zamfara) as a reprisal for the killed of one villager who was associated with them by local defense militiamen. 10 persons were killed across the locations while 10 others were killed in another village [coded separately]. 30 persons were wounded across the locations in the attacks which lasted from 10am to 3pm.

On 14 May 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Dankurmi village (Maru, Zamfara) as a reprisal for the killed of one villager who was associated with them by local defense militiamen. 8 persons were killed while 10 others were killed in other villages [coded separately]. 30 persons were wounded across the villages in the attacks which lasted from 10am to 3pm.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 15 persons from an estate at Pegi community in Kuje Area Council (FCT). The abductors shot sporadically into the air during the attack, there are no reports about ransom demands. Other sources report that three persons were abducted and a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded for one abductee's release from his family.
On 14 May 2023, a policeman shot and wounded a civilian in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) following a disagreement over taking turns at a tea shop.

On 14 May 2023, ISWAP militants engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian soldiers and MNJTF troops in Arege (Abadan, Borno). ISWAP claimed the attack and that it burned a barracks and military vehicles, seized two rifles and a machine gun. Other sources report that the militants attacked the troops in twin VBIED attacks which killed 3 soldiers and wounded 10 others while the militants were also repelled.

On 14 May 2023, Wurkum and Karimjo ethnic militias clashed in Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba) following a disagreement over the installation of a new monarch and between 13 to 20 persons including children who were from both sides were killed. A Wurkum representative claimed that the Karimjo militia were responsible for the attack after they burnt shops and building belonging to Wurkum people, while the Karimjo representative denied the claims and added that the police and local defense militia were responsible for the death of 10 Karimjo people. The state police command claimed that only two casualties were recorded.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked two pickup vehicles as they were conveying cattle to a local market in Takum LGA (Taraba). One driver was killed while the second one escaped and the cattle being conveyed were set ablaze.
On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters when they fired indiscriminately at their bus along Mararaba-Takum road in Takum LGA (Taraba).

On 14 May 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to distress call over the militia's attack on Bajinawa village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. One militia member was killed; others are assumed to have fled with bullet wounds, one rifle was recovered, five women who were abducted were rescued by the policemen

On 14 May 2023, policemen repelled an attack by a Sokoto militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Giremshi community in Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto). The clash lasted for over two hours, casualties are unknown.
On 14 May 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash in the vicinity of Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 15 May 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one person when they fired indiscriminately at Ilela Hudu village in Goronyo LGA (Sokoto). The assailants also abducted three persons.
On 15 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one farmer and abducted two others in Askawa village, Zurmi LGA (Zamfara).

On 15 May 2023, an unidentified armed group of between five and seven persons attacked travelers in a commercial bus on the Iju-Itaogbolu-Ikere road (Ikere, Ekiti). Three sustained gunshot wounds while the other three were abducted.

On 15 May 2023, a Boko Haram militant detonated a suicide vest which he was wearing and killed himself during a joint raid by operatives of DSS, policemen and soldiers on militants' hideouts at Keke community of Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna) and Kano [coded separately]. Other suicide jackets, IEDs, and weapons were recovered and three persons were arrested. No one else was killed or injured.
On 15 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with Nigerian soldiers on patrol at Allagarno forest (Damboa, Borno) which led to the troops' withdrawal.

On 15 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to targeted a Nigerian army patrol with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher on the Bosso-Malam Fatori road (Abadan, Borno). An SUV was burned and an unspecified number of soldiers were wounded.
On 15 May 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted the chief imam of Giribishi jumaat mosque in Giribishi village (Wamakko, Sokoto) coded to Wamako.
On 15 May 2023, a Zamfara militia shot indiscriminately and killed an unspecified number of commuters along Kaura-Shinkafi road, Shnikafi LGA (Zamfara). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group of five killed one person and abducted three others on Ijara - Isanlu-Isin road (Osin, Kwara). The murdered victim was a local chief from Pamo Isin who was passing on his motorcycle, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted twelve NYSC members on the Rumuji axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers) as they were returning from orientation camp in Ondo state. Five of the abductees escaped, the remaining seven were released on 21 May after an undisclosed ransom amount was paid.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two locals in Yarimawa (Tofa, Kano) when attempted to help a family that the assailants attacked. One assailant mistakenly shot and killed his partner, three suspects were arrested.

On 16 May 2023, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants engaged policemen who were on a convoy of US embassy staff in an armed clash along Atani-Osamale road (Ogbaru, Anambra) before a reinforcement of policemen and soldiers arrived. Two to four policemen who were part of the convoy, a driver and two consulate staff were killed, their bodies and vehicle were set ablaze, two other policemen, other sources report three, were abducted, an unspecified number of persons were wounded and nine persons were killed. On 19 May, the abductees were rescued unhurt by a joint team of security forces. IPOB denied being involved in the attack, and claimed that it's accusers were responsible for the attack.

Around 16 May 2023 (as reported), MNJTF troops clashed with ISWAP militants at Fedondiya and Arege general areas (Abadan, Borno). Several militants were killed, on dushka gun, dushka turrell and gun truck were recovered. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a patrol of the Nigerian Army at Allagarno forest (Damboa, Borno). A suicide bomber detonated a SVBIED which killed and wounded a number of soldiers. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 16 May 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted six persosn when they attacked Moore community in Kware LGA (Sokoto). The abductees included the wife and two sons of the local government area chairman.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed 29 women and children at Fungai and Kunwat villages in Mangu LGA (Plateau). Several persons were wounded, houses with valuables worth millions of naira were destroyed. Other sources report that the fatalities rose to 85.

On 16 May 2023, policemen together with other security agents assumed to be soldiers responded to a distress call and repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group at Tanknale village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The assailants killed 30 civilians before they fled following the arrival of the security agents, they abandoned 4 motorcycles and a car which were recovered.
On 16 May 2023, a Katsina militia wounded a man and his son and abducted his wife at a residence in Badole villages (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 16 May 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Uchen (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka. Seven members of the same family including a six-month old baby were killed, others were wounded. The state police command claimed that five persons were killed, other sources report that six people were killed in the attack while one other person fell and died after discovering the bodies of others.
On 17 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons and abducted six others at Yangoji (Kwali, FCT).

On 17 May 2023, soldiers attacked and beat up a group of special hunters [presumed to be unarmed] and wounded one of them at Zumba community (Shiroro, Niger). The soldiers accused the hunters of wearing red berets which is part of the soldier's uniform, one civilian was knocked down by the soldiers' patrol vehicle.

On 17 May 2023, a Niger militia wounded three persons and abducted eight others along Wawa-Luma road (Borgu, Niger). The abductees were passengers and the driver of a bus, one person escaped into the bush. Three of the abductees were released after a ransom of 1.5 million naira each was paid, another was murdered over delayed payment of a 2 million naira ransom [coded separately].

On 17 May 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering over 20 killed the youth leader of Patanyi village in Bugana ward (Omala, Kogi) whom they abducted when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. The victim's body was found beheaded in a river, he was abducted while on a hunting expedition with four others.
On 17 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to targeted a Nigerian army patrol with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher on at Arege (Abadan, Borno). There were no casualties.

On 17 May 2023, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants numbering over 50 who were dressed in black attire killed two brothers at their residence in Aba (Aba South, Abia) after they were suspected to have been informants for the police. The assailants also set the victims' house ablaze.

On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two staff of the Nigerian Railway Corporation at Owa-Oyibu (Ika North East, Delta). The car that he abductee were driving was destroyed, its windshield was shattered, a ransom of 40 million naira was demanded. The police spokesperson in the state denied any record of the event.
Around 18 May 2023 (as reported), some policemen beat up and wounded a commercial okada rider near a bridge at Abule Egba area (Alimosho, Lagos) as he tried to prevent him from stealing his bike.

On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Eke Awgbu market in Awgbu community (Orumba North, Anmabra) and killed 4 persons. One person was burnt alive in his shop, three others were shot and goods worth millions of naira were destroyed. The attack was a retaliation for the killing of two of the group's members by a mob the previous day.
On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one civilian from along NTA road in Mgbuoba (Obio, Rivers).

On 18 May 2023, soldiers shot and killed a man suspected to have been an informant for a Kaduna militia when they raided a hideout in Kagarko town (Kagarko, Kaduna). The victim who was decleared wanted previously attempted to escape and was shot dead, six others were arrested.

On 18 May 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged Civilian JTF operatives who were escorting civilians to work in the fields in an armed clash at Kirawa (Gwoza, Borno). One Civilian JTF was killed after he ran out of ammunition and the militants beheaded him.

On 18 May 2023, ISWAP militants fired some mortar shells targeted at Nigerian troops in Arege (Abadan, Borno). The shells fell some distance away without causing impact and the troops responded with heavy fire which caused the militants to flee.
On 18 May 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian troops on the outskirts of Wudula in Konduga LGA (Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons from Umutu community (Ukwuani, Delta). The abductees were rescued by a local defense militia who searched the bushes.

On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest while he was preparing for mass at his new adoration site in Ogii village (Onuimo, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who were conducting a stop and search in an armed clash at Ekredjebor community (Ughelli North, Delta) coded to Ughelli. The policemen were attached to the Ofuoma police division, two of them were killed and their rifles were stole by the assailants, one was wounded.

On 19 May 2023, the suspected Zamfara militia clashed with the Nigerian troops around Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The troops were trying to rescue the five students abducted by the armed group. The troops rescued the hostage.
On 19 May 2023, the suspected Zamfara militia abducted five students in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The Nigerian soldiers later rescued the students, coded separately.

On 19 May 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at their hideout in Oyigbo/Igbo-Etche forest, coded to Oyigbo (Oyigbo, Rivers). The clash lasted for about one hour and two members of the group were killed, one rifle and 18 live ammunition were recovered.

On 19 May 2023, Nigerian troops of Hadarin Daji attacked four camps of the Zamara militia in Fakai village, coded to Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). An unspecified number of the militia members were killed, coded 3; and the soldiers rescued some hostages.

Around 20 May 2023 (as reported), suspected Fulani pastoralists raped and killed an 80-year old woman on her farm in the Costain area of Ore (Odigbo, Ondo). The victim had been missing for days before her naked body was found on her farm.

On 20 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia raped some women and killed six civilians at Akpete community (Apa, Benue). The attack was launched at night and a search for more fatalities was carried out in the morning.

On 20 May 2023, suspected IPOB militants numbering five killed two policemen and wounded others at a checkpoint in Okpala junction, coded to Umuneke Ngor (Ngor Okpala, Imo). Some sources report that the assailants had warned policemen to stay way from the checkpoint, citing extortion and brutality as the reasons. Other sources report that seven policemen were killed and one was wounded. The police claimed that the militants fled after a reinforcement of policemen engaged them in a clash.
On 20 May 2023, an armed group (described as bandits, coded as UAG) killed one civilian when they attacked Gure (Baruten, Kwara).

On 21 May 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists shot and killed one farmer in Kwi (Riyom, Plateau). The victim and other farmers had tried to resist the pastoralists from grazing cattle on their farm when he was killed.
On 21 May 2023, the suspected Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters along the Illela Road, Illela (Illela, Sokoto).

On 21 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia clashed with soldiers who responded to a distress call in Iye community (Guma, Benue). 18 civilians were killed, some of them including women and children were beheaded, several others were wounded, houses and food barns were set ablaze. Other sources report that 22 persons comprising of 4 soldiers, 3 children, 2 women and 13 men were killed, many of the civilians were burnt inside their houses.

On 21 May 2023, suspected armed pastoralists clashed with a local defense militia in Umutu (Ukwuani, Delta) when the militia attempted to foil an abduction attempt by the group. Two local defense militiamen were killed, the second victim sustained bullet wounds and later dies at a hospital, and no abductions were carried out.

On 21 May 2023, a Fulani ethnic militia supported by Hausa traders engaged a Kuteb ethnic militia in an armed clash in Takum town (Takum, Taraba). Over 20 persons were killed when the Fulani militia attacked Kuteb residents following a rumor that 5 Fulani pastoralists were killed in the town, an unspecified number of persons were wounded and security agents dispelled the two groups and ended the clash. Other sources report that the clash was between Christians and Muslims and that 6 persons were killed and a 24 hour curfew was imposed on the town.

On 21 May 2023, an unidentified armed group dreesed in the uniform of a local defense militia killed two persons at Rafa Kasuwan Shanu in Takum (Takum, Taraba). The attack result in a reprisal clash between Hausa-Fulani and Kuteb residents [coded separately].

On 21 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted five members of an Islamic group along Kaduna-Abuja expressway, coded to Kachia LGA (Kaduna). The abductees who were from Oyo state were returning from a Dawah programme in Kano state. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 21 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed nine farmers and abducted three others while they were working on their farm in Unguwar Danko, coded to nearby Dogon Dawa village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Some locals confronted the assailants who shot and wounded an unspecified number of them.

On 21 May 2023, two unidentified cult militias clashed at Ire-Akari road in Isolo (Oshodi, Lagos). One person was killed. The DPO of Aswani police station claimed that policemen were mobilized to the scene and one of them was wounded.

On 21 May 2023, armed pastoralists shot and killed a commercial motorcyclist at Umuekpu Agwa, coded to nearby Obudi-Agwa (Oguta, Imo) after residents of the area confronted them over their cattle grazing in the area and damaging crops. The victim was shot by the assailants as they headed in another direction.

On 22 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Amakohia-Ubi, coded to Amakohia (Ikeduru, Imo). One of the victims was taking his children to school when he was killed, the assailants took his car after removing the children.
On 22 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a police checkpoint, killed a policeman and wounded two others at Union Bank roundabout in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi).

Around 22 May 2023 (as reported), operatives of Operation Zenda joint task force presumed to comprise of soldiers and policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideout at Gaya village in Utange ward (Katsina Ala, Benue). One member of the group was killed, three others were arrested and others fled with bullet wounds while ten abductee were rescued. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered.
On 22 May 2023, Katsina militia shot and killed a man and wounded another while raiding a farm in Kirtawa village, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina).

On 22 May 2023, Nigerian troops of sector 3 and sector 4 MNJTF engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash at Arege (Abadan, Borno). ISWAP militants fired multiple mortars at the troops who responded with artillery fire which forced militants to flee. ISWAP claimed to have fired 3 mortar shells. Casualties are unknown.

On 22 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted two housewives in Kasangwai village which is a few meters away from Akoti village in Kachia LGA (Kaduna). The abductors shot sporadically when they invaded the area.

Around 23 May 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia killed one man who they abducted alongside others on the Wawa-Luma road (Borgu, Niger) over the failure of his family to pay the demanded 2 million naira ransom within 48 hours. The victim was killed after the ransom was paid because it was delivered late.
On 24 May 2023, a Fulani militia led by a militia leader called Wariri attacked civilians in Gbajimba (Guma, Benue), Agasha and Mbawa [coded separately]. Casaulties are unknown.

On 24 May 2023, an undentified armed group engaged policemen at a checkpoint in an armed clash at Oshiri division (Onicha, Ebonyi) where the policemen were on a stop and search duty. Three policemen and two of the assailants were killed, one policeman was wounded, other assailants fled with gunshot wounds, a car, weapons ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 24 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two pastors from a residence in Nyibango area of Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The pastors were the general overseer of Freedom Power church, from whose residence they were abducted, and another pastor from the same church. A ransom of 40 million naira was demanded, the abductees were rescued by policemen and hunters who invaded the abductors' hideout on 26 May [coded separately]. Other sources report that the abductees were released after 10 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 24 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed 22 farmers who were working in their farm in Gidan Goga (Maradun, Zamfara). The victims are killed when they attempted to escape abduction when the militiamen began to shoot sporadically. The police claim that 9 people were killed and five were wounded.
On 24 May 2023, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed over supremacy at Orhuwhorum community (Udu, Delta). Two persons whose identities are unknown were killed.
On 24 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier when they attacked a military checkpoint at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno) and the other soldiers fled.
On 24 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed a clergyman in his compound at Npat village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The victim's cattle were rustled by the assailants.
On 24 May 2023, a Fulani militia led by a militia leader called Wariri attacked civilians in Agasha (Guma, Benue), Gbajimba and Mbawa [coded separately]. Casaulties are unknown.
On 24 May 2023, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Jol and Byei communities (Riyom, Plateau). Two youths were killed and one other person sustained serious injuries.
On 24 May 2023, a Fulani militia led by a militia leader called Wariri attacked civilians in Mbawa (Guma, Benue), Agasha and Gbajimba [coded separately]. Casaulties are unknown.

On 25 May 2023, a Zamfara militia fleeing from Zamfara state abducted an unspecified number of residents from Gobirawa area of Birinin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militiamen had encircled the town, the local government council imposed a curfew on the town.
On 25 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian army camp with a 40-caliber grenade launcher at Auno (Konduga, Borno). Other sources claim that there was no attack at the location.

Around 25 May 2023 (between 22 - 28 May), Nigerien and Nigerian troops of the MNJTF carried out an operation against ISWAP militants in the area of Arege (Abadan, Borno). 55 militants including senior military and religious cadres were 'neutralized' (presumably killed) and 2 soldiers were killed and 3 others were wounded, and one vehicle was damaged in the operation. 13 vehicles, 13 motorcycles, and 5 SVBIEDs were also destroyed, according to a Nigerien government statement.

On 25 May 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia of four shot and killed a man at a drinking joint in Aba (Aba South, Abia) and beheaded him before fleeing. The assailants arrived in a tricycle and also shot sporadically.
On 25 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional prime minister of Mgbele (Oguta, Imo) in the community.

On 25 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Orsu Obodo at Umuamaka junction in Izombe town (Oguta, Imo). The victim was shot in his car after which his body was set ablaze.
On 25 May 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants as they attacked Gwoza (Gwoza, Bornu). The troops repelled the attack.

Around 26 May 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadarin Daji conducted operations and clashed with a Zamfara militia at their camps in Dawan Jiya and Tungar Daji villages of Bagega district (Anka, Zamfara). Many militiamen were killed, many weapons were recovered and their camps were destroyed and taken over by the troops. Many fatalities coded as 10.
On 26 May 2023, Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and killed their leader in Wasagu (Danko, Kebbi).
On 26 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one person in the vicinity of Nasarawa Godal ward in Kiyawa LGA (Zamfara).

On 26 May 2023, policemen in collaboration with hunters and a local defense militia raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them inan armed clash at an area connecting part of Gujubabu, Bole, Yolde Pate and Yadi, coded to Yolde Pate (Yola-North, Adamawa). One member of the armed group was killed, three abductees including two pastors that were abducted on 24 May were rescued.
On 26 May 2023, a Zamfara militia shot and killed one passenger along Kaura Namoda - Magami Tandu road (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara).
On 26 May 2023, a Zamfara militia fired indiscriminaately at commuters along the Kaura-Shinkafi road in Shinkafi LGA (Zamfara). Casualties are unknown.
On 26 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one person on the outskirts of Shinkafi town (Shinkafi, Zamfara).

On 26 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest along Ogbaku-Ejemekwuru road (Oguta, Imo) as he was returning from a funeral, three others traveling with him were abducted alongside but were released to take the priest's car. The abductee was released on 28 May, there are no reports on ransom payment.
On 27 May 2023, a Katsina militia attacked a Fulani settlement at Salihawa, coded to Salihawar Kalgo (Safana, Katsina). Casualties are unknown.

On 27 May 2023, ISWAP militants abducted four firewood truck drivers and an unspecified number of passengers at Ngwom (Mafa, Borno). The passengers who were laborers were later released, a ransom of 250,000 was demanded for the release of the drivers. The abductees were rescued by soldiers of 112 task force battalion in conjuction with Civilian JTF and hunters [the means of rescue was not stated].

On 27 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have targeted a Nigerian Army base with a 40mm grenade launcher in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). The militants also claimed to have killed and wounded several soldiers when they attacked a military position in the same area. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 28 May 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person from Dogon Ruwa village (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 28 May 2023, security operatives presumed to be policemen killed a gardener when they invaded the premises of the church where he worked around Aboh (Aboh Mbaise, Imo). The invasion was related to intelligence related to the murder of two policemen on May 20 [coded separately], the leader of the worship center claimed that property worth 200 million naira was destroyed, other sources claim that the victim was killed based on a mistaken identity.

On 28 May 2023, two suspected members of an unidentified armed group detonated a suspected bomb and killed themselves at their apartment in Keffi (Keffi, Nassarawa). Some sources report that the bombers were on the wanted list of the DSS and detonated the device when the operatives circled the apartment.

On 28 May 2023, an unidentified armed group who introduced themselves as 'government' shot and killed a man at his residence in Ogbokiri community (Emohua, Rivers). The victim was a pipeline surveillance contractor with Tantita pipeline surveillance company, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 28 May 2023, troops of the MNJTF conducted clearance operations and clashed ISWAP militants at the fringe of Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Three militants were killed and one soldier was wounded.

Around 28 May 2023 (as reported), members of local defense militia killed a commercial tricycle rider at Ojoto community (Idemili South, Anambra) and stole his tricycle. The assailants including the militia's commander and two other members dumped the victim's body in a river and sold his tricycle, they were arrested by the police.

On 28 May 2023, a policeman killed a civilian at the Oregun area of Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos) when they shot sporadically while trying to disperse a crowd where people were fighting. The victim was hit by a stray bullet.

On 29 May 2023, a suspected Deebam cult militia killed four members of a local defense militia (RUSPAC) unarmed in Rundele (Emohua, Rivers) when they invaded the area, shot sporadically and also abducted and unspecified number of men. Two of the victims were beheaded, their heads were displayed, and their private parts were chopped off, the assailants who were said to have been sent away from the community for cult activities declared that they would return to reclaim their territory. Other sources report 6 fatalities while the police claimed that 4 persons were killed as a result of a cult clash.

On 29 May 2023, some Katisna militia attacked and wounded a man at his residence in Tani village near Bindawa (Bindawa, Katsina) in a failed abduction. The armed group attempted to abduct the victim but declined and was subsequently cut in the head. The police intervened and engaged in a gun duel with the militant, coded separately.

On 29 May 2023, the police clashed with Katsina Militia in Tani village near Bindawa (Bindawa, Katsina). The police responded to a distress call over a failed abduction of a man in the village, coded separately. The militia engaged in a gun duel with the police and lost two militants, later discovered by the police to be on the wanted list.

On 29 May 2023, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a man in the Abarikpo community (Ahoada, Rivers). The cultists had searched the community for three persons but killed a man in his house. He was shot in the stomach.
On 29 May 2023, PDP and APC supporters engaged in an armed clash in (Wamakko, Sokoto) coded to Wamako. Casualties are unknown.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the village chief of Unguwan Bakutunbe form the community in Ningi LGA (Bauchi) after they invaded the area and shot sporadically to scare residents away. A ransom of 8 million naira was demanded, other sources report that three persons were abducted from Balma and Unguwan Bakutunde.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked residents in Kwi (Riyom, Plateau), Jol and Rim [coded separately]. The attacks took place simulteaneously; 11 persons were killed in Kwi, entire community was burned down, hundreds of farmlands were destroyed and several others were wounded across the attacked communities. Other sources report that 29 persons were killed across the three locations.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded an unspecified number of travelers when they shot at their bus along Ajaokuta-Itobe road (Ajaokuta, Kogi). The assailants had fired several shots at the direction of the bus driver in an attempt to abduct them.
On 11 June 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted an unspecified number of people along Kaduna-Zaria (Zaria, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one resident at Balma (Ningi, Bauchi) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically to scare residents away. The village head was abducted and a ransom of 8 million naira was demanded. Other sources report that three persons were abducted from Balma and Unguwan Bakutunde.
On 11 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a civilian at Jarawa (Kala Balge, Borno) who according to them was a sorcerer.

On 11 June 2023, a local defense militia trailed the leader of the Sokoto militia and killed him along Kware-Sokoto road (Kware, Sokoto). The militia leader had killed a civilian at Illela LGA [coded separately].
On 11 June 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one person when they attacked Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara).
On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two Fulani pastoralists at Fas district in Riyom (Plateau) as they were returning from rearing cattle.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked residents in Jol community (Riyom, Plateau), Kwi and Rim [coded separately]. The attacks took place simulteaneously, seven persons were killed in Jol, several others were wounded across the attacked communities. Other sources report that 29 persons were killed across the three locations.

On 11 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked residents in Rim community (Riyom, Plateau), Kwi and Jol [coded separately]. The attacks took place simulteaneously, 2 persons were killed in Rim, several others were wounded across the attacked communities. Other sources report that 29 persons were killed across the three locations.

On 12 June 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji ambushed a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at their hideouts in Kairu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Kyaram [coded separately]. Three militiamen were killed, two AK47 rifles, one pump action gun, three motorcycles and other items were recovered. 3 fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 12 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an Akwa Ibom state PDP chieftain from his filling station in Oron (Oron, Akwa Ibom). The abductors drove the abductee to a waiting speedboat and then set the vehicle ablaze before fleeing. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 12 June 2023, a Katsina militia attacked farmers in Kirtawa village, Safana LGA (Katsina) and killed one person. Two other persons were wounded.

On 12 June 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified cult militia in an armed clash at their hideout in Ogoloma (Okrika, Rivers). Four militia members including the leader who had been decleared wanted and a female were killed.

On 12 June 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform invaded some villages in Adakam community (Ezinihitte Mbaise, Imo) coded to Itu. Residents fled into the bush and casualties are unknown. Other sources report that the invasion was instigated by the community's traditional ruler.

On 12 June 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji ambushed a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at their hideouts in Kyaram (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Kairu [coded separately]. Three militiamen were killed, two AK47 rifles, one pump action gun, three motorcycles and other items were recovered. 3 fatalities split across two events coded as 1.

On 12 June 2023, a Katsina militia engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash when they attacked a farm that the defense militia was guarding in Maitsane village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded as Dutsin Ma. Two local defense militiamen were killed and an unspecified number were wounded.

On 12 June 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a medical doctor at his residence in Jangebe (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) and abducted 10 residents including his family members. The assailants broke a wall of the doctor's house to gain entrance.
On 12 June 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked Dikwa town (Dikwa, Borno). The militants withdrew when Nigerian troops were deployed to the location, casualties are unknown.

On 13 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of travellers between Elibrada and Oduoha communities in Emohua LGA (Rivers). The abductors shot sporadically and destroyed the vehicle that the victims were traveling in.

On 13 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her child in Alapa (Asa, Kwara). The abductees were rescued by a local defense militia who pursued the abductors and engaged them in an armed clash [coded separately].

On 13 June 2023, a local defense militia pursued and engaged an unidentifed armed group in an armed clash at Ajuwon forest in Temidire community (Asa, Kwara). The armed group had abducted a woman and her child who were rescued by the militia, one member of the group was killed and two local militiamen sustained bullet wounds.

On 13 June 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of passengers from five commercial vehicle along Kaura Namoda - Shinkafi road (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 June 2023, Mbakume also called Mbaivur militia clashed with Mbasombo militia at Ikpayongo (Gwer East, Benue) during a reprisal attack after a man from Mbakume was attacked [coded separately]. Several houses and the market in the community were set ablaze, residents fled from the area.

On 13 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a policeman who is presumed to have been off-duty and two other civilians at the Ahume end of Naka-Makurdi road (Gwer West, Benue). The abductees were returning from a burial ceremony in Makurdi; a ransom of 200 thousand naira was demanded for the policeman, 1 million for the female victim and 500 thousand for the third person. The policeman and other male abductee escaped while the female paid 400 thousand naira and was released on 16 June.

On 14 June 2023, an unidentified armed group of five abducted seven students of the University of Jos from a private hostel along Bauchi-Ring road, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). There are no reports about ransom demands. The police claimed to have rescued 5 of the abductees on 16 June, one other escaped while one person was still held by the abductors, the parents of the abductees claimed that they paid an undisclosed ransom before they were released.
On 14 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The woman was with her daughter when she was abducted, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 14 June 2023, policemen wounded a woman at Alausa (Ikeja, Lagos) over suspicion that was a member of an armed group.

On 15 June 2023, Boko Haram militants killed at least 15 civilians when they attacked Molai (Jere, Borno). Seven of the victims were farmers who were beheaded, the eight others were killed in their homes and had their throats slit.

On 15 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest from the premises of a church that they invaded in Ajegbe Awume (Ohimini, Benue) coded to Idekpa-Okpiko. There are no reports about ransom demands. The police spokesperson in the state claimed that the abductee was rescued on 20 June after policemen chased the abductors and mounted pressure on them.

On 15 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed five Fulani pastoralists at Rawuru village in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). The state chairman of MACBAN claimed that the victims were ambushed as they were returning from a cattle market in Bukuru.
On 15 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted three others at Yimi community, Gwagwalada Area Council (FCT).

Around 15 June 2023 (between 7 June - 19 June), security forces comprised of soldiers, policemen and Ebube Agu operatives attacked and killed over 50 locals in Amakpurudere Izombe village (Oguta, Imo) coded as Izombe as claimed by the Ohanaeze Youth Council. Over 45 houses were destroyed in the village and more than 170 buildings in various other villages.

On 15 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a student in Wukari town (Wukari, Taraba). The victim was a student of Federal University Wukari and he was stabbed by the assailants over unknown reasons.

On 15 June 2023, policemen engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Marabar Gurbi in Kankara LGA (Katsina). One militiaman was killed and an unspecified number of others escaped with bullet wounds.

On 16 June 2023, policemen were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group when they invaded their hideout at Isiodu forest (Emohua, Rivers). Three of the group's members were killed, one person was arrested, a corpse, 8 magazine, 70 rounds of live ammunition and 10 cartridges were recovered.

On 16 June 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed eight people at Rawuru village in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). Some sources report that the attack was a reprisal for the killing of pastoralists the previous day [coded separately].

On 16 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked policemen around Ihube (Okigwe, Imo) as thet were on their way to Enugu. One policeman was killed, two others were abducted and later released on the same day and some vehicles on the convoy were shattered. The policemen were part of the security of the Enugu state governor who were directed to escort a former senator to a function in Imo state.

On 16 June 2023, an unidentified armed group of four dressed in military camouflage abducted a woman around the Kpansia axis (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The abductee was on her way to work at a bank where she is the operations manager.

On 16 June 2023, a Kaduna militia shot one civilian and abducted six others at Unguwan Ma'aji in New Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna). Eight persons were initially abducted, two escaped, it is unclear whether the person that was shot was killed or wounded.

On 16 June 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked troops of Operation Hadin Kai and engaged them in an armed clash on the road between Ajir and Wajiroko Awabrum (Damboa, Borno). The soldiers repelled the ambush and at least one soldier was wounded.

On 16 June 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted five students of Federal University Gusau from their accomodation in private hostels in Sabon Gida and Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). A ransom of 5 million naira each was demanded for the abductees' release.

On 17 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the chief imam of Uso community from his farm in Asolo Camp (Ose, Ondo). The victim was released the following day after a ransom of 2 million naira was paid by the victim's family.
On 17 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from Shande village in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 17 June 2023, a Sokoto militia killed two people and abducted an unspecified number of others from Wurno (Wurno, Sokoto).
On 17 June 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians and rustled livestock from Tozai (Illela, Sokoto) and Garu [coded separately]. 10 persons were killed, split across two events and coded as 5.
On 17 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted a shop owner at Bakin Kasuwa in Jamaare LGA (Bauchi). The assailants fired indiscriminately when they invaded the area.
On 17 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded one person at Ruwan Dinya village in Ningi LGA (Bauchi) when they invaded the area. The assailants also abducted one person.

On 17 June 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a traditional title holder and four of his sons at Dorayi village in Zaria LGA (Kaduna). The title holder was shot in the head at his house, some sources claimed that he was targeted by the assailants, 100 cattle belonging to him were also stolen. Other sources report that two other persons were shot by the assailants as they were leaving the village, it is unclear whether they were killed or wounded.
On 17 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have abducted and killed an informant of the Nigerian and Chadian forces at Kirenawa (Marte, Borno).
On 17 June 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians and rustled livestock from Garu (Illela, Sokoto) and Tozai [coded separately]. 10 persons were killed, split across two events and coded as 5.
On 18 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man in his house at Nyivu (Donga, Taraba). The victim was macheted to death.

On 18 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians when they invaded the villages of Kak, Ranyam, Nging, Lohala and Buka in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). At least 20 persons were killed and many others were wounded.

On 18 June 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two men and abducted one woman at Ishiagu (Ivo, Ebonyi). One of the murdered victims was a staff of INEC, whose wife was abducted after he was shot, the second victim encountered the assailants while he was working on his farm, as they were fleeing and they killed him by cutting his throat. The abductee was rescued by policemen who raided the hideout of the assailants on 25 June [coded separately].

On 18 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons from Wakkama village in Akwanga LGA (Nassarawa) and demanded a ransom of 30 million naira. The abductees are immediate family members of a former minister of information, Labaran Maku and they were released on 20 June after an undisclosed ransom amount was paid.

On 18 June 2023, policemen in the Katsina state command, led by the command's OC anti-kidnapping unit and OC SIB engaged a Katsina militia led by Audu Lankai in an armed clash at their camp in Jibia LGA (Katsina) and Batsari LGA [coded separately]. 5 militiamen were killed, one was arrested, 38 cows, 40 sheep and 65 goats were recovered. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 18 June 2023, policemen in the Katsina state command, led by the command's OC anti-kidnapping unit and OC SIB engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at their camps in Marake, Garin Yara, and Garin Labo villages of Batsari LGA (Katsina) and Jibia LGA [coded separately]. 5 militiamen were killed, one was arrested, 38 cows, 40 sheep and 65 goats were recovered. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 18 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of civilians when they invaded a Fulani settlement located between Shenagu and Yimi villages in Gwagwalada Area Council (FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 18 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians and wounded one person in Mangu town (Mangu, Plateau). The police spokesperson in the state claimed that the incident was a result of a problem between residents of the area, not intruders. Other sources report that many persons were killed, properties worth millions were destroyed and the attack started after a corpse was carried into a mosque. A curfew was imposed by the local council chairman.
On 18 June 2023, a Katsina militia killed one pastoralist and rustled cattle when they invaded a Fulani settlement at Badole (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 19 June 2023, operatives of EMOLVICE killed a naval rating who was off duty at his house in Oduoha (Emohua, Rivers). The victim was performing chores when they assailants arrived, shot him and fled. Other sources claim that the victim was accused of being a member of an abduction gang.

On 19 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a combined team of security operatives presumed to be made up of policemen, soldiers and a local defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Orkija (Ihiala, Anambra). The security team were on a routine patrol, two of the assailants were killed, other sources report that the assailants numberin about 15 attacked the camp of the local defense militia and an armed clash ensued.

On 19 June 2023, an unidentified were engaged in an armed clash by a local defense militia when they invaded Okanle-Fajeromi community, coded to Okanle (Ifelodun, Kwara) and abducted three members of a family. One militiaman was wounded and one of the abductees was rescued.
On 19 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Idofin and his wife along Makutu-Idofin road (Yagba East, Kogi). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 19 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a member of the Baptist church around Olodo axis, coded to nearby Ikija (Obafemi, Ogun). A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 20 June 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed an killed six civilians at Rahoss Sambak village in Ra Hoss (Riyom, Plateau). The victims were returning from a burial, two persons were first killed then four others returned to evacuate the bodies were killed. Other sources report that the victims were a local defense militia who were on surveillance.
On 20 June 2023, a Fulani militia killed at least one resident at Bwai (Mangu, Plateau). A church, and houses around the market were set blaze.

On 20 June 2023, a Fulani militia killed residents at Chisu community in Mangu LGA (Plateau) when they invaded the area. The residents fled to the house of their community where they were attacked, 11 burnt bodies were found the following morning, the house was also burnt.
On 20 June 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired indiscriminately at farmers and pastoralists in Malari village (Mafa, Borno). Two persons were wounded and five others were abducted.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a POS operator in Ugba town (Logo, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person at Nitel junction in Agege (Agege, Lagos). There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 21 June 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a man as he was returning from a beer parlor in the Kola Rewire area (Ondo West, Ondo) coded to Ondo. The victim was a civil servant and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 21 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed 6 persons who are presumed to be civilians at Ijoko-Ogbayo in Ifo LGA (Ogun). Two persons were killed in the early hours of the day and four others were killed later that day.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with security operatives presumed to have been soldiers at Enugu Umunze (Orumba South, Anambra). Two persons were wounded.
On 21 June 2023, a Katsina militia killed five civilians and wounded five others when they shot indiscriminately at residents of Doma village in Faskari LGA (Borno).

On 22 June 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group led by Kabir Bala, also known as Okwo in an armed clash at Ejule (Ofu, Kogi). The group's leader who the police claimed was responsible for a number of attacks in the area was killed, other members of the group fled with varying degress of injuries. Other sources report that Okwo was used by politicians to attack their opponents and that he was killed for withdrawing his support for the governor and giving it to the governorship candidate of the SDP.

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed at least two civilians when they invaded Ejule (Ofu, Kogi) and shot sporadically. One of the victims was hit by a stray bullet, another was the wife of community youth leader, a house was also set ablaze by the assailants.

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a member of the central neighborhood watch at Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The assailants were masked, numbered up to 30 and were marching through the streets whe the victim ran into them.

Around 22 June 2023 (between 20 June - 23 June), a suspected Fulani militia attacked commuters along Enugu-Ugwuogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu), abducted 16 persons and wounded several others. Some sources report that about seven abduction incidents took place within those days.
On 22 June 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives abushed and killed 6 ISWAP militants in Banki (Bama, Borno).

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three women, a newly-wed bride and her two sister in-laws from their house at Emir's road in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded and the abductees were released on 25 June after 7 million was paid as ransom.

On 22 June 2023, a Kaduna militia killed three farmers and abducted scores of other persons when they invaded Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) in large numbers around 12pm. The abductees consisted of farmers, travellers and traders, other sources report that the attack was a reaction to ongoing military operations in disturbed areas.
On 22 June 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked farmers in Lajinge village (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). The assailants killed one person, wounded three and abducted two others.
On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians when they attempted to abduct them on the road between Owo and Benin (Owo, Ondo). One traveler was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 22 June 2023, a soldier ordered a man to swim in a canal and threatened to stab anyone who came close at Fayose market in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). The soldier who was invited by someone at the market to help collect rent was arrested by the police later that same day.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed one person at Muna, coded to Muna Dalti (Jere, Borno) and seven others at different locations in Mafa LGA [coded separately]. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed three youths at Baram-Karuwa and Shuwari in Mafa LGA (Borno) and five others at different locations [coded seaparately]. Two persons were killed in Baram-Karuwa and one was killed in Shuwari. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed four youths who were fetching firewood at Tamsu Ngamdua (Mafa, Borno) and four others at different locations [coded seaparately]. One person was spared to report the story, the victims had their hands tied to their backs and were shot. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted

On 22 June 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed and engaged ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in an armed clash along Bula Yobe - Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno) as they were crossing into Nigeria from Cameroon. Five militants were killed.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians from Gamji and Tabla villages in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductee from Gamji was a businessman and undisclosed amount was demanded for his release, while 10 million naira was demanded for the release of the abductee from Tabla.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed a car and abducted the driver of the university's bursar on the road between Okigwe and Abia state university, code to Onuaku Uturu (Isuikwuato, Abia). The assailants did not see the bursar who is assumed to have been the target. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 23 June 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Ijoko town (Ado-Odo, Ogun). One person was killed.
On 23 June 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Bakin Gidan Gabas in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara) and wounded two people.

On 23 June 2023, Boko Haram [JAS Faction] fighters on motorcycles ambushed two vehicles conveying ISWAP fighters and engaged them in an armed clash on the road between Gajiganna and Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). Several Boko Haram fighters were killed, their rifles and motorcycles were seized by ISWAP. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically when they invaded Sabaja area of Iwo town (Osin, Kwara). The chief of Sabaja was killed by a stray bullet and three other persons including a cleric, a gate keeper and manager at a fuel station were abducted.
On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked miners at a mining site around Tanjol in Jol community (Riyom, Plateau). Three persons were killed and two others were wounded.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group of three abducted a farmer from his farm at Saparu village (Imeko-Afon, Ogun) coded to Imeko and shot sporadically to scare away the other persons who were on the farm. The abductee was abandoned when villagers chased the abductors into the bush.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her daughter from the entrance of their residence at Oju-Ilu in Imeko (Imeko-Afon, Ogun). The woman was made to drive to the outskirts of the town where her daughter was abandoned in the car while she was taken away. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons at Owube (Ogba, Rivers) after they attacked the commercial vehicle which they were traveling in. The victims were a passenger and the driver of the vehicle, other sources report that the assailants were a suspected cult militia.
On 24 June 2023, an SVC militia shot and wounded a member of Black Axe militia who is presumed to have been unarmed in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). The victim was also an NYSC member.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the Yotomi area in Owode Egba (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode. An undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom, the abductee's family claimed that he was murdered by policemen on 1 July [coded separately] after he was mistaken for an abductor.
On 24 June 2023, suspected ISWAP fighters were repelled by troops of 115 Task Force battalion when they attacked Dille (Askira Uba, Borno). One soldier was killed.

On 24 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a patrol of the Nigerian Army and killed two soldiers at Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The militants also claimed that others were forced to withdraw, and that a rifle and three motorbikes were seized.
On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters traveling from Aba to Umuahia, coded to Aba (Aba South, Abia).

On 24 June 2023, presumed IPOB militants attacked commuters at Arondizuogu junction, coded to Ndizuogu (Ideato North, Imo) and diverted their bus to a hamlet away from the road. Two of the commuters were killed, the others were robbed, one of the victims claimed that the assailants were over 50 at the hamlet, 20 of them were armed and they claimed the victims who were from Umuahia were attacked for not obeying sit-in orders and for voting in the 2023 elections.

On 25 June 2023, a Katsina militia in large numbers engaged the head of a local defense militia in an armed clash when they invaded his home in (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa. The leader was killed and his house was burnt in a revenge mission after the assailants claimed that he was responsible for the destruction of their hideouts. Two other persons were shot [not specified whether they died] and three women were raped.

On 25 June 2023, troops of 5 Battalion operating under 16 Brigade of the Nigerian Army engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideout in Azuzuama community (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The armed group were suspected unrepentant militant and oil bunkers, they fled after the soldiers engaged them, the camp was destroyed and various kinds of weapons were recovered. There were no casualties.
On 25 June 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked and killed one person in Okokolo community (Agatu, Benue).

On 25 June 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia) when the group invaded their hideout. An abductee whose husband was killed [previously coded] was rescued, three members of the group were killed and eight others were arrested.

On 25 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a naval rating who is presumed to have been off-duty at Ajegunle (Ajeromi, Lagos). The victim was walking around Olowojeunjeje area when he was killed.
On 25 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and wounded one person at Fass district in Riyom LGA (Plateau). The victim was ambushed and beaten into a coma.
On 25 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed two people at Wereng camp, coded as Unguwar Wereng (Riyom, Plateau). Two others were wounded.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person, wounded another and abducted two others when they invaded Magamin Kano in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductees were the wife and son of the village head, who were taken in his place because he escaped.
On 26 June 2023, Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants ambushed and killed seven farmers at Bula Njimbam (Damboa, Borno). One other person sustained varying degrees of injuries.

On 26 June 2023, suspected pirates attacked policemen and engaged them in an armed clash at a divisional police headquarters in Ogbia (Ogbia, Bayelsa). The assailants were repelled, there were no fatalities.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at Rumu-Osi (Obio, Rivers) as she was returning from her shop. The abductee was rescued by a team of policemen and EMOLVICE operatives [there are no reports of a clash].
On 26 June 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted three farmers from Taka-Lafiya and rustled 60 cows from Gidan-Makeri in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 June 2023, ISWAP militants killed six people when they attacked Koyeri village (Damboa, Borno).

On 26 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed eight civilians in various houses at Kyarang in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The attacked lasted through the night and the victims included a six month old baby.
On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed five persons at Kerang community in Mangu LGA (Borno). Other sources report that seven persons were killed.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform abducted eight staff of MRS petroleum company on the Tin Can waterways (Apapa, Lagos) coded to Tin Can Island as they were returning from work. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 27 June 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of passengers when they attacked a commercial bus at Karasti community in Illela LGA (Sokoto).

On 27 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a student of the Akwa Ibom state university on the school's main campus in Ikot Akpaden (Mkpat Enin, Akwa Ibom). Some sources report that the victim was killed over his emergence as winner in a contest, to the chagrin of the assailant group.
On 27 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted seven persons from Yewuti village in Kwali Area Council (Federal Capital Territory). A ransom of 7 million naira was demanded.

On 27 June 2023, a Niger militia killed six passengers travelers when they blocked the road between Pandogari and Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). One other person sustained gunshot injuries, the baby of one of the victims was also found alive the following day.

On 27 June 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins attacked a journalist and attempted to kill him at his residence in Mararaba (Karu, Nassarawa). The victim who is the deputy political editor of media at daily trust escaped, he claimed that he was shot at several times and the assailants stole his phone, wallet and car keys.

On 27 June 2023, a Katsina militia in large numbers were repelled by policemen who engaged them in an armed clash at Ruwan Doruwa village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. The militiamen had attacked the village, one of them was killed and a GPMG was recovered. Other sources report that two militiamen were killed.
On 27 June 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Wallaro village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. Casualties are unknown.

Around 27 June 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS Faction] fighters killed four members at Mandara mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno) after they were accused of rebellion. The murdered fighters were killed for attempting to form a faction.

On 28 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at Tamigbe town (Burutu, Delta). The abductee was shot in the head, her body was found by family members after they paid a ransom of 1 million naira [coded separately].

Around 28 June 2023 (as reported), policemen killed one civilian who was among the three that they arrested in Aguleri community (Anambra East, Anambra). According to his family, the victim died from torture by the policemen while the spokesperson of the police in the state claimed that he was killed by a fellow suspect.
On 28 June 2023, a Yansakai militia attacked civilians and killed six persons at Kadamutsawa community in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The assailants also wounded four persons and escaped from the area.
On 28 June 2023, a policeman killed a tricycle rider at the Bulumkutu axis (Maiduguri Metro, Borno) for refusing to stop at a roadblock.
On 28 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed a member of a local defense militia, presumed to be the Civilian JTF at Kirenawa (Marte, Borno).
On 28 June 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted a man around Gundumi town (Goronyo, Sokoto) as he was repairing his vehicle.

On 29 June 2023, soldiers attached to the 82 division of the Nigerian army shot at operatives of the Eke Neighborhood Watch who responded to a distress call over armed robbery on the road leading to Eke (Udi, Enugu). One of the operatives and a woman who was on a motorcycle were killed, three other operatives were wounded of whom were in critical states. The spokesperson of 82 division claimed that the claims of the victims were untrue.
On 29 June 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of farmers in Gandi district (Rabah, Sokoto).
On 30 June 2023, Onna and Eastern Obolo militia engaged in an armed clash over a land dispute at the Ikot Abasi/ Eket axis (Eastern Obolo, Akwa Ibom) coded to Okoro Ete. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at Benue community volunteer guards and killed one of them at Tse Anwhwan (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba. The volunteer guards were returning from a police station in Ugba when they were ambushed.

On 30 June 2023, ISWAP militants engaged operatives of Civilian JTF in an armed clash when they attacked the operatives' location in Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). The militants also fired a mortar bomb into the town, six people including women were killed, over 20 others including two Civilian JTF operatives were wounded.
On 30 June 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a local defense militia at Dugul village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. Six local defense militiamen were killed.
On 30 June 2023, policemen in a minivan ran over a civilian who was in handcuffs at Ekpoma (Esan West, Edo). The victim was seriously wounded.
On 30 June 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Two suspected militia members were killed.

On 30 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman at Ikenegbu Layout in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The abductee resisted being abducted and the assailants shot sporadically into the air to scare bystanders away. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a member of a local defense militia who is presumed to have been unarmed at Ankpa town (Ankpa, Kogi). Two other civilians were wounded by the assailants.
On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted at least 3 persons from their vehicles when they attacked Nkwelle Ezunaka junction and Umunya (Oyi, Anambra).

On 1 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two civilians when they attacked Teng and Pwaskop communities in Pushit district (Mangu, Plateau). The attack lasted for several hours, several houses were burnt and the assailants shot sporadically.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by So Safe operatives at Abule-Ori (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode when they attacked a church, killed a pastor and abducted seven parishioners. One of the assailants were killed, many of them sustained serious injuries, the abductees were rescued. The family of an abductee who was previously abducted claimed that the second person who was murdered was their relative not one of the assailants; he was taken to the location by the group and killed by the policemen over a mistaken identity.
On 1 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed a man while he was attending a wedding ceremony at Rakpami community in Toto LGA (Nassarawa). The victim was a farmer.

On 1 July 2023, Karimjo ethnic militia engaged Wurkum ethnic militia in an armed clash at Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). At least 50 persons were killed; the police claimed two fatalities, scores of others were wounded, at least five villages were burnt and many domestic animals were stolen. The state government imposed a dusk to dawn curfew in the area.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons on the road between Ogbomu and Egbe (Yagba West, Kogi). The victims who consisted of two siblings and the vehicle's driver were on transit when the abductors flagged down their vehicle. A ransom of two million naira was demanded.

On 2 July 2023, a policeman shot an artisan a few steps away from his house at Oregun (Epe, Lagos). The victim's family members rushed him to the nearby before the policeman came, threatened them with a gun and took the victim in his bus and went away. The victim was found dead later.

Around 2 July 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a woman and dumped her body near Tamigbe town (Burutu, Delta), after she was abducted from her home in the town a few days earlier. The victim's family paid 1 million naira as ransom before the assailants shot her in the forehead.
On 2 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person, wounded two and abducted two others when they attacked Garin Masau village in Safana LGA (Katsina).
On 2 July 2023, ISWAP fighters were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by MNJTF troops in Monguno town (Monguno, Borno). The clash lasted for up to one hour, casualties are unknown.

On 2 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed three persons at Jenuwa Nyifiye community in Takum LGA (Taraba). The assailants shot sporadically, while the police spokesperson in the state claimed that they were interrupted following measures by policemen and soldiers. Other sources report that 8 persons were killed, some of whom were burnt beyond recognition and that local defense militiamen attempted to repel the attack but were overpowered.

On 3 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed three farmers and abducted 15 others when they ambushed them on their farms at Gwaram village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The assailants claimed that the attack was in protest over the refusal of the new state government to negotiate with them. They were heard chanting in Hausa language saying 'they must negotiate with us now'.

On 3 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an operative of the Benue community volunteer guards at a checkpoint in Ugba town (Logo, Benue). The assailants also abducted two people and robbed some other persons. Other sources report that the assailants were armed robbers.
On 3 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians from Magama town in Jibia LGA (Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 3 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed an unspecified number of persons, wounded and abducted others at Borin Dawa (Malumfashi, Katsina). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 3 July 2023, IPOB members from the Simon Ekpa faction abducted a commercial bus driver and set his bus ablaze in the vicinity of Ngwa road in Aba (Aba South, Abia) for disobeying a sit-in order.

On 3 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked worshippers who were returning from church and killed eight persons at Takum (Takum, Taraba). Houses were also set ablaze, the attack happened in from of the 83 battalion Ada Army barracks.

On 3 July 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops who repelled the militant's attempt to attack farmers in the vicinity of Wanori, Konduga LGA (Borno). The militants retreated, casualties are unknown.
Non-violent activity: On 3 July 2023, a Zamfara militia mounted an illegal vehicle checkpoint along the Magami-Gusau highway (Gusau, Zamfara).
On 4 July 2023, IPOB militants from Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order shot sporadically at policemen at a checkpoint in Isieke (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The policemen in the area fled.
On 4 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed a farmer on his farm and also stole from the victim's farm at Tse Uikpam (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba. Some other farmers were able to escape.

On 4 July 2023, IPOB militants from Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order killed three tricycle riders at Ishieke market in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi) and shot sporadically into the air when they invaded Afiaohu market along Abakaliki/Enugu expressway. The assailants were demanding the release of Nnamdi Kanu.

On 4 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives ambushed and engaged Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in an armed clash at Mandara mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno). One militant commander was killed, one rifle with loaded ammunition was recovered.

On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order beat up teachers and primary school pupils at different locations across Enugu West senatorial district, coded to Awgu (Agwu, Enugu). The victims were flogged for not obeying the order.
On 5 July 2023, Amotekun corps and officials of NIS engaged in an armed clash at Oke Fia area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The cause of the clash and casualties are unknown.
On 5 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man at his residence in Imasayi community (Egbado North, Ogun) coded to Aiyetoro. The victim was macheted to pieces.

On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order were repelled by soldiers at Trans Ekulu (Enugu East, Enugu). The attackers managed to escape. There were no casualties.
On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants clashed with policemen at Abakpa, coded as Abakpa Nike (Enugu East, Enugu). One militant was killed.

On 5 July 2023, ISWAP militants raided the camp of Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters and engaged them in an armed clash at Bula Alhaji Garwaye in Bama LGA (Borno). Scores of Boko Haram fighters, their women and children were killed, a few of them escaped while their properties were looted by the ISWAP fighters. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 5 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a man who was accused of being a sorcerer at Bukarti in Yunusari LGA (Yobe). The militants claimed to have killed the victim in front of other villagers and given them a sermon on the dangers of sorcery to Islam.

On 5 July 2023, two unidentified cult militias clashed and killed one person at Oke-Apomu quarters in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The clash was preparatory to the 7/7 anniversary of the militias, the victim was killed when his older brother who was the target was not found at home when the assailants arrived.

On 5 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one woman and wounded another when they attacked Kwahas community in Kombun district (Mangu, Plateau). The assailants were passing along the Mangu-Bokkos road and attacked the residents when they reached the village.

On 5 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a lawyer and the welfare Secretary of the Nigerian Bar Association after they abducted him from his house in Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). The victim was taken away and his body was found along the road with several machete injuries. The victim was also the candidate of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP).

On 5 July 2023, Black Axe militia also known as Aiye confraternity and SEC militia engaged in an armed clash at Bariga (Somolu, Lagos) following a clash over the annual 7/7 celebration. Three militia members were killed, one was wounded and in a coma, the clash spread to other areas and passers-by were wounded at the Somolu area. Other sources report that the clash was between two factions of Black Axe militia, and that 5 persons were killed.

On 5 July 2023, Ebube Agu operatives and policemen engaged in an armed clash at the Imo state secretariat in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) when a group of policemen bullied an Ebube Agu operative who in turn invited his colleagues to defend him. Scores of persons who were trying to flee were wounded as a result of a stampede.

On 6 July 2023, Ishinkwo and Abba-Omega communal militias engaged in an armed clash and seven locals from Abba Omega were killed. Location coded to Abba Omega (Onicha, Ebonyi). The police spokesperson in the state denied the report of a clash and killings.
On 6 July 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants abducted a farmer at Dalori (Konduga, Borno). The abductee was a displaced person who was working as a small scale farmer.

On 6 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Kogul community in Panyam district (Mangu, Plateau) and killed five persons. An unspecified number of others were wounded and several houses were burnt.
On 6 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted 10 civilians from Kasai village in Batsari LGA (Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 6 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one woman and wounded another when they attacked Milet community in Kombun district (Mangu, Plateau) in their numbers.
On 6 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person in the vicinity of Pole Wire, along Jos-Abuja highway in Riyom LGA (Plateau).

On 7 July 2023, policemen raided the hideout of an unidentified cult militia and were engaged in an armed clash at Obelle town (Emohua, Rivers). Six militiamen were killed, six were arrested while others ran in different directions with bullet wounds.
