On 10 August 2023, a Sokoto militia killed a policeman [presumed to be off-duty] when they attacked his residence at Tudun Wada A (Sokoto South, Sokoto). The victim's valuables were also stolen.

On 10 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot at the vehicle of an former spokesperson of the PDP at Akwakuma/ Mbieri road in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) as claimed by the victim. A shop owner was abducted in the process. There were no casualties.
On 11 August 2023, two unidentified armed groups engaged in an armed clash at the kingdom hall axis of Sangotedo (Eti-Osa, Lagos). Casualties are unknown.
On 11 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two people at Nyian village (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba.

On 11 August 2023, operatives of Operation Udo Ka II comprised of soldiers, policemen and DSS operatives raided a hideout of IPOB militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Imufu in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). Three militants were killed, other sources report that two militants were killed, others escaped with varying degrees of gunshot wounds. Weapons, ammunition and other items including military camouflages and fabrics with IPOB insignia were recovered.
On 11 August 2023, two unidentified rival cult militias engaged in an armed clash at the Osun-Oshogbo groove in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). Three persons were killed and 12 others were wounded.
On 11 August 2023, an unidentified armed group shot indiscriminately and killed two commuters at Neke (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and abducted an unspecified number of others.
On 11 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted three persons when they attacked Zakka village (Safana, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, an unidentified armed man, presumed to be a member of an armed group abducted one woman from Suka village, coded to Mamman Suka (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted at least 20 people when they attacked a commercial bus that was transporting passengers from Kaduna to Isa in Isa LGA (Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, a Fulani militia attacked women who were returning from the market at Kinat community, Mangu Halle ward (Mangu, Plateau). Two of the women were killed and two others sustained injuries.

On 11 August 2023, troops sector 1 of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on a routine patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at the Marke general area (Tsafe, Zamfara). The clash lasted several hours, the troops rescued two abductees, the militiamen fled and two motorcycles were recovered by the troops. There were no casualties.

On 11 August 2023, Oyofo and Awha communal militias engaged in an armed clash over land dispute in Ezeagu LGA (Enugu). Four people were killed, one tricycle and five motorcycles were set ablaze. The police claimed that 12 persons were arrested in connection with the clash.

On 11 August 2023, troops of sector 1 of the Nigerian army conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kabode general area in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). Three militiamen were killed, one loaded rifle, three mobile phones and other items were recovered.

On 12 August 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Kofar Gayan (Zaria, Kaduna) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. Two civilians were killed, one other person was abducted and other sources report that he was later rescued by security agents [no reports on a clash].
On 12 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked and killed two members of the Civilian JTF at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno).
On 12 August 2023, Nigerian troops and presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash in the vicinity of Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia numbering about 70 ambushed soldiers and a local defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash in Zungeru (Wushishi, Niger) as they were responding to a distress call from Akare community. 30 to 50 militia members, at least 10 soldiers and an unspecified number of local defense militiamen were killed. Other sources report that 23 soldiers were killed, some of whom were set ablaze in the convoy and eight other soldiers were wounded. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. The Defence headquarters claimed that 36 soldiers died in both the ambush and a helicopter crash [coded separately], total 43 fatalities coded.
On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia attacked a bus and killed four civilians including a one year old baby and abducted seven others from New Bussa (Borgu, Niger).

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others including women from Chibiani (Muya, Niger) and Zagzaga [coded separately]. Four people each were abducted from both locations.

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others including women from Zagzaga (Muya, Niger) and Chibiani [coded separately]. Four people each were abducted from both locations.
On 13 August 2023, a presumed unidentified cult militia killed one person at Ugbokolo town (Okpokwu, Benue). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 13 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and wounded a motorcyclist along Gidan Katta-Masasa road in Illela LGA (Sokoto) and stole his motorcycle.
On 13 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two commuters along Adani-Ayamelum road, coded to Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra). A ransom of 40 million naira was demanded.

On 13 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian at Opu-Nembe community in Nembe LGA (Bayelsa) as claimed by members of the community. The PDP claimed that the assailants were working for the APC and also that the APC governorship candidate was behind the attacks, over the rejection of his candidature by the community.
On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians when they attacked Sabuwa town (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militia also rustled livestock and looted food supplies.

On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person out of the 20 civilians that they abducted from Madogara community (Batsari, Katsina). The victim was wounded when he struggled with the militia member that was holding him and sustained machete wounds. The other abductees consisted of 16 women and 3 men.

On 13 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian army barracks in Logomani (Ngala, Borno) and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. The Defence Headquarters confirmed the attack and claimed that four militants were killed, 5 rifles, one RPG and other equipment were recovered.

On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed two civilians at Tsohuwar Kasuwa quarters in Dandume town (Dandume, Katsina) and wounded several others who attempted to escape in the process. An unspecified number of persons were also abducted. Other sources report that two people including a child were wounded.
On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians, wounded three others and abducted an unspecified number of persons from Tsohuwar Makabarta in Dandume LGA (Katsina).
On 13 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) injured a civilian in an unspecified location in the Isa LGA, coded to the LGA HQ, Isa (Isa, Sokoto).
On 13 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed and injured an unspecified number of persons in an attack on Rimawa ward (Goronyo, Sokoto). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 14 August 2023, a Niger militia ambushed soldiers and engaged them in an armed clash at Madaka ward (Rafi, Niger). Thirteen soldiers were killed.

On 14 August 2023, a Niger militia led by Dogo Gide claimed to have shot down a military helicopter that was carrying out an evacuation mission in Chukuba (Shiroro, Niger) and killed those on board. The military denied the claims and insisted that the weather and other conditions may have contributed to the crash. Unknown casualties coded as 3.
On 14 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian at Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Sokoto militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers who were deployed to repel the militia's attack at Gidan Kare (Tureta, Sokoto). The militia abducted an unspecified number of persons who were rescued by the soldiers, casualties are unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Fulani militia killed two teachers and wounded the vice principal of a school in Kwi (Riyom, Plateau). The assailants had invaded the school premises to graze their cattle and started shooting sporadically when they were confronted by the security men [presumed to be gate keepers]. The security men were not harmed.

On 14 August 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and repelled the group when they attacked a group of journalists at Opu-Nembe in Nembe LGA (Bayelsa). The cameras of one of the journalists was seized by the assailants, casualties are unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted seven others when they attacked Bungudu town (Bungudu, Zamfara). The abductees consisted of two males, one of whom was the son of the emir of Bungudu and five females, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted four civilians at Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina).

On 14 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters ambushed and engaged ISWAP fighters in a supremacy battle while they were on their way to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Sixty ISWAP fighters including three commanders were captured and taken to a Boko Haram prison at Kwatan Mota while others fled to the axis of Kukawa, Madayi and Kwatan Mota. Some ISWAP fighters had previously abandoned the group and joined forces with the Bakura led Boko Haram group that conducted the attack. There were no casualties.
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded three civilians and abducted four others at Kofa village in (Kusada, Katsina).
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of persons from Unguwar Dahiru and Unguwar Fadi villages in Funtua LGA (Katsina).
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person and rustled cattle from Wadi village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 14 August 2023, a Zamfara militia who were dressed in women's attire including hijabs abducted an unspecified number of civilians from Hayi community in Maru LGA (Zamfara). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area, the abductees included women and children and a businessman, other sources report that up to 50 people were abducted.

On 14 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins attacked a pastor and his wife at their church in New Benin, coded to Benin City (Oredo, Edo) after they had trailed them. The pastor's wife was killed, the pastor and his assistant sustained gunshot wounds.

On 14 August 2023, three soldiers beat up a LASTMA official at Ojota (Kosofe, Lagos) in a reprisal attack following a fight between their colleague and a LASTMA official. Two of the soldiers were dressed in their uniform and one in plain clothes. There were no casualties.

On 14 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 1 person, injured two, and abducted several others during an attack in Tungar Loso, coded to the LGA HQ, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).
On 15 August 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a civilian and abducted three others when they attacked Idon town (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 15 August 2023, a Katsina militia was repelled by policemen who foiled their attack on Korogo village, coded to nearby Daddara (Jibia, Katsina). One militia member was killed, 60 rustled sheep, one rifle and 110 rounds of ammunition were recovered.
On 15 August 2023, a Zamfara militia fired indiscriminately and abducted 29 civilians from Janbako (Maradun, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 15 August 2023, a Sokoto militia wounded two civilians and abducted four others at Bakin Dutse village in Araba ward (Illela, Sokoto).

On 15 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted five civilians along Mile two axis of Ishiagu/Okigwe expressway (Ivo, Ebonyi). The abductees included a couple, their driver and a farmer whom they met and abducted as they were taking the other victims into the bush.

On 15 August 2023, policemen on patrol engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group suspected to be abductors at Ugbolokposo (Uvwie, Delta). Three members of the group were killed, four others were arrested.
On 15 August 2023, a Boko Haram commander [JAS faction] killed seven Boko Haram fighters at Bukkaram Island in Kukawa LGA (Borno) over an attempt by the fighters to surrender to Nigerian troops.

On 15 August 2023, a Sokoto militia wounded an unspecified number of commuters who were fleeing the militia's attack along Kunawa village (Goronyo, Sokoto). The assailants shot indiscriminately when they invaded the axis.
On 15 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person and abducted an unspecified number of others at Unguwar Maigayya in Dandume LGA (Katsina).
On 15 August 2023, Nigerian troops and presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash in the vicinity of Gabchari (Konduga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 16 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Bassambiri (Nembe, Bayelsa) over presumed political disputes. Casualties are unknown.

On 16 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked commuters around Abaji (Abaji, FCT), the driver and one other passenger were killed, while an NYSC member in the car was abducted. A ransom of 300 million which was later reduced to 1 million was paid for the abductee's release and she was released on 19 August. The NYSC denied the payment of ransom.
On 16 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded two civilians when they fired indiscriminately in Unguwar Gulbi (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.
On 16 August 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters engaged in an inter-ethnic clash amongst themselves at Baga (Kukawa, Borno). 82 fighters were killed, some fighters who survived fled into Chad.
On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be oil thieves engaged the state anti-oil bunkering unit in an armed clash at TTC in Okwuzi (Ogba, Rivers). Casualties are unknown.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians from Sanger and Billiri Gorore villages in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). An undisclosed ransom amount was demanded for the abductee from Sanger.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the entrance of his apartment in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The abductee was rescued on the same day by policemen after the abductors abandoned him.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group of about seven abducted a woman and two of her maids from her shop in Elerinjare (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. The assailants shot sporadically and another person was hit and wounded by a stray bullet, the maids were later released and the abductee's husband claimed that the assailants included women. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded and the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the abduction. The abductee was released on 23 August after one million naira and food stuff were paid as ransom, the person who went to deliver the ransom was abducted [coded separately].
On 18 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians and abducted several women when they attacked Sabon Garin Unguwar Ganau, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina).
On 18 August 2023, a Katsina militia in their numbers killed a man and abducted his wife when they attacked Maidabino, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and conducted a house to house raid.

On 18 August 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group of four in an armed clash at Rumukwashi (Obio, Rivers) coded to Rumuodomaya after the group abducted a civilian in the area. Two of the assailants were killed and the abductee was rescued, and one other person was abducted.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from Yadagungume town in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductee was a nursing mother and also the wife of a businessman based in the town.

Around 19 August 2023 (as reported), a Sokoto militia in their numbers abducted a man from Tambuwal town (Tambuwal, Sokoto). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the town and headed towards Kebbe after the attack.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians at Gumau (Toro, Bauchi). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area to scare residents.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Bargan-Fulani and Fishere communities in Toro LGA (Bauchi).

On 19 August 2023, policemen shot sporadically into the air when they attempted to quell tensions between two groups in Itobe (Ofu, Kogi). A commercial tricycle rider was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five passengers at Rumuodogo junction (Emohua, Rivers). The abductees were rescued by policemen who went to the scene and combed the bushes [no reports of a clash].

On 19 August 2023, a Fulani militia abducted five women along the Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu). One person was killed earlier on the same day [coded separately] at the same location. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded for the release of one of the abductees.

On 19 August 2023, a Fulani militia killed one tipper driver along the Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu). Five women were abducted later on the same day [coded separately] at the same location.

On 19 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted eight NYSC members in Zamfara state while they were on their way to the orientation camp in Sokoto, Location coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Eleven NYSC members were initially abducted; three of them escaped, while the bus driver was also abducted. Other sources report that the abductors demanded a ransom of 4 million naira for the release of one of the abductees. A ransom of 13 million was paid for the abductees' release, but the militia demanded another 200 million naira ransom. A female abductee was released on 20 October. The militia released an additional two female hostages on 8 December 2023, there are no details on ransom payments, and another two were released around 5 February 2024, the NYSC claimed that they were rescued through the efforts of security operatives. An unspecified number of the remaining abductees were released on 14 April 2024, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 19 August 2023, ISWAP fighters led by Abou Idris engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash near Marte (Marte, Borno) as a reprisal for the capture of 60 ISWAP militants by Boko Haram [coded separately]. More than 100 militants from both sides were killed in the clash that continued to the following day, some sources report that more Boko Haram militants were killed. 100 fatalities split across two events coded as 50.

On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group in their numbers attacked a police station in Lau LGA (Taraba) after they invaded the town in search of a target whom they were unable to find. There were no casualties, some community members claimed that the assailants shot sporadically in the air when they invaded the area.

On 20 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted an off-duty soldier along Birnin Gwari road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) while he was traveling to resume at his duty station. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded with a three-day payment ultimatum.

On 20 August 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash around Centenary City (Enugu South, Enugu) coded to Uwani. Two of the assailants were killed, others escaped with bullet wounds, one abductee was rescued, his car was recovered; a gun loaded with four cartridges was also recovered by the policemen.

On 20 August 2023, ISWAP fighters led by Abou Idris engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash near Marte (Marte, Borno) as a reprisal for the capture of 60 ISWAP militants by Boko Haram [coded separately]. More than 100 militants from both sides were killed in the clash that started the previous day, some sources report that more Boko Haram militants were killed. 100 fatalities split across two events coded as 50.

On 20 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed a man who was returning home from Tashar Biri, coded to Dan Ali (Dan-Musa, Katsina) where he was headed. The victim was hacked to death with a cutlass, the assailants also rustled several animals from residents in Dan Ali.

On 20 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot and killed a commander of the Benue state livestock guard who is presumed to have been unarmed at Tine Nune (Ukum, Benue). The victim was the fifth ward commander of the livestock guard to have been killed in the LGA.

On 20 August 2023, IPOB fighters engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash when they attempted to infiltrate the troops' forward operating base at Ukwuorji, along Owerri-Onitsha expressway (Owerri Municipal, Imo). One of the militants was killed, two were arrested and the others fled, a machete and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 21 August 2023, troops of 1 brigade garrison ambushed and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash while they were en route to attack civilians at Bobo village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). Two militia members were killed, two rifles and four motorcycles were recovered.
Around 21 August 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia killed two abductees out of the 24 that were previously abducted from Gulbin Boka in Mashegu LGA (Niger). The victims were Islamic teachers.

Around 21 August 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group shot and killed a pastoralist at Ukwulu community (Dunukofia, Anambra). The victim's decomposing corpse was found with gunshot wounds on August 23 after he went missing since 21 August.

On 21 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted six persons from the Aworo/Asi area (Odo-Otin, Osun) coded to Okuku. The abductees included the Iyalode of Oyan who escaped while the other five persons were still in captivity. The remaining 5 abductees were released after 7 million naira was paid as ransom, the NSCDC spokesperson denied knowledge of any ransom payment.

On 21 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted the wife and daughter of a man when they invaded his residence at Damba, coded as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara) and met his absence. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 21 August 2023, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Chito (Ukum, Benue) and continued the clash the following day [coded separately]. Five persons were killed; the market was also set ablaze by the assailants, other sources report that four persons were killed in Chito and one was killed in the suburbs.

On 22 August 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed an off-duty policeman in his house, one of the assailants was arrested by the police at Rumuodogo community (Emohua, Rivers). Location coded to where the assailant was arrested.

On 22 August 2023, a DSS operative stabbed and wounded a man in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) following a disagreement over a debt of 3000 naira which the assailant owed for electricity. Other sources report that the assailant stabbed the victim in order to escape a mob that attempted to attack him over accusation that he was an internet fraudster.

On 22 August 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted 42 IDPs women near Mafa town (Mafa, Borno). The abductees were from the Shuwari camp who went in search of firewood, 4 women were released while the other 42 were taken away. Other sources report that at least 48 women were abducted and they were released on 23 August after paying 20 thousand naira each as ransom.
On 22 August 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants ambushed Civilian JTF operatives at Kolkol junction in Mafa LGA (Borno). The operatives escaped the ambush. There were no casualties.
On 22 August 2023, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Gbeji (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera which started the previous day [coded separately]. Three persons were killed.
On 22 August 2023, two factions of the NURTW engaged in an armed clash along Port Harcourt-Aba expressway (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The reason for the clash and casualties are unknown.

On 23 August 2023, masked security operatives presumed to have been policemen shot sporadically in two motor parks in Nkpor (Idemili North, Anambra) in an attempt to disperse traders from their shops. The shooting caused a stampede which resulted in the sustaining of varying degrees of injuries by many people, other sources report that 5 persons were wounded by the shooting and a state official claimed that the state government was responsible for sacking the occupants.

On 23 August 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man on his farm at Rahwol Gassa in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). The assailants were fleeing with their cows after being driven from farmlands in the area when they met the victim who was tied to a tree and slaughtered.
On 23 August 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed a man while he was working on his farm in Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). The victim was also a pastor.

On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed soldiers who were on patrol at Kukar Babangida in Jibia LGA (Katsina) and wounded two soldiers. The militia also abducted about 20 civilians from the village.
On 23 August 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked a police checkpoint near Geidam town (Geidam, Yobe), killed two policemen and captured one SUV as claimed by the militants.

On 23 August 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked and engaged rival Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash at Duguri axis (Kukawa, Borno). 41 fighters from both sides including their major commanders were killed.
On 23 August 2023, the Nigerian military shot and killed four ISWAP fighters in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno) and Firgi, coded separately. Fatalities split across two locations, 2 coded.

On 23 August 2023, a Zamfara militia who rode on motorcycles attacked civilians and shot sporadically when they invaded Gidan Damo in Bilbis district (Tsafe, Zamfara). Four persons were killed on the spot while three others sustained injuries. Other sources report that three persons were killed, seven were wounded and eight others were abducted.
On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person from Bakori town (Bakori, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed a couple and wounded two other civilians when they attacked Dandume town (Dandume, Katsina). One of the wounded victims was the child of the couple.

On 23 August 2023, a presumed Ezza militia engaged soldiers in an armed clash in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) after the soldiers attempted to repel the assailants from a church which they were vandalizing. The assailants fled and casualties are unknown.

On 23 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian who went to deliver ransom for another victim who was previously abducted from Elerinjare village (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. The victim for whom the ransom was paid was released, a ransom of 5 million naira was demanded for the abductee's release.
On 23 August 2023, the Nigerian military shot and killed four ISWAP fighters in Firgi near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno) and Pulka, coded separately. Fatalities split across two locations, 2 coded.

On 24 August 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged customs operatives who were on a stop and search duty in an armed clash along Daki Gari Koko road in Koko LGA (Kebbi). Two customs operatives were killed. Other sources report that the assailants were suspected drug smugglers.

On 24 August 2023, an unidentified armed group of three who were on a motorcycle attacked policemen at a police station in Isiokolo division, coded to Isiokolo-Agbon (Ethiope East, Delta). One policeman was killed, another sustained a gunshot injury and one constable escaped.

On 24 August 2023, an armed Fulani pastoralist cut the hand of a farmer at Jital village, coded to Jitar (Bauchi, Bauchi) following a fight that ensued between them over grazing on the victim's farm. The assailant was armed with a stick and a machete and he was arrested by the police.

On 24 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have engaged Nigerian soldiers in an armed clash after they ambushed them and detonated an IED on their convoy along Waijroko-Azir road (Damboa, Borno). An unspecified number of soldiers were killed and wounded and an armored vehicle was damaged. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 24 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted eight persons from Ore, coded to its ward, Samama (Binji, Sokoto).
On 25 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted the organizing secretary of the APC from his residence in Yakasai village (Soba, Kaduna). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 25 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted two civilians from a residence in Kasuan Shanu, Bama LGA (Borno). A ransom of 5 million naira was demanded and the abductees were later released after 200,000 naira was paid as ransom.
On 25 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a village head and three farmers in Nasarawa-Burkullu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 25 August 2023, a local defense militia engaged a Katsina militia that abducted civilians in an armed clash at Jofalwa village in Kusada LGA (Katsina). Two out of the three abductees were rescued by the local defense militia.

On 25 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted two siblings when they invaded Wusasa (Zaria, Kaduna) and shot sporadically to scare residents away. One of the abductees is a health worker, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 25 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded three farmers when they attacked a farm at the outskirts of Sabuwa town (Sabuwa, Katsina).
On 25 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists shot and killed one person at Ukwulu community (Dunukofia, Anambra).
On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two wedding guests at Nsukka LGA (Enugu).

On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman who was on escort duty at D-Line in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The rifle and beret of the policeman who was escorting his principal were taken away. Other sources report that the attack was an attempted abduction.
On 25 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted a woman and her child when they attacked a residence in Musari village (Mobbar, Borno) coded to Damasak. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 25 August 2023, ISWAP militants killed one civilian and wounded another person when they fired indiscriminately in Azir community, coded to Azir Multe (Damboa, Borno).
On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five civilians from Kabusa community (Abuja Municipal, FCT). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 25 August 2023, a Benue militia attacked commuters and killed scores of persons along Chito-Zaki Biam road (Ukum, Benue). The attack was a reprisal following a clash between two militias in the area [coded separately]. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 25 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person when they attacked Sayaya village (Matazu, Katsina).
On 26 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted the village head of Kwali village (Bukkuyum, Nigeria) coded to Bukuyum when they invaded the area. Four farmers were abducted alongside the village head.
On 26 August 2023, an unidentified cult militia attacked and shot at a local defense militia member who was wounded in the leg at a burial ceremony in the Baga Eriyo area of Shagamu LGA (Ogun).

On 26 August 2023, a Niger militia killed four civilians and abducted an unspecified number of others when they attacked Tudun Magaji, Rijiyan Nagwamatse and Farin Shinge villages in Nagwamatse ward (Kontagora, Niger).
On 26 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted eight farmers when they invaded a farm and shot sporadically at Maiwa, coded to Maiwa Kura (Mafa, Borno).

On 26 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a militia which is presumed to have been the Civilian JTF in Sambisa Forest. Location coded to Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno), one militia member was killed by the militants.

On 26 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a tractor driver while he was working on a farm in Tsohon Achodi village in Abaji area council (FCT). The driver was in the company of two other persons who fled upon sighting the abductors.
On 26 August 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed a farmer who was returning from his farm in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara).

On 26 August 2023, a policemen foiled an attack by a Katsina militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Ruwan Lafiya village in Kankara (Katsina). One abductee was rescued, 94 cows, 17 sheep and two motorcycles were recovered. Casualties are unknown.

On 26 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked unarmed gate keepers at an oil spil site in Bodo (Gonaka, Rivers). Two of the victims were killed, five others escaped with various degrees of gunshot wounds. Other sources report that several other persons were missing.

On 26 August 2023, a soldier killed one person at Otto community (Lagos Mainland, Lagos) following a disagreement between locals and railway construction workers over a fence which the local claimed would obstruct a road in the community. The soldiers shot sporadically in the area.
On 27 August 2023, troops of 2 battalion engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kwana Shehu village in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed and four abductees were rescued.

On 27 August 2023, an unidentified armed group that was dressed in military uniform abducted a man from his residence in Kofa village (Bebeji, Kano). The abductee is the center officer for the Kano state pilgrims welfare board in the local government area. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 27 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 18 civilians from along the Okigwi expressway (Okigwe, Imo) where they shot indiscriminately at a commercial bus.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted a commercial driver in Magumeri LGA (Borno). The abductee was released on 30 August after 2 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants fired indiscriminately at commercial vehicles at an illegal vehicle checkpoint that the mounted along Gajiram-Maiduguri road (Nganzai, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted four civilians along Maiduguri-Monguno road (Guzamala, Borno) coded to Gudumbali. The militants had set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint along the road.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted four civilians when they attacked a commercial vehicle at Tasha Kashim village in Magumeri LGA (Borno).
On 27 August 2023, a Niger militia shot a man, wounded him and abducted his wife when they attacked Farin Shinge village in Kontagora LGA (Niger).

On 27 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged Nigerian troops whose position they attacked in an armed clash at Ngoshe village (Gwoza, Borno). Casualties are unknown and there are no further details.

On 27 August 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants were repelled by Nigerian troops when they attacked Bale general area (Damboa, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 28 August 2023, policemen killed a member of an unidentified armed group at Choba (Obio, Rivers) when he went to receive an additional ransom amount. The assailant's group had abducted and released a man after 2 million naira was paid, before making demands for an additional 3 million.

On 28 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted four farmers when they invaded their farmlands at Damfami (Kiyawa, Zamfara) coded to Birnin Magaji. There are no reports on ransom demands, farmers in the area abducted two milkmaids in retaliation [coded separately].

On 28 August 2023, a group of farmers from Birnin Magaji community abducted two milkmaids who were suspected to be Fulani in retaliation for the abduction of four farmers on the same day [coded separately] at Damfami (Kiyawa, Zamfara) coded to Birnin Magaji. The abduction of the women was an attempt by the farmers to open negotiations with the militia.

On 28 August 2023, two groups of maqurede supporters engaged in an armed clash at Aku community (Igbo Etiti, Enugu) following a disagreement over the date for closing the masquerade year. One person was killed, other sources report that at least 100 locals were hospitalized, the police claimed that one person was arrested and a firearm was retrieved from him.
On 28 August 2023, the Nigerian military attacked ISWAP fighters and killed one of them around Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno).

On 29 August 2023, presumed soldiers engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in the vicinity of Amagu Ishiagu and Lokpanta (Ivo, Ebonyi) coded to Ishiagu. One member of the group was killed, another was injured, three others were arrested. Two abductees were rescued and weapons were recovered.

On 29 August 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded Dan Umoru (Danko, Kebbi). The assailants were repelled, they escaped with gunshot wounds while one rocket launcher was recovered by the policemen.
On 29 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants ambushed a local defense militia that was on patrol in Mafa LGA (Borno). Three local defense militiamen were killed.
On 29 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from his residence in Janmbutu (Yola-North, Adamawa) coded to Yola.
On 29 August 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two persons and abducted eleven others at Unguwan Pete in Jere town (Kagarko, Kaduna). The abductees consisted of seven bakery workers and four tenants.
On 29 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a militia group suspected to be CJTF in Jakana (Bama, Borno). One of the militiamen was killed by ISWAP in the attack.

On 29 August 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at along Umuezorokam-Avu road (Owerri West, Imo) coded to Umuoguma. Two of the assailants were killed, others fled with various degrees of gunshot wounds and one abductee was rescued.
On 29 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 15 civilians at Magazu village (Tsafe, Zamfara) where they set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint.

On 29 August 2023, security operatives consisting mainly of policemen and suspected NDLEA operatives shot sporadically in an attempt to scare traders away at Timber and Allied industrial market in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). One trader was hit and killed by a stray bullet. The spokesperson of the NDLEA denied the operatives' participation, the police spokesperson claimed that the victim was not shot by policemen.

On 29 August 2023, a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideout in Elerinjare axis (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. One of the assailants was killed and five others were arrested.
On 30 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists wounded a man and abducted his wife and daughter at a residence in Bumgai (Gujba, Yobe).

On 30 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted two others at Itapaji (Ikole, Ekiti). The abductees were released on 3 September, there are no reports on ransom demands and payment.
On 30 August 2023, former Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted six civilians from a farm in the vicinity of Jege village (Gwoza, Borno).
On 30 August 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a revenue collector in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). A student was also hit and killed by a stray bullet following the assailants' attack.

On 30 August 2023, a local defense militia numbering about 60 killed two Fulani pastoralists at Bungudu central market (Bungudu, Zamfara) when they invaded the market. The assailants targeted persons whom they accused of having links with militia activities within the area.

On 30 August 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they responded to a distress call around Borromeo roundabout in Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). One abductee was rescued, two of the assailants were arrested while others fled with gunshot wounds. One pistol, ammunition and the bus used by the assailants were recovered.
On 30 August 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a revenue collector around Okhoro junction in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The attack is related to a cult war between different militias.
On 31 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two women from Dan Musa town (Dan-Musa, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 31 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed two civilians and abducted one other person at Tashar Icce (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa.
On 31 August 2023, the Nigerian military carried out a cross-border raid on an unnamed faction of Boko Haram coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Four militiamen were killed in the raid.

On 31 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted scores of passengers near Ochonyi village along Lokoja-Abuja highway (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductors shot at the tires of the buses that the abductees were travelling in and forced them to stop.
On 31 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a police outpost near Geidam (Geidam, Yobe) and captured the police vehicle. No report on fatality claims.

On 31 August 2023, the Nigerian military intercepted and killed six ISWAP fighters on the Molai- Damboa road close to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). They were intercepted on their way to Sambisa Forest. The military recovered AK-47 rifles, bicycles and other items from them.
On 31 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 15 farmers from their farms in Moriki (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 31 August 2023, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye, Supreme Eiye Confraternity also called Eiye and Maphite militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy which led to the killing of 6 persons in different areas of Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The affected areas included Upper Mission, Okhun, Oluku and Aikhionbare.

On 31 August 2023, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF who were on a clearance operation ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants who were transporting large quantities of logistics along Molai-Damboa road (Jere, Borno). Six militants were killed, one was captured alive while others escaped and the logistics were recovered by the troops.
On 1 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 14 civilians from Mayo Dassa (Yorro, Taraba). The abductees were released at an unspecified date, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 1 September 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two civilians at Tashin Dauda village in Ikara LGA (Kaduna). The victims who included a driver were killed by the assailants who were fleeing from an attack in Saya-Saya village [coded separately].

On 1 September 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked worshippers at a mosque and killed five persons in Saya-Saya village (Ikara, Kaduna). Other sources report that seven persons were killed including the leader of the local defense militia who some sources assume was the target. Police confirmed the attack and claimed five persons were killed and two others wounded.

On 1 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The woman was taken when she was returning home from an interview. The victim had expressed concern about being followed by some men dressed in police uniforms before she was abducted. No ransom has been demanded by her abductors.

On 1 September 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian military camp in Ladari, located in the northern part of Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). The militiamen claimed to have killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. They made away with a motorbike and ammunition. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 1 September 2023, ISWAP clashed with CJTF near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). One CJTS member was killed, and others were wounded in the clash.

On 2 September 2023, operatives of Operation Restore Peace comprised of soldiers, policemen and other security agencies engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Shande village in Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). The clash lasted for over two hours, scores of members of the group were killed, five abductees sustained injuries and 11 others were rescued. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 2 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the military checkpoint in Pulka (Gwoza, Bornu) forcing the soldiers to withdraw. The attackers burned the checkpoint after the withdrawal of the soldiers.

On 2 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his residence at El-Rufai estate in Bwari (Bwari, FCT) after scaling the fence of the house to gain entrance. The assailants also shot sporadically to scare other residents.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified armed group in large numbers attacked and abducted many civilians from farming communities around Garba-Chebe in Bali LGA (Taraba). The attack lasted for hours and the abductees included women and children.
On 3 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed a farmer on his cassava farm at Chembe village (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a businesswoman when they attacked her residence in Agbeku (Ifelodun, Kwara). The victim's motorcycle was stolen by the assailants, the town's traditional ruler claimed that four suspects were arrested by the police.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a man in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The victim who was reported as mentally ill was shot at, stoned, stabbed and attacked with a cutlass by the assailants before they fled. Other sources report that the victim was dismembered.
On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons who were returning from the farm at Itapaji (Ikole, Ekiti).

On 4 September 2023, the police opened fire and injured Shiia members while trying to disrupt their procession along Zaria-Panbegwa Road (Zaria, Kaduna). The Shiite members were on their annual Arbaeen symbolic trek when they were fired and gassed by the police. Arbaeen Trek is a Shiite religious practice involving mass trek. Many members got injured as they scampered for safety.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with policemen at Ogbeke-Nike along Ugwogo-Nike-Opi-Nsukka road (Enugu East, Enugu). Two of the assailants were killed; others escaped with gunshot wounds, one rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered by the policemen.
On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people from Dunami Estate, Angwan Dadi, Nyanya (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The abductors asked for no ransom.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his residence in the Area C axis of Nyanya (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The abductors demanded a 25 million naira ransom to release the hostage.
On 4 September 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). Three militia members were killed.

Around 4 September 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hakorin Damisa IV in collaboration with policemen and hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and killed five of them at Tahuwa community, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). Rifles and ammunition were recovered.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian when they invaded Bodo community (Gonaka, Rivers). The assailants fled into a nearby bush, other sources report that the attack was linked to a chieftaincy tussle between two factions in the community.

On 4 September 2023, Boko Haram/ISWAP fighters launched an attack on MNJTF in Ladari near Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). The militants retreated following a fierce fire exchange with the Joint Task Force. No fatalities were reported.
Around 5 September 2023 (week of), a Kaduna militia abducted over 44 civilians along the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari highway (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 5 September 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kuriga Wusasa, coded to Wusasa (Zaria, Kaduna) and rescued three abductees. The militia fled into the bush and abandoned the abductees. No casualties.

On 5 September 2023, a Katsina militia shot and killed six men and a woman and abducted twelve others in the Doka community near Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina). The Doka community was reported to have been impenetrable to the militia after their numerous attempts until the last onslaught. They rustled cows and many domestic animals. The police reported six people were killed and five injured.

On 5 September 2023, the Nigerian troop ambushed ISWAP fighters and killed twelve in Konduga LGA, coded to Gabchari (Konduga, Borno). The army recovered five AK rifles, two locally manufactured rifles, 2 Dane guns, ammunition, four motorbikes, and three daggers.

On 5 September 2023, a group of people mobbed and assaulted a woman in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti) over the allegation that she stole tubers of yams. The victim sustained various degrees of injury. The mobs stripped her naked, recorded her nude video and shared it on the internet. The police arrested two of the perpetrators.

Around 5 September 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with CJTF clashed with presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Bula Marwa in Banki (Bama, Borno). The military killed many of the militants. The military discovered an IED at the militants' camp. Unknown casualties coded as 3.

On 6 September 2023, troops of sector 3 of the MNJTF engaged Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] in an armed clash at Dugushewa village (Magumeri, Borno). One militant was killed, one rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 6 September 2023, policemen and hunters foiled an attempted abduction by an unidentified armed group of five at Jangra village in Gombi LGA (Adamawa). One of the assailants was killed, and others escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 7 September 2023, Benue militia shot and killed two members of the Community Volunteer Guards in Ugba (Logo, Benue). They also shot and killed a woman at Abeda-Shitile on the same day, coded separately. Many people were injured in the attack.
On 7 September 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in conjunction with CJTF killed six Boko Haram fighters [JAS faction] while raiding their camp in Garin Ba'aba near Bama (Bama, Borno).
On 7 September 2023, Benue militia shot and killed a woman in Abeda-Shitile near Ugba (Logo, Benue) after killing two community volunteers in Ugba, coded separately.

Around 7 September 2023 (week of), a Fulani militia raped five women on their farms in Ekakpamre (Ughelli South, Delta) as claimed by the women in the community who embarked on a protest [coded separately].

On 7 September 2023, DSS officers shot and wounded a tailor in Garki Ultramodern Market, Garki (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory), while trying to arrest him for failure to deliver a sewing job given to him by a lady. The lady invited the security operatives to effect the arrest, but they shot and wounded him. In the process, a stray bullet hit and injured a sales girl in her shop. The shootings drew the anger of the people who later mobbed the security agents, coded separately. A source reported that the tailor was shot dead, but other sources reported that victims were injured and taken to the hospital for treatment.
On 7 September 2023, suspected herders attacked farmers in Ungwan Rimi and Ungwa Magaji, coded to Kaduna South (Kaduna South, Kaduna). No further details.
On 7 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 19 civilians from Bwari (Bwari, FCT). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 7 September 2023, an unidentified armed group opened fire on the operatives of the Nigeria Customs Service at their checkpoint in Umuikaa Junction near Okpuala-Ngwa (Isiala Ngwa North, Abia). The armed group burned the operational patrol van of the customs service. They shot and injured a commercial bus passenger that ran into them. The whereabouts of the customs personnel are unknown. A source claimed one of them was shot and escaped with injuries. The military stationed nearby intervened and dislodged them from the checkpoint.

On 8 September 2023, a Kaduna militia set on fire St. Raphael Parish in Fadan Kamantan (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) killing one seminarian. Other seminarians, except the deceased, escaped from the building before it was set ablaze by the militia.
On 8 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have raided a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Kawuri (Konduga, Borno), forcing the soldiers to desert their position. Unspecified equipment was confiscated.

On 8 September 2023, ISWAP killed three people and burned their vehicle in a village close to Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). The victims included a religious leader, a village head and a youth working on his farm. However, ISWAP referred to them as spies. They claimed to have killed them with machine guns and burned their vehicle.

On 8 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her two daughters at Galadima district, coded to nearby Kabusa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, it was later reduced to 50 million then 10 million before 2.840 million naira was eventually paid and the abductees were released on 9 September.

On 8 September 2023, the Police clashed with the Icelanders cult militia while raiding their hideout in Ahoada East LGA, Ahoada (Ahoada, Rivers). The militia overpowered the police who later retreated except the Divisional Police Officer (DPO). The DPO was caught and taken away by the militia before they butchered him. The cult group posted a video where they chanted victory songs and displayed the chartered and decomposing remains of the DPO.

On 9 September 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted over 50 civilians around Darita forest while they were on transit to Bagega (Anka, Zamfara) for the weekly market. One of the abductees who escaped claimed that the militiamen were followers of Halilu Buzu and that the abduction was a response to the government's closure of the Bagega cattle market.

On 9 September 2023, policemen trailed an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Umuota village in Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). One abductee was rescued, one of the assailants was killed, two were arrested and others fled with bullet wounds.

On 9 September 2023, an unidentified armed group that was wearing masks killed three civilians in Agbada Nenwe, coded to Nenwe (Aninri, Enugu). The victims were located and killed at their various houses.
On 9 September 2023, Boko Haram abducted two farmers from a farm in Galameri, coded to Gongulong (Jere, Borno).
On 9 September 2023, a Niger militia abducted five civilians from Kakihun in Mariga LGA (Niger). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 September 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along Anka-Bagega road (Anka, Zamfara). Five abductees were rescued by the troops, casualties are unknown.
Around 9 September 2023 (between 8 - 10 September), an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Kwari Kwasa village (Maiyama, Kebbi). Two persons were killed, six others were abducted.

Around 9 September 2023 (as reported), soldiers beat up an pregnant woman at Ibaa town (Emohua, Rivers) when she went to the army base to inquire about her son's whereabouts. The victim was made to sit on the floor and other women protested over the incident which they claimed was against their culture [coded separately]. The army denied the attack.

On 9 September 2023, the hybrid forces of CJTF and hunters militia shot and killed a Boko Haram [JAS faction] militant in Bazamri (Konduga, Borno). They recovered two carbines from the Boko Haram fighter suspected to have come from Gaizuwa.
On 9 September 2023, former Boko Haram fighters attacked and killed five people in Jege village (Gwoza, Borno).
On 9 September 2023, ISWAP fighters abducted two people and injured one with a matchet in Jodiri village coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). The militants killed one of the hostages.
On 9 September 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two persons from Marke village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 9 September 2023, a Katsina militia abducted 13 civilians from Kuki village (Dutsinma, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 September 2023, an unidentified cult group killed a tailor apprentice in Lagos (Lagos Island, Lagos). The boy had gone to dispatch a sewn cloth when he was accused of being a spy to suspected armed robbers by the cultists who descended on him and beat him to death.

On 10 September 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia and a Yache communal militia engaged in an armed clash at Yache community (Yala, Cross River). The clash was a result of a reprisal after a mob of Tiv locals killed one Yache local [coded separately]. 7 persons were killed, 10 others including women were wounded and 15 houses were set ablaze.

On 10 September 2023, a Fulani militia killed 10 civilians when they attacked Kulben village (Mangu, Plateau). Many other locals were wounded and several houses were destroyed by the assailants who eventually fled the area, other sources report 11 fatalities.

On 10 September 2023, a policeman shot into the air and killed one person who was hit by a stray bullet from the shot at a palliative distribution center in Rijau LGA (Niger). One boy was also wounded, the assailant shot into the air in a bid to keep people in line when the orderliness of the queue was distorted.

On 10 September 2023, policemen invaded the hideout of Icelanders and engaged them in an armed at Odumude forest (Ahoada West, Rivers) coded to Akinima as claimed by the police commissioner. Four Icelanders were killed, others escaped with gunshot injuries. The clash was related to the murder of a policeman by the same assailants.

On 10 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman who is presumed to have been off-duty and a woman at Mile 6 area of Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The wife and daughter of the policeman were also abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources do not report the male victim to be a policeman, and that he was wounded not killed.

On 10 September 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed two members of a rival militia while they were drinking at a pub in Ilesa town (Ilesha West, Osun). Other sources report that the attack was between members of Aiye and Eiye cult militias.
On 10 September 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one civilian and looted cattle from Bamana community (Goronyo, Sokoto).
On 10 September 2023, Nigerian soldiers killed an unknown number of ISWAP fighters in Goniri (Gujba, Borno). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

Around 10 September 2023 (as reported), Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed some ISWAP fighters in Goniri (Gujba, Yobe). The presumed ISWAP fighters rode on two motorcycles and six bicycles when they clashed with the troops. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 10 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a presumed member of CJTF member in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). They claimed the victim was a militia member loyal to the Nigerian Army.

On 10 September 2023, security agents presumed to be policemen killed three civilians at Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers) while they were in search of members of a cult militia who killed a policeman [coded separately]. The victims attempted to flee when they sighted the agent who shot at them.
On 11 September 2023, a vigilantes group clashed with five suspected abductors in the Bumgai community (Gujba, Yobe). A stray bullet hit and killed one person (presumed to be a bystander).

On 11 September 2023, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with some Zamfara militants who abducted four people in Bunkasau village near Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abductors fled and abandoned their victims when they were overpowered by the military.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash at 1st Marine Gate (Warri South, Delta) coded to Warri. One local militia member was killed, the others fled due to superior fire from the assailants.

On 11 September 2023, policemen and hunters trailed an unidentified armed group to their hideout and engaged them in an armed clash in (Yola-South, Adamawa) coded to Tongare following the abduction of a woman from her residence. Two members of the armed group were killed, the abductee was rescued, guns charms, chains and mobile phones were recovered by the police.
On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and injured three vigilantes members in Nyibango Ward, Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The group abducted a woman in the process.
On 11 September 2023, suspected armed pastoralists killed three civilians when they attacked Opi-Agu community (Nsukka, Enugu) coded to Opi. An unspecified number of others were wounded.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a poet in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) while returning from Abuja after a performance. He was taken alongside other passengers and was taken to an unknown destination. The abductors demanded a 20 million naira ransom for his release.
On 11 September 2023, the Katsina Militia blocked the Batsari-Dutsin Ma road in Bakon Zabo, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina) and abducted two people travelling on a motorcycle.

On 11 September 2023, cult members suspected to be the Aiye (Black Axe) confraternity shot and killed a transport worker at Ado community (Eti-Osa, Lagos). The victim was shot when he visited his mother-in-law with his wife. The killing was reported to be a reprisal attack, and his death raised tension over possible full-blown cult clashes in the area.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed six civilians when they attacked Mushy village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau). The victims included five pastoralists and a two-year old as claimed by the chairman of the Plateau state chapter of MACBAN.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted at least ten passengers around the Okene area (Okene, Kogi) while they were enroute to Lagos from Benue. The abductees were travelling in two buses owned by the Benue state government which later announced the release of 18 passengers and two drivers around 13 September, there are no reports on ransom payment.
On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two civilians at Umualumaku (Ehime Mbano, Imo). An unspecified number of persons were injured.

On 12 September 2023, armed pastoralists killed one local defense militia member and wounded two others in Dobi (Gwagwalada, FCT). The militiamen were attacked when they went to inspect a farm that was destroyed by the pastoralists' cattle and resulted in a clash between the pastoralists and farmers.

On 12 September 2023, the Nigerian military intercepted and engaged in a firefight with some Zamfara militias trying to escape with some rustled animals around Tsamiyar Gezozi coded to Anka (Anka, Zamfara). The militia were overpowered and fled. The Nigerian military recovered about 130 animals and handed them over to the state government. No fatalities were reported.

On 12 September 2023, ISWAP waylaid some motorists and abducted two drivers along the Bama-Banki road near Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno). They took the drivers away with two vehicles loaded with food items.

On 12 September 2023, about 17 suspected ISWAP fighters attacked the MNJTF troops stationed in Banki (Bama, Borno), attempting to infiltrate the town. The Nigerian and Cameroonian troops of the MNJTF repelled the onslaught. No fatalities were reported. The militia insisted and launched the second attack the following morning, coded separately.
On 12 September 2023, policemen beat up a young man at the Post Office in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) after they accused him of being a suspected internet fraudster.
On 12 September 2023, the Katsina Militia abducted one person in Garhi village coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).
On 12 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of passengers along Oron road in Uyo LGA (Akwa Ibom).

On 12 September 2023, members of the NURTW and Lagos Park Management committee clashed at the union's headquarters in Garki (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The clash was related to a leadership tussle. One person was killed, several others were wounded and 23 male suspects were arrested by the police. Other sources report that the clash was between two NURTW factions.
On 12 September 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted two people from the Dusuman community (Jere, Borno)
On 12 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted four people in Asara (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).

On 12 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (coded as bandits) clashed with vigilantes in the village of Gandaba, coded to the LGA, HQ, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia members killed 1 and abducted three women, and burned down a mosque, shops, and three houses.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a female corp member in Eku (Ethiope East, Delta) while travelling to visit her fiance. The abductor demanded a 5 million naira ransom for her release.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group in large numbers abducted four persons from Maigemu district (Jos East, Plateau). The abductees included one clergyman and three others, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a Labor Party chieftain at a drinking joint in Amelechi, a village in the Akpukpa community near Onuaku Uturu (Isuikwuato, Abia). The armed group beheaded the victim and went away with his head.

On 13 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity militias clashed at different parts of Ilesa town (Ilesha, Osun). The clashes were reprisals for the killing of two persons on 10 September [coded separately]. Three persons were killed and the clashes occurred at Sabo/Irojo junction and Oke Omiru area.
On 13 September 2023, ISWP and Boko Haram (JAS) clashed around Baga (Kukawa, Borno). Four fishers were killed during the clash, and one of the belligerents seized 100 fishing boats from the fishers.

On 13 September 2023, suspected ISWAP fighters attacked the MNJTF troops stationed in Banki (Bama, Borno). The Nigerian and Cameroonian forces of the MNJTF repelled the attack and prevented the town from falling into the hands of the militia. No fatalities were reported.
On 13 September 2023, the Kaduna militia killed one person and injured twelve others in the Madaka area in Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna).
On 13 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 1 man in his home during an attack on Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto).

On 14 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 33 people in Alkaleri (Alkaleri, Bauchi). Other sources report that 39 persons were abducted, some of the abductees were businessmen who were returning from a market and a ransom of 50 million naira each was demanded. The police rescued the victims on the 15th of September 2023.

On 14 September 2023, Sokoto militia killed four people and abducted eighteen others in Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto). The attack forced the residents to flee the community, and the militia carted away some valuables, including livestock. The community people reported that thirty people were abducted, but the police claimed they were eleven. However, some of the abductees later escaped and returned to the community.

On 14 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a housewife and her brother-in-law in the Nasarawo area of Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The woman was abducted when her husband was not around. The armed group carted away the victims' mobile phones and 11, 000 naira.

On 14 September 2023, the Nigerian military, in collaboration with the police tactical team and the DSS, engaged the IPOB in a gun battle while trying to enter their shrine and hideout in Ekeagbebor Isu coded to Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The government forces killed a militant and arrested two while others escaped with various degrees of gun wounds. A police officer was shot in the leg and was taken to the hospital for treatment.

Around 14 September 2023 (as reported), Nigerian troops engaged in a gunfight with ISWAP fighters while trying to evacuate the corpse and the injured passengers from the IED explosion site in Karetu (Mobbar, Borno). The militants fled the scene when overpowered by the troops. No fatalities were reported.

On 14 September 2023, a stray bullet from an unidentified cult group hit and killed a female student of Nnamdi Azikiwe University at Miracle Junction, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants aimed and shot at a tricycle operator but missed their target. A stray bullet hit the victim and killed her instantly.

Around 14 September 2023 (between 9 September - 19 September), ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed an unspecified number of farmers in Gwoza LGA (Borno). Ten farmers were killed in ten days, fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 15 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty police officer in Toro (Toro, Bauchi). The abductors stormed the victim's village and sporadically shot into the air before taking him away. The abductors are yet to demand a ransom.
On 15 September 2023, suspected IPOB/ESN members abducted one person along the Umuahia-Enugu Road, coded to Awgu (Agwu, Enugu).
On 15 September 2023, the Sokoto militia raided and abducted three people from Wurno town (Wurno, Sokoto). There were no fatalities reported.

On 15 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). About 20 persons were killed, 6 of whom were killed in a continuation on 17 September [coded separately]. Other sources report that many of the victims had nothing to do with the clash.

On 15 September 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Yankari forest, coded to Yankari National Park (Alkaleri, Bauchi). 10 members of the armed group were killed and 39 abductees who were abducted the previous day [coded separately] were rescued.

On 15 September 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians and abducted three others when they attacked Dogonnoma community (Kajuru, Kaduna). Other sources report that 15 people were killed, several others were wounded and 32 residents were abducted.

On 15 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a PDP chieftain in Ada (Boripe, Osun). The victim was shot dead by three men, pretending to be customers, when eating in his wife's shop.
On 15 September 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed two people in Birnin Tudu Community, coded to Talata Mafara (Talat Mafara, Zamfara).

Around 15 September 2023 (week of), two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash in Ilorin metropolis (Ilorin West, Kwara). The body of one student who was declared missing on 13 September was found on the streets on 17 September and was reported to have been mistakenly killed in the clash.

On 16 September 2023, a Kaduna militia engaged and overpowered a local defense militia at Maraban Rido, coded to nearby Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). One civilian was killed, a woman and three of her children were abducted.

On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group opened fire on the police in Isu Aniocha (Awka North, Anambra). The police were on a peacekeeping mission following a chieftaincy tussle in the community. The armed group invaded the community despite the police presence and fired shots sporadically, causing tension in the community. There were no fatalities.
On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of civilians along Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi road (Nsukka, Enugu). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person in Rumuodomaya (Obio, Rivers).

On 16 September 2023, ISWAP attacked a Nigerian army checkpoint in Mairari (Guzamala, Borno). The onslaught forced the soldiers to abandon the post and flee. The militia damaged four motorbikes and seized six others and ammunition before withdrawing. There were no fatalities.
On 16 September 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two women from Bakin Hanya Hamilate in Jan Tsauni village, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 16 September 2023, a Niger militia killed two local defense militia members and a businessman who attempted to confront them during an attack in Pan Dongari (Rafi, Niger). An unspecified number of residents were abducted.

On 16 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed on civilian and wounded several others along Edem-Nrobo-Ezikolo-Abbi road (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The assailants laid seige on the road for several hours.
On 17 September 2023, the Sokoto militia blocked the Wurno-Goronyo Road coded to Goronyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). They shot and injured one person and abducted many others.
On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the Evangelical Church of West Africa (ECWA) in Nuku, Maigemu (Jos East, Plateau). There was no fatalities or injuries.

On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted several passengers traveling in at least five vehicles on the Otukpo-Enugu expressway, coded to Okpoga (Okpokwu, Benue). One of the buses belonged to the Benue state transport company, other sources report that 15 passengers including the driver were abducted from the state owned company's bus and a ransom of 50 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded for an abductee who is a staff of the Nigerian Television Authority.

On 17 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). 6 persons including secondary school students were killed. Other sources report that many of the victims had nothing to do with the clash.

On 17 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a catholic priest along Eke-Egede-Affa road (Udi, Enugu) while he was on the way back to his parish. There are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources report that the priest was abducted alongside 6 persons and that a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.

On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian when they invaded the palace of the Olokanla at Okanla community (Irepodun, Osun) coded to Ilobu. The assailants who were up to 20 set the victim's body ablaze in a car and also burnt the palace, the target who was absent during the attack claimed that it was likely related to a land dispute.

On 17 September 2023, a joint task force of security operatives presumed to have comprised of soldiers and policemen engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash in a village near Pan Dongari (Rafi, Niger). 52 militiamen including six informants who lived in the community were killed.

On 18 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man and his daughter along Afon road (Asa, Kwara) while they were returning from the farm. The police claimed that the girl was rescued, there are no reports on ransom demands for the man.
On 18 September 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up one civilian and abducted two others from Koko town (Koko, Kebbi). A ransom of 15 million naira was demanded.

On 18 September 2023, IPOB/ESN militants who were enforcing a sit-in order engaged soldiers and policemen who were on patrol in an armed clash at Ezioha (Agwu, Enugu). Three militants were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, arms and ammunition were recovered from the killed militants. A group called Intersociety claimed that the military's claims were false and that the persons who were killed were youths from the community that were labelled as militants.

On 18 September 2023, soldiers on a clearance operation engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at their hideouts in Igboro forest, between Arochukwu LGA and Ohafia LGA (Abia). Three militants were killed, and several of their camps were destroyed, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 18 September 2023, the Zamfara militia attacked the Mayaba and Mai Kogo communities, coded to Bungudu (Bungudu, Zamfara). They killed four people and injured two others.

On 18 September 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Jesse-Igueleba road (Ethiope West, Delta). Four members of the group were killed, one rifle, one magazine and 25 rounds of ammunition were recovered by the policemen.
On 18 September 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed a man and his wife along the Jengeme-Ruwan Kongo Road in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara).
Around 18 September 2023 (week of), Boko Haram/ISWAP abducted six persons, including two monarchs in the Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno).

On 19 September 2023, three naval ratings together with some other persons beat up three civilians at their residence in Egbo quarters of Uwheru (Ughelli North, Delta) over a land dispute. The ratings fled, while four persons were arrested in connection with the attack.

Around 19 September 2023 (week of), a presumed Sokoto militia killed and displaced many civilians most of whom were farmers at villages in Kebbi and Sokoto states. The villages affected in Kebbi include Zawaini Zawaini, Jangargari and Jaja, coded to Birnin-Kebbi (Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi). Many houses and shops were set ablaze, many fatalities coded as 10, split across two events and recorded as 5.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot a Fulani woman bathing in her bathroom in the Oke Akure area of Iba (Ifelodun, Osun). The victim was taken to the hospital and died on 21 September 2023. The victim was a nursing mother who left a three-month-old baby behind.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the Madaki of Pavu village in Kuje area council (FCT) when they invaded that area and also abducted nine others. The murdered victim who was the second in command to the village head was killed when he attempted to escape.

On 19 September 2023, ISWAP killed one of its members at Ajikur in Damboa LGA (Borno) over diversion of funds. The militant was sent to buy food stuff for the group but diverted the funds for personal use, he was tied up for two hours before he was slaughtered.

Around 19 September 2023 (week of), a presumed Sokoto militia killed and displaced many civilians most of whom were farmers at villages in Sokoto and Kebbi states. Karani village and three others were affected in Sokoto, coded to Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto). Many houses and shops were set ablaze, many fatalities coded as 10, split across two events and recorded as 5.
