On 21 October 2023, policemen beat up a woman into coma at the Agbarho community (Ughelli North, Delta) and wounded her husband. A child of the victims claimed that they were attacked while searching for their domestic helper, the details of the reason are unclear.
On 21 October 2023, the Sokoto militia killed two people in Sakkwai village (Tangaza, Sokoto). They also abducted an unspecified number of people.
On 21 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person in the Jekadafari area in Gombe (Gombe). The group left with the victim's phone, money and other valuables.

On 21 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked and shot at customs operatives at their office in Geidam town (Geidam, Yobe). One operative was killed, the others fled. The militants set the customs patrol van, a generating set and part of the building ablaze. According to other sources, the Customs claimed to have repelled the militants.
On 21 October 2023, ISWAP fighters abducted seven women from a farm around Bulamalumbe Kanuri and Gulwa villages, coded to Gulwa (Ngala, Borno). No further details.
On 21 October 2023, the Nigerian troops ambushed and killed ten ISWAP fighters around Charlie 3, along the Banki-Bama road, coded to Bama (Bama, Bornu). No further details.
On 21 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person while attacking Gazari village (Sabuwa, Katsina). They also injured one person and abducted nineteen others.

On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty policemen from his farm at Gidan-Idi village (Kurmi, Taraba) coded to Baissa. The abductee had gone to the farm with his workers who were taken hostage in his absence and replaced with him when he returned to the farm from running an errand.
On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person at Alu Oko, Ebge Egume, Aja-Odi, coded to Agojeju (Ofu, Kogi). No further details.

On 22 October 2023, the police and the NSVC raided a hideout of the Niger militia near Dogonruwa village, close to Kaliko (Wushishi, Niger). The police engaged the militia in a firefight. Three hostages were released. There were no fatalities.

On 22 October 2023, the police and the NSVC intercepted the Niger militia and engaged them in a gunfight around Mangoro village, coded to Gini (Muya, Niger). The police rescued eighty people abducted by the militia and returned them to their families. There were no fatalities.

On 22 October 2023, a Katsina militia that attacked civilians engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash in Dan Musa town (Dan-Musa, Katsina). Five persons including a policeman were killed; other sources report 9 killed, 10 to 12 others were wounded while 5 persons were abducted.

On 22 October 2023, a joint security team comprised of soldiers, policemen, a local defense militia, DSS and NSCDC engaged in an armed clash an unidentified armed group at Kanzanna forest (Bunza, Kebbi) coded to Tilli district where some victims were abducted by the group [coded separately]. Three abductees were rescued, one of the assailants was killed, several others escaped with bullet wounds.

On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a female lecturer from her residence at Angwan Jaba in Keffi (Keffi, Nassarawa). The abductee is a staff of the Nassarawa state university. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, the abductee was released on 25 October after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 22 October 2023, Nigerian Navy soldiers engaged in an armed clash with the security details [presumed policemen] in the convoy of the Kogi state governor near Kwali (Kwali, FCT) following the convoy's refusal to stop at a checkpoint. The state commissioner for information claimed that the soldiers were suspected to be assassins targeting the governor while the state governor denied the claims. The Nigerian police claimed that the convoy's unruliness was responsible for the clash, 4 soldiers and two of the governor's aides were wounded.

On 22 October 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted five civilians as they were returning from a market in Jere town (Kagarko, Kaduna). One of the victims who was a nursing mother was released with her child a few meters away from where they were abducted. There are no reports on ransom demands for the other abductees.

Around 22 October 2023 (week of), troops of sector 4 of Operation Udo Ka II killed an IPOB militant at a checkpoint in Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo) after he attempted to escape arrest. Two live ammunitions, a motorcycle, a bag containing charms and one mobile phone were recovered by the troops.

On 22 October 2023, the Nigerian troops and CJTF engaged ISWAP in a firefight after the latter attacked a CJTF position in Ngala (Ngala, Borno). ISWAP fighters withdrew and left a CJTF injured. There were no fatalities.
On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife and daughter of a university professor from their residence in Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 23 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed three IDPs who went to fish at a stream in Gbange/Tomgov ward. Location coded to Agagbe (Gwer West, Benue) where the victims left to go fishing.

On 23 October 2023, a Sokoto militia was repelled by locals presumed to have been a local defense militia when they attacked Tukandu village in Sakkwai ward (Tangaza, Sokoto). Two persons including one of the assailants were killed, the residents fled due to fear of a reprisal attack.

On 23 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people along the Warri-Sapele Expressway, coded to Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The Nigerian security later raided the abductors' hideout in Ibada Elume and rescued the hostage.

On 23 October 2023, the combined security forces, including the military and the police, supported by the local militia, clashed with an unidentified armed group in Ibada Elume, coded to Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The armed group had abducted two people on the highway, coded separately. The security launched a rescue operation and rescued the two hostages. There were no fatalities.
On 23 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person when raiding Garin Waziri village, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). They abducted five women.
On 23 October 2023, the Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of people while raiding Shalla village, coded to Isa (Isa, Sokoto). The victims included women and children.

On 24 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two people at a fuel station in Bagoma Dam, coded to Bagoma (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Three other people sustained varying degrees of injuries, one of the murdered victims was a local defense militia member who is presumed to have been unarmed at the time of the attack.
On 24 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed six civilians when they invaded Dan Sadau town (Maru, Zamfara) in large numbers and shot sporadically. Four other persons sustained serious bullet wounds.

On 24 October 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed two people after blocking the Yan Tumaki-Dan Musa road, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). The militia abducted an unspecified number of travellers.

On 24 October 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with Kaduna militia while on clearance operation around the Dogon daji-Saulawa area in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The soldiers engaged the militia in a firefight, forcing them to scamper for safety. They recovered a G3 rifle, 16 motorcycles, two locally-made guns and a phone. There were no fatalities.

On 24 October 2023, a Sokoto militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers when they invaded Tukandu village in Sakkwai ward (Tangaza, Sokoto) for a reprisal attack after they were repelled the previous day [coded separately]. Several militiamen were killed, one soldier was wounded, 12 motorcycles and three rifles were recovered from the assailants. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 24 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person after blocking the Maidabino-Dan Musa Road, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 24 October 2023, a joint team of soldiers and DSS operatives engaged a Boko Haram militant in an armed clash when they raided his residence at Gbaganu area of Minna (Minna, Niger). The militant fled; 150 AK 47 rifles, 20 rocket propellers and 3000 live ammunition were recovered by the security agents, occupants of the house including women and children were arrested.

Around 24 October 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted 23 civilians from Kudiri village in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna) and four of the abductees escaped about 2 weeks later. A ransom of 20 million naira which was later brought down to 10 million and three bags of rice was demanded with a 7-day ultimatum for the release of the remaining 19 abductees.
On 24 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base in Wajiroko (Damboa, Borno) with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher. They claimed neither damage nor fatalities.

On 24 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked worshippers at a mosque in Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The Imam and another worshipper were killed, many others were wounded. Other sources report that three persons were killed, two others were seriously wounded and that the assailants who were dressed in military uniform emerged from Kamuku forest and were en route to Tegina axis of Niger state.

On 24 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man and wounded his wife as they were on their way to their farm in Goh village (Gwer West, Benue) coded Naka. The victims were attacked with machetes.
On 24 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three travelers along Makurdi-Naka road (Makurdi, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 October 2023, an armed group affiliated with the APC attacked and shot at a supporter of the SDP at his residence in Dekina town (Dekina, Kogi) over his refusal to support the APC governorship candidate. The victim was critically wounded.

On 25 October 2023, the Nigerian troops of 159 Battalion engaged in a firefight with Boko Haram(JAS) in Jororo (Geidam, Yobe). The troops launched an onslaught following the intelligence received about Boko Haram's harassment of the civilians in the village, coded separately. The army killed two Boko Haram fighters and recovered two AK-47 rifles and two Motorcycles.
On 25 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a commercial motorcyclist and stole his motorcycle at a quarry along Obaagun-Iba road (Ifelodun, Osun).
On 25 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed five people in the Tsagengeni village, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). They also injured four people and looted an unspecified number of cattle.

Around 25 October 2023 (as reported), troops of 146 battalion of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash along Karetu-Wulgo axis (Mobbar, Borno). Nine militants were killed, while others escaped with gunshot wounds.
On 25 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one person while attacking a Christian community in Kudbe, around the western Chibok-western Askira area, coded to Askira (Askira Uba, Borno).

On 25 October 2023, the troops of the 27 Task Force Brigade repelled the ISWAP's attempt to overrun Buni Gari (Gujba, Yobe). The militia, in large numbers on motorcycles and two gun trucks, opened fire indiscriminately, but the Nigerian troops responded with firepower and forced them to withdraw. There were no fatalities.

On 25 October 2023, the Yansakai militia killed a policeman (assumed on duty) in Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The militia accused the police officer of being a snitch for other marauding militia groups.
On 25 October 2023, the Taraba militia attacked the Mayo Lope community, coded to Lau (Lau, Taraba). Casualties unspecified. No further details.

On 26 October 2023, suspected Fulani militiamen killed two people and injured another along the Benue - Nasarawa road near Ortese, coded to Ndzorov (Guma, Benue). The militia staged an ambush at the same place the following day and killed another person, coded separately. There were two fatalities.
On 26 October 2023, the Taraba militia abducted six people in Yorro (Yorro, Taraba). The armed group raided the community at night and took away the hostages. No further details.

On 26 October 2023, the Nigerian soldiers and the police engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia invaded Domawa village, coded to Dunya (Dan-Musa, Katsina). A soldier was killed, and the police Armoured Personnel Carrier (APC) was vandalized. An unspecified number of the militia was killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. Coded four fatalities.

Around 26 October 2023 (week of), troops of Operation Udo Ka II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at Orsumoghu forest (Ihiala, Anambra). Two militants were killed, others fled with gunshot injuries, a locally made IED and IED launchers, military boots and belt among other items were recovered.

On 26 October 2023, the troops of Sector 2 Operation Hadin Kai clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) Bajingo village, coded to Babban Gida (Tarmua, Yobe). Several Boko Haram fighters were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 26 October 2023, the troops of Sector 2 Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and killed four Boko Haram (JAS) at Kurnawa (Tarmua, Yobe). Two soldiers sustained injuries during the encounter. The army recovered one AK47 rifle and two motorcycles. Several Boko Haram fighters were also killed in Bajingo, coded separately.

On 26 October 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia attacked and killed a civilian who was a local from Yache (Yala, Cross River) on his farm as claimed by another Yache resident. Other persons claimed that the assailants were escorted by soldiers, but the soldiers denied the claims and accused Yache locals of frustrating the peace talks between both groups. The attack is related to a lingering conflict over payment of royalties between Tiv and Yache locals.

On 26 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed and beheaded a member of AVS in Isiahia village, coded to Osisioma (Osisioma, Abia). The vigilante member and the police had gone to arrest a suspect when they came under fire from the armed group. The police fled when the group overpowered them. Another report claimed the militia ambushed a police team attached to the Rapid Response Squad (RRS) while on stop-and-search duty. The police denied the report that one of them was dead.

On 26 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have damaged a Nigerian Army's vehicle with a hand grenade while attacking a checkpoint in Ajir (Damboa, Borno). They backed up their claim with the picture of a disabled/captured CS/VP3 Bigfoot MRAP vehicle. There was no fatalities claim.
On 26 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with CJTF in Ajir (Damboa, Borno). They claimed CJTF retreated, and they seized their motorbike. There was no fatality claim.

On 26 October 2023, a Zamfara militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers and policemen who repelled the militia in Maru (Maru, Zamfara). Before the arrival of the security operatives, the militia had invaded the Emir's (King) palace and killed one of his guards when they didn't meet him at home. They shot killed the other three victims within the town. The militia damaged the Emir's car with gunshots. Other sources report that 6 persons were killed and 14 others were wounded across different locations in the town.

On 26 October 2023, an unidentified armed group of up to 20 engaged in an armed clash with policemen when they invaded an estate at Kuchibiyi in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). One resident who was part of a search team was shot and wounded in the hand, three other residents were abducted from their apartments.

On 27 October 2023, suspected Fulani militiamen laid an ambush and killed one person along the Benue - Nasarawa road near Ortese, coded to Ndzorov (Guma, Benue). The attack was the second within two days. There was one fatality in the second attack.

Around 27 October 2023 (between 26 October - 29 October), a Tiv ethnic militia wounded at least nine civilians in Yache (Yala, Cross) as claimed by other Yache locals who added that the victims were abducted and they sustained bullet wounds. The attack is related to a lingering conflict over payment of royalties between Tiv and Yache locals.
On 27 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian at Okpokwu ward (Obi, Benue) coded to Obarike-Ito.

Around 27 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed the former local government chairman of Ukum LGA after they abducted him from his residence on 23 September and demanded a ransom, some of which was paid. Location coded to Sankera (Ukum, Benue) where the victim was abducted from.

On 27 October 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot three students at the Ugbowo campus of the University of Benin, Benin City (Oredo, Edo). One of the victims was shot dead, and the second victim could not be accounted for. The third person sustained gun injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment. There is one fatality.

On 27 October 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji responded to a distress call and engaged a Zamfara militia that attacked civilians in an armed clash at Nasarawa town in Maru LGA (Zamfara). Three people were killed before the troops arrived, while the clash lasted for several hours.

Around 27 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a soldier (presumed to be off duty) at the Akparata axis of Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The soldier was part of the contingent deployed to manage inter-communal clashes in the area. The State government issued an ultimatum to the warring communities to provide the soldier alive by 26 October 2023.

On 28 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian, abducted the district head of Ruwan Rana (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and five other persons when they invaded the village and shot sporadically. An unspecified number of cattle were rustled, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 28 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman her two daughters and their house maid from their residence in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The maid was later released, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 28 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Ora community (Ifelodun, Kwara) when they invaded the town and shot sporadically. One woman was killed, two others were abducted. The abductees were female POS operators, the husband of one of the abductees was wounded when he attempted to rescue her.

On 28 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base in Miringa (Biu, Borno). The militia forced the soldiers to retreat and seized two SUVs, a heavy machine gun, a light machine gun, and ammunition. There were no fatalities.

On 28 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier when they ambushed a Nigerian Army patrol team along the Katafila-Mararaba road, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). They claimed the soldiers retreated.
On 29 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons from their house in Gulum (Yorro, Taraba). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 29 October 2023, a Kaduna militia wounded two civilians and abducted one person when they attacked Old Tabanni, coded as Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The residents had put up a resistance [means not stated] in an attempt to prevent the attack.

On 29 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest from his residence at Sarkin-Kudu (Ibi, Taraba). There are no reports on ransom demands, the priest was released the following day, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 29 October 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia and Yache communal militia engaged in an armed clash in Yache (Yala, Cross River) following a lingering dispute over payment of royalties to Yache locals by Tiv settlers. At least 20 persons most of whom were women and children were killed, many sustained varying degrees of machete cuts and gunshot wounds, houses on both sides were set ablaze.

On 29 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia numbering 10 attacked civilians and killed three people at Tse Gamber in Sengev council ward (Gwer West, Benue). One other person was taken away by the assailants. The attack took place in the morning, while another council ward was attacked in the evening of the same day [coded separately].

On 29 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Camp Nagi in Mbachohon council ward (Gwer West, Benue). Three persons were killed and several others were wounded, the attack took place in the evening, while another council ward was attacked in the morning of the same day [coded separately].
On 29 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with CJTF and killed one of their members in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They seized one rifle and five motorbikes and forced the CJTF to retreat.
On 29 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Unguwan Dorowa Bakhira settlement in Maro community (Kajuru, Kaduna). A couple and the only teacher in the community were killed.

On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed a policeman on his farm in Bama town (Bama, Borno) and stole his rifle. The policeman was also stripped off his uniform and his corpse was left in only shorts.
On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants trailed a chief Imam to his house and killed him in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). The militants proceeded to set the victim's Islamic books ablaze.

On 30 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Garin Moddibo town, coded to nearby Sunkani (Ardo Kola, Taraba). The monarch's wife, son and four others were abducted before the assailants proceeded to two neighboring villages where four other people including a nursing mother were abducted.

On 30 October 2023, policemen fired teargas and water cannons at the governor of Rivers state in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) following a crisis over claims of plans to impeach him. The governor also claimed that policemen shot at him while he was on the way to the state house of assembly to assess the level of damage following an explosion at the building. The police spokesperson in the state claimed that the policemen were unaware of the governor's presence and that the policemen did not deliberately shoot at him.

On 30 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three soldiers and wounded two others after attacking the Nigerian Army base at Mussa (Askira Uba, Borno). They forced other soldiers to retreat and captured two rifles and ammunition.
On 30 October 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram militants abducted two hunters at Makinta Kururi village in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). No further details.

On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram/ISWAP militants attacked residents at Ngurokayya village, coded to nearby Kusur (Geidam, Yobe). Some sources report that the militants shot and killed 17 young men, wounded 4 others as punition for tax evasion, other sources report that the town was set ablaze while other residents fled to safety and that the other reason for the attack was that the villagers were accused by the militants of giving security operatives information.

On 31 October 2023, a local defense militia in collaboration with hunters ambushed and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Jajuwal village in Toro LGA (Bauchi). One member of the armed group was killed, an unspecified number of residents were abducted, some of whom were rescued by the local defense militia.

Around 31 October 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadarin Daji raided the hideouts of a Zamfara militia that was led by Dogo Gide at Dan Sadau, Mai Tunkuya and Babban Doka (Maru, Zamfara). The hideouts were destroyed, Dogo Gide fled with serious injuries, weapons were also recovered by the troops. Fatalities are unknown.

On 31 October 2023, an unidentified armed group of four beat up the gate keeper at a radio station in Idofian town (Ifelodun, Kwara). The assailants proceed to rob the other staff of the station, and also stole the network's cables and equipment.

On 31 October 2023, Nigerian troops stationed at Malekachi who were on a routine patrol engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Sangeko forest (Danko, Kebbi) coded to Wasagu. The group's leader Mainasara and two other members of the group were killed; five others who are suspected to be members of the group were arrested, two motorcycles were recovered and destroyed by the troops.

On 31 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Unguwan Baka community in Agunu ward, coded to Agunu Dutse (Kachia, Kaduna). One local was killed, two others were wounded and 25 people were abducted.

On 31 October 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked and shot at policemen who were conducting stop and search about 2km away from Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara). Three policemen were killed; five others and the driver of the patrol van fled into the bush, the driver was later found unconscious while the other five were missing.

On 31 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians along Naka-Makurdi highway (Gwer West, Benue). The abductees were rescued when soldiers who were on a patrol met the abductors and pursued them into the bush, leading the abductors to flee and abandon the victims.

On 1 November 2023, the Bauchi militia abducted six people after raiding Gwalada village in Toro LGA, coded to Toro (Toro, Bauchi). The militia moved their victims to a rocky forest in Bassa LGA in Plateau state, where the police clashed with them and rescued the victims, coded separately.

On 1 November 2023, the Nigerian police, on a rescue operation, clashed with an armed group in a rocky forest between Tumu, Tsaya and Rumfar Gomna in Bassa LGA, coded to Bassa (Bassa, Plateau). The militia had abducted six people from the neighbouring state (coded separately) and kept them in the forest before the police raided their camp. A hunter supporting the police and one of the militiamen lost their lives in the operation, and the police rescued the six hostages.

On 1 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Journalist around Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The victim was returning from Calabar when the group took him. They demanded 10 Million naira to release the hostage,

Around 1 November 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group shot at farmers at Temidire farm settlement (Odigbo, Ondo) coded to Ore. The assailants also destroyed farm settlements and cocoa plantations, there were no casualties. One of the assailants was caught and handed over to the police.

On 1 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with the Nigerian troops and the CJTF near Alagarno Forest, Alagarno (Biu, Borno). They claimed the Nigerian military retreated, and they captured two RPG warheads. There were no fatalities.

On 1 November 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed four Kaduna militias in Kamfanin Doka village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered one AK 47 rifle, one AK 47 magazine, one machete, one mobile phone and fourteen Motorcycles.

On 1 November 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed two people and abducted others on the Funtua - Gusau highway, Kutcheri village (Tsafe Zamfara). The militia blocked the road and attacked motorists and their passengers. A former House of Representatives member of Mafara/Anka (Zamfara State) sustained a gun wound in the attack and was taken to the hospital for treatment. Another source reported that many people were killed in the attack.

On 2 November 2023, five members of the Adamawa militia abducted the Chief of Staff of the Adamawa House of Assembly from his house in Wuro-Chekke, coded to Karewa (Yola-South, Adamawa). The armed group demanded a 20 million naira ransom to release the hostage, it was reduced to 5 million; the victim was released on Tuesday and there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 2 November 2023, five members of the Adamawa militia abducted the Chief of Staff of the Adamawa House of Assembly from his house in Wuro-Chekke, coded to Karewa (Yola-South, Adamawa). The armed group demanded a 20 million naira ransom to release the hostage.

On 2 November 2023, Kaduna militia abducted three laborers working at Nura Suraj Phase 2 Estate, near Millennium City, Doka village, Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna). The police rescued the hostages on the same day.
On 2 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a CJTF checkpoint in Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). They claimed two CJTF were wounded, and others retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 2 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians from Bmuko community in Bwari (FCT). The abductees were initially three; two siblings and a businessman, before one of the siblings escaped. A ransom of one million naira was demanded for the release of one of the abductees.

On 2 November 2023, the Nigerian troops, supported by some local farmers, killed a Kadnua militiaman in the western part of Sabon Sara village, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). One of the farmers sustained a minor injury and was taken to the hospital for treatment. Other militiamen escaped with gun wounds. The troops recovered two AK-47 rifles.

On 2 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two members of NYSC in the Yargoje community (Kankara, Katsina). The victims were in transit between Edo and Katsina State when they were abducted. The Nigerian Army and the Police swung into action and rescued the victims (it was not clear if they engaged in a firefight to rescue the victims).

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian troops killed two militiamen while conducting a clearance operation around Kankomi, Gwantu, Kujeni, Kikwari, Kaso and Juji in Chikun LGA, coded to Juji (Chikun, Kadunma). The troop recovered one AK 47 rifle, one AK 47 magazine, four 7.62MM Special ammunition, one Honda motorcycle and one Techno phone.

On 3 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two women in Kiyawa town (Kiyawa, Jigawa). The abductees were the wives of the local government chairman and one of them was heavily pregnant. On 7 November, the police confirmed that the victims were released but did not provide details on the conditions of their release, a family member of the abductees claimed that an undisclosed ransom amount was paid.

On 3 November 2023, Kogi militiamen abducted a government official and his driver along Lokoja-Obajana Road in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The militia had blocked the highway before seizing their hostages. No further details.
On 3 November 2023, the Sokoto militia killed six people in Duhuwa village, Wurno LGA (Wurno, Sokoto). An unspecified number of people were also abducted.
On 3 November 2023, Kogi militiamen killed one person at a shop in Yagba West LGA, coded to Odo Ere (Yagba West, Kogi). They injured three other people and abducted one.

On 3 November 2023, an armed group suspected to be APC killed a PDP chieftain and injured another in the Ogbolomabiri community in Nembe LGA coded to Nembe (Nembe, Bayelsa). The attack occurred about eight days before the gubernatorial election in the state.
On 3 November 2023, pirates shot and killed four NSCDC officers on the Bakana River, Bakana (Degema, River). No further details.
On 3 November 2023, Nigerian soldiers repelled an ISWAP attack on Damboa- Azir road, coded to Ajir (Damboa, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 3 November 2023, the troops of the 68th Battalion clashed with ISWAP around Kudankurgu in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). The army recovered six IEDs. There were no fatalities.

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a gunfight as the militia attempted to invade Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). ISWAP fighters retreated after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.
On 3 November 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted a Catholic priest at Godogodo (Jema'a, Kaduna). The abductee was rescued by policemen who raided Dogon Kurmi forest [coded separately].

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian security forces, coded as police, engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group along the Gwarimpa-Kubwa Expressway, in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The group abducted a victim and attempted to escape when the security engaged them. They escaped, leaving the victim and their vehicle behind. There were no fatalities.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and injured many people at the election venue of the Ano Stone Dealers Association in Isiaka (Ivo, Ebonyi). The group vandalized houses and shops and set vehicles on fire. There were no fatalities

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a judge and two other persons at Degri (Balanga, Gombe) when they went to inspect a disputed piece of land. The three victims were wounded, one of them was a court staff.

On 4 November 2023, a Zamfara militia ambushed and engaged soldiers who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Karazau village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). Several militiamen were killed and the others fled, fatalities coded as 10.
On 4 November 2023, the Kaduna militia shot and killed two people in Kudiri village Kagarko LGA, coded to Kagarko (Kagarko, Kaduna). The militia abducted nineteen others.

On 4 November 2023, policemen in collaboration with a local defense militia raided the hideout of a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Dogon Kurmi forest (Jema'a, Kaduna) coded to Jemaa. Two militiamen were arrested and two others escaped, a Catholic priest whom they abducted the previous day was rescued and one rifle loaded with two rounds of live ammunition was recovered. No casualties.

On 4 November 2023, a suspected Benue militia attacked and killed seven persons at a beer parlor in Tyoakosu (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera. The attack is suspected to be related to a supremacy battle between two militias in the area.

On 4 November 2023, a Katsina militia shot and wounded one civilian at Masaku village in Kankara LGA (Katsina). The victim who was abandoned on the roadside by the assailants was rescued by policemen.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a senior female INEC staff in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The group came in a Toyota Camry car and pretended to rent chairs from the victim. They tied one of the victim's aides with rope and put him in the refrigerator before driving her away in her car. However, a mob caught one of the gang while trying to escape and beat him up, coded separately. The abductors are yet to demand a ransom.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor who was on duty at the university of Nigeria teaching hospital in Ituku-Ozalla, coded to Ozalla (Nkanu West, Enugu). The abductee escaped from the abductors hideout later that same day.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Harm [JAS faction] militants attacked Koshebe (Mafa, Borno) and Kakuri villages [coded seaparately] on motorcycles. The assailants who split themselves into three groups killed about 15 rice farmers whom they attacked using knives and cutlasses. An unspecified number of farmers were declared missing, 15 fatalities split across two events coded as 8. Other sources report that the victims were killed in retaliation, after rival ISWAP militants invaded JAS hideouts and demanded that the farmers who were initially abducted with the aim of ransom collection, should be released.

On 5 November 2023, Nigerian troops conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Maidaro, Ngade, Ahla and Rikau villages in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, one AK47 rifle and one motorcycle were recovered by the troops.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed a man on his farm near Bama town (Bama, Borno) and abducted four of his farm workers. The murdered victim was shot dead when he resisted being abducted.

On 5 November 2023, Fulani militia attacked a farmer in Gidankwanu village, Karshi (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The victim's family retaliated and injured a Fulani herder. There were no fatalities.

On 5 November 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Kaduna militia around Kajuru forest in Kajuru LGA, coded to Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna). The military killed one of the militiamen and injured many others. Weapons were also recovered.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Harm [JAS faction] militants attacked Kakuri village in Mafa (Borno) and Koshebe village [coded seaparately] on motorcycles. The assailants who split themselves into three groups killed about 15 rice farmers whom they attacked using knives and cutlasses. An unspecified number of farmers were declared missing, 15 fatalities split across two events coded as 7. Other sources report that the victims were killed in retaliation, after rival ISWAP militants invaded JAS hideouts and demanded that the farmers who were initially abducted with the aim of ransom collection, should be released.

On 5 November 2023, five soldiers beat up the private security guards who were guarding the house of MASSOB leader, Ralph Uwazurike in Okwe (Onuimo, Imo) as claimed by the leader himself. He also claimed that that the security guards were taken away.
On 5 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two people travelling from Batsari to Tashar Gurgu village in Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari(Batsari, Katsina).

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged in an armed clash when ISWAP demanded for the release of farmers who were abducted and later killed by JAS militants in retaliation [coded separately]. Location coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno) where the abduction took place, casualties from the clash are unknown.

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two soldiers and injured another after attacking a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Bornu). They claimed to have seized two rifles and an RPG launcher.

On 5 November 2023, policemen and Ebube Agu operatives shot at the convoy of the Imo state LP gubernatorial candidate at Obibiezena (Owerri North, Imo) and prevented him from passing the road as claimed by the LP candidate. He also claimed that the was denied access to the road because he was going to a church where both he and the governor were invited. The police denied attacking him and claimed that he was only asked to not campaign in the area because the APC candidate was already doing so. There were no casualties.
On 5 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians and wounded two others at Ayati village (Ukum, Benue). Other sources report that the attack is likely the result of a reprisal.

On 5 November 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted four others at Maru town (Maru, Zamfara). The assailants shot sporadically and moved from house to house during the attack, an unspecified number of persons were wounded and the abductees included a lecturer at the college of state education. Other sources report that two civilians were killed, a police vehicle was set ablaze by the assailants and five persons were abducted, the lecture was killed by the militia around 18 December after 2 million naira was paid as ransom (coded separately).

On 5 November 2023, a Katsina militia in dozens attacked muslim worshippers from different villages who were observing a Maulud procession at Kusa village in Musawa LGA (Katsina). At least 20 to 25 persons were killed; many others were wounded and several people were abducted. The police claimed that 7 to 18 persons were killed and 16 others were wounded.

On 5 November 2023, a Benue militia led by 'Full Fire' and another militia that was contracted by Full Fire engaged in an armed clash with a rival Benue militia led by 'Chain' at Chito (Ukum, Benue) over supremacy. 15 militia members were killed, some locals claimed that they were 10.

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram shot and killed eight IDPs and injured six others in Kaluwa village, coded to Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The IDPs went in search of charcoal when the militiamen indiscriminately opened fire on them.

On 5 November 2023, Nigerian troops conducted an operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Tantatu and Antenna areas in Chikun (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, one AK47 rifle and magazine and other items were recovered.

On 6 November 2023, the Sokoto militia, numbering about 100, attacked Gidan-Buwai (Rabah, Sokoto). The militia riding on motorcycles surrounded the village and opened fire indiscriminately on the residents. They rustled over 100 cows, 200 sheep, and goats. They also razed many houses, over 60 silos, ten motorcycles, and five vehicles. The group injured seven people and killed 11 others in Gidan-Buwai and Maikujera. Five were killed in Maikujera, coded separately, and six people lost their lives in Gidan-Buwai. There were six fatalities.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), Sokoto militia attacked Maikujera village (Rabah, Sokoto). They killed five people and injured many others. The injured were admitted to the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto. There were five fatalities.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers who responded to a distress call at Alawa community (Shiroro, Niger) where the assailants ambushed civlians who were in transit. One civilian was killed while attempting to escape, two vehicles conveying goods and some motorcycles were burnt, the soldiers were declared missing.
On 6 November 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed nine people in the Gbutuku community, Madagali LGA, coded to Madagali (Madagali, Adamawa). No further details.

On 6 November 2023, Fulani herders attacked and injured seven people in Chirawa town in Bade LGA, coded to Gashua (Bade, Yobe). The security forces were deployed to restore order. There were no fatalities.

On 6 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Gandu (Lafia, Nassarawa) and killed one person. An unspecified number of residents were abducted including a businessman and a student in the area claimed that their phones were also snatched. Other sources report that the victim who is a student was shot and wounded but not killed.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), an unknown group, suspected to be the Security Watch Corps, killed a former LGA Caretaker Chairman, Alhaji Hamza Abdullahi, in Zakka (Safana, Katsina). The victim was accused of being a spy for the marauding militia group, and his killing was suspected to be part of the targeting of the alleged collaborators by the Security Watch Corps.
On 6 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted a woman from her farm on the outskirts of Garin Hambana, Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari(Batsari, Katsina).

On 6 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a CJTF checkpoint and injured an unspecified number of the force in Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). They claimed the CJTF fighters withdrew. There were no fatalities.

On 6 November 2023, a suspected Benue militia killed nine civilians at Ukoosaa-Atam community which is about 1km away from Ayati (Ukum, Benue). The victims included a tricyle rider, his passengers and some persons who were riding a motorcycle. Other sources report 10 fatalities.

On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with the APC fired indiscriminately at policemen and other security guards at the country home of the director-general of the SDP gubernatorial campaign in Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). At least one policeman and four other persons were killed, their corpses were taken away by the assailants. The police claimed that in collaboration with DSS and NSCDC operatives, it carried out an operation and killed two suspected political thugs who were housed by politicians and that two members of the team were wounded while 7 suspects were arrested.
On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two civilians at the Opolo area (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). No further details.

On 7 November 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 12 residents of Anguwar Algaita in Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and later killed two of them. The bodies of the murdered victims who were killed for refusing to follow the assailants were found in the bush the following evening and one other person was rescued with bullet wounds.

On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked residents of Iyi-Owa Odekpe, coded as Odekpe (Ogbaru, Anambra). One person was assumed killed; at least 30 vehicles and 20 houses were destroyed and the chairman of the landlords association claimed that the community's monarch and president-general were responsible for the attack, a claim which they denied.
On 7 November 2023, Boko Haram (Bakura faction) engaged in a fire fight with ISWAP in the Kainowa East Mobbar LGA, coded to Asaga (Mobbar, Borno). No fatalities.
On 7 November 2023, ISWAP shot and killed two people in Kalwa (Monguno, Borno). No further details.
On 7 November 2023, Fulani herders and farmers clashed on the outskirts of Buni Yadi town (Gujba, Yobe). Two people were injured. There were no fatalities.
On 7 November 2023, the Katsina militia killed two people in Dangani village (Musawa, Katsina). They also abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 7 November 2023, the troops of the 112 Task Force Battalion of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and killed three ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters at Manawaji (Mafa, Borno). The militias were trying to assault some farmers when the troops launched an onslaught against them. Seven hostages were released, and the troops recovered one AK-47 rifle, 2 AK-47 rifle magazines, one fabricated pyrotechnic, and two motorcycles.

On 7 November 2023, the Nigerian troops ambushed and killed one ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) fighter in Gabti, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Bornu). The militiamen were trying to cross from Nigeria to Niger when the soldiers killed one of them. The troops rescued eleven hostages from the militia. Two AK rifles, hand grenades, ammunition, and over 11 million naira ($13,700) in cash were recovered from them.

On 7 November 2023, a Katsina militia engaged policemen who responded to a distress call in an armed clash when the militia invaded Sayaya community (Matazu, Katsina). Five civilians were killed, two were wounded and five others were abducted by the assailants.

On 7 November 2023, the Nigerian military opened fire at the ISWAP / Boko Haram position after sighting the militiamen around the Kuranabasa Mountain axis, Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted and killed a 13-year-old girl in Umuolu Okehi, Etche LGA, coded to Okehi (Etche, Rivers). No further details

On 8 November 2023, the Gbagyi militia clashed with some Fulani at the Beji Weekly Market, Beji (Bosso, Niger). Two persons were killed and seven others injured during the clash. Seven victims were hospitalised with various degrees of bullet wounds. The Gbagyi are agrarians, while the Fulani are pastoralists. The reason for the clash is unknown. There were two fatalities.

On 8 November 2023, some Mayaki farmers attacked a 12-year-old herder and cut off his two hands in Mayaki (Lapai, Niger). The boy went out to graze some cattle when the farmers attacked him. The police arrested one of the suspects.
On 8 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have forced the CJTF to retreat when they advanced towards ISWAP position around Sambisa Forest, coded to Bula Korege (Bama, Bornu). There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, ISWAP attacked some laborer's in Tarmuwa, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). They stole fourteen bicycles and one pushcart. There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, Sokoto militia killed two people (a father and his son) in Kware village in Kware LGA, coded to Kware (Kware, Sokoto). The militia abducted five people during the attack.
On 8 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted three people from a commercial bus along the Tsafe-Funtua-Zaria Road, Funtua LGA, coded to Funtua (Katsina).
On 8 November 2023, two unidentified rival cult militia engaged in an armed clash over supremacy at Ojota (Kosofe, Lagos). Two militia members were killed.

On 9 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia shot at a school bus along Eke - Egede road, Eke (Udi, Enugu). A female student of St Paul's College, Eke, was shot dead in the process, and three others sustained gun injuries. The students were going home when the marauders attacked their school bus.

On 9 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a traditional ruler along Eke-Egede-Affa Road, Eke (Udi, Enugu). The chief was returning from a security meeting when the militia seized him. The incident occurred after the militia attacked a school bus and killed one of the students, coded separately.

On 9 November 2023, a local defense militia invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them an armed clash after they arrested informants who led them to the group's hideouts in the forest. Location coded to Bin Yauri (Ngaski, Kebbi), three members of the group were killed.

On 9 November 2023, the Nigerian troops and the CJTF killed six ISWAP fighters and rescued 78 captives at Gime and Muzuri villages near Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). The Military recovered some AK-47 rifles and 3 Dane guns. The rescued hostages included 30 women and 48 children. There were six fatalities.

On 9 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three soldiers after attacking a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Mararaba, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). They wounded two soldiers and seized a rifle and an RPG launcher.

On 9 November 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai shot and killed five ISWAP fighters during a clearance operation at Mulumti General Area of Buni Gari (GUjba, Yobe). The troop and the militia engaged in a heavy gunfight, killing five militias and forcing others to withdraw with gun wounds. The army recovered 1 CONQUEROR APC, 4 Ak47 rifles with four extra Magazines, 1 GPMG, 1 NSVT GUN 1, Baofeng Radio and 150 Quantities of 12.7 MM rounds. An IED killed one of the soldiers as they were returning to the base. There were six fatalities.

Around 9 November 2023 (as reported), some policemen attacked two soldiers in Ikole (Ekiti) over the harassment of a policewoman. The policewoman accused the soldiers of violating traffic rules, but they instead beat up the policewoman. The officer called for backup, and her colleagues responded and descended on the soldiers. There were no fatalities.
On 9 November 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram (Bakura group) engaged in a firefight for about two hours in Duji (Mobbar, Borno). The Boko Haram overpowered ISWAP and killed scores of them, coded as 20.

On 9 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed an Ex-Oyo Permanent Secretary at her residence in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). Her body was found the next day with her hands and legs tied. The victim had reported a threat to her life by some hoodlums around her house.

On 9 November 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted 13 commuters along the Naka road (Gwer West, Benue) as they were travelling from Oturkpo to Makurdi in the state owner transport company bus. The abductees were initially 16 until 3 escaped.
On 10 November 2023, an armed group on motorcycles shot and killed two people in the Latawa area of Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). The assailants were suspected to be cult militia.

On 10 November 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted 20 civilians at a roadblock that they mounted near Yargalma village (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abductees included farmers and a health worker who were unable to bail themselves from the militia at the road block.

On 10 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted clearance operations engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Mai-Kulu Gwanda, Rafin Gora, Funtua Badaddi and Kabawa villages in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, a radio and a motorcycle were recovered.

On 10 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch on clearance operation engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kawara forest (Igabi, Kaduna). One militia member was killed; others fled with gunshot wounds, a loaded AK47 rifle, a motorcycle and one a phone were recovered.

On 10 November 2023, the Nigerian troops repelled the Boko Haram (JAS) in a attempt to invade Damboa from the Gwoza axis in Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The ensuing firefights forced the militia to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 10 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man in Oji River town or Oji River Settlement (Orji River, Enugu). No further details.

On 10 November 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Muslim worshippers who were attending a Maulud procession at Zagami village (Faskari, Katsina) and killed one person. Many people were wounded and several others were abducted.

On 10 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF along the Dikwa- Ajiri road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). They claimed to have forced the CJTF to retreat, seized two motorbikes, and burned the third one. There were no fatalities.
On 10 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF checkpoint in New Marte (Marte, Borno). They forced the CJTF to withdraw. There were no fatalities.

On 10 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an INEC official at Amassoma jetty in Sagbama (Sagbama, Bayelsa) while waiting to board a boat to his polling Unit. The officer who was to supervise the gubernatorial election at Registration Area 06 (Ossisioma) was released the following day, there are no details on the conditions of his release.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated to the APC disrupted the voting process at polling units 14, 15 and 19 of ward 11 in Opume and Emakalakala (Ogbia, Bayelsa). There were no casualties.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform attacked a PDP chieftain at constituency 4 of Southern Ijaw LGA (Bayelsa) coded to Oporoma, after the chieftain engaged them in an argument following their invasion of the area. Hundreds of voters fled, there were no casualties.

On 11 November 2023, the security forces (coded as the military) clashed with an armed group attacking Ogiadiama Ward 9 in Unit 14, Southern Ijaw LGA, coded to Azuzuama (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The attackers were forced to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group (likely cult militia) on motorcycles shot and killed one person at Ita Oba Roundabout in Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun).

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to have political affiliation shot and killed a voter at Agala Ogane polling unit in Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). Some sources report that the victim attempted to snatch a ballot box while others report that two persons were killed; one was a voter and the other attempted to snatch a ballot box.

On 11 November 2023, Zamfara militia who were in large numbers engaged policemen and a local defense militia who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Gada village (Bungudu, Zamfara). 7-8 civilians, 6 defense militiamen and several of the assailants were killed (coded as 10), many of them fled with wounds and cattle that were rustled from the community, ten of which were recovered. Total of 23 fatalities coded.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group fired indiscriminately in the vicinity of the Abuja/Imbikiri area in Brass Ward 2, Brass (Brass, Bayelsa). The shooting was likely aimed at scaring voters away from the polling units. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, APC loyalists engaged in an armed clash with security operatives (coded as military forces) at Fangbe (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). An unspecified number of casualties were reported.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the PDP gubernatorial candidate at Ikeduru LGA (Imo) coded to Iho and wounded some of his aides. The candidate claimed that one of the assailants was a member of the state house of assembly.

On 11 November 2023, security operatives (coded as policemen) shot and killed a man for attempting to steal a ballot box at Amanwozuzu in Iho (Ikeduru, Imo). The operatives took away the victim's bag and left the body which was eventually taken away by policemen.
On 11 November 2023, a Katsina militia abducted three civilians from Gogalo village in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees were rescued by policemen who trailed the militia [coded separately].

On 11 November 2023, a Katsina militia engaged a joint team of policemen, local defense militia and Katsina security watch operatives in an armed clash when they responded to a distress call at Yankara (Faskari, Katsina). One of the assailants was killed, different types of live rounds and AK47 magazines were also recovered.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Agbeku community (Ifelodun, Kwara) and abducted three others including a pastor when they invaded a church auditorium and the victims' residence, one person was shot and critically wounded. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded for the release of the abductees.

Around 11 November 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants from the Bakoura Baduma camp invaded the camp of rival ISWAP fighters and engaged them in an armed clash at Duji village (Mobbar, Borno). The Boko Haram fighters were led to the rival camp by an ISWAP fighter whom they captured, dozens of ISWAP fighters and one Boko Haram fighter were killed, dozens coded as 12.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group of two who have an affiliation with the local palace beat up a former councilor and killed him at Precious Seed community in Oworonsoki (Kosofe, Lagos). The victim was attacked over his refusal to pay the assailants an amount they demanded because he was carrying out a construction work. The assailants fled and were declared wanted by the police.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group that were wearing masks and suspected to have political affiliation killed the YPP ward chairman for Nanka ward 1 (Orumba North, Anambra). The victim was killed shortly after he hosted the party's house of representatives candidate for the constituency over a meeting for a rerun election as directed by the Appeal court, the candidate claimed that the victim was called 'saboteur' thrice before he was shot.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a voting Registration Area Centre in Brass Ward 8, Oginibiri or Ogboinbiri (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The attack was likely aimed to disrupt the voting process. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted electoral officials and stole result sheets at Umuodu Community Primary School in Ezinihitte Mbieri (Mbaitoli, Imo).

On 12 November 2023, the Kaduna militia killed nine people after attacking the Warkan community, Zangon Kataf (Zangon Katab, Kaduna). Many people were injured, and about twelve houses were set on fire.

On 12 November 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted the District Head of Kujama around Bethel Baptist School, Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). The abductors came on motorcycles and took him away with two others at gunpoint. No further details.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed three persons at Agbowa area in Shagamu LGA (Ogun). The police claimed to have recovered three bodies with bullet wounds, expended cartridges, one cartridge and a phone from the scene and also arrested three suspects in connection with the attack.

On 12 November 2023, the Taraba militia abducted a random bearer who had approached the militia to secure the release of his relative around the Muslim Council Secretariat in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The victim was released after the militia received another ransom.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a PDP supporter at the collation center in Brass town (Brass, Bayelsa) when they invaded the center. The victim was also an aide to the local government chairman, other sources report that the assailants were affiliated with the APC gubernatorial candidate.

On 12 November 2023, policemen trailed and engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash after the militia abducted three civilians from Gogalo village in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 12 November 2023, the government security forces (coded as the military) and the local vigilante group clashed with the Katsina militia while attacking Zakka village (Safana, Katsina). Thirteen militia and two government forces were killed in the clash. There were fifteen fatalities.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a University of Calabar lecturer from his residence within the university staff quarters in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductee was taken away via a river that overlooks the quarters, a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. The abductee was released around 10 December, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 12 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted clearance operations and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash around the general area of Maro - Chibiya forest (Kajuru, Kaduna). One militia member was killed; others fled, one AK47 rifle, a locally fabricated rifle, ammunition and a mobile phone were recovered.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified cult militia were engaged in an armed clash by policemen who responded to a distress call following an attack on civilians at Odimeneyi village (Ahoada, Rivers) by the militia who killed five persons before policemen arrived. A witness claimed that the assailants said the attacks would continue until their members and a chief who were in police custody were released. The police claimed that two of the assailants were killed also. Total 7 fatalities.
On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed five people in the Odiemereni community or Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers). No further detail.

On 13 November 2023, Supreme Vikings Confraternity and Supreme Eiye Confraternity also called Eiye engaged in an armed clash at Ozoro community (Isoko North, Delta). One person was killed and the police arrested four suspects in connection with the incident.

On 13 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted six people after blocking the Kankara-Dutsin Ma Road near Garangamawa (Dutsinma, Katsina). The victims, including women and children, were travelling to attend a wedding ceremony in Kagara village.

On 13 November 2023, an unidentified armed group affiliated with the Baale (local chief) of Ilua abducted and beat up a lawyer whose vehicle was ambushed at Iware junction, 20 km away from Ilua (Saki West, Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 13 November 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted three people in Laying Mahuta in Tabanni village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia invaded the community at night, broke into the victims' room and took them away. No further details.

On 13 November 2023, the Kaduna militia attacked the Police at Kakangi Community (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They attempted to set the police Armored Personnel Carrier vehicle ablaze. The police drove the vehicle away while they were being shot at. Two police officers sustained gun wounds in the hands. There were no fatalities.

On 13 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash in the general area of Juji and Telele-Kaso (Chikun, Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed; others fled, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 13 November 2023, a local defense militia engaged suspected armed Fulani pastoralists that attacked civilians in an armed clash inside the Old Oyo National Park in Sepeteri (Saki East, Oyo). One civilian was killed by the assailants, two others were abducted, one of the abductees was rescued by the defense militia. The police claimed that there were no fatalities and that three defense militiamen were wounded.

Around 13 November 2023 (as reported), a local defense militia ambushed and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash near Dan Umoru village (Danko, Kebbi) as they were returning to Maru in Zamfara after attacking one civilian in Dan Umoru. All the four attackers were killed by the defense militia, it is unclear whether the civilian was killed or wounded.

On 13 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one person and forced others to flee after invading a Christian community near Chibok, coded to Chibok (Chibok, Borno). The militia stole unspecified property.
