On 28 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two farmers on their farms in Kwambai, also called Kpombal (Takum, Taraba).

Around 28 November 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked residents of seven villages in Kaga LGA (Borno) coded to Benisheikh and killed several civilians. The villages were attacked and asked to leave the area by the militants because they failed to provide information on the military's activity in the area. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 28 November 2023, the Nigerian police, in collaboration with the Army, Hunters and Local vigilantes, engaged the Taraba militia in a firefight in Tonti village (Bali, Taraba). The clash was a response to the distress call on the invasion of the village by the militia. The security forces ambushed them and killed more than 50 militiamen.

On 28 November 2023, a Kaduna militia numbering seven abducted eight residents of Dan-Honu, coded to near by Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna). The abductees included a couple, an Imam; his wife, children and baby. The Imam, his wife and baby escaped as they were being led away.
On 28 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Arm/CJTF checkpoint in Lingir (Monguno, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 28 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three men while attacking a Nigerian Army and CJTF checkpoint near Mairari (Guzamala, Borno). They wounded many and forced others to retreat. They also burned three motorbikes and seized nine others, weapons, and ammunition. Other sources reported four fatalities, and the attack was an ambush in nearby Lingir. There were three fatalities.

On 28 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Bolt driver and a female passenger at the staff quarters of the University of Calabar, Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductors left the Bolt cab and went away with the driver.

On 28 November 2023, soldiers and policemen from Operation Hawk invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Koka area of Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta). One policeman was killed; 125 members of the group were arrested, 8 of whom were identified as armed robbers, pistols, laptops and other items were recovered.
On 28 November 2023, the Nigerian military engaged ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) in a firefight around the Yaleri Kurna, coded to Konduga (Kodunga, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 29 November 2023, the Nigerian police and local vigilante group attacked an unidentified armed group attempting to abduct a man in Kadade (Toro, Bauchi). One of the abductors was shot dead by the police, and others escaped with gunshot wounds. The police rescued three other persons, including a pastor abducted from Raddi village in Plateau State, coded separately. There was one fatality.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three people, including a pastor from Raddi Village, coded to Bassa (Bassa, Plateau). The hostages were later released when the police attacked the militia in Bauch State, coded separately.

On 29 November 2023, Nigerian security (coded as the police) engaged unidentified group of abductors in a firefight in Yogi village, coded to Toro (Toro, Bauchi), killing one of the abductors. Two hostages were released after that.

Around 29 November 2023 (as reported), Black Axe also called Aiye confraternity members killed a gate keeper at Aiyetoro area of Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos) following the victim's involvement in brokering peace between the militia and a person whom they previously robbed. The victim was lured to where he was shot before his body was hacked to a heap of meat by the assailants.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Anyiin (Logo, Benue), Ayilamo, Iorza and Gbeji [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Iorza and Gbeji (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba, Anyiin and Ayilamo [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group loyal to a candidate for the NANS president position shot and wounded some students at the venue of the NANS convention in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). A former president of the association who is currently the SSA to the president on student engagement led the assailants to the venue. The victims of the attack were delegates for opposition candidates.
On 29 November 2023, the Sokoto militia killed one person in the Dan Abba community, coded to Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia also abducted twenty people from the community.

On 29 November 2023, NSCDC officials shot and wounded two students at a secondary school in Life Camp, Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The reason for the attack is unknown and the officials were arrested.
Around 29 November 2023 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Iyan-Era area of Ojo LGA (Lagos). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group of 5 who were hooded killed the Ogun state government house's director of finance, wounded his aides at Kuto bridge in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) and stole unspecified amount of money. The stolen money was a large sum which the victim had withdrawn for government use from a bank about 3 km away from the scene of the attack. Other sources report that the assailants were armed robbers.
On 29 November 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a firefight after the militia ambushed them in Ali Gambori village (Guzamala, Borno). ISWAP fighters retreated. There were no fatalities.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Ayilamo (Logo, Benue), Anyiin, Iorza and Gbeji [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Catholic priest and his driver in Umuekebi, Osu Owerre (Isiala Mbano, Imo). The militia robbed some shops before moving the hostages away. A ransom of 50 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded, the abductees were released on 8 December, some sources report that 500,000 naira was paid as ransom.

On 30 November 2023, suspected Fulani herders attacked and killed a lady and six men in Pukah or Pukah Pushit (Mangu, Plateau). They also raided Pinper, coded separately. The attack was aimed at avenging the killing of a Fulani man whose body was found in a well. Other sources report 8 fatalities and updated it to 11 after 3 more bodies were found in the bush when the 8 victims were being buried. Fatalities coded as 8.

On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a popular businessman in his village of Umuezikegbu in Egbuoma community (Oguta, Imo). The victim was dragged out of his house by the assailants and shot severally until he died.
On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one civilian and abducted seven locals when they invaded Igu community (Bwari, FCT).
On 30 November 2023, the Sokoto militia raided Gidan Marayu near Dundaye (Wamakko, Sokoto). They abducted an unspecified number of the residents.

On 1 December 2023, the Kebbi militia shot and killed a member of an unidentified armed group in Tunga village (Bunza, Kebbi). The suspect was killed while shooting arrows indiscriminately at the people.

On 1 December 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians at Gwamatse village in Wurno LGA (Sokoto) and killed two persons. The police claimed that at least three people were killed, and one other person was injured.

On 1 December 2023, an unspecified number of policemen abducted a civilian at the Choba axis (Obio, Rivers) and demanded for a ransom of 1 million naira. The abductors were arrested by the police and the victim was rescued around 5 December.
On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a fisher in Twon-Brass (Brass, Bayelsa). They injured many fishers and abducted an unspecified number of others.

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the security officials (coded as the police) while trying to attack the INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) at his residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The firefight raged for about 30 minutes before reinforcement arrived, and the militia fled. Properties were destroyed, including one of the attacker's cars. There were no fatalities.

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a school girl on her way back home from school at Ikotun (Alimosho, Lagos). The abductors assumed that the victim's father is a wealthy politician capable of paying ransom, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Jakana (Konduga, Borno) and forced the soldiers to retreat. 1 was wounded, and 2 ISWAP fighters were killed before they were forced to flee.

On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two CJTF members after they attacked their checkpoint in Katarko (Gujba, Yobe). They seized three rifles. Another source reported that ISWAP lost an unspecified number of fighters.
On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two Nigerian soldiers and injured many others in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The militia seized the rifles of the slain soldiers.

On 1 December 2023, the Nigerian military killed an unspecified number of IPOB/ESN in the Umuogwo forest (Ohaji, Imo). They recovered numerous weapons. Unknown fatalities coded as 3 (low-intensity conflict).

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians across different areas of Tangaza LGA (Sokoto). The assailants were enforcing strange laws on the residents, collected zakat (alms) and flogged defaulters. The sum of 500 naira was collected as levy for cows and 200 for rams from households that own livestock.
On 1 December 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed three vigilantes in an ambush on the outskirts of Kankara (Kankara, Katsina).
On 2 December 2023, a Sokoto militia killed five residents when they attacked Kojiyo ward (Goronyo, Sokoto). Many other residents were abducted.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian military and local vigilantes repelled an attack launched by the Katsina militia on Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). The group invaded the village, aiming at abducting people from five houses. There were no fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, a Niger militia attacked commuters between Luma and Babanna villages (Borgu, Niger), the bus driver was killed and at least eight passengers were abducted. A ransom of 17 million naira was demanded for the abductees.
On 2 December 2023, the Sokoto militia attacked and injured one person in the Atakwanyo community (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). They abducted three others.
On 2 December 2023, a Kaduna militia killed an off-duty soldier and abducted eleven residents of Anguwan Tudu in Azzara coded to Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). One of the abductees was later released.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP when they invaded a vigilante post in Katarko (Gujba, Yobe). The vigilante had engaged them before the military reinforcement arrived. ISWAP fighters retreated and fled with gun wounds. Two vigilante members died in the clash, but ISWAP fatalities were unknown. 2 fatalities coded.

On 2 December 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops at a checkpoint between Jakana and Mainok, coded to Mainok (Kaga, Borno). Two ISWAP fighters were killed in the encounter, and other fighters escaped with gun wounds. a Nigerian soldier got injured in the clash. There were two fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian troops repelled the ISWAP attack at Charles One, along the Monguno- Maiduguri road, coded to Monghuno (Monguno, Borno). The militia came on two gun trucks and 20 motorcycles. There were no fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a student of the Gateway ICT Polytechnic at their off-campus hostel in the Larufi area of Ode-Remo (Remo North, Ogun). They injured many other students.

On 2 December 2023, an unidentified armed group of six abducted three workers on a poultry farm at Atoyo town in the Itele area (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The abductees were initially 5, before two of them were released by the abductors on the same day. 20 fowls were killed by the assailants while the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the attack.

On 2 December 2023, over 10 NSCDC operatives beat up and wounded a journalist in Awka (Awka South, Anambra) over unspecified reasons. The victim claimed that the assailants boasted about being untouchable over the attack.
On 3 December 2023, the Sokoto militia attacked Chaco or Chacho village (Wurno, Sokoto). The militia injured one person and abducted twelve others. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen and hunters who invaded their hideout in an armed clash around Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa).Two members of the group were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, four rifles and 92 rounds of live ammunition were recovered.

On 3 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two landlords from their houses at Asokoro extension, coded to Asokoro (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victims were abducted around 11pm and a ransom of 20 million was demanded for their release.
On 3 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army checkpoint in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). The soldiers were forced to abandon the post and retreated. There were no fatalities.
On 3 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have shelled the Nigerian Army base with five mortars in Waijroko (Damboa, Borno). No damage claim was made. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2023, DSS officials clashed with NSCDC officials and private security guards at a hospital in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The clash was over a disagreement over a DSS official who was brought in sick. An unspecified number of NSCDC and private guards were wounded.

On 4 December 2023, Icelanders loyal to General Danger abducted and later killed three civilians at Egbe community, coded to Akinima (Ahoada West, Rivers). The victims' whose bodies were found a few hours after they were abducted had an altercation with the mother of the militia leader, and he threatened to deal with them.
On 4 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and wounded some residents in Gandu (Lafia, Nasarawa). They abducted many others. The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 4 December 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists belonging to a local defense militia killed 33 civilians, 10 in Ganpeto, 21 in Garbatau and 2 others in Hawan Mata villages in Bali LGA (Taraba). Many cows were rustled and up to 30 motorcycles belonging to the victims were stolen while other pastoralists fled to Adamawa state. Other sources report that the assailants disguised in the regalia of the local defense militia.

On 4 December 2023, NDLEA operatives were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group that blocked the road in an attempt to prevent the operatives from gaining access into Opuje community (Owan West, Edo) where a warehouse containing marijuana was located. Three operatives were wounded including one who sustained head injuries in a clash that lasted for two hours, their operational vehicles were riddled with bullets. At least three suspects were arrested.
On 4 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a minibus, killed the driver and abducted 8 people along the axis Luma-Babana, coded to Babanna (Borgu, Niger).

On 4 December 2023, the MNJTF troops of 242 Battalion cleared ISWAP enclaves in Ngurnoa, Gumnari, Nairawa and engaged the militia in a firefight in Amburam village, coded to Gunmari (Monguno, Borno). They killed five ISWAP fighters, and one Nigerian soldier got injured in the clash. They recovered 1 x GPMG and 4 x AK 47 magazines.

On 4 December 2023, the Nigerian police engaged ISWAP in a firefight at a police checkpoint in Mairari, coded to Konduga (Konduga, Borno). The militia invaded the checkpoint, but the police repelled them. They damaged the Police Armored Personnel Carrier and went away with two police rifles. There were no fatalities.

On 4 December 2023, policemen raided the hideout of ESN militants led by Ebube Virus and Ishaka and engaged them in an armed clash at Umuogu Amuzu, coded as Umuogu (Aboh Mbaise, Imo). One militant who was second in command to Ebube Virus was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, one rifle and 19 rounds of live ammunition were recovered.

On 4 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the house of a local traditional chief of Gujba in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Borno). They engaged in a firefight with the Chief's guards and overpowered them. They burned the house and seized five rifles. There were no fatalities.
On 4 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a CJTF member in a firefight near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). They attacked the CJTF patrol and overpowered them, forcing them to retreat.
On 5 December 2023, a Sokoto militia killed two civilians, wounded 24 others and an unspecified number of people when they invaded Rarah town (Rabah, Sokoto).

On 5 December 2023, the Nigerian soldiers, CJTF and local hunters repelled Boko Haram (JAS) and engaged them in a firefight when attempting to invade a Fulani settlement near Malari neighborhood of Konduga (Konduga, Borno). One man, likely to be a bystander, was shot and wounded. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2023, the Ambazonian invaded Belegete, also spelled Balegeta (Obanliku, Cross River) and attacked the residents. Many people sustained various injuries, including cutlass cuts. The militia opened fire sporadically and abducted some residents. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2023, a policeman shot and wounded a civilian at a stop and search checkpoint in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta) for unclear reasons. The victim who is a teenager was taken to the hospital while the policeman was arrested.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked and injured an unspecified number of Nigerian troops during a patrol between Mallam Fatori and Baga, coded to Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). They forced the troops to retreat and seized a rifle. There were no fatalities.
On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a soldier when they attacked Nigerian Army checkpoint in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). They injured another soldier and forced others to retreat.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a Nigerian soldier when they attacked the Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Borno). The onslaught forced the soldiers to retreat, and the militia seized a rifle.
On 5 December 2023, the Katsina militia attacked Gago village in Dutsin Ma LGA, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). They injured one person and abducted another.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed a machine gun attack on the Nigerian troops, but another source reported that they shot at some travelers (rather than the military) around Limankara (Gwoza, Borno). The militia retreated, and the passengers arrived safely in Maiduguri. There were no fatalities.
On 6 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a mechanic and abducted his wife and daughters in Gandu village (Lafia, Nasarawa).
On 6 December 2023, the Katsina militia killed the headmaster of the Maidabino Primary school, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 6 December 2023, the Zamfara militia attacked the Tofa Ruwan Magami community near Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) for two consecutive days. They abducted three persons within the two days of raids. They later released one of the abductees to relay the demand of a two million naira ransom to the community.
On 6 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF and injured their members near Yamtage or Yamtaji (Gwoza, Borno). They outgunned them and forced them to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 6 December 2023, an unidentified armed group injured the personal assistant of the Nasarawa State deputy governor while attempting to abduct him in the Tudun Kauri area of Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The victim escaped abduction and was taken to the hospital for treatment of his minor injuries.
Around 6 December 2023 (as reported), soldiers killed three suspected informants of a Kaduna militia at Kohoto, coded to nearby Janjala (Kagarko, Kaduna). Six other suspects were arrested.

On 7 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed a militiaman during a fire exchange with the Zamfara militia in Faru, Faru Magami ward, location coded to known village on the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). The troop acted on the information of the impending destruction of farms in the village and responded swiftly. Many of the militiamen escaped with gun wounds. There was one fatality.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman along Omuawa and Ubima road, coded to Ubima (Ikwerre, Rivers). The armed group ambushed the woman, dragged her out of her car and took her away. They left her car behind.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at the bus conveying the Sunshine Stars Football Club of Akure along the Benin-Ore Expressway, coded to Ore (Odigbo, Ondo). The gunshots injured a team official and team members. The team was travelling to Benin for a football event when the incident occurred. There were no fatalities.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted ten students of the Federal University of Lafia at their off-campus hostel in Gandu village (Lafia, Nasarawa). The armed group fired sporadically in the air before taking the students away. Other students later protested against the incessant abduction of their colleagues, coded separately. The abductees were released on 10 December, sources report that 7 to 8 students were released.
On 7 December 2023, the Sokoto militia abducted six people (four women and two men) from Bijeje village (Goronyo, Sokoto). No further details.

On 7 December 2023, the Ambazonian abducted about 30 people including the village head, some youths and women in Belegete or Balegeta (Obanliku, Cross River). The abduction followed the attack on the community by the militia on 5 December 2023, coded separately.

On 7 December 2023, the Zamfara militia, for the second day, attacked the Tofa Ruwan Magami community near Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). They abducted three persons in two days of the raid. They later released one of the abductees to relay the demand of a two million naira ransom to the community.

On 7 December 2023, the joint troops of Operation Hadarain Daji shot and killed two militiamen when they engaged the Zamfara militia in a firefight in Danjibga village (Tsafe, Zamfara). The clash thwarted the militia invasion of the village. Many of them escaped with bullet wounds, and the army recovered two AK-47 rifles, two magazines and one motorcycle. There were two fatalities.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group of up to 20 engaged policemen and a local defense militia in an armed clash at Kuchibiyi area in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). One defense militia member was shot and wounded in his hand, three civilians including a couple and one other person were abducted.

On 7 December 2023, the CJTF killed two ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters during a firefight along the Maiduguri-Mafa road, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). CJTF recovered two rifles and two motorcycles from the militia.

On 8 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man in Nsukwa (Aniocha South, Delta) and demanded a ransom of 5 million naira. The victim was rescued by policemen the following day (coded separately).

On 8 December 2023, the Nigerian military engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight in Birnin Yero (Igabi, Kaduna) after the militia raided the village and abducted eleven people. Two of the hostages were killed, and the military rescued nine others. The militia withdrew and fled the scene. There were two fatalities.

On 8 December 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians who were part of the eleven persons that they abducted from Anguwar Maharba and Dandami in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The other 9 abductees were rescued by troops who ambushed the militia [coded separately].

On 8 December 2023, troops of 1 Division ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash while on a clearance operation in the Kanzaure general area of Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The ambush followed a report that the troops received over the abduction of 11 civilians by the militia from Anguwar Maharba and Dandami villages. 9 of the abductees were rescued by the troops who also recovered weapons and ammunition. Casualties are unknown.

On 9 December 2023, policemen were engaged in armed clash with an unidentified armed group when they invaded their hideout in the bush at Egbudu-Akah (Aniocha South, Delta). The group fled and left an abductee behind, one member of the group was killed as a result of bullet wounds that he sustained.

On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one local defense militia member and wounded three others at Bakatumbe village in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). Four civilians were abducted by the assailants who shot sporadically during the raid, and fled towards Lukutu forest after.

On 9 December 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged the IPOB/ESN fighters in a firefight along the Orsumoghu-Ukpor Road, coded to Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). The troops recovered weapons, two handheld radios and pairs of police uniforms from the militia. There were no fatalities.
On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Kpambo Yache village (Ussa, Taraba). No further details.

On 9 December 2023, a Katsina militia engaged a joint security team comprised of soldiers, policemen and Katsina security watch corps operatives in an armed clash at Zakka forest (Safana, Katsina). The security team who were joined by the state governor and his convoy rescued an abductee. There were no fatalities.
On 9 December 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians at Tungun Tudu community near Asara (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). One person was killed, many others were wounded.

On 9 December 2023, some Nigerian soldiers tortured and wounded a police officer (off duty) around the Nigerian Army's 63 Brigade in Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta) over an allegation of wrong parking and refusal to comply with a soldier's directive. The victim was taken to a hospital for treatment.

On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted residents in Dei-Dei community (Abuja Municipal, FCT). 23 persons were initially abducted, 7 of them were rescued by a local defense militia who trailed the abductors, leading to their release.
On 9 December 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops around Malari, along Maiduguri-Konduga Road, Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Casualties unknown. No further details.

On 10 December 2023, a Kaduna militia were repelled by policemen who responded to a distress call and rescued a woman whom the militia abducted at Dogarawa (Sabon Gari, Kaduna). Casualties are unknown.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the aide of the traditional ruler of Akpabuyo LGA and abducted the ruler from his residence in Asin Ufot (Akpabuyo, Cross River) coded to Ikot Nakanda.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia and private security guards in an armed clash at a night club in Oba (Idemili South, Anambra) following the guards' and militia's resistance to the attempted abduction of the club owner by the group. Between 3 to 24 persons including security guards, defense militiamen and club goers were killed, the security guard who resisted the group's entry initially was decapacitated, his head and leg were cut off and taken away.
On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted another when raiding the Beti Giware community (Fufore, Adamawa). No further details.

On 10 December 2023, the Nigerian police engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight after the militia abducted a woman from her residence in the Sabon Gari area, Zaria (Zaria, Kaduna). The police rescued the hostage. There were no fatalities.

On 10 December 2023, a Katsina militia engaged policemen and operatives of the Katsina security watch corps in an armed clash at Kwari Mai Zurfi in Makera district (Dutsinma, Katsina) when the joint security team responded to a report that the militia had blocked the road. Three militiamen were killed and one Katsina security watch corps operative was wounded.

Around 10 December 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed many people in Kidandan community (Giwa, Kaduna) over their inability to meet up with the militia's demands. The militia stole from the residents, abducted an unspecified number of persons, other residents fled the area. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 10 December 2023, ISWAP claimed that they attacked a position of Civilian JTF operatives and engaged them in an armed clash at Chul (Askira Uba, Borno), forcing the operatives to withdraw. Casualties are unknown.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed four civilians and wounded an unspecified number of others when they attacked Dungwel community in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The house of the community's monarch was set ablaze with the occupants inside, until soldiers arrived and rescued them. Some sources report that the monarch escaped, others report that he was wounded in the attack.

On 10 December 2023, the Police engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight and killed three militiamen on the Dutsin Ma-Kankara highway, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia had blocked the highway and attacked the commuters before the Police were deployed there. There were three fatalities.
On 10 December 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 30 residents of Unguwan Liman in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically when they invaded the community.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and three of her children including a six-month old baby at Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors shot sporadically when they invaded the area, other sources report that 7 persons were abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands. Three abductees were released.

On 11 December 2023, soldiers in collaboration with policemen and a local defense militia raided the hideout of IPOB/ ESN militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). 1 militant was killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, ammunition, locally made hand grenades, police uniforms and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 11 December 2023, the Katsina militia abducted a woman and her baby in Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 11 December 2023, the Police engaged the Sokoto militia in an armed fight in Lugu village (Wurno, Sokoto). The Police intervened after the militia had killed two people in the village. One police officer was killed in the clash, and many militiamen escaped with gun wounds. There were three fatalities.

On 11 December 2023, a Niger and Zamfara militia led by Ali Kachalla and Dogo Gide engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash at Mangoro community (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The Nigerian Air Force provided air support to the ground troops, and killed 32 militiamen including Ali Kachalla, several others fled with gunshot wounds from the clash which lasted five hours.
On 11 December 2023, the Community Watch Corps and the vigilante group clashed with the Katsina militia in Kinfau, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). Two militiamen were killed.

On 22 December 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Sokoto militia in armed clashes at their hideouts in Saruwa Kubuta, Gundumi village and Bunwanga Gundumi forest in Isa LGA (Sokoto). On 22 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person and abducted seven others in Ketawa Birjingo, coded to Birjingo (Goronyo, Sokoto). There was one fatality.

On 23 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed three Kaduna militiamen at Maidaro in the Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered one AK-47 rifle, one AK-47 rifle magazine, one Dane gun and two motorcycles from the militia.

On 23 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed five Kaduna militiamen and destroyed their camps after a firefight in the Kidandan-Yadi general area of Birnin Gwari close to Dogara (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered 12 motorcycles.

On 23 December 2023, the Niger militia killed a Redeemed Christian Church pastor in Garam (Tafa, Niger). The militia abducted thirteen people, including a five-year-old son of the deceased pastor. Around 23 December 2023 (as reported), the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight a Katsinma militia in Yar Gamji (Batsari, Katsina). The police recovered two AK-47 rifles, two locally-made guns, and five AK-47 magazines. There were no fatalities.

On 23 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the traditional ruler of Akutara in Adani (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The police arrested eight suspects in connection with the killing of the monarch.

On 23 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured a man while trying to abduct his brother (a UN national staff) from their parents' residence in Achara Layout, Nkwo Nike (Enugu East, Enugu). On 23 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed two CJTF members near Kirenawa (Marte, Borno). No further details.
On 23 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed two ISWAP fighters in Wulgo (Ngala, Borno). Other militiamen were injured in the clash. There were two fatalities.
On 23 December 2023, ISWAP attacked a group of firewood traders at Alajiri in Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). The militiamen injured one of the traders.
On 23 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person and abducted fifteen others in El-Rufai Estate, Bwari (Bwari, FCT). No further details.

On 23 December 2023, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with the Niger militia and killed two at Madawaki in the Shiroro LGA, coded to Shiroro (Shiroro, Niger). On 23 December 2023, a Police officer shot and wounded a Nollywood actor in the neck at Iperu (Ikenne, Ogun). Another source reported that the police were trying to disperse some thugs surrounding the person he was attached to when he opened the fire, and the stray bullet hit the actor. The police officer fled the scene after the shooting but was later arrested. The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 23 December 2023, the Plateau militia shot and killed sixteen people in Mushu village in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). The attack took place at night when the villagers were already asleep. There were 16 fatalities.
Around 23 December 2023 (as reported), the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight with a Katsina militia and killed one in Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina).

On 23 December 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed a farmer and injured three others around Hambagda village (Gwoza, Borno). The farmers were fetching firewood when they were attacked. The militiamen left with two bicycles and four tricycles belonging to the farmers.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a former Vice Chairman of Yorro LGA in Dilla (Yorro, Taraba). The former chairman was abducted together with a businessman early in the morning in the village. No ransom has been demanded.

On 24 December 2023, the Plateau militia, in a coordinated attack, killed 17 persons in NTV, Hurum and Darawat in Barkin Ladi LGA, coded to Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). The militia also killed 79 others in Bokkos LGA on the same night, coded separately. They burned down over two hundred houses, twenty-seven motorcycles and eight motor vehicles. Other sources reported over 150 persons were killed in all the attacks. seventeen fatalities coded.

On 24 December 2023, a suspected cult group shot and killed three worshippers at the Immaculate Conception Catholic Church in Nkwagu (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The militia invaded the church while a priest was celebrating a vigil mass service. They also injured many others. The killing was the second in the area in recent times after the cult-related clashes led to the killing of a student, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

Around 24 December 2023 (between 23 - 25 December), the Zamfara militia abducted about 20 farmers in Madaci near Yargeda (Bakura, Zamfara). The abduction was a reaction to the military invasion and displacement of the militiamen from their camps.

Around 24 December 2023 (between 23 - 25 December), the Zamfara militia abducted eleven people in Birnin Tudu (Bakura, Zamfara). The abduction was a reaction to the military invasion and displacement of the militiamen from their camps.
On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of people from a commercial bus around Ejule (Ofu, Kogi). No further details.

On 24 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed a member of the Kaduna militia in an ambush at Kwanar Batero, Birni Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered one AK-47 rifle, one magazine, five rounds of 7.62 mm, three motorcycles and one Baofeng radio.

On 24 December 2023, a police officer shot one of his colleagues in the back after the victim arrested a cult kingpin during an operation in Ikponwosa/Egban community, coded to Egor (Egor, Edo). The attacker escaped with his rifle.

On 24 December 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted a pastor and injured his wife in Matuak Rimi, coded to Kaura (Kaura, Kaduna). The militia demanded a 5 million naira ransom but later reduced it to 1 million naira.

On 24 December 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed eight traders and abducted two near Kukar Babangida village in Jibia LGA, coded to Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). The militia shot at the vehicle, conveying the traders returning from Jibia weekly market. Four passengers were severely wounded.

On 24 December 2023, the Zamfara militia waylaid some motorists and abducted several people on the Gusau-Sokoto highway, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia burned down a vehicle during the raid.

Around 24 December 2023 (between 23 - 25 December), the joint security team, involving the police, DSS and hunters, engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Tukuba Forest, Tukuba (Kuje, Federal Capital Territory). On 24 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed twelve people and abducted three women in Kurya village (Rabah, Sokoto). On 24 December 2023, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with the Sokoto militia in Kurya village (Rabah, Sokoto). The military intervened after the militia had killed twelve people and abducted others from the village, coded separately. The militia suffered heavy losses but went away with the bodies of their members. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted twenty-five passengers along the Ofante-Emodu-Unyi Ogugu Road in Ofante (Olamaboro, Kogi). The armed group dressed in military uniforms blocked the highway during the abduction.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded three people attempting to escape abduction in Tokulo (Bwari, Federal Capital Territory). The armed group abducted six others. The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 24 December 2023, the Plateau militia, in a coordinated attack, killed 79 persons in Ndun, Ngyong, Murfet, Makundary, Tamiso, Chiang, Tahore, Gawarba, Dares, Meyenga, Darwat and Butura Kampani village in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). The militia also killed 17 others in Barkin Ladi LGA on the same night, coded separately. The militia burned down over two hundred houses, twenty-seven motorcycles and eight motor vehicles. Other sources reported over 150 persons were killed in all the attacks. Seventy-nine fatalities coded.

On 24 December 2023, a clash between suspected Eiye and Black Axe cult groups resulted in the killing of a journalist, the head of a vigilante group and another person at different locations in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). There were three fatalities.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a truck driver in his house in Etiti village in Enugwu-Agidi, coded to Enugu-Ukwu (Njikoka, Anambra). The armed group released their hostage on 26 December 2023 and dumped him by the roadside. No ransom payment was reported.

On 25 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a youth leader and abducted four others in the Nde Three Corners community, also known as Nde 3 (Ikom, Cross River). They dragged the body of their victim into the bush and proceeded to shoot and wounded two other people who were returning from the farm.
Around 25 December 2023 (as reported), a suspected cult group shot and killed a student in Nkwagu (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). No further details.

On 25 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted seven farmers in Yarkofoji (Bakura, Zamfara). The abduction was a reaction to the military invasion and displacement of the militiamen from their camps.

On 25 December 2023, the Guyik and Daklam communities clashed in Jakusko (Jakusko, Yobe) over the control and ownership of a river bordering the two communities. An unspecified number of people were injured. There were no fatalities.

On 25 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a pregnant woman in Ijebu-Igbo community (Ijebu North, Ogun). They seized the woman and the husband in front of their house but left her husband behind; the police rescued the hostage the following day.
On 25 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base with seven mortar shells in Waijroko (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 25 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed 1 person in Warankai village (Goronyo, Sokoto). The militia also injured one person and abducted four others.

On 25 December 2023, a security guard of a private company shot and killed a man in Elele Alimini (Emohua, Rivers). The victim was returning from the farm when the guard shot and killed him. On 25 December 2023, the suspected Boko Haram militants (JAS) shot and killed two people in the Kwapre community, also called Kopre (Hong, Adamawa). On 26 December 2023, a Nigerian soldier beat a truck driver to death for refusing to bribe him at a checkpoint crossing along the Dikwa-Gamboru Ngala road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The Nigerian Army arrested the soldier.

On 26 December 2023, the police, in conjunction with a local hunter group, engaged a Bauchi militia in a firefight and killed six militiamen in Ningi LGA, coded to Ningi (Ningi, Bauchi). On 26 December 2023, suspected pastoralists killed a man at a village in Logo LGA, coded to Ugba (Logo, Benue). The militia also abducted their victim's parents. No further details.

On 26 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of travelers, including a groom and his family members, along the Lokoja- Abuja Road, Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). On 26 December 2023, the Katsina militia opened fire at the Community Watch Corps' vehicle in an ambush around Dutse na Tara, Faskari LGA, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). Two of the Corps died instantly, and two others died at the hospital. There were four fatalities.
On 26 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person for resisting abduction in Sakamaru (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia attacked and injured another.

On 27 December 2023, about 50 members of an unidentified armed group abducted many traders after raiding a market in Gongon Maliki (Yorro, Taraba). On 27 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a lecturer at the Nasarawa State University after raiding his house in Old Barracks, Kokouna (Kokona, Nasarawa). On 27 December 2023, an unidentified armed group raped a 14-year old girl at Elekahia (Port Harcourt, Rivers) and threatened to kill her if she reported the incident.

On 27 December 2023, ISWAP fighters engaged in a firefight with the Nigerian military in Kwada village (Chibok, Borno). The militiamen shot and injured four soldiers and burned one armored personnel carrier. They seized a gun truck from the military. There were no fatalities.

On 27 December 2023, the Zamfara militia ambushed some commuters and abducted seven along the Federal highway in Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). On 27 December 2023, the Kaduna militia shot and killed two villagers in Fina village, under Gwada ward, Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). On 27 December 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted an off-duty Air Force officer, his wife, and a teenager who was visiting them from their residence in Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). The soldier's wife is an ophthalmologist at the eye center, and a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded. Only the officer was released on 8 March after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom. The female medical doctor and her nephew were released on 30 October 2024 after a series of protests by the Association of Resident Doctors.

On 27 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and injured a woman and her baby in the Chimola community (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia fired shots indiscriminately, and the stray bullets hit the victims. There were no fatalities.

On 28 December 2023, the police, in conjunction with the vigilante group, engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in the forest at Ogba village, Nasarawa Egon (Nasarawa Eggon, Nasarawa). The police were on the trail of an abducted University lecturer when they clashed with the armed group. They rescued the hostage and took him to the hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 21 travelers along Ajaokuta - Itobe road (Ajaokuta, Kogi) and took them into a forest in Ajaokuta. The abductees were rescued by security operatives and local defense militia men on 30 December [coded separately], some of the abductors were also arrested. Other sources report that 24 abductees were rescued.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group that was fleeing from the police killed two civilians at Wulko community (Nasarawa Eggon, Nassarawa) coded to Nasarawa Egon. The group had abducted a lecturer [coded separately] and had police forces on their trail after their hideout was discovered.

On 28 December 2023, a suspected cult group attacked and stabbed one member of the Amotekun Corps with a knife at the entrance of the Osun State Polytechnic, Iree (Boripe, Osun). On 28 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person in the Basana Community, coded to Gada (Gada, Sokoto). They also abducted an unspecified number of people from the community.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted eighteen people from Kuduru village (Bwari, Federal Capital Territory). On 28 December 2023, ISWAP fighters, armed with anti-aircraft guns, invaded the Mobile Police Base in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 28 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person in the Mallamawa community (Goronyo, Sokoto). No further details.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Chris Uba's convoy (a politician) and killed two of his police escorts in Uga junction, Aguata (Aguata, Anambra). The police recovered a Lexus SUV used by the armed group and defused an IED found therein. They also recovered an AK-47 rifle belonging to a dead officer. There were two fatalities.

On 29 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted six women in Mallamawa (Maru, Zamfara). The raid was a result of the accusation that the community men were joining the state security outfit to combat the militia. They moved the hostages towards the Dajin Gwari forest for camping.

On 29 December 2023, the Nigerian police intercepted the Zamfara militiamen and engaged them in a firefight in the Sabon Garin Damba area of Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militiamen shot the hostage in the hand when they were outgunned by the police and escaped. The hostage was rescued and taken to the hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.
On 29 December 2023, the Niger militia shot and killed three people and abducted eight others in Azu village (Tafa, Niger). No further details.

On 29 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted seven women and a one-year-old infant in Barayar Zaki (Anka, Zamfara). The raid was a result of the accusation that the community men were joining the state security outfit to combat the militia. They moved the hostages towards the Dajin Gwari forest for camping.

On 29 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians at Lut village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau) when they went to pick up their stranded relatives who escaped the previous attack on the area [coded separately].
On 29 December 2023, a Fulani militia attacked partygoers in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and killed two people. Other people were wounded by the attackers

On 30 December 2023, police forces and a local defense militia engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group at their hideout within the Adogo axis (Ajaokuta, Kogi). 24 abductees were rescued and the abductors fled. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian from Jakpa road, coded to Warri (Warri South, Delta). The victim was sitting in a car which was also driven away by the abductors, he was later rescued by the police [coded separately].

On 30 December 2023, police forces invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Ekakpamre (Ughelli South, Delta). On 30 December 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked a checkpoint in Anka (Anka, Zamfara) and killed one NSCDC operative and a retired policeman who was working on a farm as its security officer. On 31 December 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded three civilians and abducted an unspecified number of others when they shot at travelers around Nde 3 Corners at Akparabong junction (Ikom, Cross River).

On 31 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a 70-year old man as he was on his way to church in Ijebu-Igbo (Ijebu North, Ogun). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded by the abductors.
On 31 December 2023, Nigerian troops killed an unspecified number of ISWAP fighters and captured two alive in Tumbulla, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 31 December 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Kwahaslalek village in Mangu LGA (Plateau), killed two civilians and wounded two others.

On 31 December 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed the commander of a local defense militia who is presumed to have been unarmed at a tricycle motor park in Ekoshodin near Benin City (Oredo, Edo).

On 31 December 2023, police forces raided the camp of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Ogboji (Orumba North, Anambra). On 1 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the council chairman of Akwanga LGA, his friend and two NSCDC operatives who were his security detail at Ningo village, coded as Anjoju (Akwanga, Nassarawa) as they were traveling along Akwanga - Andaha road. The NSCDC operatives were armed, but hid their guns from the abductors who did not notice them. On 1 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] dressed in military uniform attacked civilians at Tsiha, coded and spelled as Chiha (Chibok, Borno). Three persons were killed, one young lady was abducted by the militants who also attacked Gatamarwa village [coded separately].

On 1 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] dressed in military uniform attacked civilians at Gatamarwa ward, coded to Chiha (Chibok, Borno). Nine persons were killed, two others were wounded by the militants who proceeded to attack Chiha village [coded separately].

Around 2 January 2024 (as reported), a soldier killed two of his colleagues when he wrongly handled an artillery weapon during an operation around Molai area (Jere, Borno). Five others were wounded, the Army spokesperson denied that there were fatalities and stated that five persons were wounded.
On 2 January 2024, a Niger militia abducted three civilians from Garam community (Tafa, Niger). The victims were members of the same family.

On 2 January 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia attacked civilians at Ikem community in Okehi division (Etche, Rivers). Two persons were killed, fours others were wounded, some of them in critical condition. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 January 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists shot one person whom they abducted with seven others around the Port Harcourt International Airport Omagwa (Ikwerre, Rivers). Other sources report an unspecified number of wounded persons. Three abductees were rescued by the police who claimed to have mounted pressure on the abductors.

On 2 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Bang, Zamtip, and Gwantim villages, Wase LGA, coded to Wase (Wase, Plateau). The troop arrested four members of the armed group and recovered three motorcycles. There were no fatalities.
On 2 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) fighters shot and killed two loggers in Dure-wale, Dure (Gwoza, Borno). The victims had gone to fetch firewood when they were attacked.
On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted two others at Furaka community, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The abductees included one female and a male.

On 2 January 2024, a Zamfara militia who attempted to attack civilians were engaged in an armed clash with security operatives [coded as military forces] and a local defense militia at Nahuche (Bungudu, Zamfara). Six civilians were killed and one was wounded by the militia.

On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with police forces at Zuma community in Bwari (FCT). On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed the paramount ruler of Anwunugbokor community at his home in Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 3 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted three travelers on the Obiri-Ikwerre - Airport Road, coded to Port Harcourt International Airport (Ikwerre, Rivers). The armed group blocked the left flank of the highway and ambushed vehicles going and coming from the airport.

On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with the Zamfara militia while on a search and rescue operation at Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara) and Dandalla, coded separately. The troops rescued nine hostages while the militiamen fled after being outgunned. There were no fatalities.

On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with the Zamfara militia while on a search and rescue operation at Dandalla (Maru, Zamfara) and Dan Sadau, coded separately. The troops rescued nine hostages while the militiamen fled after being outgunned. There were no fatalities.

On 3 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person along Kaskara-Mangu Road in Barkin Ladi LGA, coded to Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). The Nigerian military rescued the hostage and arrested one of the abductors.

On 3 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed seven people in Nahuche (Bungudu, Zamfara). The militia invaded the community early in the morning, shot and killed the people and abducted scores of others.
On 3 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base with five mortar shells in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). No further details.

On 3 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed ten people in Kwanar Dutse village, Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara).
