On 29 January 2024, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Oriuzor community (Ezza South, Ebonyi) for the second day. One person was killed. three others were killed on the day before (coded separately). The police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the incident.

On 29 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji conducted clearance operations and engaged Zamfara militias in clashes at their hideouts in Rukudawa, Dumburum, Tsanu, Birnin Tsaba, Magare and Shamshusalle in Kiyawa LGA (Zamfara) and Zurmi LGA (coded separately). The militias fled, and their hideouts were destroyed including those belonging to a militia leader called Sule. There were no fatalities.

Around 29 January 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a lawyer whom they abducted together with his brother at Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). The victim was the PDP House of Representatives candidate for Ihiala federal constituency during the 2023 elections and the assailants accused him of writing petitions against them to the state government. His brother was released unhurt.

On 29 January 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and rescued nine out of the ten victims whom the group had abducted at the Ogere axis (Ikenne, Ogun) on 25 January (coded separately). One of the victims was killed during the clash, two others were injured and the rescued persons included the PDP chairman in Lagos state who was returning from Ibadan when he and others were abducted.
On 29 January 2024, a Kaduna militia wounded a man, and abducted his wife and their three children in Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). The man was wounded for resisting the attempt to abduct him.
On 29 January 2024, the Katsina militia abducted four people from Sabon Garin Bilbis, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). No further details.

On 29 January 2024, Ifon and Ilobu communal militias clashed following renewed hostilities related to a land dispute. 3 persons were killed and residents of both towns fled, the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the clash and the state governor imposed a 6am to 6pm curfew on the towns. Location coded to Ifon (Orolu, Osun).

On 29 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted 10 civilians comprising 6 school children, three teachers, and a driver from a private school as they were returning to Eporo from Emure (Emure, Ekiti). A ransom of 10 million naira each was demanded. The abductees were released on 4 February except the driver who was murdered (coded separately), there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 29 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two policemen and two civilians at Ohii junction along Owerri - Orlu highway (Mbaitoli, Imo). The assailants also robbed some POS operators of their money.

On 29 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji on patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along the Shinkafi - Isa road (Shinkafi, Zamfara) and rescued two travelers whom the militia had abducted. There were no fatalities.

On 30 January 2024, a local defense militia clashed with a Katsina militia at Dogon Marke village in Safana LGA (Katsina). The defense militia attempted to block the escape routes of the Katsina militia who were fleeing from an airstrike by the military, five of the defense militiamen were declared missing. Fatalities unknown.

On 30 January 2024, some police officers shot and wounded a Vigilante Commander and two members of the Idjerhe Kingdom's vigilante group in Jesse town (Ethiope West, Delta). The victims were admitted to the hospital for treatment. The police command ordered the arrest and detention of the police officers responsible for the shooting after the community protested, coded separately. There were no fatalities.

On 30 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed a man along the Gusau-Funtua highway, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militiamen indiscriminately shot at commuters when the victim was hit. There was one fatality.

On 30 January 2024, troops of 114 battalion of the Nigerian Army trailed an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Apawa village (Lau, Taraba), reported as Yorro LGA. The group fled and abandoned three abductees who had previously been abducted from Ardo Kola LGA. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 January 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians at Agojeju-Odo community in Bagaji Odo district (Omala, Kogi) as claimed by the lawmaker representing Omala constituency at the state house of assembly. Four civilians were killed, and the assailants who numbered over 150, invaded the community through Bugana town which borders Benue and Nasarawa states, shot sporadically when they arrived.
On 31 January 2024, a Sokoto militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others at Katalan Kaura village in Atakwanyo (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).

On 31 January 2024, two unidentified rival cult militias who were also students of Community Grammar School and Ikotun High School clashed at a school in Ikotun (Alimosho, Lagos). Police forces intervened and shot sporadically which resulted in a stampede that led to ten persons being hospitalized, an unspecified number of students were arrested and later released.

On 31 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two women from Kobi community, coded to nearby Guzape (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductees were rescued by security forces on the same day (coded separately).

On 31 January 2024, soldiers and policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash along the Nyanya - Keffi expressway (Abuja Municipal, FCT) where they mounted security checkpoints. Two women who were abducted from Kobi village were rescued (coded separately) after the abductors abandoned them and fled.

Around 31 January 2024 (between 26 January - 6 February), an unidentified armed group tortured the Deputy Vice Chancellor of Abia state university, whom they had abducted at a filling station in Umu Opara (Umuahia South, Abia). The victim was tortured and recorded, the videos were sent to his family to threaten them and hasten the payment of ransom. He was released on 6 February after the ransom was paid, location coded to where the victim was abducted from.

On 31 January 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed fifteen people in Ugboju, coded to Bagagi (Agatu, Benue). The attack triggered panic, and many people fled in disarray. The armed group also abducted an unspecified number of children.

Around 31 January 2024 (week of), an unidentified armed group killed a driver who was abducted together with school children and their teacher as they were heading to Eporo from Emure (Emure, Ekiti). The other abductees were released on 4 February, location coded to where the abduction took place.

On 31 January 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a police inspector after raiding his house in Afaha Ube within the Uyo metropolis (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). The militia, numbering over ten, invaded the police residence and shot fire sporadically to scare the residents away before killing the police officer. The militia cut off the victim's head, placed it beside his body, and fled. A source reported the killing could be a reprisal for the police action.

On 1 February 2024, the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group while on patrol along Ngbo-Effium axis, coded to Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). One police officer was shot dead, while the other was injured and was taken to the hospital for treatment. There was one fatality.

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians at Katapka and Okudu villages, coded to Umaish (Toto, Nassarawa). Properties worth millions of naira were destroyed by the assailants.
On 1 February 2024, Buccaneers and SEC also called Eiye confraternity clashed in Ijeja (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The leader of the Eiye confraternity was killed in the clash.

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two catholic priests from their parish at Pankshin (Pankshin, Plateau) and demanded a ransom of 25 million naira. The abductees were released a week later, two of the abductors were arrested in Ogun state and one of them was the priests' parishioner.

On 1 February 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed a commercial motorcycle rider and seized his motorcycle at Tashar Nadaya, near Gazari (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militia also shot a group of four individuals (assumed to be injured) and seized their motorcycles. There was one fatality.

On 1 February 2024, the community watch corps clashed with the Katsina militia, who abducted 30-55 women, including a bride, near Damari town (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militia had abducted wedding guests, escorting the bride to the groom. Three community watch corps members were killed, and an assistant driver sustained a gun injury. 10 women and 6 minors were rescued by the Nigerian army troops who were on patrol (there are no reports of a clash).

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Federal Housing Authority Director in his home in Pambara, Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The abductors escaped through the bush with the victim. The abductee was released around 12 June, 40 million naira, 7 motorcycles and food items were paid as ransom.

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a traditional ruler in Koro town (Ekiti, Kwara). The armed group invaded the palace and shot sporadically to scare the people away before shooting the monarch dead. They abducted the victim's wife and two others, a ransom of 40 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released on 5 February, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a woman and her granddaughter at their residence in Tudun Wada area of Daura town (Daura, Katsina). The younger woman's belly was ripped open and her organs were stolen, while her grandmother was strangled. Their bodies were discovered on 3 February.
On 2 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted two others in the Fier community (Pankshin, Plateau). There was one fatality.

On 2 February 2024, troops of 114 battalion engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Gampu hills and Ban Yorro area (Yorro, Taraba). The troops rescued four abductees after the group fled. No fatalities.

On 2 February 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed a Katsina Community Corps and seven others in Damari (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militiamen went away with the Corps motorcycle. There were eight fatalities.

On 2 February 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed three people in Ungwar Kela and two in Yan Bene in Kankara LGA, coded to Kankara (Kankara, Katsina). The militiamen, numbering about fifty, invaded the communities on motorcycles. They stole over 100 bags of rain from Ungwar Kela. There were five fatalities.

On 3 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed a man and stole two cows from his residence at Unguwar Yayyara village (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa. The victim was the father of a member of the Katsina Community Watch Corps.

On 3 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted about 14 passengers who were traveling in two buses along Inele - Eteke - Ogugu road (Olamaboro, Kogi). The driver of one of the buses was rescued by a joint team of policemen, hunters, and local defense militia, and a ransom of 15 million naira was demanded from one of the abductees. The abductees were released around 8 February, there are no reports on ransom payment. The spokesperson of the police in the state claimed that the combined efforts of security operatives led to their release.

On 3 February 2024, ISWAP militants attacked a police station and engaged the police forces in an armed clash at Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). Four policemen were killed, the militants set the police station ablaze and stole a cache of ammunition.
On 3 February 2024, the Nigerian troops shot and killed one ISWAP fighter near Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). No further details.
On 3 February 2024, the Nigerian troops fired shots toward the ISWAP location on sighting them around Kanama village near Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). There was no fatality.

On 3 February 2024, ISWAP fighters engaged the Nigerian troops in a firefight after the militia raided Banki town (Bama, Borno). The militiamen infiltrated the town through the 500-Housing Estate on Banki-Bama Road. They retreated after the confrontation with the Nigerian troops. There were no fatalities.

On 3 February 2024, an unidentified armed group with affiliation to a serving commissioner in Enugu state attacked supporters of a newly elected traditional ruler at Mburubu (Nkanu East, Enugu). The victims were stripped naked and their belongings were carted away, they claimed the assailants had warned them not attend the event honoring the monarch.

On 3 February 2024, an unidentified armed group stole a ballot box, BVAS machine, result sheet, and other electoral materials at polling unit 5, Ward 13 in Oyinmo (Akoko North East, Ondo). The national commissioner of INEC supervising Osun, Ondo, and Ogun claimed that the police overpowered the armed group and that normalcy was restored.

On 3 February 2024, an unidentified armed group in the company of some security operatives, coded as police forces, abducted INEC officials and stole a ballot box at Women Center ward in Rigacikun (Igabi, Kaduna).

On 4 February 2024, BNL militants (Black Marine faction) attacked and killed at least 17 members of a joint border patrol team comprised of Nigerian and Cameroonian forces, coded as military forces at Ugenghe, coded and spelled as Unyene (Mbo, Akwa Ibom).

On 4 February 2024, a Niger militia ambushed civilians and killed 6 farmers, four men and two women at Maganda junction, on Alawa - Pandogari road (Shiroro, Niger). 20 women were abducted, three other persons were injured, and two trucks filled with foodstuff were burnt.

Around 4 February 2024 (between 3 February - 5 February), an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Opaha (Otukpo, Benue) coded to Entekpa Ward, Umogidi, and Iwili (coded separately). At least seven persons were killed, split across three locations and coded as 2, and 17 others were declared missing. Some locals claimed that the assailants migrated from Agatu LGA.

Around 4 February 2024 (between 3 February - 5 February), an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Iwili (Otukpo, Benue), Umogidi, and Opaha (coded separately). At least seven persons were killed, split across three locations and coded as 2, and 17 others were declared missing. Some locals claimed that the assailants migrated from Agatu LGA.

On 4 February 2024, troops of 17 brigade of the Nigerian army engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Tsora Hill in Safana LGA (Katsina) after the air component of Operation Hadarin Daji targeted the militia's hideout in an airstrike. Several militiamen were killed, and their hideouts were cleared by the troops. Several fatalities coded as 10.

Around 4 February 2024 (between 3 February - 5 February), an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue), Iwili, and Opaha (coded separately). At least seven persons were killed, split across three locations and coded as 3, and 17 others were declared missing. Some locals claimed that the assailants migrated from Agatu LGA.

On 4 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted nine PDP members at Jattu (Etsako West, Edo) as they were en route to the party's ward meeting. The abductees were also electoral officers of the party. They were rescued by the police around 6 February.

On 4 February 2024, an unidentified cult militia engaged in an armed clash with Black Axe, also called Aiye confraternity and another unidentified cult militia at Lafenwa and Akinolugbade areas of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). 2 people were killed including Black Axe member was killed.
On 4 February 2024, SEC also called Eiye confraternity and Buccaneers clashed in Isabo area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). One Buccaneer member was killed.

On 4 February 2024, the Boko Haram (JAS) Bakura faction attacked ISWAP positions in Daban Gajere, Dabar Waya, Dabar Giwa, and Dawashi in Kukawa LGA, coded to Kukawa, Borno). There were unspecified fatalities. Unspecified fatalities coded as 10.
On 4 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed three people in Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). No further details.

On 4 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed one civilian, wounded another, and abducted an unspecified number of residents at Kasale community (Kankara, Katsina). The abductees included many women and children, while the house of the wounded victim was sacked and set ablaze.

On 4 February 2024, a junior military officer of Operation Hadarin Daji shot and killed a senior officer in Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). Other military officers shot and killed the assaulting officer. An unspecified number of soldiers were injured. There were two fatalities.

On 4 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants attacked the collation center where bye-election results were being collated by INEC at Kukareta (Damaturu, Yobe) and killed two persons. The house of the district head was also burnt by the militants, and three hunters whom he was hosting were abducted, other sources report that one mobile policeman was also killed (unclear if he was on duty).
On 4 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) abducted nine girls around Domma village, Gwoza LGA, coded to Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). No further details.

On 5 February 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a fisher whom they shot multiple times at Uwheru community (Ughelli North, Delta) following a clash (the kind of clash not specified). One other person was wounded.

On 5 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted about 40 locals including women and children from Dangunu (Muya, Niger) and Pai (coded separately). The abduction was in revenge of the killing of their leader and 38 others by military forces in the community about a month ago (coded separately).

On 5 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted about 40 locals including women and children from Pai (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa and Dangunu (coded separately). The abduction was in revenge of the killing of their leader and 38 others by military forces in the community about a month ago (coded separately).

On 5 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked a military camp and engaged soldiers and policemen in an armed clash at Dauran, coded to Dauran Birnin Tsaba (Zurmi, Zamfara). Two soldiers, one policeman, and several militiamen were killed while the militia fled with the corpses of their colleagues and left two. The militia attacked the camp in retaliation for the arrest of their colleague who was identified in the market the day before. Unknown fatalities coded as 10, coded 13 fatalities.

On 5 February 2024, a Police officer sexually harassed a 20-year-old female in Ago Iwoye, also spelt as Ago (Ijebu North, Ogun). The victim was forced into the police patrol van by seven other officers. The victim recorded the incident on her phone, but the perpetrator was not identified.
On 5 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person around the Infra Filling Station Junction, Enugu (Enugu, Enugu North). No further details.
On 5 February 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted a former LGA councilor in Dawashi Kwata village near Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). No further details.
On 5 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of people from two vehicles around Tatti village on Takum-Mararaba-Jalingo Road, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba).
On 5 February 2024, Katsina militia abducted two women from the Shagari Low-Cost Housing Estate, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.

On 5 February 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group led by Isa Dei-Dei in an armed clash after the police raided the group's hideout. The group's leader was killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds. Location coded to Dei-Dei (Abuja Municipal, FCT).

On 6 February 2024, suspected armed pastoralists killed a man and burnt his body on his farm in Ogidi-Kabba (Ijumu, Kogi). The victim was also a chief, whose title was Elepe of Ohi-Ogidi, his corpse was found following a search after he did not return home from the farm, and there were traces of the presence of cows on the farm.

On 6 February 2024, the Nigerian military clashed with the Kaduna militia and killed four in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Other militiamen escaped with gunshot injuries. The military recovered three AK 47 rifles, seven AK 47 rifle magazines and two motorcycles. There were four fatalities.

On 6 February 2024, the Niger militia abducted eleven people from Masuku (Shiroro, Niger). The military rescued the hostages after they intercepted the militia in Kwaga village in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded separately.
On 6 February 2024, Katsina militia abducted three people gathering firewood in Dakwaro, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). No further details.

On 6 February 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers and a local defense militia who were on patrol in Katapka community (Toto, Nassarawa). Three soldiers and two members of the group were killed.

On 6 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two people from Pyakassa Estate, Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The armed group broke into the residences and took away the two hostages. One was an INGO employee, and the other was a Federal Ministry of Defence staff member.
On 6 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted six people from a vehicle around Manya village on Takum- Mararaba- Jalingo Road, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba).

On 6 February 2024, soldiers attacked policemen at their camp in Sabon Gari area of Mangu (Mangu, Plateau). An unspecified number of policemen were wounded, and they claimed that the attack was unprovoked.
On 6 February 2024, Katsina militia abducted a university lecturer, his wife and two children along Kankara-Sheme Road, coded to Kankara (Kankara, Katsina).

On 7 February 2024, the Nigerian Military intercepted a Kaduna militia and engaged in a firefight in Kwaga (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia were intercepted while trying to move eleven hostages via Kwaga. The militia abandoned their hostages and fled after being outgunned by the Military. The Military rescued the eleven hostages. There were no fatalities.
On 7 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) killed one person in Lokodisa village, also called Lokodisa Adamu (Gwoza, Borno). No further details.

On 7 February 2024, the Aye cult militiamen, also known as the Black Axe, shot and killed three members of the Eye confraternity in Ikoti, Ifofin and Omiayo areas of Ilesa (Ilesha West, Osun). The Eye confraternity, in retaliation, shot and killed three Aye members the following day, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 7 February 2024, Zamfara militia shot and killed three people and wounded one other while raiding two villages in Kungurki ward, coded to Kungurki (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). They abducted an unspecified number of people. There were three fatalities.

On 7 February 2024, the Nigerian military engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight while raiding their hideouts in Dan Ali (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and Yan Tumaki forests, coded separately. The troops rescued eighteen female hostages in the two operations and handed them over to the State Government. There were no fatalities.

On 7 February 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight while raiding their hideouts in Yan Tumaki (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and Dan Ali forests, coded separately. The troops rescued eighteen female hostages in the two operations and handed them over to the State Government. There were no fatalities.

On 7 February 2024, an unidentified armed group clashed with vigilante members after killing two people in the Alagemo community, Ikorodu (Ikorodu, Lagos). They abducted a woman and injured four vigilante members. There were two fatalities.

Around 8 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group member suspected to be an abductor along the Ikere-Igbara Odo Ekiti, coded to Ikere (Ikere, Ekiti). The military recovered a mobile phone, fabricated gun, torchlight, dagger, and charms. There were no fatalities.

On 8 February 2024, the Katsina militia abducted sixteen people while raiding Kogo, also called Birnin Kogo (Faskari, Katsina). The militia stealthily infiltrated the community and took the hostages away, including children, women and men.

On 8 February 2024, the Nigerian police engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight at their hideout along Keffi-Gidan Wire Road near Gitata (Karu, Nassarawa). The police killed an unspecified number of the armed group and recovered four AK47 rifles and a bag of ammunition. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 8 February 2024, the Eye confraternity shot and killed three Aye militiamen, also known as the Black Axe, on a farm in Osu (Atakumosa West, Osun). The onslaught was to avenge the killing of their members the previous day, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 8 February 2024, an unidentified armed group slaughtered (by unspecified means) a 16-year-old Fulani herder in Tegway village, coded to Bassa (Bassa, Plateau). The victim was rearing cattle in the area when he was killed. The military recovered his body from the riverside, where the assailants placed a stone on him. There was one fatality.

On 8 February 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists shot and killed two people before engaging the military in a firefight in Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue). The attackers injured many others and threatened to return to the village. There were two fatalities.

On 8 February 2024, the vigilantes and the Shila Boys clashed in Jimeta (Girei, Adamawa) when the cult group invaded a school to vent their anger over the arrest of one of their members by the vigilante. The group, armed with knives and daggers, assaulted teachers and vandalized cars. A source reported that the cult group stabbed the vigilante, but the knife didn't penetrate him. He then took the knife and stabbed a cult member to death.
On 8 February 2024, a Police officer sexually harassed a detained woman in the police station around Ago Iwoye, also spelt as Ago (Ijebu North, Ogun).

Around 8 February 2024 (as reported), the security operatives, coded as the police and the vigilante, engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group in Jedo estate, Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The firefight occurred when the armed group abducted a man, and the security agencies attempted to rescue him. The hostage sustained a gunshot wound and was taken away by the abductors. There were no fatalities.

Around 9 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian police clashed with an unidentified armed group and killed one in Gamu Hill, Gamu (Ganye, Adamawa). The armed group had been attacking and abducting people in Jada and Ganye LGA. The police recovered one AK-47 rifle. There was one fatality.

Around 9 February 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted two people from Tudun Wada (Michika, Adamawa). The police, in collaboration with the Nigerian military, arrested the suspect on 8 February 2024.

On 9 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the driver of a bus and abducted an unspecified number of passengers along the Akunu Akoko and Iyere road, coded to Akunnu (Akoko North East, Ondo). One girl was abandoned on the bus.
On 9 February 2024, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash at Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). One person was killed in the clash.

On 9 February 2024, Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP fighters in a firefight at a farm in Koshere village along the Pulka-Firgi Road, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). Two people were killed during the clash.

On 9 February 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at their hideout around Mpape (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The group, led by Musa Wada Magaji was active around the Mpape area, several members of the group including the leader were killed in the clash and one police operative was wounded. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 10 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed four pastoralists and dumped their bodies at Ilobi (Egbado South, Ogun) after they were abducted from Oke Irinja. Five of them were abducted when the assailants claimed that a local chief summoned the victims and offered to take them there. Their cows and other belongings were not stolen, the corpses had ropes around their necks and their hands were tied.

On 10 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted five Fulani pastoralists in Oke Irinja, Owode Yewa, also called Owode (Egbado South, Ogun). They killed four of the hostages, but one escaped. There were four fatalities.
On 10 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight in Mafa town (Mafa, Borno). No further details.
On 10 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a lawyer along Okigwe - Uturu road (Okigwe, Imo) coded to Okigwi. The victim was headed to Uturu where he was based.

Around 10 February 2024 (as reported), Cameroonian troops clashed with ISWAP around Banki (Bama, Borno). ISWAP fighters fled and abandoned a Hilux vehicle with an IED, which the military later set on fire. There were no fatalities.
On 10 February 2024, the Katsina militia killed six people and injured three others in Kurechin Dutse village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). There were six fatalities.

On 10 February 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Gwada village, Igabi LGA (Kaduna) and killed three persons. Seven others were wounded and 32 were abducted. 10 motorcycles, 25 cattle, and 350 sheep were stolen, and one bus laden with foodstuff was burnt.

Around 10 February 2024 (as reported), an unidentified militia abducted a couple and their daughters as they were traveling from Katsina to Sokoto and demanded for 10 million naira as ransom. Location coded to Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto).

On 10 February 2024, the Amotekun and armed Fulani Pastoralists clashed in Kajola (Atakumosa East, Osun). Amotekun corps had intervened after some farmers reported Fulani were destroying their crops to feed their cattle. On sighting the Corps, the Fulani opened fire, and Amotekun responded, injuring three Amotekun members and some Fulani pastoralists. There were no fatalities.

On 10 February 2024, members of the Zamfara state community protection guards killed a man whom they tortured to death after he honored their invitation in Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). The victim's brother and son were detained when they went to retrieve his phone as claimed by his political associate. The state government claimed that the death was as a result of an altercation between two factions of a local defense militia.

On 10 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian at Nkienzha village in Miango district (Bassa, Plateau). The Irigwe Development Association claimed that the assailants were armed pastoralists, but GAFDAN denied the claim. The attackers also killed two others the following day in the same location (coded separately).

On 11 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed one civilian when they invaded Goda village in Kurfi LGA (Katsina). Several houses including one belonging to a local defense militia member were set ablaze.
On 11 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted and later killed one person in Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). There was one fatality.
On 11 February 2024, the Katsina militia killed one person when attacking Kandawa village (Batsari, Katsina). They set a police van on fire. There was one fatality.

On 11 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked traders along the highway as they were returning from Jibia (Jibia, Katsina) weekly market. 9 persons were killed, one was declared missing and it is unclear if he was killed or abducted. An unspecified number of victims were abducted or wounded.

On 11 February 2024, the Zamfara militia blocked the road and attacked some commuters along the Abare-Anka Road, coded to Anka (Anka, Zamfara). They injured a motorcyclist and went away with three motorcycles, phones and money. There were no fatalities.

On 11 February 2024, Nigerian troops, a local defence militia and the Community Watch engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight at their hideout in Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). The troop killed at least fifteen militiamen and arrested one. They rescued three hostages.
On 11 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked Daudawa neighborhood (Faskari, Katsina). A man and his two wives were abducted, three of their cows were stolen, their house was ransacked.

On 11 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Nkienzha village in Miango district (Bassa, Plateau). The Irigwe Development Association claimed that the assailants were armed pastoralists, but GAFDAN denied the claim. Other sources report that three persons were killed and two others were injured.

On 12 February 2024, over 200 vigilantes and community members clashed with the Zamfara militia in Kanoma (Maru, Zamfara). The communal group had mobilized men from different villages to confront the militiamen in their camp in Dangulbi forest. The militiamen killed over sixty vigilante and community members, and many others were injured. There were sixty fatalities.

On 12 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured a commercial motorcycle rider in Tudun Wus, Dass LGA, coded to Dass (Dass, Bauchi). They went away with his motorbike. No further details.
On 12 February 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed eight people in Kwabre village, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). One person was injured during the attack. There were eight fatalities.
On 12 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and injured three traders conveying goods on camels along the Dukamaje- Gada Road, coded to Gada (Gada, Sokoto). They rustled ten camels.

On 12 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured the Adamawa State Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources Development in his residence in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The armed group went away with a Hilux van.

On 12 February 2024, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants killed a policeman when they attacked the Okigwe correctional center in Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo). The militants freed seven inmates and abducted the officer in charge of the center. IPOB denied involvement in the attack and claimed that the police is aware of the actual perpetrators.

On 12 February 2024, ISWAP, on motorcycles, attacked the Nigerian troops in Azir, also spelt Ajir (Damboa, Borno). The troops repelled the attack and engaged in a firefight with the militia. ISWAP fighters retreated and fled back to the forest. There were no fatalities.

On 12 February 2024, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants killed a policeman who was attached to a serving senator at the senator's residence in Umualumuoke (Okigwe, Imo). The senator was not at home when the militants arrived. IPOB denied involvement in the attack and claimed that the police is aware of the actual perpetrators.

On 13 February 2024, suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Gurjaji village, coded and spelled as Gurjia (Fika, Yobe) with bows and arrows. One person was killed, another was seriously wounded and most of the village was razed by the assailants. The residents were displaced to neighboring communities, other sources report that there were no fatalities and the attack was a reprisal after the villagers denied the pastoralists entry because they had destroyed their watermelon farms.

On 13 February 2024, Sokoto Community Guards Corps operatives killed Fulani locals in Kaffe market (Gada, Sokoto) after they accused them of being linked with militias operating in the area. The victims were slaughtered before a crowd in the market.
On 13 February 2024, about six members of Kebbi militia abducted one person from Kwanar Jwara village, coded to Suru (Suru, Kebbi). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and injured three miners when attacking a gold processing site in Abare village (Anka, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, ISWAP attacked Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight in Mairamri village, also spelt as Mairami (Konduga, Borno). No further details.

On 13 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked a police station where they killed two policemen and abducted 40 residents in Kasuwar Daji village, Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). The assailants attacked the house to which the police station was attached and 21 of the abductees were residents of the house and members of the same family. Other sources report 4 fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, IS/BH fighters abducted three people from Kukawa town (Kukawa, Borno). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted a village head and many residents from Tsabre village (Isa, Sokoto). No further details.

On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia opened fire indiscriminately at a truck along the Gusau-Kaura Namoda Road, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Four people sustained gunshot injuries. There were no fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, the Katsina militia killed three people when attacking Kan Biri village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia attacked Janhu village, coded to Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian Army and killed two soldiers at a checkpoint in Kanama (Yunusari, Yobe). No further details.

On 14 February 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists killed three people while attacking three communities, including Bulama Bukar village near Gujba town (Gujba, Borno). They razed many houses. They fled on sighting the military deployed to the area. There were three fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists, in a renewed attack, killed four people in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). They raided the community at night when the people were already asleep. One man was injured. There were four fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, the police and vigilantes engaged the Sokoto militia in a firefight on the outskirts of Gigani village (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia had shot a boy in his leg when the victim was fetching water from a well, and the police responded. The police killed one of the militiamen in the encounter and recovered a GPMG Rifle with six live ammunition. There was one fatality.

On 14 February 2024, the Nigerian police exchanged gunfire with the Viking cult militiamen while attacking their hideout in the Mbieri community (Mbaitoli, Imo). A militia member suffered gunshot injuries on his leg and was arrested alongside three others, including their leader. The police recovered two locally made revolvers, shotguns, five rounds of live cartridges, military camouflage shorts and face masks. There were no fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, the Katsina militia invaded a mosque and opened fire on the worshippers in Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina). The Muslims were observing the late-night prayer (Ishai) when they were shot. The militia killed two worshippers inside the mosque, and the third was butchered outside the mosque for resisting abduction. Four people sustained injuries. They abducted a man and two women. There were three fatalities.
Around 15 February 2024 (as reported), the Sokoto militia abducted three men from Gedawa (Wamakko, Sokoto). The victims paid ten million naira each to regain their freedom.

On 15 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked the Delta State Polytechnic raped two female students and shot a male student in the leg at their off-campus hostel in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed several people in the Adijah community in Ugbokpo (Apa, Benue). They opened fire on the residents in broad daylight, triggering panic among the residents who fled to neighboring villages. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 15 February 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed seven people in Nasarawa Godel in Birnin Magaji / Kiyawa LGA, Nasarawa Godel (Kiyawa, Zamfara). The militiamen invaded the community in Toyota Hilux vans. They abducted twenty other people, mostly women. There were seven fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, the Nigerian police clashed with a Kaduna militia trying to abduct some commuters along the Tumburku-Galadimawa Road, coded to Galadimawa (Giwa, Kaduna). The militiamen in large numbers, had blocked the road before the police engaged them. They fled into the bush with gun wounds. The police recovered an AK47 rifle, three AK47 magazines, five rounds of 7.62 x 39mm live ammunition, a Techno mobile phone and two Bajaj motorcycles. There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group while raiding their hideouts between Nasarawa State and the Kuje LGA, coded to Kuje (Kuje, FCT). The police arrested one member of the group and rescued two hostages. There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, a Naval officer shot and killed a man at a military checkpoint at Owerri-Nta (Isiala Ngwa South, Abia) after he refused to stop at the checkpoint. The Navy claimed that the victim was shot because he was struggling for a gun with the soldier after he was invited over an allegation of theft levelled against him.

On 15 February 2024, the Katsina militia opened fire sporadically, trying to abduct a wealthy man in Dangani (Musawa, Katsina). They abducted scores of people instead when they missed their target, who had visited the community for condolences.

On 15 February 2024, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a local defense militia when they invaded Dangani (Musawa, Katsina) and attempted to abduct a prominent businessman who was visiting. The abduction was foiled and the assailants abducted eight young men instead, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 15 February 2024, the Katsina militia attacked the house of a local defence militia member and abducted his wife and son in Ungwar Tudun Boka community in Kankara town (Kankara, Katsina). They targeted the defence militia, but he escaped through the back door.

Around 16 February 2024 (as reported), the police shot and killed a member of an unidentified armed group during a clash in Emure LGA, coded to Emure-Ekiti (Emure, Ekiti). The armed group was suspected to have been responsible for abducting some school children in the area. There was one fatality.

On 16 February 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) killed one person while raiding travelers along the Damaturu-Biu highway near Mahdiya village, Gujba LGA, coded to Gujba (Gujba, Yobe). They laid ambush for travelers and abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 16 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed three people and abducted thirty others in Gwada and Kerawa, coded to Kerawa (Igabi, Kaduna). Seven people were injured in the attack. There were three fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, around midnight, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 100 abducted 16 civilians from Lama and Dekko villages (Zing, Taraba), Monkin village (coded separately) when they invaded the area. The abductees included a catholic priest.
On 16 February 2024, the Niger militia shot and killed two artisanal miners at a mining site close to Alawa (Shiroro, Niger).

On 16 February 2024, around midnight, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 100 abducted 16 civilians from Monkin (Zing, Taraba), Lama and Dekko villages (coded separately) when they invaded the area. The abductees included a catholic priest.

On 16 February 2024, a Niger militia engaged the Nigerian military in a firefight while attempting to invade Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). The troops repelled the attack. The militia shot a vigilante member dead and abducted twelve people. There was one fatality.

On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked the Delta State Polytechnic students (for the second time in the week) at their off-campus hostel in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). They shot a male student dead and raped one female student while many other students were injured.
On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured one person at a residence in Millenium Quarters, Yelwa (Bauchi). No further details.
On 16 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed one person and injured another in Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina). No further details.

On 16 February 2024, the Nigerian troops killed four ISWAP fighters and rescued some hostages in Lamisuri village (Gujba, Yobe). The military responded to a distress call over the abduction of some commuters near Yobe State College of Agriculture, along Buni Yadi. There were four fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed six people at Kwassam (Kauru, Kaduna) and abducted five others, including a former CBN Director. Two people were injured in the attack. There were six fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, the Anti-Touting Squad shot and killed one person and injured another at the Science Equipment Market, Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). The Squad had pursued a man alleged to have urinated in a restricted area into the market. They opened fire sporadically, and two people were hit. Many traders fled for safety. There was one fatality.
On 16 February 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and killed three people and abducted thirty others in Unguwar Tofa in Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna).
On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man and abducted his wife in Mai Katako, Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). There was one fatality.
On 16 February 2024, IS/BH shot and injured one person in the Ndawang community along the Damboa-Chibok Road, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the publicity secretary of the APC in Plateau state at a pub in Pankshin town (Pankshin, Plateau). He was killed alongside one other person.
On 17 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed two people around Jege village (Gwoza, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person in Sarkin-Kudu (Ibi, Taraba). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, the community vigilante group killed three people and injured two others suspected to be spying for marauders in Damba (Illela, Sokoto).
On 17 February 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed two people and injured four others in Nahuta village (Batsari, Katsina). They abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 17 February 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and injured a male nurse in Raka School, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The victim was attacked when returning home from work. The militia went away with his phone.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted twenty commuters along the Gusau-Funtua Road coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). They set vehicles on fire.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted eight persons as they were traveling along Chokochoko - Obajana - Lokoja highway (Kabba, Kogi). The victims consisted of two women, four men and two students, and a ransom of 30 million naira which was later reduced to 2.6 million was demanded.
On 17 February 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a 73-year-old man from a Fulani settlement in Janjala village (Kagarko, Kaduna). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted thirteen people in Amala-Dam village in Kachia LGA, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna).

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group physically assaulted a group of women, and stripped them naked along Okolochi - Ihiagwa road (Owerri West, Imo) as a reprisal, after a traditional ruler whom they tried to abducted escaped (coded separately). The assailants were chased away by some youths in the area.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot at the car of the traditional ruler of Okolochi community as he was driving along Okolochi - Ihiagwa (Owerri West, Imo). The traditional ruler sustained an injury, his driver drove through the shooting and hit one of the assailants.
On 17 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed three people in Samunaka and Ungwar Sarkin Noma villages, coded to Ungwan Sarkin Noma(Kudan, Kaduna). They destroyed houses and livestock.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted nine women in Mareri (Gusau, Zamfara) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia killed one person and abducted scores of others at Gidan Kaji in Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 17 February 2024, a joint team of security operatives, comprised of police forces, soldiers and NSCDC operatives engaged an Icelander cult militia in an armed clash in their hideout at Idu-Ekpeye, Ahoada LGA (Rivers). The leader of the militia, 2baba who was declared wanted and accused of killing a police officer months prior (coded separately) was killed.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group disrupted the collation of APC primaries results at a hotel in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) and attacked the journalists and other persons at the venue. Their cameras and other equipment were damaged.
On 17 February 2024, IS/BH fighters attacked and injured an INGO vendor in Wajare Ward, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked the Yargoje community (Kankara, Katsina). No further details. Casualties unknown.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted four people from Guiwa village, Kurya Madaro district, coded to Kuriya (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). No further details.

On 18 February 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed 12 persons at Gidin Dutse Makyali village in Kufana district (Kajuru, Kaduna). Some of the victims were burned to death, nine others sustained burn injuries and about 17 houses were burned by the assailants who shot sporadically upon arriving the village.

On 18 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants and Nigerian soldiers engaged in an armed clash at Alawa (Shiroro, Niger) when the militants attacked the area, shot sporadically and shouted 'Allahu Akbar'. The militants razed over 30 houses, and stole livestock and valuables. There are no casualties, an unspecified number of civilians were declared missing.
On 18 February 2024, a suspected Fulani militia killed two civilians and injured five others at Rawuru in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau) for unclear reasons.

On 18 February 2024, overnight, a Zamfara militia killed the Divisional Criminal Officer and wounded several policemen when they invaded Zurmi town (Zurmi, Zamfara). The divisional police station in the town was set ablaze by the militia in the attack which was a reprisal after their colleagues were killed by a local defense militia (coded separately). The militia fled when they sighted military forces. Some sources report that the militia were dressed as community protection guards and also engaged the guard whom they overpowered in a clash, other sources report 7 fatalities including two policemen.

On 18 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a 16-year-old female from Buma village (Shani, Borno). The abductors demanded an eight-million-naira ransom. The police and local hunters invaded (no reported clash) the abductors' hideout around Fotta village, Gombi, Adamawa, arrested three members of the armed group and rescued the hostage.

On 18 February 2024, a Niger militia killed three civilians and abducted 15 women at Bassa community (Shiroro, Niger). The attack was a retaliation for the killing of their colleagues by security operatives three weeks earlier.

On 18 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted commuters and a corpse at Umuoka (Udi, Enugu). The corpse was being conveyed from Lagos to the deceased hometown in Enugu. The number of other occupants in the vehicle who were all abducted is unspecified and a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. Other sources report that the corpse was later recovered by soldiers (means not stated) and the abductees were three.

On 18 February 2024, troops of sector 2 of Operation Hadin Kai and Yobe state hunters group engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash during an operation at Maltari village, coded to nearby Kukareta (Damaturu, Yobe). Three militants were killed, rifles, ammunition, grenades and motorcycles were recovered by the troops.

On 18 February 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a firefight in Malari village (Konduga, Borno). The ISWAP members were extorting zakat levies from the community when the army attacked them. They killed three ISWAP members and recovered two AK 47 riffles, two magazines, two hand grenades and one motorcycle.
On 18 February 2024, a Zamfara militia killed four civilians and abducted seven others in Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The victims were working to clear a field when they were attacked.
On 18 February 2024, IS/BH shot and injured a businessman at Burum junction in Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 19 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted 30 civilians, most of whom were women from Dangunu (Muya, Niger). At least 15 other persons were abducted from Pai and Katerma, (coded separately).
On 19 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted at least 15 civilians from Pai and an unspecified number of others from Katerma (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Yar Nasarawa, coded and spelled as Nassarawa (Faskari, Katsina). Between three and six persons including the ward head were killed, about 10 others were wounded, ten motorcycles, shops and three houses were set ablaze by the assailants.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Ruwan Godiya (Faskari, Katsina), Nassarawa and Kyarbishiyar Danfillo (coded separately). An unspecified number of residents were wounded, the villages were attacked simultaneously.

On 19 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a councilor representing Ohwase ward (Udu, Delta) at his residence. Other sources report that the attack was related to cult activities.

On 19 February 2024, Opolo and Okutukutu communal militias clashed following a land dispute in Opolo (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). Two persons were killed in the clash. The Mbiama- Yenagoa road was blocked with bonfires and traffic was disrupted as a result of the clash.

On 19 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man between Ikobi and Oloba, as he was returning to Ugbokpo (Apa, Benue). Other sources claim that one other person escaped with gunshot injuries.

On 19 February 2024, police forces invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Achalla (Awka North, Anambra). The group was responsible for enforcing sit-in orders in the area. An unspecified number of its members sustained injuries, they all fled, five exotic cars, arms and ammunition were recovered.

On 19 February 2024, a local defence militia engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in the Boko community (Zurmi, Zamfara). An unspecified number of the Zamfara militia were killed, three arrested, and motorcycles were recovered. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 19 February 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and injured a United Nations Community Focal Person around Girls' high school in Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). No further details.
On 19 February 2024, the Aye, alias Black Axe, and Eiye cult militiamen clashed in Kwale (Ndokwa West, Delta). 4 people were killed.

On 19 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Makera (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) and killed nine persons. 53 others were abducted, the murdered victims were shit when they attempted to escape abduction.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Kyarbishiyar Danfillo (Faskari, Katsina), Nassarawa and Ruwan Godiya (coded separately). At least one person was killed and an unspecified number of residents were wounded, the villages were attacked simultaneously.
On 19 February 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted many women gathering firewood around Borno College of Basic Studies in Bama town (Bama, Borno). No further details.

On 19 February 2024, a joint security team, coded as police and military forces killed a Sokoto militia leader called Mai Dubu Dubu during an armed clash at Kware forest in Kware LGA (Sokoto). Other members of the militia fled, and 21 rounds of live ammunition were recovered by the troops.

On 20 February 2024, Nigerian troops came under fire from the Kaduna militia while on a clearance Operation in Yadi Forest, coded to Birnin-Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops responded and killed one of the attackers. Other militiamen fled the scene. The military recovered two AK 47 Rifles, six AK 47 Magazines, five rounds of 7.62mm Special ammunition, 331 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 PKT Machine Gun ammunition, and two PKT Machine Gun ammunition links. There was one fatality.

On 20 February 2024, Katsina militia shot and killed nine people in the Lambo community near Wurma (Kurfi, Katsina). The militia also set houses and vehicles on fire and burnt down grains. There were nine fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person around Isokan Estate, behind Premier Grammar School Abeokuta North, coded to Ibara-Orile (Abeokuta North, Ogun). No further details.
On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people in Opah (Otukpo, Benue). They killed two more people the next day, coded separately.
On 20 February 2024, a Katsina militia abducted 26 commuters at Ungwuwan Boka, Faskari LGA (Katsina) which is located along Funtua - Gusau highway. The victims were occupants of two vehicles.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP fighters on sixteen motorcycles attacked the Nigerian troops in Khaddamari (Jere, Borno) and Zabarmari (coded separately). The troops engaged them in a firefight until they retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP fighters on sixteen motorcycles attacked the Nigerian troops in Zamarmari, also spelt as Zabarmari (Jere, Borno) and Khaddamari (coded separately). The troops engaged them in a firefight until they retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP attacked Nigerian troops on the eastern outskirts of Buniyadi, also spelt as Buni Yadi town (Gujba, Yobe). The army responded and engaged them in a firefight. ISWAP killed one soldier and injured another. They set a gun truck on fire.
On 20 February 2024, a Katsina militia abducted four women and a man from Bayan Gidan Rediyo Quarters in Dutsin Ma town (Dutsinma, Katsina). The man later escaped. No further details.

On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two Ebubeagu operatives (Neighbourhood Vigilante members) in Iboko (Izzi, Ebonyi). The armed group first shot two fuel attendants dead at a fueling station before proceeding to attack the vigilante members. They axed the corpses of the vigilante members after killing them. The onslaught raised tension in the community, and the people scampered for safety. There were four fatalities.
On 20 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters at Gidan Kaji in Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 20 February 2024, a Zamfara militia were engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to a distress call at Kwaren Kirya village in Maru LGA (Zamfara) along Gusau - Sokoto highway and foiled an abduction attempt, as claimed by the Zamfara state command of the police force. Other sources claimed that 26 commuters were abducted before security operatives arrived. No casualties.

On 21 February 2024, the police exchanged gunfire with an unidentified armed group and shot one dead in Tunga Umoru village (Borgu, Niger). The clash occurred when the police ambushed the armed group attempting to pick up 3 million naira extorted from a man they threatened to abduct. The police rescued a female hostage after other members of the armed group escaped with gun wounds. There was one fatality.

On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two people in Opah (Otukpo, Benue). They raped women and burnt farm produce and other property. The armed group had killed three people the previous day, coded separately. There were two fatalities.
On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a female from her residence in Zone B, Apo Resettlement (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors demanded a ransom. No further details.
On 21 February 2024, a Katsina militia ambushed and killed at least five members of the Community Watch Corps patrolling the Dogon Daji area of Sabuwa LGA, coded to Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina).

On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a police inspector when attacking a police checkpoint at the Eliozu flyover in Obio/Akpo LGA coded to Rumuodomaya (Obi, Rivers). The police returned fire and killed one of the assailants. Other members of the armed group escaped and fled the scene. There were two fatalities.

On 21 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed an unspecified number of people while attacking Munhaye village, Faskari LGA, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). They abducted many others. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked two communities in Turan District, Kwande LGA, coded to Kwande (Kwande, Benue). No further details. Casualties unknown.

On 21 February 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation Whirl Stroke exchanged gunfire with an unidentified armed group in Jootar village in Ukum LGA, coded to Chito (Ukum, Benue). The armed group had abducted twelve people and was transporting them from Imo to Adamawa state when the troops intercepted them. They abandoned their hostages and fled after the gunfight with the military. There were no fatalities.

On 21 February 2024, a joint Task Force involving the police, KSCWC and vigilantes invaded the Katsina militia camp, newly acquired by Dankarami and Barbaru in Yar Tepa, Birdigau near Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina) in an attempt to dislodge the militia from the hideout. The ensuing firefight claimed the lives of the KSCWC commander for Kankara, four local vigilantes and two volunteers from Birdigau and Gidan Gwanji. The militia group lost about twenty fighters. Another source reported that a police officer sustained an injury, and the force rescued 332 rustled cattle. There were about twenty-seven fatalities.

Around 22 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops on patrol clashed with the Kaduna militia in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Maganda (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), Igabi and Giwa LGA, coded separately. They killed two militiamen and recovered 1 AK 47 rifle,1 AK 47 Magazine, three rounds of 7.62mm Special, 1 Techno phone, 3 Hilux and motorcycle keys, wraps of substance suspected to be marijuana, tramadol tablets and the sum of 13,200 Naira only. Many rustled cattle used as shields were shot dead in the process. Two fatalities shared within the three events-one fatality coded.

On 22 February 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight around the Bada/Riyawa general areas of Chikun and Igabi LGA, coded to Ungwan Liman Riyawa (Chikun, Kaduna). The military killed six militiamen, including Boderi Isyaku, A kingpin responsible for many attacks in the state. The troops recovered two AK47 rifles, 300 rounds of ammunition, nine AK47 magazines, one magazine carrier, one Baofeng radio set and five motorcycles. There were six fatalities.
