On 14 March 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged the AVG in a firefight when attacking their office in Amichi (Nnewi South, Anambra). AVG member fled the scene, but one of them was shot while hiding in their operational vehicle and was burnt together with the vehicle by the invading armed group. There was one fatality.

On 14 March 2024, the Nigerian troops confronted an unidentified armed group along the Akpata-Obajana road, coded to Obajana (Lokoja, Kogi). The armed group had intercepted three buses with the intent of abducting the passengers when the troops attacked them. They abandoned the hostages and escaped the scene. There were no Fatalities.

On 14 March 2024, suspected Okuama militia attacked and killed fifteen soldiers on a peace mission to their community in Okuama (Ughelli South, Delta). The troops responded to a distress call to manage a conflict between Okuama and Okoloba communities. The troops were ambushed by some community youth suspected to be from Okuama. There were fifteen fatalities.

On 14 March 2024, suspected Okoloba militia, in military uniform, shot sporadically at the Okuama people in Okuama (Bomadi, Delta), killing three people. Many people were injured, and the residents scampered for safety. They set many houses on fire. The attack continued the following day, coded separately.

On 15 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Riruwai community from his palace, coded to Lame district (Toro, Bauchi). The assailants shot sporadically in the air to scare away residents, and the abductee's corpse was recovered by a search party and there were no ransom demands. (coded separately).

On 15 March 2024, Ayeke and Enweli communal militias clashed and continued into the following day (coded separately) over a disputed parcel of land. Location coded to Onyedega (Ibaji, Kogi), four persons were killed, split across two events and coded as two and the tension was quelled when soldiers and police forces were deployed.

On 15 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian army ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at the Gwamtu- Duduwa-Kujeni route in Kajuru LGA (Kajuru, Kaduna) following an intelligence on the movement of logistics to Rijana forest for the militia. Two militia members were killed, rifles, ammunition and other items were also recovered by the troops.

On 15 March 2024, the Nigerian military and Bokkos defence militia engaged a Plateau militia in a firefight after the militia abducted a school headmaster from his residence in Maiduna village (Bokkos, Plateau). The hostage was rescued, and there were no fatalities.
On 15 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted one person in the Kapam area in Rido (Chikun, Kaduna). No further details.

On 15 March 2024, Nigerian troops raided the hideout of a Katsina militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Dutsen Kura in Batsari LGA (Batsari, Katsina). Two militia members were killed, one 81mm mortar bomb among other items were recovered by the troops.
On 15 March 2024, Civilian JTF operatives ambushed a Katsina militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Garin Rinji in Batsari LGA (Batsari, Katsina). The militia leader was killed.

On 15 March 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked a Nigerian troops' position and engaged the soldiers in a firefight on the northern outskirts of Pulka town (Gwoza, Borno). No further details. Casualties unknown.
On 15 March 2024, suspected Okoloba militia attacked the Okuama people in Okuama (Bomadi, Delta) for the second day. They set houses on fire and injured many people. There were no fatalities.

On 15 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the Edo State PDP chairman around GRA, Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The abductors trailed his vehicle after a night meeting at the Government House and took him away. A ransom of 500 million naira was demanded, the abductee was released on 26 March and there are no reports on. ransom payment.
On 16 March 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Dogonnoma (Kajuru, Kaduna) and inflicted serious injuries on one person. 14 to 17 other residents were abducted.

On 16 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Riruwai after he was abducted from his palace and dumped his body near the village, coded to Lame district (Toro, Bauchi). There were no ransom demands and the victim's corpse was found by a search party.

On 16 March 2024, Ayeke and Enweli communal militias continued a clash which began the previous day (coded separately) over a disputed parcel of land. Location coded to Onyedega (Ibaji, Kogi), four persons were killed, split across two events and coded as two and the tension was quelled when soldiers and police forces were deployed.

On 16 March 2024, an unidentified cult militia trailed a man and killed him at mile axis of Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim was a printer, his mobile phone and motorcycle were stolen by the assailants and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 17 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted 86 - 87 civilians during an attack on Kajuru Station (Kajuru, Kaduna). The militia also broke into shops and stole food items, there are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources report that the incident happened at Tantatu and Aguba villages in Kufana district.

On 17 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person when they attacked Ikobi (Apa, Benue) and two others in Ugbobi and Inyapu (coded separately). Other sources report that the assailants arrived from Nasarawa state, through Agatu LGA.

Around 17 March 2024 (as reported), Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Maiduna (Bokkos, Plateau) where the group abducted a school headmaster who was rescued by the troops. There were no fatalities.

On 17 March 2024, troops of 1 Division of the Nigerian army responded to a distress call and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Tantatu in Kajuru LGA (Kajuru, Kaduna). 16 abductees were rescued by the troops and casualties are unknown.

On 17 March 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed two pastors at the premises of their church's national headquarters in Ikot Ekang (Abak, Akwa Ibom). The assailants who were on a motorcycle disrupted an ongoing church meeting.
On 17 March 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted four men and three women from Damba village (Illela, Sokoto).

On 17 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person when they attacked Ugbobi (Apa, Benue) and two others in Ikobi and Inyapu (coded separately). Other sources report that the assailants arrived from Nasarawa state, through Agatu LGA.

On 17 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person when they attacked Inyapu (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo and two others in Ikobi and Ugbobi (coded separately). Other sources report that the assailants arrived from Nasarawa state, through Agatu LGA.
On 17 March 2024, NAF soldiers beat up a Bolt driver and two others at Osubi town (Okpe, Delta). The reason for the assault is unknown.
On 17 March 2024, ISWAP fighters clashed with the Nigerian troops after attacking their location in Gwange axis, Bama (Bama, Borno). The militiamen retreated. There were no fatalities.
On 17 March 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked the Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight in Konduga town (Konduga, Borno). The militiamen retreated. There were no fatalities.
On 17 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a couple from the entrance of their residence at Akpasak estate in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 17 March 2024, soldiers killed about 11 civilians when they raided Igbomoturu (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). At least three houses were set ablaze by the soldiers who suspected that militants that were involved in the ambush of soldiers (coded separately) used the area as their hideout. The Ijaw Youth Council claimed that over 40 residents were killed.

On 17 March 2024, an ISWAP suicide bomber suspected to have been heading to a mosque detonated an IED at Biu (Biu, Borno) and killed himself. Two civilians were also wounded in the blast, other sources report an unspecified number of wounded persons.
On 17 March 2024, a soldier shot and injured a tricycle rider in Tashan Damboa, Gwoza LGA, coded to Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno), when the tricycle collided with his bicycle.

On 18 March 2024, suspected armed pastoralists abducted 41 commuters when they ambushed them along Lapkese road coded to Ibillo (Akoko Edo, Edo). 20 of the abductees were rescued by a joint team of police, soldiers and local self defense militias on 20 March who combed the bushes, there are no reports of a clash.

On 18 March 2024, an unidentified armed group wearing masks wounded a driver and riddled his vehicle with bullets before abducted a farm manager and a farmer from farms at Idowa (Odogbolu, Ogun). The assailants who shot sporadically upon arriving the area demanded for the farm owner and took the manager upon meeting the owner's absence. The police commissioner in the state claimed that only the manager was abducted. The manager was rescued by policemen who raided the abductors' hideout on 21 March (coded separately).

Around 18 March 2024 (as reported), a suspected Okuama militia ambushed policemen who were on a mission to rescue three of their colleagues at Ohoro forest (Ughelli North, Delta). 6 policemen were killed and 6 others were declared missing in action.

On 18 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian army raided the hideout of IPOB militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Orsu Ihiteukwa (Orsu, Imo). One militant was killed, the others fled and their camp was destroyed by the troops.
On 18 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Lebanese construction worker between Umuchu and Umunze communities, coded to Umuchu (Aguata, Anambra).
On 18 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted six people from Tumba village near Matseri (Anka, Zamfara). No further details.
On 18 March 2024, a Zamfara militia killed and abducted an unspecified number of people in Bilbis (Tsafe, Zamfara). An unspecified number of fatalities, coded as 3.

On 18 March 2024, OGSPAM members engaged NURTW members in an armed clash at motor parks in Lafenwa, Kuto, Odeda, Obantoko, Brewery and Ita-Oshin areas of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) over a rivalry on the group approved by the government to collect taxes. Several persons were injured.

On 18 March 2024, police forces responded to a distress call and engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Hayin Dam in Kankara LGA (Kankara, Katsina). The police foiled an attempted abduction and rescued a couple, while the militia fled. Casualties are unknown.

On 18 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed two people in Maikwanugga village near Jangebe (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). Three other people sustained gunshot wounds. The militia rustled animals and stole some valuables.

On 18 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted at least 41 people from four commercial buses in transit along Lakpese Road in Akoko Edo LGA, near Igarra (Akoko Edo, Edo). No further details available.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), military forces raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Zamtip. coded to Pinau (Wase, Plateau). One member of the group was arrested by the troops while the second person shot and killed himself to evade arrest. One rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered.
On 19 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed the district head and four others in Pangu Gari (Rafi, Niger). There were five fatalities.

On 19 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a young Fulani pastoralist in Alkaleri LGA, coded to Alkaleri (Alkaleri, Bauchi). They gouged out the victim's eyes. The police arrested the attackers. There was no fatality.

On 19 March 2024, suspected armed pastoralists attacked and killed two farmers on their farms in Onipi community (Otukpo, Benue). Other farmers were injured and some were declared missing. The caretaker council chairman claimed that 12 persons were injured and that tricycles loaded with yams were burned.
On 19 March 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed a communal militiamen (off duty) at his residence in Kwari Mai Zurfi near Makera (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 19 March 2024, a Modakeke militia attacked and killed three civilians in Ife villages, coded to Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun) as claimed by an Ife group who also claimed that two persons were missing and some villages were sacked. One of the murdered victims was a chief from Wanisanni village.
On 19 March 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two people in Mai Ido village near Awon (Kachia, Kaduna). No further details.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Rafin Bauna (Bassa, Plateau). One abductee was rescued, the troops recovered one rifle and two motorcycles. Casualties are unknown.
On 19 March 2024, a Zamfara militia, riding on motorcycles, fired indiscriminately and killed two people in Ruwan Baure, close to Ruwan Bore (Gusau, Zamfara). They injured five people.

On 19 March 2024, a Zamfara militia clashed with the Community Protection Guards and a communal militia in Ruwan Bore (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia killed two members of the Protection Guard and a communal militiamen and burned down an unspecified number of houses and shops. There were three fatalities. The militia attacked Gidan Zuma the following day (coded separately) and five civilians were wounded in the two attacks.

On 19 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Yongia Ukambie Tiev, coded to Ngambe-Tiev (Logo, Benue) and killed two people. The armed group returned to the village the following day and killed five more people, coded separately. There were two fatalities.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), military forces responded to a distress call and foiled an abduction attempt by a Zamfara militia on the outskirts of Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). Three abductees were rescued, one of them sustained injuries and was taken to the hospital.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from her residence at Abuja layout in Bukuru (Jos South, Plateau). The abductee was rescued by soldiers at Rafin Bauna (coded separately).

On 20 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted not less than ten people between Ifon and Sobe, coded to Sobe (Owan West, Edo). The hostages included five men and five women. No ransom was demanded.

On 20 March 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a man and his pregnant wife in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). The killing took place amid a series of cult killings within the community. There were two fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two soldiers and three civilians in Shege (Toto, Nassarawa). The soldiers were responding to a distress call but were ambushed and killed on their way from Katakpa to Shege. The armed group set many houses on fire. There were five fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Ugbobi village (Apa, Benue) and killed two people. The armed group returned to the village and killed eight more people the following day, coded separately. There were two fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Gidan Zuma in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara) and demanded that the residents provide all of the Ramadan relief materials that were donated to them. The militia had attacked Ruwan Bore the previous day (coded separately) and 5 persons were wounded in the two attacks.

Around 20 March 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops shot and killed a Taraba militiaman in Kutoko village, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba). An AK-47 Rifle and a magazine containing four live rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition were recovered.

On 20 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Yongia Ukambie Tiev, coded to Ngambe-Tiev (Logo, Benue) and killed five people. The killing was in addition to the two people they killed when they attacked the community the previous day, coded separately. There were five fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, the Nigerian troops and a local defence militia killed a Sokoto militiaman during a firefight in Sokoto state, coded to Sokoto (Sokoto North. Sokoto). The militiaman often disguised as a policeman and abducted his victims. His logistic base was destroyed during the operation.

On 21 March 2024, the police and other security agencies, likely to be the military, clashed with the IPOB/ESN in their hideout in the Omni community forest in Izzi LGA, coded to Izi (Izzi, Ebonyi). The government forces killed three militiamen and arrested five. Others escaped and fled into the bush. One AK47 rifle with 16 rounds of live ammunition, a bag containing 2,000 rounds of live ammunition, A Police Warrant Card, and an Identity Card were recovered. There were three fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, the Anti-kidnapping unit of the Nigerian police engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight, killing five of them in a forest in Odogbolu LGA, coded to Odogbolu (Odogbolu, Ogun). The police trailed the armed group to their hideout after they abducted a poultry manager in the area. The police rescued the hostage unharmed while other members of the armed group escaped with gun wounds. Money, one sword, cell phones, hard drugs, charms, empty shells of AK47 riffles and sticks were recovered.

On 21 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted four people around Emecourt Road Junction, Nnewi North LGA, coded to Nnewi (Nnewi North, Anambra). The armed group had abducted three people before their vehicle developed a fault. They stopped and seized a passing car and its driver and transferred the three hostages. One of the hostages escaped, but the abductors fled the scene with the remaining two and the female driver of the seized car.

On 21 March 2024, the Police engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight near Corner Ugara, Buruku (Chikun, Kaduna). The Police were on a routine patrol when they sighted the militia hibernating by the roadside, attempting to abduct the commuters. The Police opened fire on them. The militiamen escaped with injuries. There were no fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed the village Head of Anguwan Bala and his two wives in Majanjan District, coded to Maguga (Rafi, Niger). The militia later attacked Madaka Market the same day, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Ugbobi village (Apa, Benue) and killed eight people. The armed group had earlier killed two people a day before, coded separately. There were eight fatalities.

Around 21 March 2024 (as reported), a Katsina militia shot and killed a driver and injured two others on Dustin Ma Road, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia shot the driver dead after a driver had earlier resisted abduction and escaped with injuries. There was one fatality.

On 21 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked a market and killed 65 people, including the village head in Madaka (Rafi, Niger). The militia invaded the market when trading activities were in full swing and opened fire sporadically on the people. They abducted many people, including women and children, and set many properties on fire.
On 21 March 2024, a Niger militia killed nine abductees at Kukoki village (Rafi, Niger) and nearby the village. The victims were part of those who were abducted from Madaka market (coded separately).

On 21 March 2024, the special team of the Nigerian Military, the police, DSS and NSCDC attacked the IPOB/ESN camp in Mgbalukwu (Izzi, Ebonyi) and killed one of the militiamen. Other members escaped and fled into the bushes. The Nigerian security operatives recovered one AK-47 rifle, two AK-47 magazines, 54 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, two handheld radios and three stolen Sienna buses.

On 21 March 2024, the Tsafe defence militia engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in Magazu village (Tsafe, Zamfara). The Zamfara militia had attacked the village and abducted at least seven people, rustled animals and stole some valuable items. The hostages were rescued after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.
On 21 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed a man and his son on a farm in Wanzamai village, Chafe, also spelt as Tsafe LGA, coded to Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). There were two fatalities.

Around 21 March 2024 (as reported), a Zamfara militia opened fire indiscriminately and shot at least four people dead in Mashaya village, Jangebe District (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The shooting triggered panic in the village.

On 21 March 2024, Boko Haram attacked a Fulani settlement around Fadana Garuwa near Duji (Mobbar, Borno). They opened fire on the residents, forcing them to scamper for safety. There were no fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, the Nigerian Military, the police, and members of the Community Watch Corps engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia intercepted a bus and abducted its passengers at Gidan Kifi village, between Burdugau and Yargoje, coded to Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina). The security forces rescued fourteen out of eighteen passengers abducted from the bus. There were no fatalities.

On 22 March 2024, suspected Boko Haram fighters attacked Garkida (Gombi, Adamawa) and shot a woman dead. The militiamen set a military vehicle ablaze and shot fire indiscriminately at the residents. The villagers scampered for safety, and some fled to the bush for safety.

On 22 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two Tiv farmers who went fishing at the Tse-Aber Azir area in Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa). One of the victims died the following day and a Fulani was killed in a reprisal (coded separately). The IDP resettlement camp was invaded by the assailants and the occupants fled to other areas including Giza. Other sources report that scores were wounded and the clash resulted from a disagreement over a stream.

On 22 March 2024, a Tiv ethnic militia killed a Fulani at Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa) in a reprisal after two Tiv farmers were killed when they went fishing (coded separately). Other sources report that the victim was killed when he confronted Tiv fishers over a shared stream in the community and his death led to a reprisal against the Tiv.

On 22 March 2024, two members of rival unidentified cult militias clashed at Pataka area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) over a disagreement. One person was killed and members of his militia carried out a reprisal (coded separately).

On 22 March 2024, hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight when the group attacked the Pompo community along the Damaturu-Buni Yadi-Biu Road, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Borno). The hunters recovered the cattle rustled by the group. There were no fatalities.
On 22 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted ten passengers of a commercial bus in Jootar, Ukum LGA coded to Chito (Ukum, Benue). No ransom was demanded.

On 22 March 2024, Nigerian troops in clearance operations attacked BH/IS enclaves in Bula Dalo, Bula Dalo extension and Yamanci, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno) and Ngurusoye, Mairamri 1 and 2, Sabon Gari, Gargaji coded separately. The military rescued seventy-eight hostages, comprising thirty-five women and forty-three children. At least five militiamen were killed in the operation. Five fatalities split across six events coded as 1.

On 22 March 2024, Nigerian troops in clearance operations attacked BH/IS enclaves in Ngurosoye (Bama, Borno) and Sabon Gari, Mairamri 1 and 2, Bula Dalo, Bula Dalo extension, Yamanci, and Gargaji, coded separately. The military rescued seventy-eight hostages, comprising thirty-five women and forty-three children. At least five militiamen were killed in the operation. Five fatalities split across six events coded as 1.

On 22 March 2024, Nigerian troops in clearance operations attacked BH/IS enclaves in Sabon Gari (Biu, Borno) and Ngurusoye, Mairamri 1 and 2, Bula Dalo, Bula Dalo extension, Yamanci, and Gargaji, coded separately. The military rescued seventy-eight hostages, comprising thirty-five women and forty-three children. At least five militiamen were killed in the operation. Five fatalities split across six events coded as 1.

On 22 March 2024, Nigerian troops in clearance operations attacked BH/IS enclaves in Mairamri 1 and 2, coded to Mairami (Konduga, Borno) and Ngurusoye, Sabon Gari Bula Dalo, Bula Dalo extension, Yamanci, and Gargaji, coded separately. The military rescued seventy-eight hostages, comprising thirty-five women and forty-three children. At least five militiamen were killed in the operation. Five fatalities split across six events coded as 1

On 22 March 2024, Nigerian troops in clearance operations attacked BH/IS enclaves in Gargaji, also spelt as Gargash (Bama, Borno) and Ngurusoye, Mairamri 1 and 2, Sabon Gari Bula Dalo, Bula Dalo extension and Yamanci coded separately. The military rescued seventy-eight hostages, comprising thirty-five women and forty-three children. At least five militiamen were killed in the operation. Five fatalities split across six events coded as 1.

On 23 March 2024, suspected Boko Haram militants (JAS faction) attacked a military base and engaged soldiers and Civilian JTF operatives in an armed clash at Gujba (Gujba, Yobe). One soldier was killed. The troops repelled the militants.

On 23 March 2024, overnight, Tarok and Montol ethnic militias engaged in an armed clash at Ponglong community (Mikang, Plateau) coded to Tunkus. The clash had began between two persons before it escalated over unknown reasons and between 6 to 9 persons were killed, houses and barns were burned. The state commissioner for information claimed that the clash was related to a land dispute.
On 23 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted nine people from Azare village near Bishini (Kachia, Kaduna).

On 23 March 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian military outposts in Madagali and Vurangolda in Madagali LGA, coded to Madagali (Madagali, Adamawa). The Nigerian troops engaged them in a firefight and forced them to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 23 March 2024, two rival armed groups clashed in the Okere community (Warri South, Delta). At least ten members of the armed groups were injured. There was no fatality.

On 23 March 2024, a Safana defence militia engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight in Dawan Barau Forest, Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). Five defence militia members were shot dead in the encounter. There were five fatalities.

On 23 March 2024, IPOB militants ambushed policemen attached to Mopol 18 Owerri who were on patrol and engaged them in an armed clash along old Gariki road in Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo) and also detonated three dynamites at them. Two policemen were killed, four others survived.

On 23 March 2024, Hausa and Fulani militias clashed in Jimjimi village coded to Balle (Gudu, Sokoto), which led to the killing of two persons on each side. The clash was over a land dispute and both group accused the other of being the aggressors. There were four fatalities.

On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed three people in Taka-Lafiya village, coded to Kunkuna (Safana, Katsina). They injured an unspecified number of others. There were three fatalities.

On 23 March 2024, a soldier shot and killed one person and injured two others during an altercation in Chake Quarters, Katsina (Katsina). The youths set one of the soldiers' motorcycles on fire. There was one fatality.

On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed two people in Torawa village, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). They also shot and wounded an unspecified number of others. There were two fatalities.
On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed seven people in Kukar Rabo village (Safana, Katsina). An unspecified number of people were injured and abducted. There were seven fatalities.

On 23 March 2024, an unidentified cult militia attacked civilians at the home of a member of a rival militia in Gana compound, Pataka area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) as a reprisal for the murder of their colleague. Several residents were wounded and over six cars were destroyed.
On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed a politician in Mairuwa village, also called Kamanji (Faskari, Katsina). The victim was killed for resisting abduction.

On 24 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a man in Unguwan Kedaw in Ikara LGA, coded to Ikara (Ikara, Kaduna). The police later rescued the hostage in Unguwar Gajere, Sabon Garin Daji area, Makarfi LGA.
On 24 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed three Eggon farmers at Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 24 March 2024, the Nigerian troops and CJTF ambushed Boko Haram (JAS) along Pulka-Bokko, coded to Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). One Boko Haram fighter was killed, and others escaped with bullet wounds. There was one fatality.

On 24 March 2024, a Kaduna militia killed four people and injured two others when attacking Ungwan Saidu village, coded to Magajin Gari 3 (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They abducted fifty-eight people, but thirty of them later escaped. There were four fatalities.
On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Gidan Zuma village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). 11 persons were killed, 20 women and an unspecified number of children and were abducted.

On 24 March 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed a man at the village of Kudu (Pankshin, Plateau) over unknown reasons. The victim's burnt corpse was found hanging on a mango tree, sources in the area claimed that over the last four weeks, civilians were killed or attacked every Sunday night by the cult group.

On 24 March 2024, the Gigane defence militia engaged a Sokoto militia in a firefight after the Sokoto militia attacked and injured three people in Buwadi village (Illela, Sokoto). The Sokoto militia retreated after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.

On 24 March 2024, a Katsina militia who attacked civilians were engaged in an armed clash with policemen, community watch corps operatives and a local defense militia at Mairua (Faskari, Katsina). Two persons were killed and one other was wounded before the troops arrived, the wife and daughter of one of the victims who was a prominent businessman in the area alongside an unspecified number of residents were also abducted and later rescued when the assailants were repelled.

On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia who divided themselves into three groups clashed with the state community protection guards when they attacked Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara) and attempted to abduct civilians. Two community protection guards including a commander were killed; two military operational vehicles were burned and 6 to 14 civilians four of whom were construction workers were abducted, other sources report that all the abductees were construction workers. The police and soldiers responded and provided reinforcement that repelled the militia.
On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted two siblings from a residence in Damba coded and spelled as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). No further details.

On 24 March 2024, the Ezeagu defence militia engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group attempting to abduct some people in Aguobu-Owa (Ezeagu, Enugu). One of the abductors was killed, and weapons were recovered. There was one fatality.

On 7 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia clashed with soldiers, police forces and neighborhood watch operatives who trailed them in Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu) after the militia abducted a woman. The abductee was released following the gunshots from the security agents. Casualties are unknown.

On 8 April 2024, an unidentified armed group wounded a civilian and shot at the tires of a vehicle when they laid siege on the Otukpo-Adoka-Oweto highway (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo. One woman was also abducted.

On 8 April 2024, presumed soldiers killed two aides of the rivers state gubernatorial candidate of the NRM and arrested him from his residence at Usokun (Degema, Rivers). The man who also a former militant leader in the Niger-Delta, the police claimed it was another security agency that carried out the operation and sources described them dressed in military uniform. The reason for the attack and arrest is unknown, the NRM candidate was released on 10 April.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Babban Doma, coded to Baba-Doka (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Dansadau and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 2

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Babban Doma and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 3.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Dan-Gurgu (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Dansadau and Babban Doma. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 2.

On 8 April 2024, a Zamfara militia killed the officer in charge of Talata Mafara LGA after he was abducted alongside other travelers that day before along Gidan Kano village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The militia dumped the victim's corpse in the bush and directed his family to where it was, they claimed to have killed him 20 hours after he was abducted.

On 8 April 2024, the Dan Karami camp of the Zamfara militia attacked the Kachalla Dan Chaki camp in an infighting in Dangara village, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). Dan Karami attacked Kachalla Dan Chaki when he learned his plan to avenge the killing of his boss, Sani Dangote, whom Dan Karami had killed on 7 April 2024, coded separately. He killed Kachalla Dan Chaki and scores of his fighters. Scores coded as 20, in addition to the fatality of Kachalla Dan Chaki.

On 8 April 2024, a Zamfara militia was repelled by NSCDC operatives when they attempted to attack a community near the Federal College of Education in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia fled and casualties are unknown.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops of the 145 Battalion in Damasak, with air support, attacked ISWAP fighters around Bulaburin, coded to Bula (Fika, Yobe). The troops killed an ISWAP fighter and dislodged others from the enclave. There was one fatality.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Mai Tukunya (Tsafe, Zamfara), Dansadau, Babban Doma and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 3.

On 8 April 2024, a suspected Tiv militia attacked commuters who were traveling from Sukundi to Wukari (Wukari, Taraba) and killed three persons. Two other victims sustained varying degrees of injuries and the assailants stole two. Motorcycles belonging to the victims.

On 8 April 2024, Nigerian army troops raided the camp of a Zamfara militia led by Yellow Janbros and engaged them in an armed clash at Dangunu in Maru LGA (Zamfara). One militia member was killed, the camp was destroyed, firearms and 15 bags of stolen grains were recovered.

On 8 April 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man and injured his son when they attacked them on their farm at Onicha-Ebia in Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and then abducted a man and his daughter from Umueje in Ikem-Etiti (Isi Uzo, Enugu).
On 9 April 2024, Klansmen and Black Axe militia engaged in an armed clash at Afaha Atai (Eket, Akwa Ibom). One person was killed after he resisted being abducted.
On 9 April 2024, Icelander and Greenlanders engaged in an armed clash at Amarata (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). One person was killed in the clash.

On 9 April 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai engaged Boko Haram (JAS) in a firefight and killed four at Ngauru Forest in Bama (Bama, Borno). The troops arrested seventeen Boko Haram family members and profiled them for rehabilitation. There were four fatalities.

Around 9 April 2024 (as reported), the Hybrid forces comprising the military, police, and State Security Service, in conjunction with CJTF, ambushed and killed four Boko Haram (JAS) fighters along Dikwa- Gajibo road, coded to Gajibo (Dikwa, Borno). The troops recovered food items and other logistic materials.

On 9 April 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two IDPs on their farms in Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue). They injured two others and abducted one person. They demanded a five-million-naira ransom for the release of the hostage. The IDPs had left their camp at Adoka in search of food in their home before they were attacked. There were two fatalities.
On 9 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person at the UNIZIK temporary site junction in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The attack was related to an ongoing cult clash.

On 10 April 2024, the Nigerian troops attacked the Sani Tari camp of the Zamfara communal militia in Birnin Magaji LGA, coded to Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara). Sani Tari, the kingpin, escaped, but the Nigerian military killed several of his fighters. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 10 April 2024, NSCDC shot and killed a woman in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) while they were chasing after armed youths. The victim was hit by a stray bullet at the Eid prayer ground and her death resulted in a riot (coded separately).

On 10 April 2024, soldiers beat up a journalist at Kuje (Kuje, FCT) as he was returning from work. The victim claimed that the soldiers attack residents from 9:30pm and accuse them of returning home late.

On 10 April 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with suspected armed Fulani pastoralists after the pastoralists attacked Upu village (Otukpo, Benue). The pastoralists retreated and fled to the bush. There were no fatalities.

On 11 April 2024, the Nigerian police engaged the head of Orashi Marine Iceland Deck Cult in a firefight and shot him dead at his herbalist house in Ibusa (Oshimili North, Delta). The cultist has been on the police wanted list since 2017 for killing many people. He opened fire, trying to escape from the police, when the police invaded his hideout. The police recovered a tinted Black Toyota Highlander with an AK 47 rifle, Pump Action gun, Improvised Explosive Devices (IED), Police and Armed Camouflage.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a police checkpoint at the Isheke Junction on the outskirts of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One police officer was shot dead, and another was fatally injured. The armed group set a police patrol van on fire. There was one fatality.

On 11 April 2024, the Bilya Mai Logo Rumawa group of Katsina communal militia invaded another militia camp around the Rugu Forest in Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). The two rival camps engaged in a supremacy war, resulting in the killing of several militiamen. Several fatalities coded as 10.
On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a driver at Chikara village (Kogi, Kogi) and abducted his 16 passengers. Six of the abductees were later released on the same day.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed two suspected members of a rival militia at the Campus II gate of Auchi polytechnic in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). The attack was related to a clash between rival militias.

On 11 April 2024, the Nigerian military invaded Olota (Ughelli South, Delta) in connection with the killing of 17 military officers in the neighboring Okuama community a few weeks back. They burned two houses and destroyed another. The troops beat and injured a community leader before taking him away with nine other suspects. They recovered four G3 rifles and magazines, one Pump Action Semi-Automatic Gun, three Sub-Machine Guns and magazines, as well as 476 live cartridges from the village. They also recovered five locally fabricated guns, a large plastic bag containing a substance suspected to be cannabis sativa and two-speed boats with 75 horsepower.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Channel TV reporter from his home at Rumu-Osi (Obio, Rivers). The abductors demanded a 30 million naira ransom for his release. The armed group released the hostage on 12 April 2024, and no ransom payment was declared for his release.

On 11 April 2024, hunters clashed with Yan Babeli militia who were part of the entourage of the district head of Miri at Tashan Babiye in Bauchi (Bauchi, Bauchi) when the district head was making a procession to the state government house as part of the Eid celebration. Four persons including the son of the district head were killed in the clash, the district head claimed that the hunters attacked his entourage and planned to assassinate him.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a former President General of Amansea Development Union at his residence in Amansea, also spelt as Amansee (Awka North, Anambra). The victim was offering morning prayer when the assailant entered his house and shot him point blank.

On 12 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked Mandung-Mashu, also called Mandung (Bokkos, Plateau) and Kopnanle villages, coded separately. The armed pastoralists shot and killed at least twelve people from the two villages. They also set fire to homes and worship places. Twelve fatalities split across two events coded as 6.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Baba-Doka (Maru, Zamfara), Kaboro and Gobirawar Challi (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Kaboro (Maru, Zamfara), Baba-Doka and Gobirawar Challi (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, overnight, an unidentified armed group attacked residents of Egan Oriomi in Oto Awori local council development area in Oto (Ojo, Lagos) over a leadership tussle. 10 persons were shot (it is unclear if they died), houses were broken into and set ablaze, and an unspecified number of persons were injured. A one-year old child was burned to death.

On 12 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two people and injured others after attacking some residents in the Maitubi area of Minna (Minna, Niger). They looted houses and shops. They also vandalized cars, tricycles and motorcycles.
Around 12 April 2024 (as reported), ISWAP and Boko Haram (JAS) clashed in Lake Chad, coded to Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Scores of militia members were killed. Scores fatalities coded as 20.

On 12 April 2024, a Black Axe militia member also known as Aiye confraternity killed a civilian at Ile film, Bolanta area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The victim was shot for challenging the militia who were searching for a member of a rival group. Some sources claimed that the incident happened on 12 April, while the police claimed 13 April.

On 12 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked Kopnanle, coded to Tangu (Bokkos, Plateau) and Mandung-Mashu villages, coded separately. The armed pastoralists shot and killed at least twelve people from the two villages. They also set fire to homes and worship places. Twelve fatalities split across two events coded as 6.

On 12 April 2024, about 4 soldiers from the Nigerian Air Force beat up four staff of a hotel where an air force cadet drowned in Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia). One of the staff was killed as a result of the beating while others sustained injuries.

On 12 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a man at UNIZIK Junction, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The shooting added to a series of cult killings that occurred in the city in recent times.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Gobirawar Challi in Maru LGA (Zamfara), Baba-Doka and Kaboro (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, two unidentified cult militias from Nasamu and Iyalode streets engaged in an armed clash at Ajegunle (Ajeromi, Lagos). One person was killed after he sustained injuries and was taken to a hospital where he died, six commercial vehicles were vandalized and two suspects were arrested by the police.

On 12 April 2024, suspected armed pastoralists shot and wounded a man, abducted his wife and their house help in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). The man was the former chief of staff of former governor Ortom, they were returning from his farm when the assailants attacked. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released on 16 April after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 13 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two abductees around Rijana forest (Kachia, Kaduna) after they were abducted from Azzara (coed separately). The abductees were killed over their inability to pay a ransom of 5 million naira.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed Benue state livestock guards and community volunteer guards at Mbabuande (Gwer West, Benue) and killed six of them. The guards were deployed to provide security for a family that was burying their relative in the community.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a group of mourners who were part of a burial procession at Edikwu Ankpali, coded as Ankpali (Apa, Benue) and killed one person. The victim and others in the procession were IDPs, and were forced to flee to the Ugbokpo IDP community after the attack.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia attacked and wounded a motorcycle rider with a machete at Ile-Alawo compound, Igboro area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The reason for the attack is unknown and the victim who sustained an injury to his head was taken to an unknown location by his brother. Fatality is unknown.
On 13 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked the Mbar settlement near Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau), killing three defense communal militia.

On 13 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked GSS Kopyal and Baba Rafi in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). They killed two people and injured four others. They also rustled cattle from the villages.
On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed 14 civilians when they attacked Jaroa community, coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue).

On 13 April 2024, Yoruba Nation agitators clashed with police forces and other security agents, coded as military forces at the Oyo state government secretariat in Agodi (Ibadan North, Oyo). The agitators attempted to take over the secretariat and declare independence of the Yoruba nation, some of them manned the house of assembly entrance and other were in front of the governor's office. 20 of the Agitators were arrested by the police, weapons, cartridges and an Odu'a nation flag were recovered.

Around 14 April 2024 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia attacked and killed two persons at Amuzu and Ezzama communities (Ezza South, Ebonyi). The victims were a motorcycle mechanic and a wheel barrow pusher.
On 14 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed a suspected member of a rival militia at South Ibie (Etsako West, Edo). The attack is related to clashes between rival militias.

On 14 April 2024, suspected unidentified cult militias from rival groups engaged in clashes at Baboko, Ile Onimago, Adabata and Eruda areas of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) using stones and broken bottles. Police forces from C division were deployed to quell the clashes, casualties are unknown. The policemen arrested 46 suspects, 14 of whom they claimed had links to the cult clashes.

On 15 April 2024, members of the Enugu state neighborhood watch shot and killed a restaurant owner at Ogrute junction in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The victim was shot in the back following an altercation between him and the assailants who tried to arrest a client from the restaurant.

Around 15 April 2024 (as reported), soldiers ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Rafin Sarki village in Giwa LGA (Kaduna). Two militia members were killed and the soldiers recovered a rifle, ammunition and a locally fabricated revolver frame.

Around 15 April 2024, a Zamfara communal militia abducted an unknown number of people while raiding Gidan Dan Zara village in Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). They also burned two vehicles and stole food items.
On 15 April 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed one person and injured two others in Kwalawa village near Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara).
On 15 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted nine people from Dumfawa village, coded to Gurbi (Zurmi, Zamfara).

On 15 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a student from his off-campus hostel in Nsukka (Nsukka, Enugu). The abductee was a campus blogger and the abductors arrived in a Hilux vehicle and a jeep. There are no details on ransom demands.
On 15 April 2024, a suspected Zamfara militia killed the Zamfara state secretary of the PDP at the front of his residence in Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 15 April 2024, the Nigerian troops killed an unspecified number of Zamfara communal militia in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). They destroyed the militia's camps. The troops recovered ten operational motorbikes and 18 rustled cows. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 15 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a community along Naka - Adoka road (Gwer West, Benue). Six persons were killed and their bodies were recovered, many others were injured.
Around 15 April 2024 (month of), two unidentified rival cults clashed in the Ikorodu area (Ikorodu, Lagos), killing 3 people for unknown reasons.

Around 15 April 2024 (month of), ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) members abducted 40 people, including children and women, in Muya LGA, coded to the LGA HQ Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). They were rescued at the beginning of July 2025, after some of the women had been forcibly married and held at an unspecified location in Muya LGA.
On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians in Anguwan Tanko Dogon Sarki and abducted some locals from Tashar Keji, both under Kakangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

Around 16 April 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group that attempted to abduct civilians were engaged in an armed clash by military forces who responded to a distress call at Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). One of the assailants was killed, a beretta pistol with four rounds of ammunition was also recovered by the troops.

Around 16 April 2024 (week of), a Kebbi communal militia abducted two people from Suru LGA, coded to Suru (Suru, Kebbi). A joint security team involving the military, NSCDC, DSS and Zuru communal defence militia trailed the abductors to Zugu Liba forest and rescued the hostages.

On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted nine people in Unguwar Iya in Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). They demanded a 30-million-naira ransom for their release. They later released the hostages on 15 June 2024 after collecting a 16-million-naira ransom and killing the ransom bearer, coded separately.

On 16 April 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to have come from Obbo-Ayegunle community in Kwara state seriously wounded one person when they attacked the local government secretariat in Eda-Oniyo (Ilejemeji, Ekiti). The assailants vandalized the building and other council property and the attack was related to a land dispute between the two communities.
On 16 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people in transit between Mayanchi and Talata Mafara, coded to Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara).
On 16 April 2024, the Nigerian troops of 151 Battalion shot and killed a Boko Haram fighter in Banki Junction, Banki (Bama, Borno). The militiaman was alleged to be on an espionage mission.
On 16 April 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed one person on the road between Birnin Gwari and Funtua, coded to Funtua (Funtua, Katsina).

On 16 April 2024, an unidentified armed group led by a suspected land grabber clashed with NURTW members at a motor park in Iyana-Ipaja, coded as Ipaja (Alimosho, Lagos). The clash was over control of the park, one transporter was killed, several other persons sustained bullet wounds.
On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian at Rafin Gora village, two kilometers aways from Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Seven other persons were abducted by the militia.

On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked Anguwar Danko, also spelt as Ungwan Danko (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Kanawa, coded separately. They killed nineteen people and abducted many others. The militia also rustled cows in the community.
On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted scores of civilians from Anguwan Doka in Kakangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically during the attack.

On 17 April 2024, the Nigerian police and Community Watch engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight in Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina) as the militia attempted to overrun the community. One Community Watch member sustained gun wounds, and a militia member got killed in the confrontation. Other members escaped with gun wounds. The police recovered one walkie-talkie as well as a military-grade hand grenade. There was one fatality.

On 17 April 2024, a customs operative shot and killed a civilian at Gamjin Makaho village, along Dankama road (Kaita, Katsina). The victim was one of the passengers in a truck, whose driver refused to stop at a customs checkpoint and was shot at by the operatives.

On 17 April 2024, EFCC operatives shot sporadically when the convoy of the Kogi state governor was leaving the home of the immediate past governor of the state at Wuse Zone 4 (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The EFCC had laid siege to the former governor's home in an attempt to arrest him, before the governor arrived and took him away which prompted the shooting. There were no casualties.

Around 17 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops, Hybrid Forces and CJTF clashed with ISWAP and killed scores of their fighters in Timbuktu Triangle, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). Unspecified number of fatalities coded as 10.

On 17 April 2024, a policeman shot a businessman at a checkpoint along Aba - Owerri road (Aba South, Abia). The victim was heading home when an argument ensued between him and the policemen following is refusal to give a bribe of 500 naira and he died at a hospital on 19 April. The police claimed that the assailant was arrested.

On 17 April 2024, a Niger militia abducted a retired prison guard from along Ilorin - Minna road (Ilorin West, Kwara). The abductee was released on 28 April after soldiers invaded the abductors' camp (coded separately).

Around 17 April 2024 (as reported), ISWAP executed a CJTF member captured around Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). They accused the victim of supporting the Nigerian military. His execution took place in an unknown place and was videoed and circulated online.

On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked Kanawa, coded to Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Ungwar Danko, coded separately. They killed four people and abducted many others. The militia also rustled cows in the community.

On 17 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a man in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The victim was a tricycle revenue collector. The militia trailed him from the Ifite area and shot him at close range. The killing forced the traders in the area to close their shops and scamper for safety.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked Tilengpat village (Pankshin, Plateau). The victims were mostly women. The attackers invaded the community at night and opened fire on the residents, killing between twelve and fifteen people. Fatalities coded as 12.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked the Mandung community (Bokkos, Plateau), Butura and Chikam, coded separately. They sporadically fired at the residents and killed six people, including a student of Plateau State University in his off-campus hostel. Six fatalities split across three events coded as 2.

Around 18 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops repelled the IPOB attack and killed scores of the militia in Orkija (Ihiala, Anambra). The militia, armed with AK-47 rifles, were riding in two Lexus vehicles and motorbikes when they launched the attack on the Nigerian troops. One soldier died, and two others were injured. Scores of the militia and a Nigerian soldier were killed. There were at least 21 fatalities.

On 18 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the traditional ruler of Sensani in his palace, also spelt as Sansani village (Gassol, Taraba). The assailants invaded the community on motorcycles at night and shot him dead. They also shot and wounded a motorcyclist who met them on the way as they were leaving. The monarch was killed at the time he was hosting the Nwonyo Fishing and Cultural Festival. The assailants went away with his two mobile phones. There was one fatality.

On 18 April 2024, a local defense militia clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists at the weekly market in Gada (Gada, Sokoto) following an attempt by the defense militia's leader to arrest a suspected cattle rustler that was seen at the market. Between 6 to 50 people were killed from both sides, including the leader and deputy leader of the defense militia and unspecified number of others were wounded.
On 18 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two farmers in Entekpa (Otukpo, Benue).

On 18 April 2024, a Katsina communal militia abducted at least fourteen people from Kasai close to Nahuta (Batsari, Katsina). They also stole grains, money and other household items. They raided the village concurrently with Madogara, where they abducted thirty people, coded separately.

On 18 April 2024, a Katsina communal militia abducted thirty people, including women, in Zamfarawar Madogara, also called Madogara (Batsari, Katsina). They also stole grains, money and other household items. They raided the village concurrently with Kasai, where they abducted fourteen people, coded separately.

Around 18 April 2024 (as reported), an unidentified cult group hacked a man to death at his residence in the Ibite-Okpatu community, coded to Okpatu (Udi, Enugu). The cultists, numbering about six, were invited by the victim's niece, who had a misunderstanding with him.

On 18 April 2024, three rival Zamfara communal militias engaged in a firefight in Kaurar Zomo village in the Kunchin Kalgo (Tsafe, Zamfara). The confrontation started when Kachallan Jafaru invaded the Alhaji Tsauni enclave and killed Kachallan Gwande and his fighters. Kachallah Madagwal attempted to avenge the death of Gwande and was also killed by Jafaru. Two militia kingpins and twelve other fighters died in the onslaught. There were fourteen fatalities.

On 18 April 2024, a Zamfara militia injured one person after mounting a checkpoint at the Kadauri-Mayanchi axis of the Gusau- Sokoto Highway in Maru LGA, coded to Mayanchi (Maru, Zamfara). They abducted eleven others. The victim got injured while trying to escape abduction.

Around 18 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops and hunters killed a militia member in the clearance operation conducted in some communities in Karim Lamido LGA, coded to Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). The militia had been raiding Garau, Paskere, Tella, Jukun, Farin Ruwa, Mashingi, Jeb Jeb, and Rafin Kada Villages before the troops cleared their hideouts. There was one fatality.

Around 18 April 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with an unidentified armed group specialized in cattle rustling in Mangu (Mangu, Plateau). The troops arrested them and recovered one fabricated rifle, one fabricated pistol, seven rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, a motorbike, and two phones from them. There was no fatality.

On 18 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a SOSAFE agent attempting to intervene after two traditional rulers were shot and wounded between Alabe and Okesa villages near Papalanto (Ewekoro, Ogun). The armed group attacked the two rulers of Keleu and Abule-Oko Villages while returning from a meeting. One was shot in the head and the other in the hand. They were taken to the hospital for treatment. There was one fatality.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked Butura, also spelt as Batura community (Bokkos, Plateau), Mandung and Chikam, coded separately. They sporadically fired at the residents and killed six people, including a student of Plateau State University in his off-campus hostel. Six fatalities split across three events coded as 2.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked Chikam, coded to Mbar (Bokkos, Plateau), Butura and Mandung, coded separately. They sporadically fired at the residents and killed six people, including a student of Plateau State University in his off-campus hostel. Six fatalities split across three events coded as 2.

On 18 April 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed an ARTMA warden at the Aroma Roundabout in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants were driving against the traffic, trailing their target, when the traffic warden stopped them and made them lose their target. One of the assailants shot the warden in the head and fled the scene.
On 18 April 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed three people and injured six others in Munhaye town near Sabon Layi (Faskari, Katsina). The militia abducted 32 other people.
Around 18 April 2024 (week of), a Katsina communal militia abducted twenty people, including women and children, from Na-Alma village (Malumfashi, Katsina).
On 18 April 2024, suspected Mahmuda abducted eight farmers on their way to their fields in Gbeji (Borgu, Niger).

On 19 April 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed four communal defence militia in Maraban Agyaro in Kakangi Ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The defence communal militia and other people were returning from the market when they were attacked. The militia also burned seven motorcycles and stole five. The victim was waiting to take a motorcycle ride into the campus when his assailants gunned him down.
On 30 May 2024, a Katsina militia killed seven farmers on their farms at Katsalle village (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 30 May 2024, troops of 1 Division of the Nigerian Army clashed with a Kaduna militia and killed six at the Market Square of Galadimawa (Giwa, Kaduna). They also arrested three collaborators and logistic agents for the militia. They recovered two motorcycles and four mobile phones.
On 30 May 2024, IPOB/ESN members shot and killed two people while enforcing a 'sit at home' order in the Okwe community (Onuimo, Imo).

On 30 May 2024, a Zamfara militia stormed the residence of the Zamfara State Hajj Commission, killing his son and a watchman in Gusau (Zamfara). They abducted his other son and many other people in the area. The chairman of Hajj (Muslim pilgrimage) was the target of the abduction, but the militia shot and killed his son and watchman.

On 30 May 2024, a suspected IPOB militia shot and killed five Nigerian soldiers at a checkpoint at Obikabia Junction (Obioma Ngwa, Abia). The militia was enforcing a 'sit at home' order restricting people's movement in commemoration of the victims of the Biafra civil war. They were numbered about fifteen, drove in three tinted Prado Toyota SUVs and a Sienna car and opened fire on the soldiers. They also burnt a military patrol vehicle and some shops in the area.

On 30 May 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed five people, including the driver, after waylaying a commercial vehicle near Dan Marke village along Kankara - Marabar Kankara road, coded to Kankara (Kankara, Katsina). Other passengers sustained various degrees of injuries. Two people, including the driver's son, were abducted.

On 30 May 2024, a suspected cult militia killed two members of a rival cult group in a renewed supremacy battle between the Black Axe and Vikings around the Ogheghe area (Ovia North East, Edo). The assailants trailed the victims to the area and opened fire on them.

On 30 May 2024, Nigerian troops and the Pulka defense militia ambushed IS/BH fighters and engaged them in a firefight, killing four in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They destroyed the food items and the bicycle recovered from the militia.

On 30 May 2024, police and LASBCA agents attacked and injured a journalist covering a collapsed building site at Iga Idunganran, Lagos Island (Lagos). The reporter was asked to vacate the site, but his insistence on reporting the incident caused the police and the agency's members to beat and injure him.
Non-violent activity: On 31 May 2024, a local defense militia raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group in Anam forest (Anambra West, Anambra). One Toyota vehicle and charms were recovered.
On 31 May 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SVC militia clashed at the Auchi polytechnic campus 3 gate (Etsako West, Edo). Two people were killed.

On 31 May 2024, an OSPAC member shot and killed one of the community youths returning from a protest in Egbeda (Emohua, Rivers). The killing sparked outrages and riots in the community, coded separately.

On 31 May 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a member of a rival cult group in a renewed supremacy battle between the Black Axe and Vikings at Ikpoba Slope (Ikpoba Okha, Edo). His assailants shot him in the head while waiting to board a vehicle.

On 31 May 2024, IPOB/ ESN militants enforcing a sit-in order attacked a military checkpoint and engaged soldiers in an armed clash at Ohafia (Ohafia, Abia). The clash continued till the militants withdrew, an unspecified number of militants were killed, one was arrested, and weapons were recovered. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
Around 31 May 2024 (as reported), a Katsina militia killed two people after attacking their vehicle at Unguwar Daudun Noma, coded to Kankara (Kankara, Katsina).
On 31 May 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted one civilian from a Fulani settlement in Salka (Magama, Niger).

On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group, suspected to be members of the host community, abducted and killed a student of Alex-Ekwueme Federal University, Ndufu Alike Ikwo (Ikwo, Ebonyi). The decomposing body of the victim was recovered under the bridge at Ako stream in Nwakpu village on 17 June 2024. The police arrested four suspects.
On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a police station at Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue). At least one policeman was injured.
On 1 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SVC militia clashed at the Auchi polytechnic campus 2 gate (Etsako West, Edo). Two people were killed.
On 1 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists shot and killed a man at Opanda (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victim was coming from Adani to Opanda when he was attacked.
On 1 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists gang-raped a 13-year-old girl and killed another man trying to rescue the girl in Ugwu-Uvuru (Uzo Uwani, Enugu).
On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man at his residence in Akunba (Akoko South West, Ondo).

On 1 June 2024, a Plateau militia waylaid two Rigwe youths on a motorcycle while returning from the Gero mining site, coded to Gero (Jos South, Plateau). They killed one of the victims and injured the other.

Around 1 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted 5 civilians along Takum - Katsina-Ala road (Takum, Taraba). The victims include the brother of a retired general, his wife, daughter and two other women. The man was released after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom, the abductors refused to release his wife and daughter and one of the other women escaped around 30 June.
On 1 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and Maphites clashed at different locations in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) including Idokpa Auchi road and Agbor road. Two militia members were killed.
On 1 June 2024, a presumed unidentified cult militia killed a member of an unidentified cult militia at the 3rd East Circular road in Benin City (Oredo, Edo).
On 2 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted six people from Adogo Mallam near Mashegu (Mashegu, Niger).

On 2 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted thirty people from Kankuru village, a kilometer away from Kuchi (Muya, Niger). They proceeded to Adogon-Mallam and Tungan-Kawo villages and abducted 26 people there on 2 and 3 June, coded separately.

On 2 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman around the Federal Science Technical College, Ijebu Imushin (Ijebu East, Ogun). The hostage was on a motorcycle with her daughter when the armed group waylaid them and dragged her into their vehicle. No ransom was demanded.
On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, clashed with SVC militia at Osisioma (Osisioma, Abia). Casualties are unknown.
On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SEC militia clashed in the vicinity of Olode (Egbeda, Oyo). One militia member was killed.
On 2 June 2024, ISWAP militants fired mortar rounds targeting a position of state force, coded as military forces at Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 2 June 2024, a Taraba militia shot and killed the village head of Usmanu in Karim Lamidu LGA, coded to Karim Lamido (Taraba). Many residents fled the community.

On 2 June 2024, Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia attempting to rustle cattle from a Fulani settlement in Gidan-Makeri near Janjala (Kagarko, Kaduna). The troops were on patrol around the Janjala-Gidan Makeri axis when they engaged the militia. They killed two members of the militia.

On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, attacked a member with an unidentified rival cult militia in a shop at Wire road in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The targeted militia member escaped, one sales attendant was mistakenly killed.

On 2 June 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed the Malumfashi LGA Administrative Secretary in Malumfashi (Katsina). The militia had traced him to his house before they finally caught him at the mosque. The assailants shot him while leaving the mosque after the evening prayer. His assassination might be related to his role in the peace and stability program in the council. The militias were not favorably disposed to the program.

On 3 June 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a local lawmaker and a youth leader at Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The duo were riding on a motorcycle when the assailants waylaid them and opened fire at them, killing the two. One of the victims was the councilor representing Enuagu ward in the Onicha Legislative Council, and the other was the Onicha LGA coordinator of the National Youth Council of Nigeria.
On 3 June 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye militia clashed with Maphite militia at Siluko road (Ovia South West, Edo), coded to Iguobazuwa. One militia member was killed.

Around 3 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed the father of a former Attorney-General of Nasarawa state around Akwanga (Akwanga, Nassarawa). He was abducted a few days before his killing, coded separately. His abductors killed him for refusing a ransom payment for his release.
On 3 June 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye militia members wounded a member of Maphite militia a KB estate in Ikpoba hill (Ikpoba Okha, Edo), coded to Idogbo.

On 3 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted about 20 people from communities around Tunga-Kawo, also called Kawo (Shiroro, Niger). They also rustled over two hundred cattle from the communities. The militia moved from house to house, selecting their victims without any interference.

On 3 June 2024, ISWAP abducted 4 civilians including an elderly man at an illegal vehicle checkpoint which they mounted at Azare (Hawul, Borno). The elderly man was later released, there are no reports on ransom payment or demands.

On 3 June 2024, ISWAP militants ambushed an engaged state forces, coded as military forces in an armed clash at Bula Yobe - Kote area (Bama, Borno). One soldier and an unspecified number of militants were killed, three soldiers were declared missing, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person from El-Rufai Estate in the Kuchiko Resettlement Development Area (KRDA) of Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The armed group, numbering about sixteen, visited two houses but only succeeded in one due to the timely arrival of the military.

On 3 June 2024, a Katsina militia abducted two lecturers of the Federal University, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia raided their houses at the Government Reservation Area (GRA) and forced them out. The son of one of the lecturers was also abducted. Other residents were dispossessed of valuables items.

On 3 June 2024, police engaged a Plateau militia in a firefight and killed two in the Fangha area of Daffo (Bokkos, Plateau). The militiamen attempted to abduct some people when the police were alerted and responded. Other militiamen escaped with gunshot wounds. The police recovered a locally fabricated revolver gun loaded with four 7.62MM rounds of ammunition, two phones, one dagger, and one knife.

On 3 June 2024, a Plateau militia shot and killed five people, including a pastor and his wife, in Kimakpa, coded to Kwal (Bassa, Plateau). The assailants attacked their victims in the middle of the night. Two other persons were injured during the attack.

On 3 June 2024, a Plateau militia shot and killed two people out of the three people returning from the farm around Miango (Bassa, Plateau). The third person hid in the bush and escaped from the assailants. The incident took place on the same day a pastor and four other people were killed in the area, coded separately.

On 3 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured between six and ten people in the Antsa community (Makurdi, Beneu). They attacked the people with knives and machetes around 1 am when some residents were still drinking in the community. The assailants fled when the military arrived and started shooting (no confrontation). The attack triggered a demonstration in the community, coded separately.

On 3 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured people with machetes in Akawe Torkula Polytechnic at North Bank (Makurdi, Benue). They fled when the military arrived and started shooting (no confrontation).

On 3 June 2024, a Niger milita (described as bandits) abducted a groom during his wedding ceremony in Papiri (Agwara, Niger). The attackers accused his fiance of having a romantic relationship with a Niger milita leader.

On 3 June 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) fired warning shots and abducted two civilians on the Zungeru-Tegina road, location coded to Tegina (Rafi, Niger) while the militia were crossing the road with stolen cattle.

On 4 June 2024, a Kogi militia abducted a pastor's wife from her residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductors were said to have trailed the woman from an eatery to her house and sporadically opened fire to scare off the people before they took her away. They demanded a 32-million-naira ransom for the release of the hostage.

On 4 June 2024, police clashed with an unidentified armed group attacking the Divisional Police headquarters in Ezzamgbo, also spelt as Ezamgbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The armed group, numbering about eight, invaded the police station and opened fire sporadically before the police repelled them. The confrontation triggered panic in the area and disrupted the palliative sharing program organized by the LGA chairman. The attackers set a vehicle and motorcycle ablaze while retreating. There were no fatalities.

On 6 June 2024, a communal clash took place in Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta) and one person was killed.
On 6 June 2024, ISWAP militants fired mortar rounds targeted at position of state forces, coded as military forces at Banki town (Bama, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least seventeen people in Boraye village, Gada district, coded to Gada (Bungudu, Zamfara).
On 7 June 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings cult militias clashed and killed one militiaman in Emene (Enugu East, Enugu).

On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man abducted in Jilli village (Gubio, Borno). The abductors claimed they killed the hostage when he attempted to escape their custody. They released his body after his family paid a 5 million naira ransom out of the 10 million naira demanded.

On 7 June 2024, NSCDC officials abducted a businessman at Amaedim Ngwogwo community in Ishiagu (Ivo, Ebonyi) over a land related dispute. The NSCDC claimed the abductee was arrested for obstructing a land matter in the community.

Around 7 June 2024 (as reported), some hunters arrested, tortured and killed a 14-year-old teenager in Maiha LGA, coded to Maiha (Maiha, Adamawa), over the suspicion of stealing 20,000 naira. The police arrested the hunters.

On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted at least 30 travelers including several students at Uke (Karu, Nassarawa) as they were travelling to Abuja from Nassarawa state. There are no reports on ransom demands. The families of two of the victims were contacted and a ransom of 10 million naira each was demanded. The abductees were released on 11 June after a collective ransom of 40 million naira was paid.

On 7 June 2024, suspected Boko Haram fighters numbering about fifty, attacked and killed twenty people in Bassa (Shiroro, Niger). Ten youths among the victims were beheaded for refusing to join the militant group. The militia had threatened the villagers who refused to join them not to return to their homes; otherwise, they would be killed. The victims returned to the village to get some food items for their families at the IDP camp when the Boko Haram fighters attacked them.
