Four members of the group were arrested, the camps were destroyed and abductees were rescued. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group injured many people while raiding a residence around Rafin Zurfi (Bauchi). They went away with an undisclosed amount of money and some valuable items.

On 7 June 2024, police and the Katsina Community Watch clashed with a Katsina militia and killed three militiamen in Duva village, Maibakko (Sabuwal, Katsina). The militiamen were intercepted while trying to abduct some women from the village. They opened fire at the police, and the police responded, killing them and thwarting the abduction. The police rescued all the hostages.

On 7 June 2024, police forces in collaboration with the DSS and hunters raided the hideouts of an unidentified armed group in Kweti forest (Kachia, Kaduna) , coded to Kachia, and Gidan Dogo (coded separately). Four members of the group were arrested, the camps were destroyed and abductees were rescued. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with soldiers and wounded three of them at the Okomu oil palm plantation (Ovia South West, Edo).

The victim was an aspirant for Isi-Uzo LGA chairperson. His assassination was not unrelated to his political aspiration and growing popularity in the area. Other sources report that a former councilor of Ikem 1 ward who was the victim was abducted by the assailants who demanded for a ransom of 100 million naira.

Around 7 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by an off-duty soldier who disarmed a member of the group after they abducted him along Ekpoma - Okene - Lokoja road (Esan West, Edo). The soldier rescued himself and other civilian abductees, he also recovered a pistol. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, two unidentified cult groups clashed and killed a rival member along Ngwa Road, Aba North LGA, coded to Ehere (Aba North, Abia).

On 8 June 2024, military troops of Operation Udo Ka engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at Igboro forest in Arochukwu LGA (Abia). 6 militants were killed, one soldier was wounded, arms, ammunition and 3 IEDs were recovered in the operation which was a reprisal by the troops over a previous attack that happened on May 30.
On 8 June 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian and abducted 31 others at Kokob village in Kufana ward (Kajuru, Kaduna). The abductees consisted of 24 females and 7 males.

On 8 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed nine civilians at Tarorshi and Apirgwa villages in Kente ward (Wukari, Taraba). An unspecified number of persons were injured and properties were destroyed.
On 8 June 2024, the Buccaneers cult militia and the Eiye clashed at the Moshood Abiola Polytechnic, Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). No further details.

The troops rescued the hostages and recovered the rustled cows. There were no fatalities.
On 8 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Tse-Deke village (Wukari, Taraba). An unspecified number of persons were injured and properties were destroyed.

On 9 June 2024, a Niger militia killed a man while he was working on his farm at Kuchini community (Shiroro, Niger) coded to Kuta.

On 9 June 2024, an unidentified armed group and Nigerian army troops who responded to a distress call engaged in an armed clash along Ughelli - Patani road (Ughelli North, Delta). An unspecified number of civilians who were abducted while they were traveling in a commercial vehicle were rescued. Some occupants of the vehicle were declared missing.
On 9 June 2024, ISWAP fighters gathered 100 civilians and opened fire on them, killing an unspecified number of people in Doro Naira (Kukawa, Borno). Unspecified fatalities coded as 10.

Police recovered four AK-47 rifles, four locally made semiautomatic pistols, nine AK-47 magazines, three walkie-talkies, one POS machine and a loudspeaker. They also recovered one black Toyota 4Runner and a blue Lexus RX350.
On 5 July 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted thirty people from the Gwadodi community in Rabah LGA, coded to Rabah (Sokoto).

On 5 July 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight after storming their hideout in the Oviri-Ogor community (Ughelli North, Delta). One member of the group was fatally injured and later died while receiving treatment at the hospital. The police had arrested three members of the group before the clash. They recovered an AK-49 rifle from the scene. The armed group was responsible for the abduction of one person in Edjakita on 1 July 2024, coded separately.

On 5 July 2024, policemen fired gunshots into the air and killed a civilian at Imala/ Elega area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) as he was locking up his shop. The victim was hit by a stray bullet, some sources claimed that the policemen were pursuing a suspect in a raid, while others claimed that they were drunk.

On 5 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted at least nine people, including a woman and her three children, in Akure North LGA, coded to Irese (Akure North, Ondo). One of the hostages escaped.

On 5 July 2024, Nigerian troops, in conjunction with CJTF and Hybrid Forces, killed 11 ISWAP fighters during a firefight in Jongo, Sambisa Forest in Bma LGA, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). One Hybrid Forces fighter got injured. The troops recovered 99 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammo links, 19 rounds of 7.62mm x 39 special ammo, three AK-4 rifle magazines, 47 rounds of ammunition, two locally made guns, and two hand grenades.

On 5 July 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a 79-year old man from his residence at Biniki community (Kauru, Kaduna). The abductee was the former president of the National Union of Electricity and Gas Workers which is now called NUEE. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 5 July 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured some Amotekun Corps officers on the Akure-Ado expressway in Akure (Akure South, Ondo). They came under attack while moving about 120 cows seized over the allegation that they grazed on a farm and destroyed farmlands in Osi and Igboba Communities. The Corps repelled the attack and evacuated the injured officers to the hospital. There were no fatalities.

On 5 July 2024, a Fulani militia engaged Amotekun Corps in an armed clash at Igoba (Akure North, Ondo) when the corps responded to a report of cows destroying farms in the area. One Amotekun operative was seriously wounded, others sustained different degrees of injuries and they retreated from the area.
On 5 July 2024, IS/BH fighters shot and killed the Bulama Bacha community leader around Horre Nayiwa in Gujba LGA, coded to Gujba (Yobe). They also set his house on fire.

On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops and hunters ambushed Boko Haram fighters, attempting to blow up the powerline near Kasesa Village on the outskirts of Damaturu (Damaturu, Yobe). The militiamen abandoned their vehicle with two damaged tyres and blood stains from injuries sustained during the confrontation. The troops recovered eight improvised explosive devices (IEDs) with detonating cords. There were no fatalities.
On 6 July 2024, a Niger militia abducted five civilians from Garam community (Tafa, Niger). The abductees included a pregnant woman, and four other persons.

On 6 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a juju priestess and eleven people in Egbo community (Ughelli South, Delta) while they were performing sacrifices. Five other persons had been abducted prior to that of the priestess' group.
On 6 July 2024, a policeman shot and injured a lady in the Oria- Abraka community, Abraka (Ethiope East, Delta).

On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai, with the Hybrid Forces and CJTF, killed four Boko Haram fighters during a confrontation in the Sambisa Forest area in Bula Dalo, coded to Bula Dadobe (Bama, Borno). The troops recovered 80 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 metal links, 2 FN rifle magazines, and 2 G3 rifle magazines.
On 6 July 2024, soldiers raided the camp of a Kaduna militia in Iche forest, Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). 162 cattle that were previously rustled by the militia were recovered, casualties are unknown.

On 6 July 2024, a Katsina militia numbering up to 100 who were dressed in hijabs killed one person and abducted 22 to 25 residents from Runka village (Safana, Katsina). The abductees 14 of whom were members of the same family included men, women and children, residents claimed that the assailants may have been coordinated from three camps.

On 6 July 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted two journalists and some members of their families from their homes in Danhono 2 community (Chikun, Kaduna). The wife of one of the journalists was released on the same day because of health issues. The hostages were released on 12 July 2024 after six days in captivity. There was no report of ransom payment.
On 6 July 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted three people who were fetching firewood in Awulari village in Bama LGA, coded to Garno (Bama, Borno). The militia demanded a million-naira ransom.

On 6 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) clashed with ISWAP in Kwatar Shalla Shuwari, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). They killed sixteen ISWAP fighters and seized eight water vessels, several weapons, and a large amount of cash (Naira).

On 6 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants clashed with ISWAP militants at Shuwari, Kwantan Kawule and Tumbun Rogo in Kukawa LGA (Borno), coded to Kukawa. An unspecified number of ISWAP militants were killed by the rival group who were from the Buduma faction of JAS and also seized eight water vessels carrying ISWAP fighters. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 6 July 2024, ISWAP fighters shot and killed a community leader in the Mahadiya community in Gujba LGA, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe).
On 6 July 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and killed two people and injured two others after setting up a checkpoint along the Birnin Yero- Jangeru Road, coded to Jangeru (Shinkafi, Zamfara).
On 6 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) killed a member of an Unidentified cult group along the Mbak Road, Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom).
On 6 July 2024, a Plateau militia abducted one person from his shop at Anguwan Hauawa in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Plateau).
On 6 July 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Ikpele (Agatu, Benue). Three people including an elderly couple were killed, several other people were injured.
On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops engaged IS/BH fighters at Garin Bayero, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). The militiamen escaped with gunshot wounds. There were no fatalities.

On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops and hybrid forces engaged ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in an armed clash at the militants' hideout in Jongo, also called Jongo Ngrabawa (Gwoza, Borno). 11 militants were killed, others fled and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition and grenades.

On 7 July 2024, Black Axe militia, also called Aiye and an unidentified cult militia clashed at Cele bus stop in Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos). One Black Axe member was killed while he was on his way to meet up with members of his group, the day was also their 7/7 celebration.

On 7 July 2024, KADVIS and hunters clashed with a Kaduna militia and killed two of them in Maraban Issa village near Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). The militia invaded the community with the intent to rustle cows when KADVIS and hunters engaged them.

On 7 July 2024, Nigerian troops clashed with a Taraba militia after they invaded Ikaiyo Forest in Chonku, also spelt as Chonke (Wukari, Taraba). The troops killed one militiaman and recovered one AK-47 rifle, 39 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, and one magazine. They destroyed the militia's camp.

On 7 July 2024, security forces, coded as military and police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Katibu mountain (Lau, Taraba). Two women who were abducted on the same day were rescued, three members of the group were arrested. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 July 2024, two rival armed groups clashed at Chinka (Wukari, Taraba) and two persons from the same group were killed. The deceased were on the wanted list of security agencies.
On 7 July 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of people, including women and children, from Dianawa town in Wurno LGA, coded to Wurno (Sokoto).
On 7 July 2024, the Vikings cult militia killed an Aye (Black Axe) cult member in Amaikwoin Ayamelum LGA, coded to Anaku (Anambra).
On 7 July 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and injured one person in the Kwanawa community (Dange-Shuni, Sokoto). They also rustled cattle.
On 7 July 2024, a Zamfara militia killed nine people and injured four others in Yar Tashar Sahabi village in Dan Sadau district (Maru, Zamfara). They abducted an unspecified number of people.
On 7 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) clashed with the Eiye, killing one person in the Akesan area of Igando (Alimosho, Lagos).

On 7 July 2024, the Nigerian troops, police and community Protection Guards repelled an attack from a Zamfara militia in Kofar Jange within Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). On 7 July 2024, a Zamfara militia killed two gatekeepers who tried to repel their attack at the residence of a businessman whom they also abducted at Kofar Jange area of Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara).
On 7 July 2024, suspected Black Axe members killed a civilian in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). The day was the militia's 7/7 celebration.

On 7 July 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash at Umuaka (Njaba, Imo). Three local defense militia members and one teenager were killed. Total 4 fatalities.
On 7 July 2024, a member of Black Axe militia, also called Aiye was killed by a joint task force team, coded as police forces in Abia. Location coded to Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia).
On 7 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings clashed and killed one person at Amuzukwu (Umuahia North, Abia).

On 7 July 2024, Black Axe militias and a rival unidentified cult group clashed and two Black Axe militia members were killed in Amikwo and another neighborhood of Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The day was also the celebration of the Black Axe militia's 7/7 day.
On 7 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a former NLC chairman around Gwarinpa (Abuja Municipal, FCT).

On 7 July 2024, suspected Black Axe militia also called Aiye killed a member of Eiye also called SEC at Iwo road area of Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). The attack took place on the day of Aiye militia's 7/7 celebration.

Around 7 July 2024 (as reported), task force operatives beat up a truck driver and injured him along Aba - Ikot Ikpene road, coded to Onicha Ngwa (Obioma Ngwa, Abia) while trying to enforce the government approved hours for movement of trucks.
On 7 July 2024, Black Axe militia and rival SVC militia clashed at MCC and around the state university in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). Four militia members from both groups were killed.

On 7 July 2024, Black Axe militia, also called Aiye and an unidentified cult militia clashed in different parts of Lagos, coded to Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos) during the 7/7 day celebration of the Black Axe militia. Several persons were injured.

On 8 July 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked residents of Dagwarga (Kachia, Kaduna) and killed two persons. The attack was a reprisal following a clash between residents of nearby Maraban Walijo and the militia which resulted in the death of one militia member (coded separately).

On 8 July 2024, soldiers abducted two civilians from the Kelebe area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) when they stormed a gathering of Kelebe-Omu Landlord Association members who had gathered to enforce a court judgement.
On 8 July 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured a woman around Yelwa in Toro LGA, coded to Toro (Bauchi). The woman later died in the hospital.
On 8 July 2024, a Zamfara militia clashed with the Kaya defense militia in Kaya village (Maradun, Zamfara). No further details.
On 8 July 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked the residents of Maguru village near Bamawa (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Casualties Unknown.

On 8 July 2024, an unidentified armed group from the Niger Republic invaded Dinawa (Wurno, Sokoto). They abducted many people and killed a man, preventing them from abducting his wife. Many residents fled their homes due to the attack from the militia, who were reported to have stormed the community riding on twenty motorcycles. They moved the hostages to Gundumi forest.

On 8 July 2024, Nigerian troops, MNJTF, CJTF and Hybrid Forces clashed with ISWAP fighters and killed two in Kwatan Dawashi in Kukuwa LGA, coded to Kukawa (Borno). Other militiamen fled with gunshot wounds. The troops recovered seven AK-47 rifles, magazines, ammunition including tax/levy receipts, jotters containing names written in Arabic, phones, radios, drugs, and ISWAP uniforms.

On 8 July 2024, Cameroonian troops and MNJTF clashed with ISWAP fighters in Kwatan Dawashi in Kukuwa LGA, coded to Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). 2 militants were killed. The troops recovered seven AK-47 rifles, magazines, ammunition including tax/levy receipts, radios, and drugs.
On 8 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) clashed with ISWAP in Dawashi Kwalta, coded to Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). They killed over twenty ISWAP fighters, with others drowned while escaping via the river.

On 8 July 2024, a Katsina militia opened fire sporadically, killing an unspecified number of people and abducting others in Kwakwari village (Faskari, Katsina). They stole motorcycles and phones. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 8 July 2024, a Taraba militia abducted two students of the Federal University Wukari in Wukari (Wukari, Taraba). A male and female were taken from their off-campus accommodation along the Wukari-Zaki Biam road at about 11pm.
On 8 July 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Maiyanga (Bassa, Plateau) and killed three of them. The victims were attacked as they were returning from Kwal with machetes.
On 8 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings cult militias clashed and killed one person in Awka (Awka South, Anambra).
On 8 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings cult militia clashed and killed one person at Lafia Junction in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue).
On 8 July 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) killed 2 people and abducted 3 others in Konkoso district, also spelled as Kwankwaso, coded to Konkwesso (Borgu, Niger).
On 9 July 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Okpe-Abavo, coded as Abavo (Ika South, Delta), killed a farmer and abducted his wife.
On 9 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and killed one person around Meiran Road, Meiran (Alimosho, Lagos).

On 9 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted six passengers from a vehicle along the Akunu Akoko and Iyere road, coded to Akunnu (Akoko North East, Ondo). The police and the Amotekun pursued the abductors and rescued two of the hostages.

On 9 July 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Olegomachi (Agatu, Benue) coded to Bagagi. At least 10 to 13 persons were killed, the assailants looted and burned houses in the attack.

On 9 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a former DVC (Academic), Ekiti State University at his residence in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). They also went away with his security guard. The group demanded a 50-million-naira ransom. The abductors later killed the hostage, and the police announced the discovery of his body on 1 August 2024. Many suspects have been arrested.

On 9 July 2024, Nigerian troops clashed with a Katsina militia, killing six on the outskirts of Kankara town (Kankara, Katsina). The militiamen were on motorcycles attempting to attack a market when the troops intercepted them, and many of them escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 9 July 2024, IS/Boko Haram (JAS) staged an illegal checkpoint along the Mafa-Dikwa Road in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). They set a truck on fire and abducted an unspecified number of people. The commuters were compelled to carry some looted items to militants' enclaves.
On 9 July 2024, IS/BH shot and killed one person after setting up an illegal checkpoint around Maiwa Kura (Mafa, Borno). They went away with a vehicle carrying food supplies.

Around 10 July 2024 (as reported), a Katsina militia who mounted a road block clashed with army troops that responded to a distress call along Ruma - Yargamiji road (Batsari, Kaduna), coded to Ruma. The militia fled and 3 empty AK-47 magazines were recovered along their escape route.

On 10 July 2024, troops of Operation Safe Haven (coded as immigration, police and military forces) led by an immigration officer clashed with an unidentified armed group in Fan district of Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau) during a raid to recover rustled cattle. The immigration officer was killed.

On 10 July 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an OSPAC member in the Igwuruta community (Ikwerre, Rivers). The group was responding to a distress call concerning an abduction case when its members were ambushed, and one got shot and killed.

On 10 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a driver and 18 passengers after waylaying an Akwa Ibom Transport Company bus around Azumini (Ukwa East, Abia). The armed group opened fire sporadically in the air before marching the hostages into the forest.
On 10 July 2024, a Kaduna militia ambushed and attacked Nigerian troops in Manini (Chikun, Kaduna). Casualties Unknown.
On 10 July 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and killed one person in Gidan Madi village (Tangaza, Sokoto). They abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 10 July 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and injured an unspecified number of people in Garin Maiwa in Tasha Kaiwa along the Anka-Mayanchi Rod in Anka LGA, coded to Anka (Zamfara). The militia also abducted nine people.

On 10 July 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Akwondo community, near Awon (Kachia, Kaduna). Three people were wounded, an unspecified number of others were abducted, a house and two shops were set ablaze.

On 10 July 2024, Nigerian troops attacked a fleeing Katsina militia group, killing several of them in Bakai village (Kankara, Katsina). The troops recovered some AK-47 rifles. The clash led to the escape of 30 hostages kept in the militia's hideout. Several fatalities coded as 3.

Around 10 July 2024 (as reported), military forces acting on intelligence engaged a Katsina militia planning to attack civilians in an armed clash in Kankara LGA (Katsina). One militia member was killed, an AK47 rifle and ammunition were recovered.

On 10 July 2024, a Plateau militia killed an immigration officer in Fan, coded to Foron (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). The officer was killed while leading an operation to retrieve some cows rustled from the area the previous Friday, coded separately.
On 10 July 2024, IS/BH abducted two people traveling along the Maiduguri-Dikwa Road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The militants snatched their two vehicles.
On 10 July 2024, a local defense militia killed 2 suspected Mahmuda members in Kpepiya (Borgu, Niger).

On 11 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the acting rector of Benue Polytechnic and two other staff members along Otukpo- Otukpa Road, coded to Otukpa (Ogbadibo, Benue). The abductors demanded a 70 million naira ransom. Four days later, the rector was released.

On 11 July 2024, Nigerian troops of Operation Whirl Stroke clashed with a Taraba militia in Geshi village, Damisa Ward (Donga, Taraba). The troops, acting on intelligence that the militia was attacking Geshi village, responded and confronted the militiamen. The militia escaped with gunshot wounds. The troops trailed them and arrested two and two motorcycles. There were no fatalities.

On 11 July 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and killed a ginger farmer at his home in Dagwarga (Kachia, Kaduna). The militia invaded his house on motorcycles and moved to a neighboring Gidan Busa and abducted six family members, coded separately.

On 11 July 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and wounded two villagers who managed to escape abduction in Gidan Busa (Kachia, Kaduna). They abducted six family members when they did not meet their main target at home. The militia had killed one person in the neighboring Dagwarga before the abduction before they moved to Gidan Busa, coded separately.
On 11 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and killed one person in Oko-Afo, Badagry (Badagry, Lagos).

Around 11 July 2024 (as reported), a Kaduna militia shot and killed two farmers in Kurutu village (Kachia, Kaduna). The militia invaded the village from neighbouring Azzara and killed the people for failing to pay the N100,000 demanded from each farmer as a precondition to farm in the area. They abducted four others, including a woman, for spying on them for the government forces.

Around 11 July 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops, acting on intelligence, intercepted and clashed with a Kaduna militia along Mallum Forest in Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Kaduna). The troops killed one militiaman while others managed to escape the onslaught. They recovered one AK-47 rifle, five AK-47 rifle magazines, 18 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, 19 rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition, and two motorbikes.

On 11 July 2024, police clashed with a Plateau militia and killed one of them in the Bukier community, coded to Bokkos (Plateau). The militia had rustled 100 cattle (coded separately) before the police engaged them and recovered 100 stolen cows.
On 11 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings cult militia clashed and killed one person in Umukwa in Awka South LGA, coded to Awka (Anambra).

On 11 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the Deputy Registrar of the Federal College of Education, Technical, in his quarter in Akoka (Somolu, Lagos). The group broke into his staff quarters and took him away.

On 12 July 2024, suspected Tiv Militia gang-raped a pregnant woman while working on her farm at Kadiri (Kokona, Nassarawa). Another man was stabbed and wounded on the farm. The pregnant woman later died in the hospital. The Alago youths retaliated and killed two Tiv men who had come to make peace with them, coded separately.

On 12 July 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked a commercial bus on the Ughelli-Agbarho road, coded to Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta). They killed a male passenger and shot and injured a female on the two legs. The whereabouts of other passengers remained unknown.
On 12 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and Eiye clashed and shot one person dead at Ewegbemi in the Ile Iwe area, Alimosho (Alimosho, Lagos).

On 12 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops around Gajibo village (Dikwa, Borno). The attack resulted in a firefight, killing one Boko Haram militant. The troops recovered his rifle.

On 12 July 2024, ISWAP militants killed two people and abducted six others in Morai village in Mobbar LGA, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). They demanded a five million naira ransom for their release.

On 12 July 2024, Nigerian troops with CJTF and Hybrid Forces killed six Boko Haram fighters in Sambisa Forest, Bama LGA, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). Other militiamen fled with gunshot wounds, and the troops rescued 57 persons, including 20 adult females and 37 children.

On 13 July 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) and killed three militiamen in Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Borno). The troops rescued 22 hostages and destroyed the militants' infrastructure.
On 13 July 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists (based on the pattern and recurrence of attacks in the area) killed a farmer with machetes in the Odomosibi area of Ijebu-Igbo (Ijebu North, Ogun).
On 13 July 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked the residents of Dogon Kade village (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Casualties Unknown.
On 13 July 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked Dan Abashi village in Kekun Waje District (Bungudu, Zamfara). No further details.
On 13 July 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked Ruwan Dawa village (Gusau, Zamfara). No further details.

On 13 July 2024, an armed Fulani pastoralist shot and killed one member of an armed group that rustled cows in the Awawa community in Kwali LGA, coded to Kwali (FCT). On 13 July 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire sporadically, scaring people away, and abducted a man from his car in Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The armed group took the hostage away and his car. Another person was later abducted in the area in the evening of the same day (unclear if the armed group was the same), coded separately.

On 13 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man driving in a Lexus 350 vehicle at Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). On 13 July 2024, ISWAP clashed with Nigerian troops in Goniri town (Gujba, Yobe). The militant killed three soldiers in the onslaught.

On 13 July 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a petrol station attendant at St. Michael's Secondary School junction, Nimo (Njikoka, Anambra). The armed group abducted the victim's boss, who was in the same car with him when the armed group killed him.

On 13 July 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed an unspecified number of people and injured many others in Gidan Dawa village in Tsafe LGA, coded to Tsafe (Zamfara). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 13 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man in Oraukwu (Njikoka, Anambra). The event was one of a series of abductions that took place in the state on the same day.
On 13 July 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed an NDLEA officer around the Tipper Garage in Gwarinpa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victim was on a night operation when he was killed.

On 13 July 2024, IS/BH abducted a man and his three children from a farm inside the Government Girls Secondary School in Bama (Bama, Borno). The abductors demanded a three-million-naira ransom for their release. They released the hostages the following day without the ransom payment.

On 13 July 2024, IS/BH attacked the Nigerian troops around Pump House in Ngala LGA, coded to Ngala (Ngala, Borno). The attack resulted in a firefight, forcing the militants to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 13 July 2024, the Nigerian troops attacked the IS/BH militants, attempting to launch an onslaught on some farmers around the University of Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The militia retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 14 July 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists shot at villagers returning from their farm, killing one person in Tse Iyo in Sengev Ward (Gwer West, Benue). They wounded another person, who was later taken to Naka Hospital for treatment. Five other people were missing.

On 14 July 2024, a Zamfara militia invaded Dan Isa, a few kilometers from Bamawa (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). They shot and killed between 2 - 3 people and rustled animals. They abducted about 150 people, mostly women and children. Some of the hostages managed to escape and returned to their village.
On 14 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) clashed with the Eiye and injured one member in front of the Bradevic Hotel on Opeyemi Street in Badagry (Badagry).

On 14 July 2024, police clashed with a Zamfara militia and foiled their activities in Damba near Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). They killed an unspecified number of the militia. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 14 July 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Egwuma village in Agatu LGA, coded to Bagagi (Agatu, Benue). They attacked the community in the afternoon and hacked not less than five people to death. Fatalities range from 5 to 12. Five fatalities coded.
Around 14 July 2024 (between 3 - 24 July), suspected Fulani pastoralists abducted six people in the area of Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Four of them were released after paying a ransom.
On 14 July 2024, IS/BH militants attacked and killed a tractor driver in Fadagwe (Gwoza, Borno). They stole the tractor.

On 15 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a naval officer (assumed to be off duty) and seven others in Ibaka (Mbo, Akwa Ibom). They were abducted from the Classic Point Hotel, where they had gone for relaxation.

On 15 July 2024, the Anambra Vigilante Service shot and killed a man who was also a shop owner in front of his shop in Oba (Idemili South, Anambra). The killing triggered a violent demonstration the following day, coded separately.

On 15 July 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded an APC leader after invading his house in Yangoji (Kwali, FCT). The armed group abducted five people, including two of his children. The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 15 July 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and wounded one person in Dan Isa village near Bamawa (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The militia returned in the day to rustle animals and looted foodstuffs. They also abducted women and children from the village.

On 15 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) ambushed and killed a commercial truck driver around Daral Jama village in Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Borno). On 6 October 2025, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked an unspecified village in the Fan district of Barkin Ladi LGA, coded to LGA HQ Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi).

Around 6 October 2025 (as reported), the United Hunters Association clashed with a Kaduna militia in Yakawada (Giwa, Kaduna). The troops weathered the storm and broke through the ambush, though one Mine-Resistant Ambush Protected (MRAP) vehicle had its engine and tires damaged. There were no fatalities.

On 17 October 2025, ISWAP militants and Nigerian troops clashed at the military FOB in Gudunbali, coded to the LGA HQ Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno), after the militants attacked the site. 40 militants were killed. The army also recovered two armored tanks, seven trucks loaded with weapons, 19 AK-47 rifles, three mounted GPMGs, one PKT machine gun, and two police Hilux trucks. Thirty motorcycles were also set on fire.
